items.title: Modular OCR pipelines you can run anywhere
items.text:
An Intertype C4 linecaster (1961), after a photograph in the Science Museum Group Collection, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Credit

Linecaster turns page images into text. You build an OCR pipeline from interchangeable steps (a model that reads the text, layout, tables, formulas, post-processing) and run it unchanged on a laptop, a GPU server, a Ray or Slurm cluster or Hugging Face Jobs.

  • 🧩 Any step is replaceable. A vision-language model or a line recognizer reads the text; layout, table and formula models and rule-based post-processing are separate steps.
  • 🌍 Any machine. Only the command line changes, never the pipeline.
  • 🎯 The same result everywhere. A page's text depends only on that page and the pinned models.
  • 🔁 Built for long runs. Interrupted runs resume; failed pages are set aside with the reason.
  • 🏛️ Built on standards, not on one collection. Folders, buckets, IIIF and METS manifests, OAI-PMH; ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, Parquet and JSON Lines out. Project-specific code belongs in projects built on it.

📖 Docs: storytracer.github.io/linecaster: the reference, a page for every component and catalog entry, and llms.txt for coding agents.

items.title: 🚀 Quick start
items.text:
You need Python 3.12 and uv 0.13.6 or newer.

git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
uv run launch.py                               # list the recipes and models
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium         # the modular pipeline, a preset per step
uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/   # run a vision-language model (needs vLLM and a GPU)

You get one page record per page in out/pages/. Add --files out/files --formats md,alto for per-page files.

Note

Every pipeline is a self-contained uv script with pinned dependencies and a lock file next to it. uv run installs what it needs on the first run; models download on first use.

items.title: 🧭 Three ways to transcribe
items.text:
1. A recipe: a tested combination of presets, one per step, and the texts it writes. Each recipe has a script of its own in recipes/, which brings exactly the engines it needs:

uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/

The same without a checkout, from the script's URL:

uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py scans/ out/

2. A vision-language model reads each page, or each layout region. It runs behind vLLM or SGLang, so it needs an NVIDIA GPU and the vllm command on the PATH.

uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0

3. The modular pipeline: layout, lines and a line recognizer, then post-processing. You choose a preset for every step; linecaster presets lists them.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium \
  --hierarchy ratios --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document
Flag Effect --layout single-region the whole page as one region, no layout model --tables, --formulas add table and formula recognition --hierarchy headings and their levels --paragraphs running text in paragraphs (without it, the page stays as laid out) --document the page's document, for Markdown, HTML and JSON --set recognition.batch_size=4 change one option of a preset --files DIR --formats md,alto per-page files: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, JSON --dry-run print the plan and its graph, run nothing

Options after a recipe's name override single steps; the run record lists them.

items.title: 📥 Input
items.text:
Pages from Flags a folder of images IMAGES (--item-from-parent: each subfolder is an item) a list of images IMAGES --paths-file pages.txt Parquet with an image column --parquet PATH (--image-key, --item-key, --sequence-key) IIIF or METS manifests --manifests FOLDER, --manifests list.txt, or --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url an earlier run --pages OUT/pages

Any fsspec path works: local, s3://, hf://, http(s)://. linecaster reads IIIF Presentation and METS/MODS manifests itself; --existing-ocr also keeps the library's own OCR as ocr_original. PDF files are read by the PdfReader component (extra pypdfium2). --sample 10000 --sample-per-item 8 reads a fixed sample of the input instead, chosen by hashes of its ids before any image is read and the same whatever the setup (OUT/sample.parquet; linecaster sample without a run).

For large collections, fetch the images once, then transcribe, then bind the pages into items:

uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url OUT --rate-limit 5/1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT2/pages OUT3 --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document \
  --text literal:txt --text latin-historic+flow:md

items.title: 📦 Output
items.text:
Output For 🗂️ Page records (JSON Lines, Parquet) later pipelines: every intermediate result 🏛️ ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR libraries and viewers: every word with its position 📝 Markdown, HTML, JSON (linecaster's document) documents with headings, notes, tables, figures and formulas 📜 Texts per item (--text STRATEGY:FORMAT) literal:txt, the text exactly as read, for checking against a transcription; a strategy you name for reading and training: latin-historic+flow:md folds historic letterforms and flows the paragraphs 🖼️ Page images as JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP (pipelines/convert.py) publishing and downloads: decoded and encoded on NVIDIA GPUs where the machine has them

The text as read is always kept, exactly; nothing is normalized, joined or dehyphenated unless a text names a transcription strategy that does it (nfc, long-s, flow, unicode-marks, ... in the catalog), and spelling is never modernized. Rejected pages go to rejects/ with the reason. Every run is traced with OpenTelemetry into OUT/traces/ (nothing is sent anywhere unless you set the OTEL_* variables), and linecaster traces OUT shows where the time went.

items.title: 🌍 Run anywhere
items.text:
Where Flags 💻 this machine none: models load inside the pipeline 🖥️ this machine, with a model server --backend served 🧮 a Ray cluster --on ray --tasks 64 ☁️ Hugging Face Jobs --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> 🏛️ a Slurm cluster from Python, with datatrove's SlurmPipelineExecutor (below)

On Ray and HF Jobs every task gets one GPU and starts its own model server. A rerun into the same output folder runs only the tasks that didn't finish.

A model server that stays up 
P="--layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve $P
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1

A recipe's script serves its models too: uv run launch.py squiddle serve, then uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/ --backend served --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1.

For a vision-language model, --recognition-endpoint points transcribe_vlm.py at a running vLLM or SGLang. Servers listen on loopback only.

Ray

ray runs Ray's own command line with the pipeline's packages, so every machine has the same versions:

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --on ray --tasks 64

Images, output and the logging folder must be on storage every machine can reach, such as an s3:// bucket.

Each task reserves --cpus-per-task CPUs (default 12), --mem-per-cpu-gb GiB of memory per CPU (default 4, so 48 GiB), or --mem-per-task-gb GiB whatever its CPUs, and one GPU. Start every worker with at least that much: ray start --num-cpus, --memory and --num-gpus. Before it submits anything, a launch checks that a live node can run a task, and stops with what a task needs and what the nodes have. It also logs how many tasks fit at once. --no-fit-check leaves the check out, for a cluster that adds nodes on demand. Each task sizes its thread pools (OpenMP, BLAS, OpenCV, torch) to its CPUs, not to the machine's.

On Kubernetes, one Deployment can run the head and another the workers:

  • Start Ray in each pod through the pipeline script (uv run pipelines/<script>.py ray start …), so the pods run the script's locked packages.
  • Give each worker pod the CPUs, memory and GPU a task reserves, plus room for /dev/shm (Ray's object store), and pass the same amounts to ray start --num-cpus/--memory/--num-gpus. A pod with one GPU holds one task.
  • With the data on object storage the pods need only ephemeral storage: the environment, the model weights and Ray's temporary files.
  • Submit the run to the head with ray job submit, so it runs inside the cluster and outlives the session that submitted it. A driver outside the cluster must reach every node.
Hugging Face Jobs

One GPU per Job; each Job installs Linecaster at a pushed commit with the pipeline's pinned dependencies.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py s3://<bucket>/images hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/<run> $P \
  --paths-file hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/pages.txt --env FSSPEC_S3_ANON=true \
  --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --tasks 4000 --workers 64

--workers Jobs run at once. --flavor l4x4 --gpus 4 runs four tasks per Job. --dry-run launches nothing.

items.title: ✍️ Your own pipeline
items.text:
A Pipeline is a list of components; datatrove runs it. This is the modular pipeline, cut down:

from linecaster import Pipeline
from linecaster.backends import InProcess as P
from linecaster.components.document import DocumentComposer
from linecaster.components.hierarchy import HierarchyDetector
from linecaster.components.paragraphs import ParagraphBuilder
from linecaster.components.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.components.lines import (
    LineAssigner, LineDetector)
from linecaster.components.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.components.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.components.writers import PageFileWriter

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLayoutEngine")),
    LineDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLineEngine")),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer(
        P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleRecognitionEngine")),
    HierarchyDetector("ratios"),
    ParagraphBuilder("unicode-paragraphs"),
    DocumentComposer("linked-document"),
    PageFileWriter("out/", formats=("md", "alto"),
                   strategy="latin-historic+flow"),
])
pipeline.run("out")

The same list runs on a Slurm cluster through datatrove's Slurm executor: one array job, one GPU per task, in an environment that has the engines (venv_path):

from datatrove.executor import SlurmPipelineExecutor

SlurmPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline.steps(), tasks=64, time="04:00:00", partition="gpu",
    gpus_per_task=1, venv_path="/path/to/venv",
    logging_dir="out/logs").run()

Every component declares what it reads and adds, so pipeline.check() (which run calls first) finds a pipeline that cannot work before it starts: a recognizer without lines fails at once, with every problem listed. Put the script in pipelines/ with the # /// script block of pipelines/transcribe_modular.py (it brings the engines) and build it with linecaster.execution.run.main to get the pipelines' command line on every machine. The pipelines reference covers backends, partial runs (--until, --after) and the builder.

items.title: 🧩 How it works
items.text:
1. One record per page. Every step reads the page's Transcription and adds its annotations under its own annotator: regions, lines, readings, tables, classifications, edits. Nothing is overwritten, and documents, files and texts are rendered from the record under a rendering policy. Steps share the data model and nothing else.
  2. Contracts. Each component declares what it reads, adds, replaces or removes; the builder checks the pipeline and draws its graph from them.
  3. Backends. A model step runs InProcess, Served (a model server reached through saturate, which keeps the GPU busy) or Chat (a vision-language model behind an OpenAI-compatible server).
  4. Executors. datatrove splits the pages into tasks, runs them locally, on Ray, on Slurm or on HF Jobs, and resumes where a run stopped.

Models batch only the lines of one page, and model revisions and numerically relevant libraries are pinned, so a page's output never depends on the machine or on what else runs. Different GPU types can still differ in rare single characters.

items.title: 🧰 Models and components
items.text:
Every configuration is a preset in Linecaster's catalog: an engine, a model at a pinned revision with its original model card, and settings. The release versions the catalog: each entry's hash is in catalog.index, and a run record names every entry it used with its hash. Vision-language models run behind vLLM or SGLang; the other models run inside the pipeline or behind linecaster serve, one package per engine: linecaster-kraken (kraken), linecaster-paddlex (PaddleX) and linecaster-tesseract (Tesseract).

Every preset and recipe, with its model and settings: the catalog.

Every component by step, with its contract, backends and options: the components.

items.title: 📚 Reference
items.text: Page What it covers glossary every term linecaster uses, one meaning each architecture the packages, how a run fits together, the tests pipelines components and their contracts, the builder, partial runs, failed pages, the run record data model what a page record holds: Item, Page, annotation sets and their annotators, raw outputs and annotations, rendering policies, documents and transcription strategies evaluation scoring transcriptions against ground truths: benchmarks, lanes, score records, evidence serialization how pages are written to and read from ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR, the IIIF annotation page and the importers catalog models, presets, recipes, policies, conventions, normalizations and strategies, release versioning, and where measurements live http how readers fetch over http(s): the defaults, components, retries, unexpected HTML and the HTTP policy broker how workers share proxies and other resources across tasks, runs and machines tracing where a run's time went: OpenTelemetry traces per task and for a trace sample of pages compatibility what counts as a breaking change and how one is announced conventions the repository's rules: names, spelling, YAML and Markdown, docstrings, logging, errors, secrets components, catalog every component, engine, model, preset and recipe, generated from the code

items.title: 🏷️ Versions
items.text: The current release is v0.13.0; CHANGELOG.md lists each release's changes, upgrade notes first. While the version is 0.x, a breaking release raises the minor version (0.3 → 0.4) and every other release the patch version (versions and releases); there are no deprecation periods yet. The docs site keeps a version per release, latest for the newest. For main, run uv run linecaster docs and then uv run --group docs zensical serve in a checkout.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: All notable changes to linecaster. The format follows Keep a Changelog; each release lists upgrade notes first, then additions, changes, deprecations, removals and fixes. Versions follow the tags; the first is v0.1.0.

A pipeline is a thing of its own, and the packages are layers. Pipeline checks, draws, runs and records a list of components; a component and a backend come back from what they recorded; linecaster exports the four names most code starts from; and a test holds every package to importing only from its own layer or below. No output changes (the golden test of 0.12 holds). Engine packages need linecaster>=0.13,<0.14 (kraken, paddlex, tesseract, surya, indra, services 0.2.5; mediawiki 0.2.3).

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
python tools/codemod_0_13.py PATH moves the imports below; code written for 0.11 goes through tools/codemod_0_12.py first.

  • Modules that moved to their layer. linecaster.execution.secrets is linecaster.secrets (EnvVar); linecaster.execution.observers is linecaster.core.observers; the rules of the hierarchy and paragraphs steps are linecaster.text.hierarchy and linecaster.text.paragraphs (0.12 had put them under linecaster.engines.hierarchy.rules and linecaster.engines.paragraphs.rules, above the document builder that uses them), and their engines linecaster.engines.hierarchy and linecaster.engines.paragraphs; linecaster.formats.omnidocbench is linecaster.evaluation.omnidocbench; linecaster.catalog.docs is linecaster.docs.catalog. Who: imports of these modules. What to do: run the codemod.
  • Evidence formats and the format registry left the catalog's schema. Evidence, Evidence2, Evidence3, read_evidence and upgrade_evidence_2 are in linecaster.evaluation.evidence_format (were in linecaster.catalog.schema; linecaster.catalog no longer exports Evidence); FORMATS, json_schemas and write_schemas are in linecaster.schemas. Who: evaluations that validate evidence records with these models. What to do: import them from their new modules.
  • Tests that patch the pipelines' command line. linecaster.execution.run is four modules: options (the parser and its checks), wiring (the reader, the backends and servers, --set), allocation (tasks and workers) and run (records, executors, recipes, main). run still gives every name (run.reader, run.main, ...), but a function is looked up in the module that defines it. Who: tests that monkeypatch.setattr(run, "available_cpus", ...) and the like. What to do: patch allocation (or wiring, options) instead.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• linecaster.Pipeline: Pipeline(components, servers=[...]) with check() (the plan, or every problem), draw() (the graph as Mermaid), run(out) (datatrove's local executor, stage after stage), run_pages(docs), plan(**options) for any other executor, and to_dict() / from_dict(). Servers are named apart from the components and put last, where datatrove needs them.
  • Component.from_dict and linecaster.backends.backend_from_dict: a component and a backend rebuilt from their to_dict(), secrets as EnvVar by name. Every public component is tested to come back as it described itself.
  • from linecaster import Pipeline, Component, Page, Transcription, loaded when first used.
  • The layers of the packages, in architecture, with tests/test_import_rule.py::test_packages_import_downward.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • The README's and the docs' example pipeline is a Pipeline.

One vocabulary. linecaster's words had grown several meanings each ("block" five, "step" four), and its packages no longer said what they held. This release renames; it changes no output: a golden test holds the page records, page files, documents and texts of the sample pages to what 0.11.0 wrote, apart from the names below. The docs have tutorials and concept pages, and a glossary half the size. Engine packages need linecaster>=0.12,<0.13 (kraken, paddlex, tesseract, surya, indra, services 0.2.4; mediawiki 0.2.2).

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
python tools/codemod_0_12.py PATH rewrites code, scripts, YAML and Markdown written for 0.11 (imports, class names, step ids, flags); --dry-run lists the files. Read its diff: it renames whole words, and prose that used a word in another sense needs a look.

  • Blocks are components. A pipeline's unit was a "block", which in OCR is a text block and in linecaster also a document's Block. linecaster.blocks is linecaster.components, its base classes are in linecaster.core (Block is Component, PageBlock PageComponent, ModelBlock ModelComponent, RuleBlock RuleComponent), linecaster.testing.check_block is check_component. A document's Block keeps its name. Who: everyone who imports components or writes one. What to do: run the codemod.
  • Component packages follow the steps, one class per module. blocks.composition, blocks.conversion, blocks.binding and blocks.recognition.recognizers are divided: components.hierarchy, components.paragraphs, components.document, components.images, components.importers, components.items, components.tables, components.formulas. Who: imports from those packages. What to do: run the codemod; it splits the imports.
  • Descriptive names for the print-shop components and their steps. Typographer is HierarchyDetector, Recomposer ParagraphBuilder, Composer DocumentComposer, Binder ItemAssembler, Splitter ItemSplitter. Their steps are hierarchy, paragraphs and document (were typography, recomposition, composition): the flags --hierarchy, --paragraphs, --document, the --set paragraphs.OPTION=VALUE keys, a recipe's presets: keys and a preset's step:. The engines are hierarchy.ratios.v1, paragraphs.unicode.v1, paragraphs.by-script.v1 and document.linked.v1; the presets unicode-recomposition and linked-composition are unicode-paragraphs and linked-document (the old ids resolve with a warning). The normalization typography keeps its name. Who: command lines, recipes and presets that name these steps. What to do: run the codemod over scripts and YAML; change command lines by hand.
  • Server components say what they start. ModelServer is EngineServer, ChatModelServer VLMServer, ServiceServer VendorServer. Who: pipelines that list them. What to do: run the codemod.
  • Packages say what they hold. linecaster.runtime is linecaster.execution, linecaster.pipelines linecaster.templates (a "pipeline shape" is a pipeline template; shapes() and shape(id) are templates() and template(id)), linecaster.markup linecaster.conventions, linecaster.scoring linecaster.evaluation, linecaster.adapters linecaster.engines.chat, linecaster.broker linecaster.net.broker, linecaster.serve linecaster.serving; linecaster.text.normalize, latex and formulas are in linecaster.normalization (normalize is rules), and the rules of the hierarchy and paragraphs steps are with their engines (linecaster.engines.hierarchy, linecaster.engines.paragraphs). Who: every import of these. What to do: run the codemod.
  • A contract's role is its kind. Contract.role and a component's class attribute role ("reader", "writer", "model", ...) are kind. "Role" now only means a content role. Who: components that set role, and code that reads contract().role. What to do: rename the attribute.
  • Commands and options. linecaster models is linecaster presets; linecaster truth is linecaster ground-truth; --truth is --ground-truth (linecaster export, pipelines/score.py) and --truth-transcription --ground-truth-transcription; --trace-sample is --trace-share. Who: command lines. What to do: change them.
  • SourceDocument is SourceFile, and the conventions decision block is text_block (its class TextBlock). Who: importers, and conventions entries that decide block. What to do: run the codemod; change decision: block to decision: text_block.
  • Page records are linecaster.page/6, run records linecaster.run-record/2. page/6 names the annotators of the renamed steps by their new ids; page/5 and earlier are upgraded on load. A page's error entries name their component (was block). A run record's entries have component (was block), a contract's kind (was role) and a composite's components. Trace attributes are linecaster.component*; linecaster traces reads traces written by 0.12. Who: code that reads these files itself. What to do: read the new keys; for traces of earlier runs, use the linecaster that wrote them.
  • Hashes change, outputs do not. Every recipe's pipeline hash and the hashes of the renamed presets and of the conventions entry differ from 0.11's, because they hold the names. A run started with 0.11 is not resumed by 0.12. Who: evaluations comparing hashes across the two releases. What to do: compare by output, or score again.
  • The docs' addresses. The generated component pages are under components/ (were blocks/), by the new package names.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Tutorials (docs/start/): run a recipe, run a vision-language model, score a run against ground truth. Concept pages (docs/concepts/): an overview with diagrams, components and pipelines, models, engines and presets, page records, text and normalization, evaluation. The site's navigation is by purpose: Get started, Concepts, Reference, Operations, Contributing.
  • tests/test_vocabulary.py: retired terms stay out of code, catalog and docs, and the glossary defines each term once. tests/golden/: the sample pages' outputs are held to a stored copy.
  • Conventions for words and prose (conventions).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• The glossary has one meaning per word and no "not" column; the terms of fetching, tracing, vision-language models, ground-truth sources and contributing have sections of their own.
  • Imports inside the package are absolute.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• The generated pages of LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer and ModularTranscriber show their contract again. They said "not built" since catalog references lost their edition in 0.10; a test now fails when a component's page does not build.
  • Help texts and docstrings no longer speak of preset, recipe and policy editions or of id@edition.
  • The engine packages' catalog tests (tests/test_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py) pass again: they read a preset's edition, which 0.10 removed.
  • linecaster serve's docs name the protocol it speaks, the current page record format.
  • aiohttp, which linecaster serve imports, is a declared dependency (it was installed through saturate).
  • The reference lists every pipeline script (import_transcriptions.py and score.py were missing).

linecaster reads, keeps, writes and scores texts in any writing system: languages, scripts and writing directions are recorded where a source or a step says them, ordering follows the writing direction, and the word metrics count words in scripts with combining marks and without spaces. Runs are scored element by element by default, as OmniDocBench does, but in any script and with extra text counted; classification schemes have vocabularies with prose definitions, and a tagging step labels pages by rules or by a panel of models; ground truths are checked, sampled, published and turned into benchmark definitions by linecaster's own commands. External benchmarks are exports: linecaster runs none of their code. English outputs are as before, except where their source records a language and where Changed outputs says. Engine packages need linecaster>=0.11,<0.12 (kraken, paddlex, tesseract, surya, indra, services 0.2.3; mediawiki 0.2.1).

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
• linecaster runs no external benchmark's code: OmniDocBench is an export. The pipeline harness.v1 (pipelines/harness.py), linecaster harness, the blocks OmniDocBenchScorer and OmniDocBenchWriter, linecaster.scoring.omnidocbench, linecaster.scoring.harness and the extra omnidocbench (all 0.10.5) are gone. Who: anyone scoring runs with OmniDocBench through linecaster. What to do: linecaster export omnidocbench OUT --truth TRUTH --pages RUN and OmniDocBench's own evaluation on OUT (its README.md says how), in OmniDocBench's environment.
  • Benchmarks score elements by default. A benchmark that names no metrics now scores the element metrics (elements, tables, formulas, and reading_order where its ground truth supports reading order) beside the page metrics, so its hash changes; a benchmark that names metrics keeps its hash. A run's scores get elements.parquet beside the score records, and its result and evidence the element rates and strata. Who: evaluations whose benchmarks name no metrics, and code reading every Parquet file of a scores/ folder. What to do: name metrics: [cer, token_recall, over_extraction] for 0.10's metrics and hash, or score again; read scores.parquet by name.
  • Words are Unicode's words (uax29) by default. A benchmark that names no tokenizer counts words by UAX #29's word boundaries: a word keeps its apostrophe (note's one word, was two) and its number punctuation (1,887.5), and Chinese and Japanese count by character instead of a line as one word. Who: anyone comparing word recall or over-extraction with earlier scores. What to do: score again, or name words: whitespace in the benchmark for the earlier cut (with marks kept, below).
  • Word metrics keep combining marks and joiners. 0.10's word metrics cut words at every combining mark and format character, so Devanagari, vocalized Arabic, pointed Hebrew and Thai words fell apart; they are whole now (version 2 of the word metrics' rules). Who: anyone comparing word metrics of such texts with earlier scores. What to do: score again; evidence records name the rules' version (scoring.words), and records written before are not comparable with new ones (Evidence3.comparable).
  • language, script and direction classifications are checked where they are made: a language must be a well-formed BCP 47 tag, a script an ISO 15924 code (four letters, the first a capital), a direction one of horizontal-lr, horizontal-rl, vertical-rl, vertical-lr; anything else is a ValueError. Importers make a source's language value a tag where it is one (en_US as en-US) and leave out what is none. Who: code that recorded free-form languages or scripts. What to do: record tags and codes.
  • A benchmark refuses an output strategy that changes structure (divided-words, flow: their rules join rows or words across lines). Scoring compares line by line, so such a strategy failed only when the first page was scored; it now fails when the benchmark is read.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Element-level scoring, after OmniDocBench's methodology (linecaster.scoring.elements, .matching, .teds, .order, metrics.score_elements): each side cut into elements (regions' runs of lines, tables, formulas; a region-less output by its Markdown and HTML blocks), the ground truth's matched to the output's by grapheme n-grams and local containment into match groups (one, split, merge, many, missed, extra), each group compared as a whole and its edits attributed to its elements (counts.edit_counts_by). Rates element_cer, element_ned, teds and teds_s (tree edit distance from the tables' cells, Zhang–Shasha, no dependency), table_recall, table_precision, formula_cer, formula_ned, order_kendall and order_edit. Unlike OmniDocBench's evaluation, extra text and unmatched output tables are counted, and text is compared by the benchmark's lanes in any script. A benchmark's elements sets the matching lane (alnum by default) and thresholds; evidence records the scorer's rules' version and matching lane (scoring.elements, linecaster.scoring.ELEMENTS_VERSION) and compares by them.
  • Normalizations for comparing international typography, adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (Apache-2.0; NOTES.md): typography (low quotes, guillemets, primes, TeX's quotes, the minus sign and other dash-likes, special spaces, arrow families, the fraction slash, …, a decimal middle dot, ≦, ♢), cjk-punctuation (CJK and full-width punctuation as ASCII), checkboxes (☒ and ☐), footnote-markers ([1], [^a] as their label), bullets, leaders, superscript-digits. Also romanian-comma-below (ro; output and comparison) and line-end-hyphens (a line-end hyphen joined before a lowercase letter; comparison only, in no shipped strategy).
  • The lane typographic: reading plus those normalizations, except line-end-hyphens and romanian-comma-below, which a lane names to opt in (typographic+line-end-hyphens).
  • A normalization pattern may set engine: regex (the regex package: Unicode properties such as \p{Ll}, variable-width lookbehind); the default re is left out of the hash, so every existing normalization keeps its hash.
  • The rendering policy page-layers-described: page-layers with descriptions (a picture's description, alt text) in the body, after their region, in the scored texts, the elements and documents (a paragraph block with the role description); RenderingPolicy.described, and RenderingPolicy.layer_of takes a motivation.
  • Vocabularies, a catalog entry type (vocabularies/<scheme>.yaml, linecaster.vocabulary): each value of a classification scheme with its definition, what counts and what does not; a property scheme's also names its answers. The catalog ships role (every content role), status (with its reasons), production and the property schemes degraded, tiny, rotated, multi_column and form (definitions adapted from Omni Parse Bench, Apache-2.0); hashed in catalog.index (vocabularies), checked against the data model by catalog verify, each with a generated page.
  • Property schemes (linecaster.data.PROPERTIES, in SCHEMES): values yes and no only (Transcription.classify refuses others).
  • The tagging step, with the part tags and the measurements tagged, undecided, body_line_height, asked, cached, agreed and settled: tagging.geometry.v1 (preset geometry-tags, experimental) tags rotated and tiny lines and multi_column regions by rules on geometry, its evidence a raw output; tagging.chat.v1 asks a panel of two vision-language models, and a third on splits, behind OpenAI-compatible servers, with questions generated from the vocabularies, answers cached under a hash of everything shown (~/.cache/linecaster/tagging) and undecided items written for review (linecaster.tagging-review/1); no preset of it yet. The block Tagger (linecaster.blocks.tagging) runs either.
  • Strata (linecaster.scoring.strata): element rates by role and kind always, and by a benchmark's strata: layer, match, table_kind, a recorded language, script or direction, any classification (a tag), and for page rates slice and the page's recorded values; unrecorded where nothing is recorded. Evidence records them (strata).
  • linecaster export omnidocbench (linecaster.formats.omnidocbench.export): a ground truth and a run as the folder OmniDocBench's own evaluation reads (truth.json, predictions/), with export.yaml and a README.md; --strategy applies an output strategy (nfc) to both sides; a run's tables follow the ground truth's rule (--tables).
  • linecaster truth check (linecaster.scoring.truth): what a ground truth's page records hold, per page and in total: lines with and without text, boxes outside the image, reading order (none, partial, complete), conventions' coverage, illegible characters, recorded languages, scripts and directions, duplicate pages, roles, statuses, tables by kind, formulas, notes and continuations; a report, or JSON (--json, linecaster.truth-check/1).
  • linecaster benchmark init: a linecaster.benchmark/2 definition from a ground truth's data: supports from the data, the page ids with their hash (every page, or a sample, stratified or of one split), the lanes diplomatic and reading, and a comment per recorded script.
  • Stratified samples and item-level splits (linecaster.data.sample): SampleRule(stratify=…, per_stratum=…) by page values the caller gives, and splits/split with every page of an item in one split (split_of); rules without them select and hash as before. A benchmark's sample rule now chooses its pages where it lists no ids (wanted_pages), stratified by the pages' recorded values.
  • OmniDocBench ground truth is read (linecaster.formats.omnidocbench.from_omnidocbench, entries, import.omnidocbench.v1, preset omnidocbench-import), so models are scored on its pages by linecaster's scorer.
  • linecaster truth publish (linecaster.scoring.publish): a ground truth as Hub-ready Parquet (a row per page with its image, text and page record) and a generated dataset card (sources and licenses, conventions with their hashes, languages and scripts with counts, what it supports, normalizations embodied, splits).
  • Tokenizers for the word metrics: uax29 (Unicode's word boundaries, the default: Chinese and Japanese by character, Katakana runs whole), whitespace and characters (grapheme clusters), linecaster.scoring.tokens. A benchmark names its tokenizer (words; a benchmark that names the default keeps its hash), score rows name it (words), and evidence records it with the rules' version (scoring.words).
  • Role word counts as the texts count them: role_words writes each region's text by the output strategy and leaves out illegible spans, as the text metrics do.
  • Writing directions: the classification scheme direction (linecaster.data.writing), and Transcription.language(), .script() and .direction(), which resolve a target's value from the nearest enclosing target that records one (a word or span, its line, its region and the regions around it, the page).
  • What a text says about its writing system, on request only: linecaster.text.scripts (dominant_script, first_strong_direction by Unicode's bidirectional algorithm, scripts, script_of, default_direction).
  • Reading order in any writing direction: XY-cut, XY-Cut++, the line assigner's rows, slotting unordered regions, the recomposition's margins and drop capitals order right-to-left text from the right and vertical text by columns (from the right for vertical-rl, from the left for vertical-lr), by a direction option of the line assigner, the modular transcriber (transcribe_modular --direction) and the PaddleX layout engine, else the recorded direction (linecaster.data.geometry.frames).
  • Normalizations for other writing traditions: arabic-tatweel, arabic-marks, arabic-letters, persian-arabic-letters, hebrew-points, greek-monotonic (after nfc), cyrillic-prereform and japanese-iteration-marks; the folds of marks, letter forms and iteration marks are for comparison only.
  • Script samples for tests: linecaster.testing.scripts lays out pages in twelve writing systems and all four writing directions, with their language, script and direction recorded.
  • Languages, scripts and directions in the file formats. PAGE-XML reads and writes primaryLanguage, primaryScript, readingDirection and textLineOrder on pages, regions, lines and words (language on words), its English language names mapped to BCP 47 tags by a table generated from the PAGE schema and ISO 639-3 (linecaster.formats._languages); ALTO LANG (with OTHERLANGS read) and BASEDIRECTION; hOCR lang, dir and writing-mode on every element. Each value is kept on the narrowest target that states it, and what a format cannot hold is kept in linecaster's extension.
  • The HTML importer keeps languages and directions: lang and xml:lang on any element (notes, cells and furniture included), dir, <bdi>, <bdo> and CSS writing-mode.
  • Documents state their language and direction (Document.language, .direction, and a block's or a span's where it differs): HTML writes them as lang, dir and writing-mode; absent from the JSON where nothing records one, so documents stay linecaster.document/2.
  • IIIF annotation pages are read (linecaster.formats.iiif.from_annotation_page, import.iiif.v1, preset iiif-import, and auto-import): linecaster's own and other software's, with media fragments in pixels or percent, fragment and SVG selectors and the bodies' languages. The bodies written carry each line's and word's own language.
  • TEI is read (linecaster.formats.tei.from_tei, import.tei.v1, preset tei-import, and auto-import by the TEI namespace): one page of a TEI P5 document, a sourceDoc surface with its zones and lines, a text with its facsimile zones, or a text without geometry; choice as the source's edits, unclear and gap as statuses, @rend as formatting, fw and note as furniture and notes, lb[@break='no'] as divided words, xml:lang as languages.
  • Line-level ground truth: text-import's option line_image reads the text of an image of one line as a page whose one line is the whole image, and a source's context (language, script, direction, as columns of a dataset: import_transcriptions --context-key language) states the page's writing system for every importer. import_transcriptions --read-images reads the page images for their size.
  • The HTML importer counts language values that are no BCP 47 tag (the measurement ill_formed_languages).
  • Tesseract presets for other scripts (experimental): tesseract-best-fraktur, -greek, -cyrillic, -arabic, -hebrew, -devanagari, -thai, -hangul, -han-simplified, -han-traditional, -japanese, -han-traditional-vertical and -japanese-vertical, tessdata_best's script models (added to the tessdata-best pin). tesseract.recognition.v1 reads a line recorded as vertical in page segmentation mode 5 and takes the option preserve_interword_spaces (set by the Thai, Hangul, Chinese and Japanese presets: without it Tesseract spaces their letters; NOTES.md).
  • linecaster.formats.omnidocbench.reading_blocks: a page's blocks in reading order (was private).

items.title: Changed outputs
items.text:
• A source's language is written back where it is recorded: an hOCR page with <html lang="en"> gives PAGE-XML primaryLanguage="English", ALTO LANG="en", a document "language": "en" and HTML <html lang="en">.
  • Languages are recorded as BCP 47 tags in their canonical form: ALTO's and hOCR's three-letter codes as the two-letter code where ISO 639-1 has one (eng as en, ger and deu as de).
  • An HTML page whose root states a language records it once for the page, no longer on every span of text; spans of another language are merged into one per run.
  • Run records list the line assigner's new parameter direction (null unless it is set).
  • A document's HTML writes a run of one language as one span lang, where formatting inside it made one span per formatted piece.
  • tesseract.recognition.v1 writes a line's text as Tesseract writes it (its line text, in logical order), no longer its words joined by spaces, and its words as the words of that text: right-to-left lines had each word's letters reversed, and Thai, Chinese, Japanese and Korean lines spaces between letters (and a word per letter). On the English and Latin-script lines tried, the text is the same (NOTES.md). The hashes of tesseract-best-eng and tesseract-best-latin change with the tessdata-best pin's added files, not what they do.
  • An IIIF annotation page's edit of a span targets those characters of the line's annotation (a TextPositionSelector), and an edit of a word the word's annotation; they targeted the whole line's annotation, so the span was lost (an ALTO page's divided words, for example).
  • Table kinds read contents lists in any script (linecaster.scoring.tables): a reference may be in any script's digits and follow any abbreviation of up to four letters with its period (S. 12, стр. 5, Vol. 3) or be written 第12頁; in a script written without spaces an entry's words are counted as Unicode's words. More German, Russian, Arabic or Chinese contents lists are contents, no longer data, in the tables slice and the OmniDocBench export; English counts of words are unchanged.
  • The OmniDocBench export writes only data tables as tables (--tables data, the default; --tables all as before), on both sides alike: a table is data (printed as a table: at least two rows and two columns of filled cells, text or numbers alike), contents (a table of contents or an index laid out as a table: titles or entries with page, chapter or section references) or layout (one row, one column or one cell, a table that is one column in practice, a brace grouping lines), by linecaster.scoring.tables.table_kind, computed from the table alone. A contents or layout table is exported as its text, so its words are still scored as text. On English Wikisource's ground truth: 3,028 data, 1,466 contents and 16,924 layout tables of 21,418.
  • The slice tables counts only data tables, and the slice table-heavy is gone (also as an OmniDocBench page attribute): a table is a data table, wherever it is on the page. page_slices(gt) takes the ground truth alone.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• The HTML importer and from_hocr (tag-soup hOCR) parse HTML given as text (not bytes) as the UTF-8 it is encoded in; a page without a declared charset had its non-ASCII text garbled.
  • divided-words pairs a first half that ends with ¬, ⸗ or = (ALTO's division marks besides the hyphens), as it paired one ending with a hyphen; such words stayed divided.

items.title: Added
items.text: • OmniDocBench's own evaluation on any linecaster ground truth (pipelines/harness.py, harness.v1; linecaster.scoring.omnidocbench): OmniDocBench's code at a pinned commit (7ddb8df), imported and run in linecaster's process on pages in memory: its matching per page, its metric classes (text, tables by TEDS and TEDS-S, display formulas, reading order) per task, its aggregation at the end, into OUT/result.json and OUT/harness.yaml. Blocks OmniDocBenchScorer and OmniDocBenchWriter; formats in linecaster.formats.omnidocbench; the extra omnidocbench (what its code imports). linecaster harness runs the pinned harness itself, unchanged, in its own environment: the reference to check the in-process scoring against (not yet done on real pages). Checked: a ground truth scored against itself gives text and formula edit distance 0 and TEDS 1, and the results do not depend on how pages are grouped into tasks.

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text: • LightOnOCR-3 runs in grounding mode by default. Who is affected: anyone running lightonocr-3-0.8b or lightonocr-3-4b, by id or by the model's Hugging Face id. What to do: nothing to get grounding mode, which labels furniture, headings and footnotes and keeps figure descriptions out of the text; for the card's plain transcription call (the page as Markdown) name lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain or lightonocr-3-4b-plain. Records name the preset with its hash, so a run of 0.10.3 or earlier that names lightonocr-3-0.8b ran the plain mode (hash sha256:86ddce22…, now -plain's).

items.title: Changed outputs
items.text:
• lightonocr-3-0.8b, lightonocr-3-4b: now grounding mode, the presets lightonocr-3-0.8b-grounding and lightonocr-3-4b-grounding were (same settings, same hashes). The plain mode they ran until 0.10.3 is lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain and lightonocr-3-4b-plain, with the hashes the bare ids had. The -grounding ids resolve to the bare ones with a warning (RenamedWarning); lightonocr-3-0.8b@N from before 0.10 resolves to lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain, the mode it ran.
  • The lanes reading and alnum start with the new normalization latex-text: each LaTeX formula ($…$, $$…$$, \(…\), \[…\]) as the characters it prints, so a formula compares equal to the same text typed ($\frac{1}{2}$ and ½, $\alpha$ and α, $x^{2}$ and x² once NFKC folds them; $5 or $10 stays text). Without a formula both lanes are as before. diplomatic is unchanged: a formula there is compared as written.
  • The scored text of a formula region is its LaTeX, $LaTeX$ as a ground truth writes a formula, in place of what the line recogniser read there (squiddle's display formulas were scored as their line text, or not at all when the region had no lines). A table or formula region without lines takes its place in the regions' reading order. On the 836 Wikisource pages with formulas, squiddle's CER (full page, diplomatic) goes from 16.9 % to 13.8 %.

items.title: Added
items.text: • Page slices in the evidence (linecaster.scoring.slices): each page is in the slices its ground truth meets: plain (no table, no formula), tables, table-heavy (a table of at least 2 x 2 with 6 cells or more, its cells at least 30 % of the page's full text) and formulas; the evidence record's slices give each slice's definition, pages and CER and word recall on them, with intervals (an added field: evidence/3 stays). The page summaries name their slices.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• LightOnOCR-3's grounding mode reads its tables and inline formulas: a table block's HTML is also a Table of its region (linecaster.formats.html_table.table_from_html: cells on the grid with their spans, th a header), so the page's text and the scorer render it as every other table; an inline formula in a text line ($ q_1 $, \(…\)) is a Formula on its span, delimiters included, as a ground truth marks one ($5 or $10 stays text). The lines keep the completion as written. On the 141,461 stored grounding pages of 2026-11-13 every one of the 3,592 table blocks is read, and 29,628 inline formulas are marked.
  • On Ray, a run without engines runs every task at once by default (--workers): Ray's reservations (--cpus-per-task) decide how many fit, not the CPUs of the machine the driver runs on (a driver on a 16-CPU pod ran a 32-task scoring job 16 at a time). Rate limits and proxy lists keep their own rules.
  • More tasks than page-record files: PageRecordReader shares each file among the tasks it falls to, each keeping every k-th record, so every task has work (scoring a run written by 32 tasks over 100 cores); with as many tasks as files or fewer, each file is read whole by one task, as before.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Scoring as a pipeline (pipelines/score.py, score.v1): a run scored over many tasks, here or on Ray, like every other pipeline: PageScorer and ScoreWriter per task (each task's ground truth read in one pass, only its pages' lines decoded), then linecaster.scoring.run.aggregate on the driver (missing pages, rates, intervals, conventions) into scores.parquet and evidence.yaml, the same records as linecaster score. score_run is now score_pair per page and summarize; score and evidence files can be written to object storage. A pipeline's build can give run() an after step, run once every task is done.
  • The server here, else built by uv (--server-env auto, the default): a preset is served by the server on PATH or in the image when it is the preset's release (vLLM's image at linecaster's pin serves every preset on it), else by one uv builds (--server-env uv always; path the one there, whatever it is; linecaster.blocks.servers.provision): ChatModelServer and ServiceServer install the server a preset names at its release (vLLM: linecaster's; SGLang: its serve.version with the preset's server_packages) into an environment of its own, once per machine (LINECASTER_SERVER_ENVS, else ~/.cache/linecaster/servers), resolved as of the day after the release was uploaded to PyPI. SGLang's environment also gets a CUDA toolkit from PyPI (the compiler, headers and runtime at torch's cuda-toolkit release, laid out as a toolkit) for the kernels it compiles as it starts, as CUDA_HOME; so does vLLM's (some warm-ups compile), and each server gets its environment's CUDA libraries on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. --server-env path keeps the server on PATH or in the image.
  • Each Ray job's workers run its script's own environment (--worker-env script, the default): the job uploads its checkout and starts every worker as uv run --locked <script> python ... (the scripts' new python pass-through), built on each node the first time. One cluster of nodes with uv and linecaster's Ray then runs any pipeline script's jobs, from any commit. --worker-env node keeps the node's Python.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• One vLLM for every preset: linecaster's, 0.30.0 (linecaster.catalog.schema.VLLM_VERSION). A vLLM serve block that names no version runs on it, and its image defaults to that release's vllm/vllm-openai image. Every preset's own vLLM version and image are gone (0.26.0 for most, 0.25.1 for Surya OCR 2.5, a 0.32.1rc1 nightly in its own image for MiniCPM-OCR 1.0); a preset names another version only where linecaster's fails it. Each preset's page records the version it was validated on. By the maintainer's decision. Who: anyone running a vLLM preset, on HF Jobs (the image) or with a pinned server environment. What to do: run vLLM 0.30.0; to reproduce a run on an earlier version, name it in the preset's serve.
  • One Ray for every environment: 2.59.0, the ray extra's exact pin (was >=2.40, which resolved 2.59.0 in some scripts' locks and 2.60.0 in others). Every lock resolves it (tests/test_locks.py), so one cluster runs every pipeline script's jobs. Who: environments with another Ray. What to do: run Ray 2.59.0.

items.title: Changed outputs
items.text:
• Presets that name their own vLLM, where linecaster's 0.30.0 fails them (2026-11-16, A40s): lightonocr-2-1b and lightonocr-2-1b-regions on 0.26.0 (0.30.0's LightOnOCR model imports a class transformers 5.17 removed), minicpm-ocr-1.0 on 0.33.0 (the first release after its validated nightly; 0.30.0 has no --trust-request-mm-kwargs).
  • unlimited-ocr-2: the completion's layout blocks (<BLOCK>label[box]<FORK>text) are read into regions and text by the HTML importer (read_blocks; running head and foot, page numbers, footnotes by their labels), where the page's text was the completion's lines, markup included. Runs read again from their stored completions.
  • Presets (the resolved serve.version and serve.image): chandra-ocr-2, deepseek-ocr, deepseek-ocr-2, dots-mocr, dots-ocr, glm-ocr, lightonocr-2-1b, lightonocr-2-1b-regions, minicpm-ocr-1.0, nemotron-3.5-parse, olmocr-2-7b-1025-fp8, ovisocr2, ovisocr3, paddleocr-vl-1.6, qianfan-ocr, qwen3.5-9b, smoldocling-256m-preview, surya-ocr-2.5, unlimited-ocr. The LightOnOCR-3 presets already ran on 0.30.0.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • The served backend on a Ray worker in the script's environment: linecaster serve was started from the script's path on the job's driver, which a worker does not have (it runs Ray's copy of the job's code): every task of a --backend served job failed to start its model server (can't open file). The job now tells its workers where its code was (LINECASTER_CODE_ROOT), and a worker runs the same file in its copy (linecaster.runtime.run.here).

items.title: Not yet run on a GPU
items.text: The server-environment fixes for olmOCR-2 (the CUDA libraries on LD_LIBRARY_PATH) and Surya (vLLM with a CUDA toolkit), and the vLLM fallbacks of lightonocr-2-1b (0.26.0) and minicpm-ocr-1.0 (0.33.0), are tested only in unit tests; the Ray worker environments ran LightOnOCR-3-0.8B and squiddle (in-process).

items.title: Changed
items.text: • The default lane is diplomatic (DEFAULT_LANE; was alnum): NFC and whitespace only, the comparison with the fewest assumptions (two encodings of the same text, and a text in printed lines against one in paragraphs, compare equal; case, punctuation, ſ, ligatures, diacritics and markup count). Every other lane adds decisions: reading folds case, ſ, ligatures, quotes and dashes; alnum also drops punctuation. A patch by the maintainer's decision. Who: a benchmark that names no lanes, and code calling score_page, words or role_words without a lane. What to do: name lanes: [alnum] (or pass lane="alnum") to keep the old numbers.

items.title: Changed outputs
items.text: • chandra-ocr-2: the adapter reads the model's layout HTML (<div data-bbox data-label> blocks) with linecaster's HTML importer: regions with roles and their text (running head and foot as furniture, footnotes as notes), the completion still kept verbatim as the raw output. Before, the HTML itself was the page's text, so a score counted the markup and the boxes' numbers. Stored runs can be read again from their raw outputs.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • divided-words paired a word's halves in the order of the document's blocks, so a first half in a page's running foot (where Wikisource's editors sometimes put the last line, with {{hws}}) came after the paragraph that continues onto the next page and was never paired: the body lost the word's first half (subject written ject). Halves now pair in the order of the pages they stand on.

linecaster no longer changes a text unless it is asked to. Records and documents hold the text exactly as read; a transcription strategy (literal, or the catalog's normalizations in order) writes a text when it is written. Nothing is normalized, joined or dehyphenated by default. The catalog is versioned by the release (no editions, no lock), and the data formats keep versions of their own.

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
• Texts are named, not fixed variants. verbatim_txt, readable_txt and readable_md are gone, and so are bind's --variants, --no-texts, --no-documents, --formats and --files, and --normalization of bind and transcribe_modular (whose --files and --formats still write the page files). Who: every run that writes item texts. What to do: name each text, --text STRATEGY:FORMAT, repeatable: --text literal:txt for the text as read (the item's document, blocks separated by a blank line, the running heads with --furniture; no NFC, drop capitals not joined), --text latin-historic+unicode-marks+flow:md for 0.9's readable_md (also squiddle's second text). bind writes the literal document as JSON unless --text names others, one file per item and text (OUT/documents/<strategy>/<item>.<ext>); --jsonl adds the JSON Lines (OUT/texts/<strategy>.<format>/), whose rows carry spec, strategy, strategy_sha256 and normalizations instead of variant, fidelity, flow and scope. ItemTextWriter and ItemDocumentWriter take texts=("literal:txt", ...) and read the item's document, so an item-level Composer comes before them; PageFileWriter takes strategy (--strategy, default literal).
  • No dehyphenation by default. A division mark is resolved only by the source's own marking (divided-words: Wikisource's {{hws}}/{{hwe}}, ALTO's SUBS_CONTENT) or by a rule a strategy names (unicode-marks, squiddleocr's rule; squiddle names it). Under flow, a mark nothing resolved is joined without a space and kept (de-pends). Who: anyone who relied on 0.9's readable texts or reflowed documents being dehyphenated. What to do: name unicode-marks in the strategy where that rule suits your material. (Measured on Wikisource's 10,067 page-break words: the rule joins 99.7 % of ordinary words rightly but 94.5 % of compounds divided at their own hyphen wrongly.)
  • No NFC by default. A reading stays as the model or source gave it (kraken writes decomposed text). What to do: name nfc (or a strategy that includes it, latin-historic) where you need composed text. Scoring is unaffected: lanes normalize both sides, and errors count grapheme clusters by default.
  • Page records are linecaster.page/5; older records are upgraded when read. The derived text is dropped: nfc and normalized edits, Paragraph.text, ParagraphRow.charspan, the decisions on division marks (mark_removed, hyphen_kept) and Decision.separator. A drop capital is a part_of link to its line (the document writes its letter there), no longer a joined edit with the region removed. Who: code that read those fields. What to do: write the text with a strategy (linecaster.document.strategy.apply, or Catalog.strategy(ref).text(s) for a string).
  • Documents are linecaster.document/2: block text literal (rows as laid out, Block.wraps the layout's breaks), the source's edits as spans (Span.edit, edit_text), and strategy and producer fields. A document/1 file is read as it is, its strategy not stated. Markdown writes a wrap as a plain newline and other row breaks as hard breaks.
  • Removed: the NFC step (UnicodeNormalizer, linecaster.text.unicode), the normalization step (CharacterNormalizer, the engines normalization.latin-historic.v1 and normalization.by-script.v1, the preset latin-historic: now a strategy), the block family text, linecaster.text.variants, linecaster.data.page.Text, the rendering policy's edits, AS_WRITTEN (Transcription.text_of is the reading), and linecaster_mediawiki.join_divided_words (link_pages links only; divided-words pairs the halves).
  • The catalog has no editions and no lock. Entries are referred to by id; id@N from before resolves to the release's entry with an EditionWarning. catalog.lock, linecaster catalog release and catalog migrations are gone; linecaster catalog index writes catalog.index (every entry's hash), which verify checks. Catalog file formats are unversioned (linecaster.preset, schemas/preset.json). Who: derivatives with catalog entries of their own. What to do: drop edition from your YAML and @N from references; run catalog index.
  • Scoring: lanes are the catalog's comparison strategies: alnum (0.9's alnum@2, the default), alnum-nonmark (alnum@1), diplomatic, reading (without reading@1's hyphen join), ascii-alnum; old names resolve with a warning. A character error counts a grapheme cluster by default (unit: codepoint for 0.9's counts, identical numbers). Benchmarks are linecaster.benchmark/2 (output strategy, lanes, unit), evidence linecaster.evidence/3 (lanes and output by hash); older files are upgraded when read, and evidence/2 is comparable to none written since.
  • Engine packages need linecaster>=0.10,<0.11: linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra and -services 0.2.2 (no code change), linecaster-mediawiki 0.2.0 (join_divided_words removed).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Normalizations and strategies, two kinds of catalog entry: 23 normalizations (nfc, nfkc, long-s, ligatures, r-rotunda, superscript-e, quotes, dashes, invisible, whitespace, casefold, lowercase, markup, html-tags, letters-digits, letters-marks-digits, ascii-letters-digits, editors-corrections, editors-expansions, editors-regularizations, divided-words, unicode-marks, flow) and the strategies latin-historic (output) and diplomatic, reading, alnum, alnum-nonmark, ascii-alnum (comparison); a+b+c names an unnamed one. linecaster.text.normalize, linecaster.document.strategy, linecaster.text.offsets, linecaster.text.page.
  • Conventions declare what their source's text already is (transcription): importers copy it into Source.normalized; mediawiki declares nfc, enwikisource nfc, long-s, ligatures, r-rotunda, divided-words (from Wikisource's style guides). Scoring checks each lane against it: a score record names what the lane does not apply (conventions), and the run warns (ConventionsWarning).
  • ALTO divided words: SUBS_TYPE/SUBS_CONTENT read as each half's joined edit and written back.
  • Run records list every catalog entry the run used, with its settings and hash (catalog), the strategies its texts were written by among them. Every data file names the linecaster that wrote it (Annotator.linecaster, a document's producer, Parquet metadata). JSON schemas for page records and documents.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• The Recomposer finds paragraphs and changes no text; the DocumentBuilder writes literal blocks (a line without a row of its own in the order, or without geometry, is a row of its own; a continuation after a division mark is a wrap even in verse).
  • Markdown escapes a row that would start a Markdown block (#, -, 1., a setext underline).
  • Word recall and role words follow the lane scored; rate keys keep the lane's full id; the scorer is named by the linecaster that scored.

items.title: Changed outputs
items.text: Entries whose hash in catalog.index changed: squiddle (no normalization slot; its texts literal:txt and latin-historic+unicode-marks+flow:md), page-layers (no edits), mediawiki and enwikisource (transcription); latin-historic moved from presets to strategies. Entries whose files are the same but whose engines write differently: unicode-recomposition (paragraphs without text or mark decisions), ratios (a drop capital is a part_of link), linked-composition (literal documents), and every lane (0.9's names, now strategies).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • linecaster-mediawiki 0.1.2: join_divided_words compares a half with the whole word in Unicode's compatibility form (a half printed with a ligature, {{hws|ﬂush|flushed}}, was left unpaired) and pairs halves on one page too (a transcription that keeps the print's lines).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • The document builder kept no formatting, languages or inline formulas of a line edited as a whole (a joined edit whose text differs in length from the reading): with 0.9.1's divided words, every paragraph of an item that holds a word joined across a page break lost its italics and formulas. The spans now move with the text they cover; a span on removed text goes, one on a half written as the whole word covers the word.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• enwikisource@4: words divided across a page break ({{hws}}/{{hwe}}, {{hyphenated word start}}/end): each half is read as printed, with a joined edit giving the whole word from the span's title. The conventions' edit decision takes the kind joined.
  • linecaster-mediawiki 0.1.1: join_divided_words (called by link_pages) pairs an item's halves and gives each line a joined edit of the whole line, the first half left out and the second written as the whole word, as the wiki's main namespace writes it, a compound divided at its own hyphen keeping it (inter-crossing); the document builder writes these edits, so an item's document has the word whole where a plate, caption or table stands between the halves, and no division mark rule decides it. The reader marks a template call inside a line too when a rule of the conventions names its template ([data-mw-template=...]), outside links and tags, and an inline element a call writes first carries the call's attributes.

Ground truth from any source: importers (a new step), conventions of public sources in the catalog, an HTML importer, and anchors into the source text. And linecaster's own document in place of Docling's: pages and items are composed into linecaster.document and written as HTML, Markdown, text and JSON by linecaster; docling-core is an optional extra. The decisions are in NOTES.md (2026-11-14).

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
• Engine packages accept linecaster>=0.8,<0.10 (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -indra, -surya, -services 0.2.1; their engines are unchanged). linecaster-mediawiki 0.1.0, the first release, requires linecaster>=0.9,<0.10 (the import step).
  • Docling is no longer linecaster's document. A page's or an item's document is linecaster.document.Document (linecaster.document/1: pages and blocks, each with its kind, role, layer, text, formatting spans, section and origins), built by linecaster.document.DocumentBuilder / build_document and written by to_html, to_markdown, to_text, to_json / export (formats md, txt, html, json; from_json reads the JSON back). What to change: linecaster.formats.docling.build_docling, compose, DocumentBuilder, to_markdown, to_text, to_html, to_json, export, load_docling, EXPORT_FORMATS → their names in linecaster.document (build_docling → build_document; compose returns the document alone); to_markdown(..., region_of=...) → to_markdown(..., dividers=True) (each block's origins name its regions); docling_dict(doc) → doc.model_dump(by_alias=True). Removed with no replacement: the DocLang export (doclang, to_doclang) and table_data. The Composer puts the document into doc.metadata["document"] (was ["docling"]) and its transcription into ["document_transcription"] (was ["docling_transcription"]); ["region_of"] is gone. The files differ: the HTML is linecaster's (HTML5, DPUB-ARIA roles for notes and furniture, formatting kept), the Markdown linecaster's by the policy's MarkdownRules, the JSON a linecaster.document/1 document.
  • docling-core is the extra docling (linecaster[docling]), used only by the Docling importer (import.docling.v1, linecaster.formats.docling.from_docling) and the SmolDocling adapter; without it they raise an ImportError that names the extra. wcwidth is no longer a dependency.
  • Catalog: a one-time exception to "released editions never change". docling-composition@1, squiddle@1 and the recipe item-texts@1 (with recipes/item-texts.py) are removed from the catalog and its lock, not kept as legacy: their engine is gone. Run records that name them no longer resolve with this version (linecaster 0.8.x does). Use linked-composition@1 (engine composition.linked.v1, LinkedCompositionEngine, was composition.docling.v1, DoclingCompositionEngine) and squiddle@2; the item stage names its presets (pipelines/bind.py --recomposition unicode-recomposition --normalization latin-historic --composition linked-composition). squiddle@2 differs from squiddle@1 only in the composition: the transcriptions are the same, the document files are linecaster's.

  • Region labels are linecaster's (the strings are the same, so no layout preset changes): docling_label → region_label, DOCLING_ROLES → LABEL_ROLES (linecaster.data.policy), _xml.DOCLING_TO_PAGE_TEXT, DOCLING_TO_PAGE_ELEMENT, PAGE_ELEMENT_TO_DOCLING, RAW_TO_DOCLING, docling_from_raw → LABEL_TO_PAGE_TEXT, LABEL_TO_PAGE_ELEMENT, PAGE_ELEMENT_TO_LABEL, RAW_TO_LABEL, label_from_raw; TEXT_LABELS moved from linecaster.formats.docling to linecaster.data.policy.

  • Page records are linecaster.page/4. page/4 only adds fields (Zone.anchor, Source.revision, Classification.reason, Annotator.conventions and conventions_sha256, Formula.source); PageRecordReader and linecaster score read page/3 rows as they are. A server and its clients must run the same version.

  • TranscriptionConverter is TranscriptionImporter, and takes an importer: a preset of the new step import (auto-import@1, alto-import@1, page-xml-import@1, hocr-import@1, text-import@1, docling-import@1, html-import@1) or an engine spec. format=... becomes the preset; ground_truth=True becomes the option ground_truth, which is now the default (options={"ground_truth": False} for a library's own OCR); the default transcription is ground_truth. The builder and pipelines/harvest.py insert TranscriptionImporter("auto-import@1", transcription="ocr_original", options={"ground_truth": False}). The stat pages_without_file is pages_without_document.
  • sniff and from_text moved from linecaster.blocks.conversion.transcriptions to linecaster.formats.text.
  • The upgrade of stored rows is one chain in linecaster.data.upgrade (upgrade(row)); page_2_to_3 takes only page/2 rows.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• linecaster.document: a page's or an item's document, its model (Document, Block, Origin, Span, Grid, Page), its builder (DocumentBuilder, build_document, block_kind) and its serializers (HTML, Markdown, text, JSON). A block keeps what the Docling document lost: formatting, languages and inline formulas as spans (Span.formula), a picture's image (file), the region of every origin; a block's lines are hard line breaks in Markdown. A table cell keeps its formulas too (Cell.formulas in the data model: their spans in the cell's text, where the source marks them), so that a printed $ in a cell is no formula. A text region that continues another (its continues link, a transcription without recomposition, as an imported ground truth) is one block with it; regions and lines without geometry make blocks without boxes; origins are clamped to the page.
  • linked-composition@1 (engine composition.linked.v1) composes it, and squiddle@2 uses it.
  • Rendering policies' table and Markdown rules (TableRules: one cell as text, one column as lines, a one-row table after a table of its width that table's next row, holes filled; MarkdownRules: tables as HTML or pipe tables, escaping, the image placeholder, scripts as HTML, a dollar that is no formula as \$ (escape_dollar), a displayed formula between $$ or $ (formula_display), a line break as a backslash or two spaces (line_break)), applied by the builder and the Markdown writer.
  • The pipeline import_transcriptions.v1 (pipelines/import_transcriptions.py, shape linecaster.pipelines.import_transcriptions): a source's documents into page records by an importer; ImageParquetReader(read_images=False) reads a table without images.
  • The import step and its engines, the importers (linecaster.engines.importers): a source document (linecaster.data.SourceDocument: content, format, URI, record, revision, dataset, the page image's size, context) in, a transcription out, a ground truth by default. Built in: import.alto.v1, import.page.v1, import.hocr.v1, import.text.v1, import.docling.v1, import.html.v1, import.auto.v1, with a preset each. The engine check (check_engine, source=) covers importers.
  • Conventions (linecaster.markup, the catalog kind conventions, linecaster.conventions/1): what a public source's markup means, declaratively: rules of a match (tree: a CSS selector with text, style and ancestor conditions; json: a JSONPath, RFC 9535, extra jsonpath-rfc9535; text: a regular expression) and a decision in the data model's vocabulary (remove with a reason, invisible, unwrap, block, cell, picture, caption, note, edit, language, format, break, describe; engine packages may add more through the entry points linecaster.decisions). An entry extends at most one other at a pinned edition (replace by rule id, disable, before/after); Catalog.conventions(ref) resolves the chain with its hash. Released like policies; verify checks them (resolvable, decisions applied by their importer, prose and its headings, and across a parent's children: promotion, redundant overrides, lagging editions). The catalog's first entries: mediawiki and enwikisource (format html). Docs pages for conventions entries and for rendering policies.
  • linecaster.formats.html.HtmlConverter: HTML into a transcription by HTML's semantics (blocks, headings, lists, tables with spans, figures, MathML formulas with their LaTeX, formatting, lang), ARIA and DPUB-ARIA roles (heading, doc-pageheader, doc-pagefooter, doc-footnote, doc-noteref), the page's CSS cascaded (display: none, visibility: hidden, text-transform, from style sheets and inline styles), and a source's conventions; its coverage (what no rule matched) and whether the page's last paragraph runs on. Each line of the source is a line of its own (verse keeps its lines); a row of cells without a role is the running head at the top of the body and body text below its text or a picture (a plate's caption).
  • Anchors: Zone.anchor (characters [start, end) of the source text at Source.revision) and linecaster.markup.anchors.SourceMap, which anchors an importer's lines by aligning them with what its processor saw (verbatim pieces and opaque calls).
  • Status reasons (linecaster.data.REASONS): why something present in a source is no text of the page, on a status classification (hidden, invisible, generated, editorial, error, metadata, apparatus, elsewhere, layout).
  • linecaster.text.formulas: LaTeX without its presentation commands (a formula's content), for importers.
  • Measurements rules_matched, unmapped, anchored, ends_paragraph, starts_paragraph, table_continues, table_runs_on, unexpanded, wikidata, texvc_rejected.
  • linecaster-mediawiki (engines/mediawiki, 0.1.0): import.mediawiki.v1 reads a ProofreadPage Page: page's wikitext through wikitextprocessor (pinned to a commit) in the wiki's own context (its templates, Lua modules and style sheets, taken in from a dump by linecaster-mediawiki intake), builds HTML by MediaWiki's rules (Cite's notes, Math, Poem, Gallery, TemplateStyles, the page's header and footer as DPUB-ARIA furniture) and reads it with the HTML converter under the wiki's conventions; every line and region anchored in the revision. It reads no network: the interwiki map is the siteinfo's, and Wikidata is never asked (a well-formed id exists, nothing about it is known), so a Wikidata link prints only the text its call brings; the ids asked about are recorded (measurement wikidata). Formulas are LaTeX as MediaWiki's TeX checker writes it (texvcjs, pinned, installed by intake into the site folder and run in Node: MediaWiki's own commands as standard LaTeX, every argument in braces), the TeX as written their source; what texvc rejects stays as written (measurement texvc_rejected). link_pages links an item's pages where a paragraph runs on or a footnote continues (Cite's <ref follow=...>): as ProofreadPage joins a main-namespace page's pages, only from text into text (the importer's ends_paragraph and starts_paragraph, from the page's first and last body blocks, seeing through a block the page leaves open, a block across its parts, and its frame). A table one page leaves to the next (the footer closes it, the next page's header reopens it: table_runs_on, table_continues) is linked too, and where the header ends inside a cell, that cell; the document builder makes one table of them, the continued row joining the last by column. The reader records each top-level template call on the first element it writes (data-mw-template, data-mw-param-<name>, as Parsoid's data-mw), for conventions to match what a page's HTML does not say; tags the parser left as text print nothing. Two faults of wikitextprocessor are mended in the site's context: a Lua module's mw.html result prints its HTML (it printed "table"), and an attribute's character references are decoded, as MediaWiki's sanitizer does ({{SIC}}'s tooltip [sic] 'the').
  • The decisions continues and runs_on: a page's first block continues the previous page's last, its last runs on into the next, though a block would end there; the page reads as it is, an item joins them. enwikisource@3 uses them for {{ppoem}}'s stanzas across a page break (start=follow, end=follow).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• The catalog's kinds of entry are one table (linecaster.catalog.registry.KINDS): loading, ids, the lock tables and the prose rule are the same code for every kind; Directory.entries/bodies/paths by kind, Catalog.index.
  • The steps are defined once (STEPS); a preset's step is derived from them.
  • linecaster's scope (CLAUDE.md) includes reading, preparing and scoring ground truth; declarative conventions of public sources are the one kind of entry that names a source.
  • The docs site uses the window's full width (docs/stylesheets/layout.css); the theme capped its page grid at 61rem, which squeezed the wide tables of the reference.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • The docs site is built by Zensical (zensical==0.1.1, reading mkdocs.yml) instead of Material for MkDocs, which reaches its end of life in May 2027; versions are published with Zensical's fork of mike, as before one folder per release on gh-pages. The docs dependency group changes accordingly; preview with uv run --group docs zensical serve.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • A | inside code in a generated table (a type such as dict[str, Any] | None on a block's page) no longer shows its escaping backslash.

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text: • The default lane is alnum@2 (DEFAULT_LANE): a benchmark that names no lanes, and score_page called without them, now score alnum@2 instead of diplomatic@1. Evidence of such a benchmark from 0.8.0 is not scored like the new one (the lanes differ); name lanes: [diplomatic@1] to keep the old scoring.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • Item texts flow regions without paragraphs. The readable variants (body_blocks) took a page's text only from the recomposition's paragraphs, so a transcription without one (a ground truth, an imported ALTO, PAGE or Docling file, whose regions are its paragraphs) contributed only its tables and formulas to the item's text. A region with lines and no paragraph is now a paragraph of its own: its lines flowed, its runs_into and continues links (the latest of each, by any annotator) joining it across page breaks with a space. Regions with paragraphs are read as before.

items.title: Added
items.text: • Lane alnum@2, letters and digits of any script: reading@1's markup removed, NFKC, invisible characters removed, casefolded and NFKC again, letters, combining marks and digits (Unicode L, M, N) kept. Unlike alnum@1 a combining mark stays in its word (Devanagari vowel signs, decomposed accents), a long s or a ligature matches its plain letters, and HTML tags and LaTeX macros are not counted as words. alnum@1 and ascii-alnum@1 are unchanged.

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
