When at least half of the attempts in the last minute (20 at least) got a server error (5xx), requests pause; a probe goes out after a minute, then after waits that double up to ten minutes, and the first answer that is not a server error ends the pause. The pages wait instead of failing, and the progress line says paused: server errors. Cloudflare's 520-524 are retried like 502-504 (pybookget 91d39e4).
  • With --proxies a server error is retried through another proxy without blacklisting the one it came through (resilient-httpx blacklist_on={429}, storytracer's fork 1.5.0 at f706598): only a 429, a timeout or a connection or proxy error counts against a proxy, so an outage no longer empties the pool.
  • With --proxies (or a host's proxies), an HTML page where another format was expected is that proxy's block: the proxy is left out and the item goes on through the next one (linecaster.net.http.ProxyBlocked; HTTPFetcher.submit(..., expect=)), with no breaker pause. Without proxies such a page fails as before. The HTTP policy sets how long a blocked proxy is left out and after how many failures (blacklist_ttl: 72h, blacklist_threshold; durations in s, m, h or d). A host with no proxy left stops the run (StopRequests, a ServerError) naming when the first returns, where every following item failed with AllProxiesExhausted.
  • The HTTP policy can name statuses besides 429 that leave the proxy they came through out (blacklist_on: [403], resilient-httpx's blacklist_on); they are retried through the next proxy instead of failing the item.
  • Proxy blocks are shared through a folder of markers (--proxy-blocks FOLDER or the HTTP policy's proxy_blocks, default OUT/logs/proxy-blocks; linecaster.net.proxy_blocks), as datatrove shares finished tasks: each block is a marker written once and never changed, and every fetcher reads a host's markers at its first request there and every 30 s after. Every worker in every deployment mode, and every later run pointed at the same folder, leaves the blocked proxies out; a restarted run no longer sends requests into the blocks it found. linecaster pins resilient-httpx 1.6.0 (storytracer's fork, cdebe7d, block_proxy).
  • Through proxies, only a proxy's own failures leave it out: a block (a 429, a status in blacklist_on, an HTML block page) or a broken proxy (PROXY_ERRORS: a proxy error, no connection to it). A timeout, mostly a slow server, is retried through another proxy and leaves this one in, where it was left out for an hour (or a host's blacklist_ttl). A block no longer uses up one of the request's attempts, and the next proxy is tried without a backoff wait; the pool bounds the blocks. linecaster pins resilient-httpx 1.7.0 (storytracer's fork, bc9de0a: blocks_count_as_attempts, block_exceptions, blacklist_on_exception).
  • --on ray: a pipeline without engines (pipelines/harvest.py) runs on datatrove's RayPipelineExecutor, so on CPU-only Ray workers (--cpus-per-task, --mem-per-cpu-gb); every single-stage pipeline asked for a GPU per task.
  • A Ray run stops as a local one does (linecaster.runtime.ray.RayExecutor, also under RayGPUExecutor): an error that is not the pages' (a host's stop_on, a server, the configuration) in one task writes a stop marker to the logging folder (stopped.json), every later task ends before its pipeline starts, and the launch fails with that error. datatrove only ended the task and started the next, whose first request went straight into the block (a JSON API run sent about 990 requests into a host's 429 block that way). A launch with unfinished tasks fails too, where the Ray job ended as succeeded with "Only 8/1000 tasks completed".
  • --address joins the Ray cluster it names (linecaster.runtime.run.connect_ray: auto, HOST:6379, ray://HOST:10001); it was read but not used, so a run only found a cluster started on its own machine.
  • A task that fails no longer stops a local run with several workers (datatrove's pool stopped at the first exception, and the launch then hung): it is logged, the others go on, it runs again on the next launch, and the summary counts the unfinished tasks. Configuration, catalog and server errors, and 20 failed tasks in a row in one worker, still stop the run. kill -USR1 <pid> writes every thread's stack to the terminal.
  • --retry-failed (local): finished tasks that left rejects run again; with harvest.py their images that are there are read back and only the failed pages fetched, and the task's rejects file is written anew.
  • A proxy answered with a 429 or 503 whose Retry-After is shorter than the blacklist TTL (3600 s) is left out only that long (resilient-httpx's blacklist_ttl_from_retry_after, from storytracer's fork, pinned at 238582e as resilient-httpx 1.4.0); everything else keeps 3600 s.
  • pipelines/harvest.py runs one item per task (task_per_item of ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader): every item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item. Items are grouped by their --item-key value, so a table whose item rows are apart still gives one task per item (tables.item_runs). Other pipelines keep their task sizes. A harvest run folder started with the 1,000-page tasks has another task count: run into a new folder.
  • A resumed harvest does not fetch images again that an earlier launch wrote: ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader take reuse_folder (harvest.py: OUT/images), list an item's folder once when they reach it (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing.ExistingImages; names and sizes) and read a page whose file is there from the storage instead of fetching it from the source. Only pages of items whose task was interrupted are read back (with one item per task, at most one item per worker and restart), so storage egress stays small. Its record is complete (sha256, width, height) and says image.extra.reused; ImageFilesWriter leaves the file as it is; the reader counts it in pages, media_size (the bytes it read) and reused; the console counts it as done, apart from the downloads and their rate. Not with --existing-ocr. ImageFilesWriter writes local files as <name>.part and renames them when whole.
  • The console's size on a restart starts with the finished tasks' images: their readers' media_size from datatrove's stats files (linecaster.runtime.local.size_before), read in batches in the background while the run starts (size … until then).
  • --proxies FILE: http(s) requests through a list of proxies (one per line: a URL, or host:port[:user:pass] as Webshare lists them), with resilient-httpx (the extra resilient-httpx): each attempt through the next proxy, a proxy that fails an attempt left out for an hour (PROXY_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD 1, PROXY_BLACKLIST_TTL 3600 s), the attempt retried through another. Each proxy's client is pybookget's, so the rate limits (shared by all proxies), the deadline per attempt and the trace records hold as without; retries follow pybookget's counts and waits, without Retry-After. The progress line shows the proxies in rotation; credentials are never logged, and the run record keeps the file's name, not its lines.
  • --user-agent TEXT and --random-user-agent (a random browser User-Agent from pybookget's fake-useragent, a new one for each task, HTTPFetcher.new_user_agent) for every http(s) request. The default User-Agent is datatrove's, HF-Research/1.0 (linecaster.net.http.USER_AGENT), where it was linecaster (+https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster).
  • The console of a local run (linecaster.runtime.console, linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor): one line naming the pipeline, a live progress line for the whole run (pages of the total, rate, size, failed pages, task, time left), a line per finished task and a summary, in human units; a progress log line every 30 s off a terminal. datatrove's pipeline listing (with the builder's boundary steps) and stats blocks go only to the task logs. The completion markers are listed once per launch instead of looked up task by task. With several workers the worker processes report their counts to the console (a multiprocess manager's dict), and every worker's task lines show. On a terminal the progress line is pinned to the top row and everything else scrolls below it (a scroll region, console.Pinned), so log lines and output from worker processes or libraries never break it.
  • ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader pass pages on as their http(s) requests finish, not in row order, so a slow or retried request delays only its own page (prefetched(..., ordered=False)); pages read without a request keep their order. Requests in flight are capped at the rate limits times the deadline per attempt (HTTPFetcher.max_ahead). In a 2,000-page smoke run the oldest request, being retried, held the window full of finished pages for minutes (94 pages/min against 150).
  • Fetch records and traces carry each attempt's outcome (tries, the span attribute http.tries): a status for a response read whole, <status>-cut for one the deadline cut, no-response for a timeout or a connection error.
  • --max-pages N (--parquet, IMAGES; max_pages of ImageParquetReader and ImageFolderReader): the first N pages of the input for the whole run, in the same automatic tasks, so a smoke test is the real setup stopped early (--limit counts per task).

  • A response that trickles no longer holds a task: the deadline per attempt (above) cuts it and fetches it again, usually through another proxy exit. In a smoke run one such response took 150 s while the 199 pages behind it waited; the trace shows a cut attempt as http.attempts 2.

  • Four more page readers, each run on a 60-page sample (NOTES.md): model entries surya-ocr-2.5, indra-ocr, oxr-1.0, falcon-ocr (Falcon OCR pinned at the revision its vendor image ships) and their presets surya-ocr-2.5@1, indra-ocr@1, oxr-1.0@1, falcon-ocr@1 (step recognition, unit page).

  • Page engines: PageRecognizer runs an engine whose unit is the page on the InProcess or Served backend (or a page engine's preset by name), besides a chat VLM on Chat. Engine packages linecaster-indra (indra.recognition.v1: the indra-ocr package on the CPU), linecaster-surya (surya.recognition.v1: the surya-ocr package's full-page path attached to vLLM) and linecaster-services (falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1: clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's page pipelines behind their own HTTP APIs).
  • ServiceServer (servers): starts the service a page preset's serve block names, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the fetched model pin, or a vendor image's entrypoint (serve.server: vendor with command, health, weights_dir, new optional fields of the preset schema), ready once its health URLs answer.
  • pipelines/transcribe_page.py (transcribe_page.v1): a page engine per page, with the service its preset names unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one; launch.py runs a page engine's preset there.
  • linecaster.testing: FakePageEngine (fake.recognition.page.v1) and fake_service(), an HTTP service on loopback answering given routes. tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py checks the page engines in the environment of pipelines/transcribe_page.py.
  • Versioned docs: the docs workflow publishes the site with mike to the gh-pages branch, served by GitHub Pages: every release tag as version <major>.<minor> (latest the newest release, the default); mike joins the dependency group docs.
  • pytest-xdist joins the dependency group dev: uv run pytest -n auto runs the tests on every core, as CI does; a plain uv run pytest stays serial. CI keeps uv's cache between runs.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• The engine packages (linecaster-kraken, -paddlex, -tesseract, -surya, -indra, -services) 0.1.1 accept linecaster >=0.1,<0.3; the engine API only gained the optional image_input.
  • The docs site publishes releases only; the reference for main is built in a checkout (linecaster docs, then mkdocs serve).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• The run's description of its HTTP policy includes the run's own --rate-limit, --proxies and --random-user-agent, which hold between the file's root and its hosts' entries; before, a file without rate limits read "no rate limit" although the options' limits applied.
  • A blocked or broken proxy is marked in the broker and logged once per block: the requests already on their way through it come back blocked too and go on through another proxy without a mark, a message or a failure of their own (before, each rewrote the mark and logged the block again).
  • ServiceServer notices a service that exits while it boots at once, instead of at its next look at the health URLs (every 2 s).
  • A resumed harvest's listing of an item's folder in OUT/images (the images already written, to reuse) could hang forever on object storage, and with it the worker: with 250 workers writing to S3-compatible storage only 28 got to fetch. The readers now wait at most linecaster.blocks.readers.existing.LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) for it (fsspec is given the timeout too, so it cancels the listing on its IO loop); one that times out or fails is a WARNING (listing <folder> for files to reuse took over 60 s; its pages are fetched again) and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and the item's pages are fetched again (their files are overwritten, which is safe).
  • A page could fail with HTTP 520 during an outage the breaker had seen: when the request's last server error opened the breaker and another request's probe was answered (closing it) before that error got back to the fetch, the fetch found the breaker closed and gave up. It now tries again whenever the breaker opened during its attempts (Breaker.openings).
  • The rate limits started afresh with every task (each made its own fetcher), so a worker's next task could send a whole window's requests at once; and ImageParquetReader never closed its fetcher, leaving a thread per task. The readers share one fetcher per process and configuration (HTTPFetcher.shared).
  • ImageParquetReader: an image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after the retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) no longer fails the task. The page comes without image and with the error in doc.metadata["errors"] (field image, raw_value its URI), so the page records and rejects keep it and a rerun of the task does not fail on the same dead link again; the reader has an error budget (max_page_errors, set by --max-page-errors), so a server that is down still fails the task. ImageFilesWriter passes a page that carries errors and no image through without writing a file. A row with neither image bytes nor a path still fails the task.

items.title: Upgrade notes
items.text:
The first release, after the refactoring of November 2026 in six phases; each phase's renames are listed here, and all of them in one table at the end of these notes. There are no compatibility aliases: old imports, flags and ids fail.

Phase 1: layout and names

  • Packages: linecaster.transcription, linecaster.page → linecaster.data (data model) and linecaster.formats (ALTO, PAGE, hOCR; formats.docling was linecaster.document); text.py, unicode.py, reflow.py, retyper.py → linecaster.text.variants, .unicode, .recomposition, .typography; images.py, plots.py → linecaster.images; run, jobs, ray_executor, provenance → linecaster.runtime.* (run.rows() → run.pages()); linecaster.models → linecaster.adapters; blocks/http.py → linecaster.net; blocks by family under linecaster.blocks.<family> (old modules filters, media, models, serve, texts, document, readers, writers are gone); specs/ → docs/reference/.
  • Blocks: PageStep → PageBlock, ModelStep → ModelBlock, WorkingImages → ImageConverter, AttachImage → ImageFetcher, LayoutStep → LayoutDetector, LinesStep → LineDetector, AssignLinesToRegions → LineAssigner, RecognitionStep → LineRecognizer, ChatRegionStep → RegionRecognizer, ChatPageStep → PageRecognizer, TablesStep → TableRecognizer, FormulasStep → FormulaRecognizer, NormalizeUnicode → UnicodeNormalizer, Typography → Typographer, ComposePage → Composer, ValidatePages → PageValidator, RejectSink → RejectWriter, RecipeStamp → RecipeStamper, ServeModels → ModelServer, ServeChatModel → ChatModelServer, PageRowReader → PageRecordReader; writers: PageFilesWriter + PageExportsWriter → PageFileWriter (text_fallback=False is the old PageExportsWriter), ItemExportsWriter → ItemDocumentWriter, ItemTextJsonlWriter + ItemTextFilesWriter → ItemTextWriter(format=...). Datatrove display names changed with them (stats and logs).
  • Engines: …Model → …Engine (KrakenRecognitionEngine, PaddleLayoutEngine, ...); ids unchanged. Adapters: ChatModel → ChatAdapter, each VLM adapter X → XAdapter.
  • Pipeline scripts: transcribe_chain.py → transcribe_modular.py; ids chain.v1 → transcribe_modular.v1, vlm.v1 → transcribe_vlm.v1, new harvest.v1, bind.v1.
  • Flags: --recognizer → --recognition; --vlm, --vlm-endpoint → --recognition, --recognition-endpoint; --texts → --item-texts; --exports DIR → --files DIR --formats md,txt,json --naming flat --suffix .paddle --furniture (in today's terms); --rows → --pages.
  • Stored output: the default transcription ocr → ocr_new; page records in OUT/rows/ → OUT/pages/; item text fidelity normalised → normalized; typography measurement levelled → leveled. Page records written before phase 1 keep ocr; read them with transcription="ocr".
  • Catalog: no step page (page presets are step recognition, unit page, under presets/recognition/); entries are <id>.yaml with prose in <id>.md; YAML is read as YAML 1.2 with ruamel.yaml (replaces PyYAML); lock format linecaster.lock/2. Edition numbers are unchanged; 20 hashes were recomputed (the page presets and squiddle@1), so files stamped by a recipe carry the new hash; old hashes still resolve (previous_sha256).
  • American spelling throughout (e.g. normalize, NORMALIZE_MAP, quantize_confidence, COLORS).

Phase 2: contracts and the builder

  • Pipeline scripts check their pipeline before they launch: a pipeline whose contracts do not fit exits with code 2 and lists every problem. Own blocks without a contract() pass unchecked.
  • With --tasks over 1, a binder after the page blocks (--item-texts) cuts the run into two stages: page records in item shards (OUT/pages/<shard>/), then the item stage; their logs are OUT/logs/pages/ and OUT/logs/items/. One stage logs to OUT/logs/ as before.
  • --dry-run prints the plan under plan and the Mermaid graph after the JSON.
  • A page an in-process block fails on no longer fails the task: it carries the error (doc.metadata["errors"]: block, step, preset, type, error; served failures in the same shape, no longer {step, error}), later model blocks pass it on at once, and it is written to OUT/rejects/<rank>.jsonl and kept in the page records. More failures than --max-page-errors (1 % of a task's pages, counting at least 100) fail the task.
  • ImageConverter(output_folder, rejects_folder, ...) → ImageConverter(output_folder, ...) and PageValidator(rejects_folder, required, prefix) → PageValidator(required): they record why on the page and pass it on (no longer dropped); the RejectWriter (now a writer block, RejectWriter(output_folder, prefix=""), which the builder puts before the first writer of a run) writes the rejects. A derivative that used either adds a RejectWriter where it wants the file, or lets the builder add one.
  • Library code raises linecaster.errors (PipelineConfigError, CatalogError, PageError, ServerError) instead of SystemExit, ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError and TypeError for configuration, catalog, page and server errors (e.g. an unknown preset is a CatalogError, an unknown block option a PipelineConfigError); pipeline scripts raise PipelineConfigError from pipeline().
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit) without a script raises; give the pipeline's script, runtime.jobs.ENGINE_SCRIPT (the modular pipeline's engines) or engines=False (linecaster alone).
  • The run record's schema is linecaster.run-record/1 (was linecaster.run/1): pipeline lists the stages with every block's to_dict() and contract (was a list of block entries; the separate stages is gone), and pipeline_sha256 is new. A run into an OUT whose record has another pipeline_sha256 (or none: a record from before) is refused unless --new-pipeline; another --tasks always is.
  • Page records carry schema: linecaster.page/1 in their row. Records without one (written before phase 1) are read with ocr as ocr_new, and a pages/ folder without records is read from its sibling rows/: no transcription="ocr" needed any more.
  • Engines load in warm_up() before the first page, not on it: a page's measured seconds no longer include loading; the load time is the block's warm_up_seconds stat. ModelServer and ChatModelServer start their servers in warm_up() (stat warm_up_seconds, was the boot time stat).
  • engine_spec(ref) and preset_models(models) take installed=True; tests that replace engine_spec accept it.
  • On HF Jobs the tasks log JSON lines (LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1, runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor; the run record's executor is JobsExecutor).
  • Every run is traced (OpenTelemetry, a new required dependency: opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http): OUT/traces/ appears in every run folder, and a sampled page's record carries metadata.trace_id. Every stage with a run folder now has observers, so its pipeline has boundary steps.
  • Observers: on_task_end(error=None) (was on_task_end(); an own observer adds the parameter), and new hooks on_task_event, on_leave, environment(). Stream blocks notify request (with a carrier) after prepare, and done with tokens and finish_reason; PageRecognizer notifies prepare once (was twice).

Phase 3: rule-based steps, recomposition, binding

  • Text without geometry (lines without boxes, e.g. a delivered plain text): a paragraph now continues across a page break only after a division mark; before, the simple line flow joined such pages whenever the text did not end a sentence.
  • linecaster.blocks.writers.item_texts(doc, variants, transcription, token_counter) renders an item record's text variants as datatrove documents, for derivatives writing them in a format of their own; ItemTextWriter uses it.
  • linecaster.catalog.schema.RULE_STEPS lists the rule-based steps, to tell a recipe's rule-based slots from its model slots.
  • Data model: ModelInfo → StepInfo (new field engine, the engine's code id, filled by the model blocks, linecaster serve and the chat adapters), Transcription.model → Transcription.steps, ChatAdapter.model_info() → step_info(). New: Transcription.paragraphs (Paragraph, ParagraphRow, ParagraphRef, Decision), Line.normalized, and the measurements vocabulary linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS (the keys a step writes; an engine package in this repository adds a new key there first, a test checks it).
  • Page records are linecaster.page/2 (steps instead of model, paragraphs, normalized). PageRecordReader reads linecaster.page/1 records and those from before phase 1 as /2; code that reads the JSON itself reads steps.
  • The page files' step records (ALTO processingStepSettings, PAGE Labels, hOCR linecaster-step-<n>, METS agents) carry engine for steps an engine ran.
  • Catalog: the steps image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition with built-in engines in linecaster.engines, in-process only (linecaster serve refuses them); presets may name by_script strategies; capabilities.unit may be item and produces names parts (PARTS). preset-1.json gains them; no released hash changes. engine_spec(ref, installed=True, served=False) and preset_models(models, installed=True, served=False): tests that replace engine_spec accept served.
  • regex is a new core dependency (Unicode scripts).
  • The rule-based blocks take a preset or an engine spec, with options over it: Typographer() → Typographer("ratios@1"); Composer(text="reflow", sections=..., rtl=...) → Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", options={"rtl": ...}) + Composer("docling-composition@1", options={"sections": ...}), and text="lines" is a Composer without a Recomposer before it (the document is composed from paragraphs when there are, else from lines); ImageConverter(output_folder, effort=80) → ImageConverter(output_folder, "working-image@1", options={"effort": 80}). New blocks Recomposer (composition, unit="page"|"item") and CharacterNormalizer (text); Composer also takes unit="item".
  • DocumentBuilder(name, text=..., sections=..., rtl=..., stats=...) → DocumentBuilder(name, sections=...): it no longer recomposes, it composes a page's paragraphs when it has them (add_page(..., page_id=...) names the page for paragraphs continued across pages); build_docling(...) loses text, rtl and stats; formats.docling.TEXT_MODES is gone. In linecaster.text.recomposition, join_paragraphs → join (the joined text, the separator and the decision on the division mark), new break_reason, kept_reason, mark_decision, Thresholds (the geometric thresholds and the convention marks, parameters of reflow_rows, Margins.of, continues, ...); Row.bbox may be None (text only). text.typography.retype takes ratios (Ratios) and records no step (the engine does); typography.SETTINGS is gone.
  • Page records and page files: with a recomposition (--recomposition, the squiddle recipe) the transcription carries its paragraphs (with their decisions); the typography step is recorded by its engine (name and engine typography.ratios.v1, preset ratios@1 and its hash, every option as settings, seconds and datetime), and the recomposition and composition steps have step records of their own. The documents and their exports are unchanged.
  • Binding: BindItem and ItemTexts are removed. BindItem(text="reflow", sections=S) → Binder() + Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", unit="item") + Composer("docling-composition@1", unit="item", options={"sections": S}) (text="lines": without the Recomposer); the item documents are the same, the item document's metadata is the item record plus docling, region_of, item_id (no page_ids, pages, text_mode, sections). ItemTexts(variants=V, token_counter=F) → Binder() + Recomposer(..., unit="item") + CharacterNormalizer("latin-historic@1", unit="item") + ItemTextWriter(DIR, variants=V, token_counter=F): the writer renders the variants from the item record (one row per item and variant, the same columns). ItemDocumentWriter gains by_format (<format>/<item>.<ext>).
  • The readable variants (readable_txt, readable_md) are made from the item's recomposition and normalization (Paragraph.normalized) instead of text.variants' own line flow, so they change (paragraph breaks, kept hyphens; NOTES.md has the comparison). linecaster.text.variants: join_lines, page_blocks, item_blocks, continues, HYPHENS and SENTENCE_END are gone; variants(pages, page_ids=None) needs recomposed, normalized pages; body_blocks and Block.normalized are new. The normalization engines also set each table cell's normalized.
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py: --text lines|reflow → the slots --typography, --recomposition, --normalization and --composition (presets; an empty slot leaves the step out: --text lines is no --recomposition). Without a recipe the rule-based steps run only when picked (before: typography and composition always). --item-texts needs --recomposition and --normalization (the recipe squiddle has them). --set takes the rule-based steps too (--set composition.sections=true).
  • pipelines/bind.py (bind.v1, now with recipes): Binder → item recomposition → normalization → item composition, texts in OUT/texts/<variant>/ (JSONL; --files also one file per item there, was OUT/files/<variant>/) and item documents in OUT/documents/<format>/; slots --recomposition, --normalization, --composition (the new recipe item-texts@1 fills them), --variants, --formats, --furniture, --dividers, --no-texts, --no-documents, --set.
  • squiddle@1 names the rule-based presets (ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1, latin-historic@1, docling-composition@1) instead of the option text: reflow: a catalog migration, so its hash changed (files stamped by it carry the new one) and the lock's previous_sha256 lists both earlier hashes (previous_sha256 may now be a list, oldest first; Resolved.previous_sha256 is a tuple).
  • The builder carries the parts across a binder and a splitter (an item record holds its pages), apart from image and the item's document; the role splitter is new. Recomposer's contract replaces paragraphs too (it makes them anew). RecipeStamper has unit any (it stamps the pages of item records).

Phase 4: backends and families

  • VLMs are the Chat backend (linecaster.backends.Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None, headers=None, prefer="page")): PageRecognizer(spec, Served(endpoint, model=name, max_window=W, ...)) → PageRecognizer(Chat(spec, endpoint, served_name=name, max_window=W, ...)), the same for RegionRecognizer(spec, backend, labels=..., pad=...) → RegionRecognizer(Chat(...), labels=..., pad=...); either also takes a chat preset's ref (PageRecognizer( "dots-ocr"): on the task's ChatModelServer, port 8000). The adapter is block.adapter (was block.spec), the served name Chat.served_name (was the Served backend's model). Without an endpoint Chat asks http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1. The page records are unchanged.
  • The run record: a chat block's parameters are backend ({"backend": "chat", "adapter", "preset", "preset_sha256", "model", "revision", "served_name", "endpoint", ...}) instead of spec and a served backend; pipeline_sha256 covers the adapter, preset edition and hash, model and revision (no longer the served name), so a run of transcribe_vlm.py into an OUT of before is refused unless --new-pipeline.
  • ModelBlock streams for every served block, and a block names its requests with _rows, _unit, _request, _parse and _done (an own served block that overrode _run_served or RegionRecognizer._run_regions uses them). Model blocks also take a preset ref as their backend (LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3@1"): in-process).
  • SingleRegionLayout is removed: SingleRegionLayout() → LayoutDetector("single-region@1") (the built-in engine layout.single-region.v1; label and region_id are its options). The region is the same; the page now records a layout step for it (engine, preset, settings, seconds, datetime), which page files list too, and the block reads the page image instead of the record's size. ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition) needs its layout: ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition, "single-region@1").
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py needs --layout like --lines and --recognition: a run without one is --layout single-region. Presets of built-in engines stay in-process with --backend served (runtime.run.engines), and the pipelines' serve leaves them out.
  • ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) only fetches the library's OCR, as a document media with metadata["format"] (alto, hocr); its contract adds transcription_file (a new page-level part) instead of ocr_original:*. The TranscriptionConverter reads it into ocr_original: the builder puts one right after such a reader when no block reads the file, and pipelines/harvest.py has its own, so OUT/ocr/ and the page records are as before. Its hash changes (a new block), so a harvest into an OUT of before needs --new-pipeline. A file that cannot be read is now the page's error (it goes to rejects/; before, the page went on without it and ocr_failed counted it); a failed download is still counted as ocr_failed. hOCR files that state another image size are scaled to the page image (before: read as they were).
  • PARTS gains transcription_file (no released hash changes).
  • A new extra, [pypdfium2], for the PdfReader; the locks list it.

Phase 5: docs

  • linecaster catalog docs [--out docs/catalog] [--readme README.md] → linecaster docs [--out docs] [--readme README.md] [--check]: --out is now the docs folder (the catalog's pages go to <out>/catalog/). It also writes the block pages, the README's block table (between <!-- blocks:start --> / <!-- blocks:end -->), the site's docs/index.md and docs/changelog.md, and docs/llms.txt / docs/llms-full.txt; --check writes nothing and exits with 1, naming each file that differs. linecaster catalog no longer has the action docs.
  • Generated pages start with a comment saying so; their links to files outside docs/ (sources, pipeline scripts, model cards) go to GitHub. The evidence tables have two more columns, Hardware and Backend.
  • A new dependency group, docs (MkDocs and Material), not an extra: uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict.
  • CLAUDE.md holds rules only; what it described is in docs/reference/architecture.md, the data model and serialization pages.

Phase 6: tests and engine hygiene

  • Contracts name the parts a block removes (Contract.removes, parts_removed; the run record's contracts and schemas/run-record-1.json have removes). ImageConverter without keep_bytes removes image: a pipeline in which a later block reads the image (without an ImageFetcher in between) no longer passes the builder's check; it failed on its first page before.
  • RegionRecognizer(pad=None): an explicit pad wins over the adapter's region_pad, which is the default (else 8). Callers that passed pad with a preset that has a region_pad (minicpm-ocr-1.0: 0, lightonocr-2-1b-regions: 8) now get their pad. The run record names pad: null when none is given, so pipeline_sha256 of a pipeline with a RegionRecognizer changes (no released recipe has one): resuming into an older run folder needs --new-pipeline.
  • Engine packages are version 0.1.0 and depend on linecaster>=0.0.1,<0.2; they import from linecaster only linecaster.data and linecaster.engines.api. A derivative's own engine package should do the same.
  • Tests: pytest runs with --strict-markers; tests/conftest.py's make_transcription is linecaster.testing.sample_transcription.

Every rename, old → new

Blocks

Old New Family Phase PageStep PageBlock base 1 ModelStep ModelBlock base 1 WorkingImages ImageConverter (preset working-image@1 in phase 3) conversion 1 AttachImage ImageFetcher conversion 1 LayoutStep LayoutDetector layout 1 SingleRegionLayout LayoutDetector with the engine layout.single-region.v1 layout 4 LinesStep LineDetector lines 1 AssignLinesToRegions LineAssigner lines 1 RecognitionStep LineRecognizer recognition 1 ChatRegionStep RegionRecognizer (backend chat in phase 4) recognition 1 ChatPageStep PageRecognizer (backend chat in phase 4) recognition 1 TablesStep TableRecognizer recognition 1 FormulasStep FormulaRecognizer recognition 1 — TranscriptionConverter conversion 4 NormalizeUnicode UnicodeNormalizer text 1 (inside text.py) CharacterNormalizer text 3 Typography Typographer composition 1 (inside document.py, text.py) Recomposer composition 3 ComposePage Composer composition 1 BindItem, ItemTexts Binder (+ Recomposer, Composer at the item level, + item writers) binding 3 — Splitter binding 3 ValidatePages PageValidator validation 1 RejectSink RejectWriter writers 1 RecipeStamp RecipeStamper validation 1 ServeModels ModelServer servers 1 ServeChatModel ChatModelServer servers 1 PageFilesWriter, PageExportsWriter PageFileWriter writers 1 ItemExportsWriter ItemDocumentWriter writers 1 ItemTextJsonlWriter, ItemTextFilesWriter ItemTextWriter writers 1 PageRowReader PageRecordReader readers 1 other readers, PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter, ImageFilesWriter unchanged readers, writers — ModularTranscriber (composite) composites 2 — PdfReader (skeleton) readers 4

items.title: Added
items.text:
• linecaster.testing: sample pages (sample_page, sample_boxes, sample_png, sample_layout, sample_document, sample_documents, sample_transcription); fake CPU engines (FakeLayoutEngine, FakeLineEngine, FakeRecognitionEngine, FakeTableEngine, FakeFormulaEngine), registered as fake.<step>.v1 by register_fakes() (catalog.registry.REGISTERED); fake_chat_server() and completion(); the conformance checks check_engine and check_block (with transcription_changes and page_changes); the pytest markers and hooks (linecaster.testing.markers). Every built-in engine and every public block has a conformance test.
  • linecaster.engines.api: the Engine protocol, Capabilities, weights_of, hf_file, hf_snapshot, model_entry.
  • Markers gpu, network, slow, parity; gpu and network tests skip where the device or the network is missing.
  • Tests of each engine package in engines/<engine>/tests/ (conformance on the CPU, and on CUDA for kraken, and units), run with uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests; the engine READMEs give the install and test commands.
  • A missing engine's CatalogError names the engine package that provides it and the pipeline scripts that install it (catalog.code.install_hint).
  • The CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml (CPU, no secrets): uv sync --locked --all-extras, the tests without gpu, network and parity, linecaster docs --check, linecaster catalog verify, the strict site build.

  • tests/integration/ray_data_spike.py: the squiddle blocks through Ray Data (NOTES.md, 2026-11-06).

  • The block pages (docs/blocks/): an index by family and a page per block with its contract, backends, catalog step and presets, where it comes in a pipeline, the pipeline scripts that use it, its options, behavior and example, all from code; blocks whose constructor needs arguments declare docs_args for them.

  • The docstring standard (docs/reference/conventions.md, "Docstrings") and tests/test_docstrings.py: every public block, built-in engine, backend, serializer, build, run_pages, runtime.run.main and public catalog function has a summary line and Args: for its whole signature; examples for the serializers, build, main and the catalog functions.
  • docs/reference/architecture.md, docs/reference/compatibility.md (what counts as a breaking change), READMEs for the engine packages, and the docs site (mkdocs.yml).

  • Tests: the generated docs are current, and the README's "Your own pipeline" builds and checks.

  • The Chat backend (linecaster.backends.Chat) for PageRecognizer and RegionRecognizer.

  • TranscriptionConverter(format="auto"|"alto"|"page"|"hocr"|"text", source="media"|"uri", transcription="ocr_original", uri_key=None) (conversion): a library's own transcription delivered with the page, or named by a URI in its metadata, read at the page image's size.
  • The engine layout.single-region.v1 and its preset single-region@1.
  • IIIF Collections (a skeleton): ManifestReader reads a collection entry as its manifests, one item each, one level deep (a collection in a collection raises NotImplementedError), with pybookget's read_collection (a pybookget that has it).
  • PdfReader(data_folder, paths_file=None, glob_pattern="**/*.pdf", dpi=300, ...) (a skeleton, extra [pypdfium2]): one item per PDF, its pages rendered as lossless WebP; the text layer (text_layer=True) raises NotImplementedError.
  • Block contracts (contract(), Part, Contract, PARTS), the builder (linecaster.runtime.builder: build, Plan, checks, branches with when=/group=, composites, stages, run_pages), observers (linecaster.runtime.observers), the composite ModularTranscriber, the error classes (linecaster.errors), partial runs (--until, --after, --tap-after), --page IMAGE and linecaster page; docs/reference/pipelines.md.
  • docs/reference/glossary.md and docs/reference/conventions.md.
  • warm_up() on every block and backend, with the observers' on_warm_up(block, seconds); per-page failures, RejectWriter as a block, the error budget (--max-page-errors, build(max_page_errors=...)).
  • to_dict() on every block, backend and chat adapter; the run record's pydantic model (linecaster.runtime.record.RunRecord, schemas/run-record-1.json); provenance.functional_pipeline and pipeline_sha256; --new-pipeline.
  • The describe mode (runtime.run.describe_script, describe_recipe, load_script, parse); a recipe edition's expanded pipeline in the lock (pipeline, pipeline_sha256), checked by catalog verify; catalog release --migrate-pipeline. squiddle@1 has its pipeline recorded.
  • Secrets as references: linecaster.runtime.secrets.EnvVar; Served(api_key=..., headers=...).
  • linecaster.runtime.logs (JSON-lines task logs), runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor.
  • Tracing (linecaster.tracing, docs/reference/tracing.md): task spans, page traces sampled by page id (--trace-sample, build(trace_sample=...), default 0.01) plus every failed page, OUT/traces/<rank>.jsonl.gz (OTLP JSON lines) and OTLP/HTTP when the OTEL_* variables say so; served blocks send the page's traceparent in the request body and linecaster serve continues it (--traces FILE, LINECASTER_TRACES); ChatModelServer starts vLLM with --otlp-traces-endpoint when OTLP is configured; fetch spans from net.http.HTTPFetcher (fetch_record); trace_id and span_id on log records; linecaster traces OUT [--by block|preset|task] [--slowest N] [--json].
  • Rule-based engines (linecaster.engines): image.webp-lossless.v1, normalization.latin-historic.v1, typography.ratios.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1, composition.docling.v1, the engine protocol for page and item units, and dispatch by script (ScriptDispatch, linecaster.engines.scripts, normalization.by-script.v1, recomposition.by-script.v1, a preset's by_script); their pages in docs/catalog/engines/. Every threshold of the typography and the recomposition is an option (today's values the defaults). The recomposition makes Transcription.paragraphs with their rows and decisions (division marks removed and hyphens kept with the reason, paragraph breaks, continuations with their separator), continues paragraphs across regions and, recomposing an item, across pages (a page number between them does not close one), grows the item's lexicon page by page, and recomposes text-only transcriptions (a region one paragraph); CharacterNormalizer fills Paragraph.normalized too.
  • Presets of the rule-based steps, edition 1: working-image, latin-historic, ratios, unicode-recomposition, docling-composition; pipelines/transcribe_modular.py runs ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1 (with --text reflow) and docling-composition@1.
  • Item records in a stream (linecaster.blocks.base.item: doc.metadata["item"], the pages in order) for the item-unit Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer; Binder (pages → item records) and Splitter (item records → pages, with what the item-level steps added); the recipe item-texts@1 (bind.v1).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• PageRecordReader(fetch_images=True), ImageFetcher and ImageConverter dropped the fragment of page.image.uri and fetched the whole file: for a PdfReader page (file.pdf#page=n) the PDF, for an ImageParquetReader row with embedded bytes the Parquet file. A PDF page is now rendered as PdfReader renders it (at the record's metadata["pdf"]["dpi"]), a Parquet row's image read (columns id and image), and any other fragment is the page's error (field image), never the wrong bytes (linecaster.blocks.readers.fragments).
  • ImageConverter without keep_bytes declared only metadata replaced although the page leaves without its image bytes: its contract now removes image, so the builder no longer treats the image as available after it.
  • ImageFilesWriter rewrites page.image.uri and extra (to name the copy) without declaring it: its contract now replaces metadata.
  • RegionRecognizer replaces the transcription's earlier lines but declared lines only as added: its contract now replaces lines and text, so it may follow a line step.
  • RegionRecognizer ignored an explicit pad when the adapter has a region_pad.
  • RegionRecognizer failed the task on a page without image bytes; the page now carries the error (found by check_block).

  • PageValidator(required=("image",)) declared that it reads the image bytes, although it checks the page record's image entry: a page field is now read as metadata, so the validator may follow an ImageConverter that removes the bytes.

  • PageParquetWriter writes a fixed schema: datatrove took a file's columns from its first row, so a page's errors were dropped when the first page of a file had none. Page records in Parquet now always have an errors column (null without errors).

  • Tracing holds no page documents: a page a block drops no longer stays in memory, with its image, until the task ends; its trace ends when the next page enters that block.
  • A sampled page's metadata.trace_id is derived from the run and the page id, so a rerun of a run writes the same page records.
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies() reads the pipeline script and its lock as they are at the commit the Jobs install, not as the checkout holds them (with a warning when the commit is not in the checkout).

items.title: enwikisource
items.text:
Conventions · format html · extends mediawiki

English Wikisource's templates, as the classes and attributes their output carries: running heads, the end of a page's paragraph, corrections and tooltips, sidenotes, ditto marks, dot leaders, figures, editors' errata, stanzas across a page break and words divided across a page break.

Resolved: mediawiki>enwikisource, 15 rules.

Written against wiki English Wikisource (en.wikisource.org) dump enwikisource-20261101-pages-articles (Template, Module and Index namespaces) importer import.mediawiki.v1 (linecaster-mediawiki 0.1.1, wikitextprocessor 6f96ddf)

items.title: Source
items.text: English Wikisource (en.wikisource.org), its Page: pages as their wikitext is read by the MediaWiki importer: expanded with the wiki's own templates, Lua modules and style sheets from the dump of 2026-11-01, built into HTML. The rules match the classes and attributes the templates write; they extend mediawiki, which holds what MediaWiki and its extensions write on every wiki.

items.title: How the markup works
items.text:
English Wikisource's editors transcribe a scanned page into its Page: page: the running head and anything printed above the text in the page's header, the text in its body, a footer below. They mark what the page prints with templates whose output is HTML with classes of their own (wst-*, ws-*) and TemplateStyles style sheets: the running head's left, centre and right ({{RunningHeader}}, {{rh}}), centred and indented blocks, poems ({{ppoem}}), sidenotes, ditto marks, dot leaders in tables of contents, figures ({{FreedImg}}), corrections of printing errors ({{SIC}}) and notes of the editors ({{tooltip}}, {{Errata}}). Most of it is read by HTML's own semantics: blocks and inline elements, visibility: hidden ({{dhr}}, {{gap}}), text-transform in the style sheets ({{uc}}, an Index's styles), ARIA headings, lang. The rules say the rest: what a class means where HTML does not.

A page's last paragraph runs on onto the next page unless the page ends it: {{nop}} marks the end of a paragraph at a page's end.

  • Stanzas across a page break (editions 2 and 3): {{ppoem}} writes a complete poem on each Page: page, and start=follow / end=follow join a stanza only in the main namespace. The reader records each top-level template call on the first element it writes (data-mw-template, data-mw-param-<name>), so the rules match the call: a page's first stanza continues (on the poem's element), its last runs_on (on its stanzas: one element takes one decision, and a call can have both). Each page reads as it is; an item joins them.
  • Words divided across a page break (edition 4): {{hws}} and {{hwe}} ({{hyphenated word start}}, {{hyphenated word end}}) write each half as printed, in a span whose title is the whole word; the main namespace prints the whole word where {{hwe}} stands and nothing for {{hws}}. Each half is read as printed with a joined edit giving the whole word; an item's pages read together (link_pages) pair the halves and write the whole word, including a compound's own hyphen (inter-crossing), where the wiki does. The reader marks a call inside a line too when a rule names its template, so the rule matches the span the call writes.

The transcription itself is already normalized, and the entry says so (transcription, copied into each page's Source.normalized; scoring checks a lane against it): the long s is written s and typographic ligatures (ﬁ, ﬂ, ﬀ, ﬅ) as their letters, æ and œ kept, r rotunda modernized (Wikisource:Style guide/Orthography); a word broken over two lines is rejoined, a true hyphen kept (Help:Beginner's guide to typography); MediaWiki stores the text in NFC.

items.title: Not in the rules
items.text:
• Templates whose output has no class of its own and that no rule names cannot be matched in the HTML: {{ua}} (an editor's note, its text followed by "(Wikisource contributor note)"). Its text is read as printed text.
  • A word divided across two pages is joined only where an item's pages are read together, not on one page.
  • What {{FreedImg}} and a file link show is a picture region with the file's name; the importer has no image.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
• {{ua}}: a rule naming the template ([data-mw-template=Ua]) would match its output as {{hws}}'s is.
  • Dot leaders (ws-noexport) are removed whole; a list of illustrations that sets credits inside the leader element loses them.

items.title: Rules
items.text: Rule Match Decision Why running-head-cells {'css': '.wst-rh-cell'} cell {{RunningHeader}} ({{rh}}, {{rvh}} and their variants) prints the running head's left, centre and right as one line: its cells are one region of the page's furniture, each cell a region of its own. no-run-on {'css': '.wst-nop'} break {{nop}} ends the paragraph: at the end of a page it says that the page's last paragraph does not run on onto the next page. corrections {'css': ".wst-tooltip[title^='[sic]']"} edit {'kind': 'corrected', 'attr': 'title', 'extract': "^\\[sic\\]\\s*'(.*)'$"} {{SIC}} shows the text as printed and the editors' correction in its tooltip ("[sic] 'the'"): the printed text is the page's, the correction an edit of it. tooltips {'css': '.wst-tooltip'} describe {'kind': 'note', 'attr': 'title'} {{tooltip}} shows a note of the editors when the pointer rests on the text; the note is not printed. sidenotes {'css': '.wst-sidenote'} note {'role': 'marginalia'} {{left sidenote}} and {{right sidenote}} print a note in the margin beside the paragraph where they stand: a region of its own (marginalia), not part of the paragraph's text. ditto-hidden {'css': '.__ditto_hidden'} invisible {{ditto}} prints a ditto mark where a word is repeated; the word itself is kept, invisible, to give the mark its width. dot-leaders {'css': '.ws-noexport'} remove {'reason': 'generated'} Elements of class ws-noexport (dot leaders of tables of contents, navigation) are drawn by the templates and left out of exports by WS Export; the page prints leaders, not text. figure-captions {'css': '.wst-freedimg-caption'} caption {{FreedImg}} prints a figure's caption under or over it. figure-boxes {'css': 'span.wst-freedimg'} text_block {'role': 'picture'} {{FreedImg/span}} sets a figure in spans; its box is a block of its own, as the figure is on the page. errata-notes {'css': 'aside[data-group=errata]'} remove {'reason': 'editorial', 'keep_text': True} {{Errata}} shows the printed text and adds the editors' correction as a note of the group errata; the note is the editors', not the page's. stanza-continued {'css': '[data-mw-template=Ppoem][data-mw-param-start=follow]'} continues {{ppoem|start=follow}}: the page's first stanza continues the previous page's last; the module writes a complete poem on the Page: page, so only the call says it (the reader's data-mw-template and data-mw-param-start). stanza-runs-on {'css': '.ws-poem-stanza', 'inside': '[data-mw-template=Ppoem][data-mw-param-end=follow]'} runs_on {{ppoem|end=follow}}: the page's last stanza runs on into the next page's first. Matched on the poem's stanzas, since a call with start=follow too has its poem's element decided by stanza-continued. divided-words {'css': "span[data-mw-template=Hws], span[data-mw-template=Hwe], span[data-mw-template='Hyphenated word start'], span[data-mw-template='Hyphenated word end']"} edit {'kind': 'joined', 'attr': 'title'} {{hws}} and {{hwe}} write each half of a word divided across a page break as printed, the whole word in the span's title ("de-", "pends": "depends"); in the main namespace the wiki prints the whole word in its place. Each half is the page's text, the whole word a joined edit of it; an item joins the two (linecaster-mediawiki's link_pages). Matched by the call (the reader's data-mw-template), since the span has no class of its own.

items.title: mediawiki
items.text:
Conventions · format html

What MediaWiki and its extensions write on every wiki, as the MediaWiki importer's HTML has it: the software's error messages, Cite's continued notes and its note groups that are no part of the page.

Resolved: mediawiki, 2 rules.

Written against software MediaWiki 1.48 (wmf.4) with Cite, Scribunto, ProofreadPage, TemplateStyles, Math importer import.mediawiki.v1 (linecaster-mediawiki 0.1.0, wikitextprocessor 6f96ddf)

items.title: Source
items.text: MediaWiki's own markup and that of its extensions as every wiki has it, independent of any wiki's templates: Cite (<ref>, <references>), Scribunto (Lua modules), ProofreadPage (Page: pages with their header, body and footer, Index pages), TemplateStyles, Math, Poem. Written against MediaWiki 1.48 and the MediaWiki importer (import.mediawiki.v1), which expands a page's wikitext with wikitextprocessor and writes it as HTML.

items.title: How the markup works
items.text:
Most of MediaWiki's meaning reaches the importer as standard HTML, which the HTML importer reads without conventions: ProofreadPage's header and footer become the page's doc-pageheader and doc-pagefooter, Cite's notes doc-footnote elements where their marks stand, Math's formulas MathML math elements with their TeX in alttext, Poem's lines line breaks and its stanzas paragraphs, TemplateStyles' style sheets <style> elements. What remains is what only MediaWiki's classes say: the software's error messages (.error), and a note that continues one from an earlier page (mw-ref-follow, the importer's class for <ref follow=...>).

MediaWiki stores every text it saves in Unicode NFC: the entry's transcription names nfc.

items.title: Not in the rules
items.text:
• A reuse of a named note (<ref name=x/>) prints nothing where it stands; the importer leaves it out.
  • <references/> prints nothing: the notes are read where their marks are, as on the printed page.
  • Templates whose output carries no class of its own cannot be told apart in the HTML; a wiki's conventions say what its templates' classes mean.

items.title: Open questions
items.text: • Note groups (<ref group=...>) are kept as an attribute (data-group); whether a wiki's group is part of the page (a group of printed notes) or an editors' apparatus is the wiki's convention.

items.title: Rules
items.text: Rule Match Decision Why software-messages {'css': '.error', 'not_inside': 'math'} remove {'reason': 'error', 'keep_text': True} Messages of the software (a Lua error, a missing template, "Cite error ..."), not of the page; kept as a removed region so a reading can be checked for them. continued-notes {'css': 'aside.mw-ref-follow'} note {'continued': True} Cite's : the rest of a note that began on an earlier page; on the page it is a footnote that continues, not a new one.

items.title: chat.v1
items.text:
Engine · recognition · package linecaster

Base class of a chat-VLM adapter. A subclass sets adapter (its registry name) and implements request; parse has a text-only default. Every value comes from the preset:

  • model / revision: the Hugging Face id and pinned commit; served_name: the name the server hosts it under (options.served_name, default the Hub id);
  • sampling, prompt, page_longest (the page size the model expects, longest side in px; also the scale RegionRecognizer cuts regions at), region_pad and the adapter's own settings;
  • server (vllm or sglang), server_version, job_image, serve_args (the server's flags after the model, not port/host) and server_env from the serve block;
  • revision_flag (pass --revision; False for a server that must load the default branch, which the serve block then checks file by file against the pin, pin_ignore aside) and server_packages (installed into the server's Python first) from the serve block or, until the serve schema has them, options.

A run may set the options of Options over the preset's settings (chat_model(..., overrides=...), --set recognition.<option>=<value>): max_tokens, temperature and top_p replace the preset's settings.sampling values; repair_max_tokens and repair_temperature its settings.repair values (max_tokens and temperature; default off, and 0.1); repetition_detection its settings.sampling.repetition_detection (below). The values that differ from the preset's are the adapter's overrides, recorded with it (to_dict()) and so in pipeline_sha256.

Repetition detection (repetition_detection): vLLM's own guard against a completion that loops (RepetitionDetection), sent with every request of the page (its repairs too). A loop then ends early with finish_reason repetition: the text as returned (what came before the loop and the repeats up to the stop), counted (stat finish_repetition) and never repaired. On by default wherever the preset's server takes it (vLLM 0.17.0 and later, by the preset's serve.version: takes_repetition_detection), with linecaster's defaults, unless the preset's settings or the run set it: false turns it off, true gives the defaults, repetition_detection.<field>=<value> sets one field over the preset's (or the defaults). An older vLLM, SGLang or another server would ignore the field silently: there it is off by default, and asking for it is refused (PipelineConfigError). The setting in effect is in the step's settings and, while on, in the adapter's record (to_dict()) and so in pipeline_sha256.

The repair pass (repair_max_tokens above 0; PageRecognizer runs it): a page whose completion stopped at max_tokens (finish_reason == "length") is sent once more, the same request (the same image and prompt, the same top_p) with max_tokens raised to repair_max_tokens (less where the served context leaves less room: repair_cap) and the temperature repair_temperature. The repair's completion is kept where it finished ("stop"), the first one otherwise, even when the repair's is longer. With a list of caps (repair_max_tokens: [8192, 12288]) a repair that stops at its cap is sent once more with the next, and the page keeps the first completion that finished, else its first one. The procedure is the reference script's (uv-scripts/ocr lighton-ocr3-saturate.py at e2b0aa5, its docstring "Truncation and repair"), which repairs at the end of a run; PageRecognizer repairs a page as soon as its first completion is back, with the same outcome. A completion cut off at max_tokens is often a repetition loop, which a repair does not end, but a dense table can simply need more tokens and finish with more room. repair_max_tokens must be larger than max_tokens (PipelineConfigError).

Class linecaster.engines.chat:ChatAdapter Source init.py

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description max_tokens int | None None the completion's cap (default: the preset's settings.sampling.max_tokens) temperature float | None None the sampling temperature (default: the preset's) top_p float | None None nucleus sampling (default: the preset's); the repair pass keeps it repair_max_tokens int | list[int] 0 the repair passes' caps: a page whose completion stopped at max_tokens is sent again with the first cap, and again with the next while it stops at its cap (a number: one repair; a list: one per pass, rising, the first larger than max_tokens; 0 or []: off; lightonocr-3-0.8b: [8192, 12288], twice and three times its 4096) repair_temperature float 0.1 the repair pass's temperature (the reference script's, uv-scripts/ocr lighton-ocr3-saturate.py at e2b0aa5) repetition_detection RepetitionDetection | StrictBool | None None vLLM's repetition detection (vLLM 0.17.0 and later; on by default there): false turns it off, true gives the defaults (patterns of 8 to 100 tokens repeated 16 times), or its fields; repetition_detection.min_count=12 sets one field

items.title: document.linked.v1
items.text:
Engine · document · package linecaster

Composes a page's or an item's document (linecaster.document) from its regions, paragraphs or lines, and tables, following the continuation links.

The document is built by linecaster.document.DocumentBuilder under the rendering policy: a block per region by its content role (titles and headings at their levels, paragraphs, list items, captions, notes, page headers and footers in the furniture layer), tables by the policy's table rules, formulas, pictures with the image and the text read inside them, optionally sections. A text region is composed from its paragraphs when a recomposition made them (a block per paragraph), else from its lines as laid out (a block per region, one row per line: diplomatic composition); a paragraph or region that continues another (its continues link, on the same or an earlier page) is one block with it.

Composition is a rendering: a call adds nothing to the annotation sets it reads (no annotator, no annotation). The page unit is the call; an item's document (all its pages, in order) is item_document.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:LinkedDocumentEngine Source document.py Reads pages Produces document Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

items.title: hierarchy.ratios.v1
items.text:
Engine · hierarchy · package linecaster

Determines a page's hierarchy from its type sizes, every rule a ratio to the page's own body type.

The rules of linecaster.text.hierarchy. Heading levels from the type size, section headers in body type made text, headlines split off the text region they were merged into, drop capitals joined to their line, uncertain page numbers removed; each decision an annotation by the call's annotator (role and heading-level classifications, a headline region with part_of links, a joined edit, status removed, a new reading order), nothing that was there changed. The rules cover every script that is set in lines of type sizes. Every threshold is an option, the ratios preset's values the defaults. The annotator records the counts (leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped).

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

items.title: image.convert.v1
items.text:
Engine · image · package linecaster

Converts a page image into JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB (linecaster.images.transcode): the working image's colour handling (the ICC profile to sRGB, 16 to 8 bit, alpha onto white), the size limit before decoding, image warnings recorded.

Decoding runs on a GPU for JPEG, JPEG 2000 and TIFF in 8-bit gray or RGB, encoding on a GPU for JPEG and JPEG 2000, wherever the machine has an NVIDIA GPU and nvImageCodec (linecaster[nvimgcodec]); everything else, and every image on a machine without them, with Pillow. accel forces either side. Each image's record names its decoder and encoder. decode and encode are the two steps (a block runs them as stages with windows of their own); calling the engine does both.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:ImageConvertEngine Source image.py Reads pages Produces image Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

items.title: paragraphs.unicode.v1
items.text:
Engine · paragraphs · package linecaster

Recomposes the rows of each text region into paragraphs from geometry and Unicode's character properties.

linecaster.text.paragraphs: the rows of each text region joined into paragraphs, the typesetter's division marks removed, from geometry and Unicode's character properties (line, word and sentence breaks), never from a language name; the document's own words decide the one ambiguous case (a hyphen that may belong to the word). A paragraph left open at the end of a text region continues in the next one, and at the foot of a page on the next page of the item (a region of digits only between them, a page number, does not close it); the pages of an item share the lexicon, growing page by page in order. Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph, decided by the character rules alone. Covers every script whose text runs in horizontal lines.

Each page's paragraphs are ranges (Paragraph, ids <region id>_p<n>, p<n> on a page without regions) by the call's annotator of that page, made anew by each call; each decision is recorded on its paragraph (Paragraph.decisions); a continuation links the two paragraphs (runs_into on the first, continues on the second, <page id>#<id> across pages) and removes the division mark it decided on from the first one's text. Regions a status puts nowhere (removed, suppressed, duplicate) are left out.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

items.title: tagging.chat.v1
items.text:
Engine · tagging · package linecaster

Classifies zones in property schemes (and other closed schemes) by a panel of vision-language models behind OpenAI-compatible chat servers: one question per target and scheme, generated from the scheme's vocabulary, two members asked and a third on their splits, a rule per scheme for what the third decides, the answers cached under a hash of everything shown, the undecided written for review.

Each member sees the page with the target's box drawn and the target enlarged (views), and the question: the vocabulary's definition with what counts and what does not, the answers named after the property (or the scheme's values), cannot_tell and not_here, and the reply asked for as JSON, the reason first. The two members (panel) agree: that is the classification. They split, or one gives no answer: the referee is asked, and the scheme's rule (settle, else default_settle) decides: first_with_referee (the referee must give the first member's answer; where the first gave none, the second's), majority (two of three) or first (the first member alone, no referee). An item no rule settles is undecided: nothing is recorded, and it is written to review as a JSON line. The call's annotator (kind model) records the members (their presets, revisions and sampling; never their URLs or keys), the views, the rules and each vocabulary's hash; every member's completion is a raw output (its settings name the member, target and scheme), and each classification names the one it follows. Answers are cached (cache) under the hash of the request and the model's revision ($LINECASTER_CACHE/tagging, else ~/.cache/linecaster/tagging). A request that fails after retries is a ServerError. The design is in the module's docstring (linecaster.engines.tagging).

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:ChatTaggingEngine Source tagging.py Reads pages Produces tags Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

one of the targets of every scheme's vocabulary skip_roles list[str] ['separator', 'noise'] regions of these roles (and their lines) are not asked about panel list[Member] the two members asked about every target, the one a review found right more often first referee Member | None None the third member, asked where the two split or one gave no answer; none: splits are undecided, except by the rule first settle dict[str, Literal['first_with_referee', 'majority', 'first']] dict() scheme -> the rule that settles a split (first_with_referee, majority, first); schemes not named: default_settle default_settle Literal['first_with_referee', 'majority', 'first'] 'first_with_referee' the rule of the schemes settle does not name views list[Literal['page', 'crop']] ['page', 'crop'] the images each member sees: the page with the target's box drawn, the target enlarged with the same box (a page target: the page alone) page_longest int 1280 the page view's longest side at most, in pixels crop_longest int 1024 the crop view's longest side at most, in pixels context float 0.5 the margin around the target in the crop, as a share of its longer side (at least 16 pixels) box_width int 3 the red box's line width in the images sent, in pixels cache bool True answers cached under the hash of everything shown and the model's revision, and read from there cache_dir str | None None the cache's folder (operational; items.title: tagging.geometry.v1
items.text:
Engine · tagging · package linecaster

Classifies lines as rotated and tiny and text regions as multi_column from their geometry, by rules.

rotated: a line whose recorded writing direction is vertical, or whose baseline (else its polygon, when it is clearly longer than high) is tilted by max_tilt degrees or more, is rotated; one tilted less is not. tiny: a line lower than tiny times the median height of the page's body text lines is tiny; one at least that high is not. multi_column: a text region with another text region beside it is in columns; one that spans full_width of the page's text width with nothing beside it is not. Each decision is a classification of the narrowest target (a line, a region) by the call's annotator (kind rule), with its evidence (the line's tilt, height and ratio, the regions beside it) in the call's raw output (format json); the annotator records the counts (tagged, undecided) and the body lines' median height (body_line_height). Where the evidence does not decide (a line with only a box, too few body lines, a narrow region alone), nothing is recorded; with decide_no off only yes is, so that a model tagger asks about the rest. Lines and regions whose status is duplicate, removed or suppressed are left alone. The vocabularies' definitions (rotated, tiny, multi_column) are what the rules implement; the thresholds are options.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:GeometryTaggingEngine Source tagging.py Reads pages Produces tags Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description schemes list[Literal['rotated', 'tiny', 'multi_column']] ['rotated', 'tiny', 'multi_column'] the property schemes it decides decide_no bool True record no where the rules find the property absent; false: only yes, the rest left to a model tagger max_tilt float 5.0 rotated: a line tilted by this many degrees or more is rotated (the vocabulary's about 5 degrees) elongation float 3.0 rotated: a line without a baseline is measured from its polygon only when that is at least this many times longer than high (a single glyph says no angle) tiny float 0.6 tiny: a line lower than this share of the median body line height is tiny (6 pt fine print against 10-12 pt body type; a running header at 8-9 pt stays above it) min_body_lines int 5 tiny: fewer body lines than this on a page decide nothing body_roles list[str] ['paragraph', 'list_item'] tiny: the roles of the regions whose lines are the page's body text column_roles list[str] list(COLUMN_ROLES) multi_column: the roles of the text regions that make columns min_overlap float 0.25 multi_column: two regions are beside each other when their extents across the lines overlap by at least this share of the shorter one max_overlap float 0.1 multi_column: and their extents along the lines overlap by at most this share of the narrower one full_width float 0.8 multi_column: a region alone that spans at least this share of the page's text width is not in columns

Benjamin Kiessling's PP-OCRv6 (medium) line recognizer for kraken (ALMAnaCH, Inria Paris), as mirrored byte for byte on the Hugging Face Hub by Small Models for GLAM; the canonical release is the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.21788410, which is provenance only: linecaster always downloads from the mirror (Zenodo throttles). On three pages (text, table, formulas) it gave the same output as PaddleX's own download (2026-11-03).

items.title: qianfan-ocr
items.text:
Model · Qianfan-OCR · Apache-2.0

Qianfan-OCR is the Baidu Qianfan team's 4B end-to-end document model (arXiv 2603.13398): direct image-to-Markdown parsing plus prompt-driven tasks (layout analysis, table extraction, key information extraction to JSON, document questions), with an optional "Layout-as-Thought" thinking phase that first emits boxes, element types and reading order. It uses the Qianfan-VL architecture: a Qianfan-ViT encoder, a Qwen3-4B language model and an MLP adapter; the card names no base checkpoint. It claims 192 languages without a list. License: Apache-2.0 (some bundled third-party source files MIT; license file copied as upstream/623bf5d20d446abdb36606aa4547cd0c18886fe5/LICENSE). The upstream card is in upstream/623bf5d20d446abdb36606aa4547cd0c18886fe5/README.md.

items.title: unlimited-ocr-2
items.text:
Model · Unlimited-OCR 2 · MIT

Unlimited-OCR 2 ("Unlimited OCR Works 2") is Baidu's successor to Unlimited-OCR: Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA) keeps decoding cost and memory nearly constant with document length, so whole documents of hundreds of pages can be parsed in one pass. Pages go in as <PAGE><image> per page with the Multi page parsing. prompt and the output has one <PAGE> per input page. It needs trust_remote_code (custom code); upstream recommends a customized SGLang build for serving. The card says "multilingual" without a list and names no base checkpoint. License: MIT (card front matter; no license file was copied at pinning). The upstream card is in upstream/9cf077c4b206e0e2a31879df937b0b0bcba3661c/README.md.
