items.title: arabic-letters
items.text:
Normalization · for comparison · scripts Arab

Arabic spelling variants folded, as Arabic search does: alef with madda above (U+0622), with hamza above (U+0623) and below (U+0625) and alef wasla (U+0671) as bare alef (U+0627); alef maksura (U+0649) as yeh (U+064A); teh marbuta (U+0629) as heh (U+0647). On composed text (after nfc). For comparison only: these letters are spelling, and Persian and Urdu write yeh without dots.

Rule: map: آ → ا, أ → ا, إ → ا, ة → ه, ى → ي, ٱ → ا

items.title: arabic-marks
items.text:
Normalization · for comparison · scripts Arab

The Arabic script's vowel and other combining marks removed: the honorific signs and small high letters U+0610 to U+061A, the harakat, tanwin, shadda and sukun U+064B to U+0652, the further vowel signs and marks U+0656 to U+065E, the superscript (dagger) alef U+0670, and the Quranic annotation marks U+06D6 to U+06DC, U+06DF to U+06E4, U+06E7, U+06E8, U+06EA to U+06ED. The madda and hamza above and below (U+0653 to U+0655) and the wavy hamza below (U+065F) stay, as do the small waw and yeh (U+06E5, U+06E6, letters) and the end of ayah, rub el hizb and sajdah signs: they belong to the letters or the text. For comparison only: a reading text keeps its vocalization.

Rule: map: U+0610 removed, U+0611 removed, U+0612 removed, U+0613 removed, U+0614 removed, U+0615 removed, U+0616 removed, U+0617 removed, U+0618 removed, U+0619 removed, U+061A removed, U+064B removed …

items.title: arabic-tatweel
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Arab

The tatweel (kashida, U+0640), which only stretches a word, removed.

Rule: map: ـ removed

items.title: ascii-letters-digits
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Only the ASCII letters a-z and digits and U+FFFD; every run of anything else one space: an accented letter separates its word.

Rule: keep: a-z, 0-9 and U+FFFD

Strategies with it: ascii-alnum.

items.title: bullets
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

A bullet glyph (• ‣ ◦ ▪ ▶ ∙ ●) starting a line, after any indentation and before whitespace or the line's end, as a space, for comparison: a list item compares equal with or without its bullet. The same glyphs elsewhere in a line stay, as do Markdown's - * + (markup's) and ■ (a checked box: checkboxes). Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 1 pattern: ^([ \t]*)[•‣◦▪▶∙●](?=\s|$)

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: casefold
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Unicode case folding (ß as ss, final sigma as sigma).

Rule: case: fold

Strategies with it: alnum, alnum-nonmark, reading, typographic.

items.title: checkboxes
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Checkboxes as two glyphs, for comparison: a checked box (☑ ☒ ■ ▣ ✓ ✔ ✗ ✘, and [x], [X], [✓], [✗], [checked] in any case) as ☒; an unchecked one (☐ □ ◻ ◼ ❏ ▢ ⬜, and [ ], [], [unchecked] in any case) as ☐. Every such glyph is read as a box wherever it stands (■ too, which some texts use as a bullet); other brackets stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 4 patterns: \[(?:[xX✓✗]|checked)\], \[ ?\]|\[unchecked\], [☑☒■▣✓✔✗✘], [☐□◻◼❏▢⬜]

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: cjk-punctuation
items.text:
Normalization · for comparison · scripts Hani, Hira, Kana, Hang, Bopo

CJK and full-width punctuation as ASCII, for comparison: the ideographic full stop 。 and the full-width full stop ． as ., the ideographic comma 、 and the full-width comma ， as ,, the full-width : ; ! ? ( ) % = # $ & * + - / < > @ \ ^ _ ` | ~ [ ] { } and their half-width forms (｡ ､ ｢ ｣) as their ASCII characters; the corner brackets 「」『』, the double prime quotation marks 〝〞〟 and the double angle brackets 《》 as ", the single angle brackets 〈〉 as ' (as typography folds « » and ‹ ›); the lenticular and tortoise shell brackets 【】〔〕〖〗〘〙〚〛 as [ ]; the wave dash 〜 as ~. A table, so it works without nfkc (which folds the full-width forms but not 。、「」 or the brackets). Full-width letters and digits (nfkc's), the middle dots ・ ･ and the iteration and prolonged sound marks stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0), extended to the brackets and quotation marks.

Rule: map: 。 → ., ｡ → ., ． → ., 、 → ,, ､ → ,, ， → ,, ： → :, ； → ;, ！ → !, ？ → ?, （ → (, ） → ) …

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: cyrillic-prereform
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Cyrl · languages ru (language-specific)

Russian letters of the orthography before 1918 as today's: yat (ѣ U+0463, Ѣ U+0462) as е, Е; the decimal i (і U+0456, І U+0406) and izhitsa (ѵ U+0475, Ѵ U+0474, with double grave ѷ U+0477, Ѷ U+0476) as и, И; fita (ѳ U+0473, Ѳ U+0472) as ф, Ф; the hard sign (ъ U+044A, Ъ U+042A) removed after a letter at a word's end, kept inside a word (объявление). Spelling otherwise as printed: the endings -аго, -яго, ея and the prefixes без-, из- before voiceless consonants stay. Russian only: Ukrainian and Belarusian write і today.

Rule: 7 patterns: [ѣ], [Ѣ], [іѵѷ], [ІѴѶ] …

items.title: dashes
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

The dashes U+2010 to U+2015 (hyphen, non-breaking hyphen, figure dash, en dash, em dash, horizontal bar) as the hyphen-minus.

Rule: map: ‐ → -, ‑ → -, ‒ → -, – → -, — → -, ― → -

Strategies with it: reading, typographic.

items.title: divided-words
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

A word divided across lines or pages written whole where the source marks it (joined edits: Wikisource's hws/hwe, ALTO's SUBS_CONTENT): the first part left out, the whole word where the second stands, a compound's own hyphen kept. In a ground truth's conventions (transcription): its text writes such words whole.

Rule: divided_words: source

items.title: editors-corrections
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

The source's corrections applied (corrected edits: a [sic] read as the editors corrected it); the printed form is the literal text.

Rule: edits: ['corrected']

items.title: editors-expansions
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

The source's expansions applied (expanded edits: an abbreviation written out).

Rule: edits: ['expanded']

items.title: editors-regularizations
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

The source's regularizations applied (regularized edits: a spelling as the editors regularized it).

Rule: edits: ['regularized']

items.title: flow
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

A block's rows joined into running text (a space unless Unicode's line breaking joins the two words), a block continued on the next page joined to it; a division mark nothing resolved is kept, the rows joined without a space.

Rule: flow: True

items.title: footnote-markers
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Footnote markers in brackets as their label after a space, for comparison: [1] (one to three digits) and the Markdown footnote [^1] or [^a] (one to three letters or digits) as " 1", " a", so that "12.3%[1]" does not read as "12.3%1" and a marker written as a reference matches one written as text. Spaces inside the brackets are allowed; other brackets ([12a], [1, 2], [1234]) and a marker without brackets stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 1 pattern: \[\^\s*(\w{1,3})\s*\]|\[\s*(\d{1,3})\s*\]

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: greek-monotonic
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Grek

Polytonic Greek letters as monotonic (the 1982 convention): the breathings (psili U+0313, dasia U+0314) and the iota subscript and adscript (ypogegrammeni and prosgegrammeni, U+0345) dropped, the oxia, varia and perispomeni (U+0301, U+0300, U+0342) as the tonos; the diaeresis (dialytika) stays, ῒ and ῗ as ΐ. A table of the composed letters of Greek Extended (U+1F00 to U+1FFC), so it applies to composed text (after nfc). Character by character: the accents monotonic drops on monosyllables (τὸν as τόν, not τον) and an enclitic's second accent stay as the tonos.

Rule: map: ἀ → α, ἁ → α, ἂ → ά, ἃ → ά, ἄ → ά, ἅ → ά, ἆ → ά, ἇ → ά, Ἀ → Α, Ἁ → Α, Ἂ → Ά, Ἃ → Ά …

items.title: hebrew-points
items.text:
Normalization · for comparison · scripts Hebr

Hebrew points and cantillation removed: the accents U+0591 to U+05AF, the points (niqqud) U+05B0 to U+05BD, rafe U+05BF, shin and sin dot U+05C1, U+05C2, the upper and lower dot U+05C4, U+05C5, qamats qatan U+05C7 and the Judeo-Spanish varika U+FB1E; the pointed presentation forms U+FB1D to U+FB4E as their bare letters. The maqaf (U+05BE), paseq (U+05C0), sof pasuq (U+05C3), nun hafukha (U+05C6) and the letters stay. For comparison only: without its points a pointed text is not the unpointed spelling (which adds vowel letters), and in Yiddish the points are part of the spelling.

Rule: map: U+0591 removed, U+0592 removed, U+0593 removed, U+0594 removed, U+0595 removed, U+0596 removed, U+0597 removed, U+0598 removed, U+0599 removed, U+059A removed, U+059B removed, U+059C removed …

items.title: html-tags
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Every HTML tag (anything between < and >) removed, as a space.

Rule: 1 pattern: <[^>]+>

Strategies with it: ascii-alnum.

items.title: invisible
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

Invisible format characters removed: soft hyphen, zero-width space, non-joiner and joiner, word joiner, byte order mark.

Rule: map: U+00AD removed, U+200B removed, U+200C removed, U+200D removed, U+2060 removed, U+FEFF removed

Strategies with it: alnum, reading, typographic.

items.title: japanese-iteration-marks
items.text:
Normalization · for comparison · scripts Hira, Kana, Hani · languages ja (language-specific)

Japanese iteration marks written out: the kana marks (ゝ U+309D, ヽ U+30FD) as the kana before them, the voiced kana marks (ゞ U+309E, ヾ U+30FE) as its voiced form (かゞ as かが), the ideographic iteration mark (々 U+3005) as the ideograph before it (人々 as 人人). A mark after a character it cannot repeat stays, as do the marks for two kana and more (〳〵, 〴〵). For comparing texts that write a repetition one way with texts that write it the other; not for output, since both are standard spelling.

Rule: 45 patterns: かゞ, きゞ, くゞ, けゞ …

items.title: latex-text
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Each LaTeX formula ($…$, $$…$$, (…), […]) as the characters it prints, its delimiters and TeX's whitespace gone: a formula compares equal to the same text typed (\frac{1}{2} and ½, \alpha and α, x^{2} and x², once compatibility forms are folded). For comparison: the structure is lost.

Rule: latex: text

Strategies with it: alnum, reading, typographic.

items.title: leaders
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Leaders and blanks as a space, for comparison: a run of three or more dots, ellipses or middle dots (. … ·), of dashes (- and U+2010 to U+2015, the minus sign), of underscores, of = or of asterisks (* ∗), optionally spaced (. . .), as one space, so that a table of contents' dot leaders or a form's blank compare equal however long they are. Dots and dashes form one mixed run; a dash before a digit after a space is a sign, not a leader (....... -4.8% keeps its -4.8%). Three dots are a leader too (an ellipsis compares as a space). Runs of fewer than three and single characters stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 1 pattern: (?:(?:[.…·]|(?<=\S)[-\u2010-\u2015\u2212]|[-\u2010-\u2015\u2212](?!\d))\s*){3,}|(?:_\s*){3,}|(?:=\s*){3,}|(?:[*∗]\s*){3,}

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: letters-digits
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Only letters and digits (Unicode categories L, N) and U+FFFD; every run of anything else one space: a decomposed accent separates its word.

Rule: keep: L, N and U+FFFD

Strategies with it: alnum-nonmark.

items.title: letters-marks-digits
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Only letters, combining marks and digits of any script (Unicode categories L, M, N) and U+FFFD (an illegible character); every run of anything else one space.

Rule: keep: L, M, N and U+FFFD

Strategies with it: alnum.

items.title: ligatures
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Latn

The typographic ligatures ﬀ ﬁ ﬂ ﬃ ﬄ ﬅ ﬆ as their letters.

Rule: map: ﬀ → ff, ﬁ → fi, ﬂ → fl, ﬃ → ffi, ﬄ → ffl, ﬅ → st, ﬆ → st

Strategies with it: latin-historic.

items.title: line-end-hyphens
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Dehyphenation, for comparison only: a hyphen (- ‐ ‑) ending a line after a letter, followed on the next line by a lowercase letter (Unicode Ll), is removed with the line break, joining the word (develop- ers as developers). A hyphen before an uppercase letter, a digit or anything else stays, as do dashes, a hyphen inside a line and one at a paragraph's end. A guess: a compound divided at its own hyphen (self- evident) is joined wrongly, so no default lane names it; a lane opts in by name. Needs the regex engine (\p{Ll}). Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0), restricted to line ends.

Rule: 1 pattern: (?<=\p{L}\p{M}*)[-‐‑][ ]*(?: |[  ])[ ]*(?=\p{Ll})

items.title: long-s
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Latn

The long s (ſ) as s.

Rule: map: ſ → s

Strategies with it: latin-historic.

items.title: lowercase
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Lowercase (Python's str.lower).

Rule: case: lower

Strategies with it: ascii-alnum.

items.title: markup
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Markup removed, each match as a space: special tokens, box arrays, HTML tags of a fixed list, Markdown headings, bullets and rules, LaTeX macros, and the marks of emphasis, tables and formulas.

Rule: 8 patterns: <\|/?[A-Za-z0-9_]+\|>, \[\[\s*\d[\d,\s]*\]\], </?(?:a|b|big|blockquote|br|caption|center|code|col|colgroup|div|em|figcaption|figure|font|h[1-6]|hr|i|img|li|mark|ol|p|pre|s|small|span|strike|strong|sub|sup|table|tbody|td|tfoot|th|thead|tr|tt|u|ul)(?:\s[^>\n]{0,80})?\s*/?>, ^[ \t]*#{1,6}[ \t]+ …

Strategies with it: alnum, reading, typographic.

items.title: nfc
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

Unicode's canonical composition (NFC): the same characters, composed where Unicode composes them.

Rule: unicode: NFC

Strategies with it: alnum-nonmark, diplomatic, latin-historic.

items.title: nfkc
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

Unicode's compatibility composition (NFKC): ligatures split, the long s as s, superscripts and full-width forms as their plain characters.

Rule: unicode: NFKC

Includes the effect of nfc, long-s, ligatures.

Strategies with it: alnum, reading, typographic.

items.title: persian-arabic-letters
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Arab · languages fa, ur (language-specific)

Arabic yeh (U+064A) as Farsi yeh (U+06CC) and Arabic kaf (U+0643) as keheh (U+06A9): the letters Persian and Urdu text uses, where Arabic keyboards and fonts put the Arabic ones. Alef maksura (U+0649) and every other letter stay; text already written with U+06CC and U+06A9 is unchanged.

Rule: map: ك → ک, ي → ی

items.title: quotes
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

Single quotes, apostrophes, the backtick and the acute accent as ', curly double quotes as ".

Rule: map: ’ → ', ‘ → ', ʼ → ', `` →',´→',“→",”→"`

Strategies with it: reading, typographic.

items.title: r-rotunda
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Latn

The r rotunda (ꝛ, Ꝛ) as r, R.

Rule: map: ꝛ → r, Ꝛ → R

Strategies with it: latin-historic.

items.title: romanian-comma-below
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Latn · languages ro (language-specific)

Romanian s and t with a cedilla (ş ţ Ş Ţ, composed or as a letter and U+0327) as the letters with a comma below that Romanian writes (ș ț Ș Ț, U+0219, U+021B, U+0218, U+021A), as keyboards and fonts long gave the cedilla forms. Only for Romanian: the cedilla forms are the letters of Turkish, Azerbaijani, Gagauz and others. Other letters stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: map: ş → ș, ţ → ț, Ş → Ș, Ţ → Ț, U+0073 U+0327 → ș, U+0074 U+0327 → ț, U+0053 U+0327 → Ș, U+0054 U+0327 → Ț

items.title: superscript-digits
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Superscript digits (⁰ to ⁹) right after a digit set apart by a space, for comparison: 1,240¹ as "1,240 ¹", so that a footnote marker never joins the number it follows once nfkc folds it (1,240 1, not 1,2401), as a set apart by markup reads. Superscripts after anything else (m², x³) stay. Runs before nfkc. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 1 pattern: (?<=\d)([⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹]+)

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: superscript-e
items.text:
Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts Latn · languages de (language-specific)

A combining superscript e (U+0364) over a, o, u (A, O, U) as ä, ö, ü (Ä, Ö, Ü): German print's umlaut; over any other letter it stays.

Rule: map: U+0061 U+0364 → ä, U+006F U+0364 → ö, U+0075 U+0364 → ü, U+0041 U+0364 → Ä, U+004F U+0364 → Ö, U+0055 U+0364 → Ü

Strategies with it: latin-historic.

items.title: typography
items.text:
*Normalization · for comparison · scripts **

Typographic forms beyond quotes and dashes unified, for comparison: double primes (″ ‴ ‶ ‷ ⁗, and two to four primes ′′ as NFKC writes ″) and TeX's quotes (‘‘ ’’ '') as "; the low and reversed quotes „ ‟ and the guillemets « » as "; the low, reversed and single angle quotes ‚ ‛ ‹ ›, the prime and reversed prime ′ ‵, the saltillo ꞌ Ꞌ and the IPA stress mark ˈ as '; the minus sign U+2212, the two- and three-em dashes and the small and full-width hyphen-minus and em dash as -; the fraction slash ⁄ as / (½ after NFKC reads 1/2); the ellipsis … as ...; the no-break, en to hair, narrow, medium mathematical and ideographic spaces as a space; the asterisk operator ∗ as *; a middle dot (· ∙) between two digits as a decimal point; ≦ as ≤, ♢ as ◊; each family of arrows (double, white, heavy, long, harpoons) as its plain arrow → ← ↑ ↓. Whatquotesanddashes` fold (curly quotes, U+2010 to U+2015) is theirs, so a strategy names them too; a middle dot elsewhere, letters, digits and case stay. Runs after nfkc in a lane (it folds what NFKC leaves, ⁄ and ′′) and works without it. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0).

Rule: 15 patterns: [″‴‶‷⁗]|[′‵]{2,4}|‘‘|’’|``|'', [‚‛′‵ꞌꞋˈ‹›], [„‟«»], [\u2212\u2E3A\u2E3B\uFE58\uFE63\uFF0D] …

Strategies with it: typographic.

items.title: unicode-marks
items.text:
*Normalization · for output · scripts **

Division marks no source marked, resolved by squiddleocr's language-free rule: a hyphen after a letter at a row's end removed unless a capital, a digit or another script follows, or the document attests the hyphenated form and not the joined one. A guess, and wrong for most compounds divided at their own hyphen: opt-in, never a default.

Rule: division_marks: unicode-marks

items.title: whitespace
items.text:
*Normalization · for output and comparison · scripts **

Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

Rule: whitespace: collapse

Strategies with it: alnum, alnum-nonmark, ascii-alnum, diplomatic, reading, typographic.

items.title: bind.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · bind.py · template linecaster.templates.bind

The item stage (binding): an item's pages (book, issue, manuscript) bound into one item record, recomposed as one (paragraphs continued across page breaks) and composed into the item's document, written by transcription strategies. It reads the page records of a transcribe run; written in item shards (--item-shards N), each task reads whole shard folders, so it sees every page of its items. No engine or GPU is needed: the steps are rule-based, each a preset.

uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document
... --text literal:txt --text latin-historic+flow+unicode-marks:md    # texts by named strategies
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT1 ... --tasks 4000 --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 ... --tasks 64
... --set composition.sections=true          # an option over the preset's
... --jsonl                                  # the texts as JSON Lines too
... --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --flavor cpu-upgrade --tasks 64

Each text (--text STRATEGY:FORMAT; by default the literal document as JSON) is one file per item, OUT2/documents//.; with --jsonl also OUT2/texts/./.jsonl.gz. Nothing is normalized unless a text names a strategy. linecaster.execution.run has the options every pipeline shares (IMAGES is the page records folder here).

items.title: Slots
items.text:
Each slot takes a preset of that step; a recipe fills them all.

Slot Option paragraphs --paragraphs document --document

items.title: Options
items.text:
Besides the options every pipeline shares (linecaster.execution.run).

Option Values Default Description --paragraphs recomposition preset: the item's pages as running text, paragraphs continued across page breaks (e.g. unicode-paragraphs) --document composition preset: the item's document (e.g. linked-document) --set [] an engine option over the preset's, e.g. composition.sections=true; repeatable --text [] an item text, one file per item (OUT/documents//.): a transcription strategy (literal, a catalog strategy, or normalizations joined by +) and a format (md, txt, html, json); repeatable; default literal:json, the document as it is --jsonl flag also the texts as JSON Lines, a row per item and text: OUT/texts/./ --furniture flag item documents: keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html --dividers flag item documents: --- between the items of consecutive layout regions in md --policy 'page-layers' the rendering policy (a catalog policy) the documents, files and texts are rendered under: which content roles are body, furniture, notes or nowhere

items.title: convert.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · convert.py · template linecaster.templates.convert

Image conversion: page images (any format Pillow reads) converted to JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP at full resolution by an image preset (--preset, ImageConverter), decoded and encoded on the machine's NVIDIA GPUs where it has them and they support the format (linecaster[nvimgcodec]), else on the CPU. Images in OUT/images//., page records (each image's size, hashes, decoder and encoder) in OUT/pages, failed pages in OUT/rejects. 

uv run pipelines/convert.py IMAGES OUT --preset webp-lossy-q80 --item-from-parent
uv run pipelines/convert.py IMAGES OUT --preset jpeg-q90 --set image.quality=85
uv run pipelines/convert.py OUT --pages OUT1/pages --preset jp2-lossless           # an earlier run's pages
uv run pipelines/convert.py OUT --parquet pages.parquet --image-key path --item-key item --id-key page \
    --preset webp-lossy-q80                                  # a table of source paths and the ids they get
... --set image.accel=cpu                                    # never the GPU; =gpu: an error where it cannot

The presets (linecaster presets, step image): webp-lossy-q80, jpeg-q90, jp2-lossless, png, working-image (lossless WebP); --set image.OPTION=VALUE over a preset's options (format, quality, lossless, psnr, method, compress_level, accel). A page goes through two stages, decoding and encoding, each with a window saturate's controller adapts to the throughput and the machine's memory (--window fixes it); a GPU batches the decodes that arrive together. One worker process per GPU, or without a GPU (or with image.accel=cpu) one per CPU, since Pillow's JPEG 2000 decoder holds Python's GIL (threads do not decode in parallel), unless --workers says otherwise, and one task per worker unless --tasks does: long tasks let the windows grow, and a rerun of a task skips its files written already; with --on ray each task reserves its worker's share of the CPUs (--cpus-per-task) and, where GPUs decode, one GPU; the image files are read in the stages, many at once, not by the reader. A run into the same OUT resumes: finished tasks are skipped, and within a task an image whose file is there already is not converted again (--overwrite converts it again). Files are written under a temporary name and renamed when complete.

An image the GPU does not decode (nvJPEG2000 rejects some JPEG 2000 code streams, e.g. with the vertically causal context) is decoded on the CPU and counted (gpu_decode_refused; gpu_fallback in its record); nvImageCodec itself prints nothing about it (PYNVIMGCODEC_VERBOSITY=0 unless the environment sets it). A GPU that fails is logged once per kind of failure and counted (gpu_decode_errors). Ctrl-C stops the run: the summary says what runs again on the next launch, and the process ends by the signal. Under uv run a shell loop still goes on (uv turns the signal into exit code 130, astral-sh/uv#11886): trap 'exit 130' INT before the loop stops it.

items.title: Slots
items.text:
Each slot takes a preset of that step; a recipe fills them all.

Slot Option image --preset

items.title: Options
items.text:
Besides the options every pipeline shares (linecaster.execution.run).

Option Values Default Description --preset the image preset: what to convert to (e.g. webp-lossy-q80; needed) --set [] an engine option over the preset's, e.g. image.quality=85; repeatable --overwrite flag convert images whose file is there already again --window int pages in flight per stage, fixed (default: adapted) --max-window int decoding and encoding: the adapted windows' upper bound per worker (default: twice the CPUs, shared by the workers) --max-io-window int 256 fetching and writing: the adapted windows' upper bound per worker (they wait on storage)

items.title: harvest.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · harvest.py · template linecaster.templates.harvest

The harvest stage: items' page images (and, with --existing-ocr, the library's own OCR) from their manifests (IIIF or METS; a folder, a list of links, or item tables with --manifest-key), or from http(s) image URLs in a page table (--parquet), downloaded once into item folders, with page records that keep where everything came from. No engine or GPU is needed; the transcribe stage then reads the page records without waiting on the libraries' servers. With --items it fetches items' other remote files (resources: catalogue records, API JSON, manifests) as served, from URL templates (--resource KIND=URL with {item}) or a resource table, into OUT///. with a record each in OUT/resources/.jsonl.gz; --http-policy gives settings for every host and overrides per host (rate limits, proxies or direct, retries, statuses that stop the run). --reuse-from DIR (repeatable) takes the files earlier harvests into other folders already hold: a resource whose source URL one of them fetched (by DIR's records, the newest successful one per URL across the folders, its copy checked by sha256) is read from there and written into OUT under its current item and name, with the earlier fetch's provenance and reused_from; only the rest is fetched. So a changed list gets one complete folder of its own instead of a resume whose tasks no longer fit it; a resume of that folder with other --reuse-from folders is an ordinary resume. Page-image harvests (--parquet, --manifests) take --reuse-from too: each launch first indexes the earlier folders' page records once (OUT/logs/reuse-from.parquet: source URL, copy, sha256; the newest folder wins), each task looks up only its own URLs there, and a page read from an earlier copy says image.extra.reused_from; not with --existing-ocr. 

uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key manifest_url --item-key item_id OUT \
    --rate-limit 5/1 --existing-ocr
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --items pages.parquet --item-key lccn OUT --http-policy http-policy.yaml \
    --resource marcxml=https://catalog.example.org/{item}/marcxml
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --items files-v2.parquet --item-key item OUT2 --reuse-from OUT --reuse-from TOPUP
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --parquet pages.parquet --item-key book --sequence-key page --image-key url OUT \
    --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1
uv run pipelines/harvest.py ... SMOKE --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1 --max-pages 2000     # a smoke test
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --recipe ...                 # keeps the metadata
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py OUT/images OUT2 --item-from-parent --recipe ...   # or the plain folder

OUT/images//. as the server sent them; with --existing-ocr OUT/ocr//.xml|.html; the manifests as fetched in OUT/manifests/.json|.xml; page records in OUT/pages/.jsonl.gz (image.uri the copy, image.extra.source_uri the source, metadata.manifest the item's and page's manifest data, the transcription ocr_original with the existing OCR).

Nothing needs sizing: --rate-limit holds per worker, and with it one worker runs the tasks (the run states what a server sees before it starts). Each item is a task (a --parquet page table with --item-key: a run of rows with the same item, whatever the files; --manifests: a manifest or a row of an item table; without --item-key tasks of about 1,000 pages), so an item is whole in its task and a rerun into the same OUT repeats at most the item each worker was in (datatrove's resume is per task); with --reuse, its pages whose images are already in OUT/images are read from there instead of fetched again (one listing of the item's folder; their records are complete and say image.extra.reused); without it (the default) they are fetched again and their files overwritten. The worker's requests ahead (manifests' pages and http(s) images alike) grow until the rate limits are kept busy, and the limits hold across its tasks. --tasks and --workers still override; with --workers N a server sees N times --rate-limit, so give each worker its part. With --proxies the limits hold per proxy instead, and the workers (of this run, and of other runs given the same --broker) share the proxies through the broker (default OUT/logs/broker), each proxy used by one worker at a time and left out where it was blocked; each worker holds a fair share of them (an HTTP policy's proxies: {per_worker: 1} for one each, or N). The run's workers follow the available proxies (those not blocked and not held by another run): one per proxy up to one per CPU, with 1 or N one per proxy divided by N (not capped by the CPUs: the workers wait on the network), at most one per task and at most 64 with OUT on object storage (s3://, gs://, hf://, ...), which it states before it starts. --max-pages N runs the first N pages of the input in the same automatic tasks, a smoke test of the real setup (--limit counts per task, as in datatrove). An outage of the server pauses the requests until it answers again; a book that fails anyway runs again on the next launch, and --retry-failed also runs the finished books with failed pages again: with --reuse only their failed pages are fetched (the others are read from OUT/images), without it every page of those books is fetched again. linecaster.execution.run has the options every pipeline shares.

items.title: Options
items.text:
Besides the options every pipeline shares (linecaster.execution.run).

Option Values Default Description --reuse flag before fetching an item, list its folder in OUT and read the files an earlier launch wrote instead of fetching them again (one listing per item; off by default, since on some object storage a listing is slow even for an empty folder) --reuse-from [] an earlier harvest's folder (any fsspec path; repeatable): a file whose source URL it fetched is read from its copy there (by its records: DIR/resources for --items, the newest successful one per URL; DIR/pages for page images, indexed once per launch; checked by sha256) and written into OUT, instead of fetched; not with --existing-ocr

items.title: import_transcriptions.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · import_transcriptions.py · template linecaster.templates.import_transcriptions

Importing transcriptions (import_transcriptions.v1): a source's documents read into page records by an importer, a ground truth by default, for scoring (linecaster score) or as a dataset's records.

The documents come from a Parquet table (--parquet: a row per page, its id in --id-key, its item in --item-key) or a folder of files: in a column of the table (--data-key, the document's content, as a wiki page's wikitext), in a file a column names (--uri-key), or delivered with the page (a manifest's OCR file). The importer is a preset of step import (auto-import, alto-import, ...) or an importer's engine id (import.mediawiki.v1 from linecaster-mediawiki); --set import.OPTION=VALUE sets its options (ground_truth, conventions, an engine's own such as site). --context-key columns go to the importer as the document's context (language, script and direction state the page's writing system); record, revision and dataset columns go to the transcription's source. The page images are named, not read (--image-key, or none), unless --read-images reads them for their size (a transcription is fitted to it; a line image's line is the whole image). Page records in OUT/pages, failed pages in OUT/rejects.

uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py OUT --parquet pages.parquet --id-key page --item-key item \
    --data-key wikitext --context-key title --context-key revision \
    --importer import.mediawiki.v1 --set import.site=SITE --set import.conventions=example
uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py OUT --parquet ocr.parquet --data-key alto --importer alto-import
uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py OUT --parquet lines.parquet --data-key text --context-key language \
    --importer text-import --set import.line_image=true --read-images

items.title: score.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · score.py · template linecaster.templates.score

Scoring: a run's page records against a ground truth's, by a benchmark, over many tasks (score.v1). Each task scores a share of the run's pages (PageScorer: their ground truth read in one pass, each page rendered and normalized as the benchmark says) and writes their score records (ScoreWriter: OUT/records, OUT/pages); when every task is done the driver puts them together (linecaster.evaluation.run.aggregate: the pages the run lacks scored as empty outputs, the corpus rates with their bootstrap intervals, the conventions check) into OUT/scores.parquet and OUT/evidence.yaml, as linecaster score writes them in one process.

uv run pipelines/score.py RUN/scores --pages RUN/pages --ground-truth TRUTH --benchmark benchmark.yaml
uv run pipelines/score.py s3://bucket/run/scores --pages s3://bucket/run/pages --ground-truth s3://bucket/truth \
    --benchmark benchmark.yaml --preset lightonocr-3-0.8b --on ray --tasks 32
... --workers 64                                   # tasks at once on this machine

The run's page records are read without their images. Any number of tasks: with more tasks than page-record files, the tasks share each file (every k-th record each), so --tasks 100 uses 100 cores whatever the run wrote. The benchmark's file is read here and travels with the tasks; the ground truth folder must be readable where the tasks run (object storage on a cluster). --preset names the preset measured when the run follows no recipe (as linecaster score), --context the rest of the pipeline it was measured in.

items.title: transcribe_modular.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_modular.py · template linecaster.templates.transcribe_modular

The modular pipeline: smaller models, picked step by step from the catalog's presets (linecaster presets): a layout (a layout model, or single-region for the page as one region), text lines and a line recognizer, optionally table and formula models after; then the rule-based steps, each a preset too: typography (--hierarchy), recomposition (--paragraphs; without one the page stays as laid out) and page composition (--document). Page records in OUT/pages; with --files per-page files in the --formats asked for (<item>/<page><suffix>.<ext>, or with --naming flat <page><suffix>.<ext> in one folder; --suffix SUFFIX, e.g. .paddle), written literally or by a --strategy; with --item-texts one file per item and --text (an item stage: the item recomposed and composed as one, written by each text's transcription strategy). Nothing is normalized unless a strategy is named. The script's environment has PaddleX and Tesseract; kraken's presets (the squiddle recipe's recognition) run in the recipe's own script, recipes/squiddle.py (uv run launch.py squiddle IMAGES OUT), or here with --backend served --endpoint against a server started from it.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout single-region --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium
uv run recipes/squiddle.py IMAGES OUT                     # the recipe squiddle, in its own environment
... --hierarchy ratios --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document
... --item-texts OUT/texts --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document \
    --text literal:txt --text latin-historic+flow+unicode-marks:md     # texts by named strategies
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition tesseract-best-latin --tables slanet-plus --formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l
... --set recognition.batch_size=4          # an option over the preset's
... --set composition.sections=true         # also for the rule-based steps
... --backend served                        # a server in the task
... --files OUT/files --formats md,txt,json --naming flat --suffix .paddle --furniture   # <page>.paddle.md, ...
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve --layout pp-doclayoutv3 ...    # linecaster serve with the presets named
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8        # then --on ray --tasks 64
... --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --tasks 64

items.title: transcribe_page.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_page.py · template linecaster.templates.transcribe_page

A page engine reads the whole page (PageRecognizer on its engine): a vendor's package in the pipeline's process (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). Each task starts the service the preset names (VendorServer, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint, or the vendor image's entrypoint) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one. Page records in OUT/pages; the engine's raw output is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition indra-ocr --tasks 8 --workers 8   # CPU, in-process
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition surya-ocr-2.5        # needs `vllm` (0.25.1) on PATH
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition falcon-ocr           # inside the vendor's image
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition oxr-1.0 --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000

--recognition takes a page engine's preset (linecaster presets; id); chat presets run in pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py. A vendor's service runs inside the vendor's image (the preset's serve.image): the pipeline runs there too, in its own uv environment, and the service in the image's own environments (VendorServer leaves the pipeline's out of its environment). Its entrypoint listens on the image's ports, so one task per machine starts it; more tasks share one service with --recognition-endpoint. On HF Jobs the Job's image is the preset's serve.image unless --image is given; it needs uv (the vLLM and OXR images have it, the Falcon-OCR image does not).

items.title: transcribe_vlm.v1
items.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_vlm.py · template linecaster.templates.transcribe_vlm

A vision-language model reads the page: the whole page (PageRecognizer) or, with a --layout preset, each region it finds (RegionRecognizer, a region preset), on the Chat backend. Each task starts vLLM or SGLang for the model itself (VLMServer, last in the pipeline) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running server; with --layout it also serves the layout model (--backend, --endpoint as for any engine). Page records in OUT/pages; the model's raw answer is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr                     # vLLM here, else built by uv
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha> --recognition unlimited-ocr-2
... --set "recognition.repair_max_tokens=[8192, 12288]"   # repair passes (below); =0: off (on in lightonocr-3-0.8b)
... --set recognition.max_tokens=6000 --set recognition.temperature=0   # the sampling over the preset's
... --no-repetition-detection                             # loops run to max_tokens again (below)
... --set recognition.repetition_detection.min_count=12   # one of its settings over the defaults
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py OUT2 --pages OUT/pages --repair-only --recognition lightonocr-3-0.8b
                                                      # the repair pass over page records written before

The server is the preset's release (vLLM: linecaster's VLLM_VERSION unless the preset names another; SGLang: its serve.version, with the preset's server_packages): the one on PATH or in the image when it is that release (--server-env auto, the default: vLLM's image at linecaster's pin serves every preset on it), else in an environment uv builds once per machine (--server-env uv always; path takes the one there, whatever it is).

--recognition takes a chat preset of the catalog (linecaster presets; id) or a Hugging Face id (that model's page preset, with --layout its region preset where it has one). On HF Jobs the server runs in the Job's image: the one the preset was validated with (its serve.image) unless --image is given. It has uv, Python 3.12 and vllm on PATH, so the pipeline runs in the uv environment the executor builds (linecaster alone for page presets; with --layout also linecaster-paddlex for the layout model), and VLMServer starts the image's own server. SGLang presets and region reading start it outside that environment (outside_venv), so neither the image's Python nor its CUDA libraries see the pipeline's packages. vLLM takes --gpu-memory-utilization of the GPU (0.8, linecaster's default; SGLang: the preset's own share); with --layout the layout server loads into the rest after vLLM's memory profiling. The server listens on port 8000 in every run: two runs on one machine need a GPU each (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) and cannot both start their own server; on a machine without a CUDA toolkit vLLM starts with VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 (VLMServer).

--set STEP.OPTION=VALUE sets an option over the preset's: for --recognition the chat engine's max_tokens, temperature, top_p, repair_max_tokens, repair_temperature and repetition_detection (linecaster.engines.chat.ChatAdapter), for --layout the layout engine's options. They go into the run record and change its pipeline_sha256.

vLLM's repetition detection is on by default for presets served by vLLM 0.17.0 or later (patterns of 8 to 100 tokens repeated 16 times): a completion that loops ends early with finish_reason repetition (stat finish_repetition) and is not repaired, instead of running to max_tokens and through the repair passes. --no-repetition-detection (--set recognition.repetition_detection=false) turns it off. Presets on another server (SGLang, an older vLLM) run without it, and asking for it there is refused: those servers would ignore it.

The repair pass (--set recognition.repair_max_tokens=N, N larger than the preset's max_tokens; page presets only): a page whose completion stopped at max_tokens is sent again right away, the same image, prompt and top_p, with max_tokens N (at most the served context minus the page's prompt) and temperature repair_temperature (0.1); with a list of rising caps ([8192, 12288]), each repair that stops at its cap is sent again with the next. The page keeps the first completion that finished (stop), its first one otherwise, and its transcription records every pass as a raw output (outputs: its pass, and kept for the one kept). The procedure is the reference script's (uv-scripts/ocr lighton-ocr3-saturate.py at e2b0aa5), which suggests 8192 for LightOnOCR-3; lightonocr-3-0.8b repairs at 8192 and then 12288 (twice and three times its 4096), since dense tables needed up to about 9,000 tokens. A page that stops at max_tokens is often a repetition loop, which a repair does not end, but a dense table can simply need more tokens and then finishes; the repair adds the second requests' tokens to the run (NOTES.md has the trials). A page whose prompt leaves no more room in the context than the first request had gets no repair (stat repair_skipped); a run warns at the start when N plus a page's largest prompt exceeds the context. With --repair-only (and --pages, page records of an earlier run of the same model) only the repair requests are sent: for the pages that stopped at max_tokens and have no repair yet; every other page is written as it was read.

items.text:
Rendering policy

page-layers, with what an annotator wrote about a figure (a description, alt text) in the body, after its region: for scoring outputs that describe pictures against a ground truth that does, and for documents that read them. What is suppressed, duplicate or removed goes nowhere, its descriptions too.

items.text: Role Production Status Layer any any suppressed none any any duplicate none any any removed none any any any body

items.title: page-layers
items.text:
Rendering policy

Every content role in its default layer: body, furniture for running heads, running feet, page numbers, catchwords and signature marks, nowhere for separators and noise. What is suppressed, duplicate or removed goes nowhere; what an annotator wrote about a figure goes to the metadata. The as-written texts apply NFC and drop capitals joined to their lines, the readable ones also the normalization.

items.text: Role Production Status Layer any any suppressed none any any duplicate none any any removed none

items.title: linked-document
items.text:
Preset · document · core

linecaster's document (linecaster.document) of a page or an item, in reading order, its paragraphs linked across page breaks. Each region is a block by its content role: titles and headings at their levels, paragraphs, list items, captions, notes, and page headers and footers in the furniture layer. Text regions come from their paragraphs when a recomposition made them, else as laid out, one row per line. A paragraph or region that continues another (its continues link) is one block with it, on a new row: the text stays as read (a strategy's flow joins the rows, unicode-marks or a source's divided words resolve a mark at the join). Tables follow the rendering policy's table rules, formulas keep their LaTeX, and pictures their image and the text read inside them.

  • sections false: no sections. With it, every title or heading opens a section that holds every block up to the next one (in the JSON, Block.section; HTML, Markdown and text read the same).

items.title: ratios
items.text:
Preset · hierarchy · core

The hierarchy of a page from its own type sizes, every rule a ratio to the body size (the median row height of the page's text regions); the squiddle combination's typography.

  • levels: a heading whose rows are at least 2.5 times the body size is level 1, 1.7 times level 2, else level 3.
  • demote 1.2: a section header set in about the body size is text: typography classifies it as a paragraph again (layout models often call a bold run-in heading a section header).
  • split 1.6, max_headline_rows 3: up to three leading rows of a text region this much taller than the rows after them and the body size are a headline the layout model merged into the text; they become a section header of their own.
  • page_number_min_conf 0.75: a page-number region read with a lower mean character confidence (or empty) is an ornament or a blob, and is removed: typography classifies it status removed (with its confidence), and the rendering policy leaves it out.
  • Drop capitals (a layout model's drop-capital class) are linked to the first line of the text region they belong to (a part_of link); the document writes the letter at that line's start, and the line's own text stays as read.
Step hierarchy (reads pages) Engine hierarchy.ratios.v1 Produces hierarchy

items.text: Option Value page_number_min_conf 0.75 demote 1.2 split 1.6 levels [[2.5, 1], [1.7, 2], [0.0, 3]] max_headline_rows 3 heading_labels ['section_header', 'title']

items.text:

Lossless JPEG 2000 (the reversible 5/3 wavelet, colour transform on, JP2 container) at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB, with the working image's colour handling and size limits; image warnings are recorded. The pixels decode exactly to the converted image's.

Decoded and encoded on an NVIDIA GPU where the machine has one and nvImageCodec is installed (linecaster[nvimgcodec], nvJPEG2000); else with Pillow (OpenJPEG). Each image records its decoder and encoder.

  • lossless: the reversible wavelet; --set image.lossless=false --set image.psnr=40 gives lossy JPEG 2000 at a target PSNR.
  • accel auto: the GPU where it can.

A GPU and a CPU encoder write different bytes at the same quality: each image records its encoder, and --set image.accel=cpu keeps both steps on the CPU.

items.title: webp-lossy-q80
items.text:
Preset · image · core

Lossy WebP at quality 80 (libwebp, method 4) at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB: working copies of page images for publishing and downloads, at a fraction of the working image's size. The colour handling is the working image's (the ICC profile to sRGB, 16 to 8 bit, alpha onto white) and so are the size limits; image warnings are recorded.

Decoding runs on an NVIDIA GPU where the machine has one and nvImageCodec is installed (linecaster[nvimgcodec]): JPEG (nvJPEG), JPEG 2000 (nvJPEG2000) and TIFF (nvTIFF) in 8-bit gray or RGB; everything else with Pillow. WebP is always encoded on the CPU (libwebp): no GPU library writes it. Each image records its decoder and encoder.

  • quality 80: libwebp's quality (Pillow's default).
  • method 4: libwebp's effort, 0 fast to 6 small (libwebp's and Pillow's default). In a whole conversion methods 0 to 2 are faster but give files about 20 % larger; 5 and 6 save a few percent more at up to 1.6 times the time (CHANGELOG.md names the evidence).
  • accel auto: the GPU where it can; --set image.accel=cpu decodes with Pillow everywhere.

Editions: 1 used libwebp's default effort (method 4); 2 the fastest (method 0); 3 method 4 again, after a whole-run comparison of all methods.

Step image (reads pages) Engine image.convert.v1 Produces image

items.title: working-image
items.text:
Preset · image · core

The working image: any page image Pillow decodes, as 8-bit sRGB (its ICC profile applied, alpha flattened onto white) in lossless WebP at full resolution, method 0, exact, so the pixels the models see are the delivered ones. Pages over WebP's size limit (16,383 pixels a side) or Pillow's decompression-bomb threshold are refused from the header, before decoding, and go to rejects/.

  • effort 80: libwebp's lossless compression effort (Pillow's quality); it changes the file size and the time, never the pixels.

items.title: pp-doclayout-plus-l
items.text:
Preset · layout · experimental

PP-StructureV3's layout model. It gives boxes only, no polygons and no order; the engine orders the regions with XY-Cut++ (reading_order: xy-cut++, linecaster.data.geometry.xy_cut_plus_plus): titles, figures, tables, captions, footnotes and text running across columns are masked, the remaining text is cut at whitespace gaps (vertical cuts first unless the cross-column text dominates), and the masked regions are matched back by label priority and distance; page headers lead and page footers close the page. Post-processing as PP-StructureV3 configures it, written out: per-class score thresholds (0.3 for paragraph titles and formulas, 0.4 for text, 0.45 for seals, 0.5 elsewhere), layout NMS, large box merging.

Labels: PaddleX's labels are mapped to DoclingDocument labels as linecaster_paddlex.layout.LABEL_MAP does; number (a page number) is not in labels: because the engine places it by position: page_header when its center lies in the top header_zone (15 %) of the page, else page_footer. seal stays seal, which is not a DoclingDocument label (the serializers write it as a picture). Regions contained in another by more than max_containment (80 %) of their area are dropped.

Edition 2 (2026-11-07): reading_order: xy-cut++. Edition 1 ordered the regions with plain XY-cut (the engine's default, xy-cut), horizontal cuts first; it stays resolvable from the lock.

items.title: unicode-paragraphs
items.text:
Preset · paragraphs · core

The rows of each text region grouped into paragraphs, from geometry and Unicode's character properties, never from a language name; the squiddle combination's recomposition. It decides structure only (where a paragraph breaks and where it runs on) and changes no text: a transcription strategy writes the text (flow joins the rows; unicode-marks resolves division marks by the rule below).

  • Paragraph breaks: a row indented by indent (0.8 em) from the start margin, a gap above it of about a blank line (more than gap_leading 0.6 of the leading and gap_height 0.5 of the taller row), or, in justified text (at least justified_rows 3 rows, justified_share 0.6 of them ending within end_margin 0.6 em of the end margin), a row before it that stopped short_row 1.5 em and short_row_width a quarter of the width short.
  • A row that ends in a division mark (Unicode's hyphens by Line_Break, and convention_marks, the not sign some transcription conventions write) after a letter leaves its paragraph open. Whether the mark goes is no decision of the recomposition: the normalization unicode-marks removes it when a text is written, unless the next row starts with a capital or a digit, a Hebrew letter is not followed by Hebrew, or the document attests the hyphenated form and not the joined one (the document's words as the lexicon).
  • A paragraph without sentence-final punctuation that ends with a division mark or reaches the end margin continues in the next text region whose first row is not indented and starts with a letter, and, recomposing an item, on the next page; a region of digits only between them (a page number) does not close it.
  • Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph.
Step paragraphs (reads items) Engine paragraphs.unicode.v1 Produces paragraphs

items.title: chandra-ocr-2
items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

chandra-ocr-2 as the vendor's own vLLM client runs it, chandra-ocr v0.2.0 (chandra/model/vllm.py: generate_vllm), with the ocr_layout prompt of the CLI. Where linecaster departs from the client, the item says so.

  • The page image, then the ocr_layout prompt (verbatim from chandra/prompts.py at v0.2.0, hash-checked).
  • RGB, the vendor's scale_to_fit (pixel count clamped to 3072 x 2048 and up to 1792 x 28, both sides snapped to multiples of 28, LANCZOS), PNG.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 12384 (the vendor's MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS); the chat template opens an empty <think></think>, so thinking needs no switch.
  • One attempt per page (linecaster's choice): the vendor client retries a page up to six times at a raised temperature when it detects a repetition loop; here a loop shows as a loop.
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 20480 (linecaster's choice, where the vendor's launcher has 18000: 6144 visual tokens at the cap + 12384 + the prompt do not fit in 18000), the vendor's --mm-processor-kwargs pixel bounds and --dtype bfloat16, one image and no video per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching; no --trust-remote-code. linecaster's vLLM (validated on 0.26.0; the vendor's launcher pins 0.17.0).
  • The model answers with HTML layout blocks (<div data-bbox=.. data-label=..>), stored verbatim; converting them to Markdown (the vendor's parse_markdown) is left to whoever reads the output. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice.

items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

DeepSeek-OCR-2 in grounded document mode, following the model card and the uv-scripts recipe deepseek-ocr2-vllm.py (the DeepSeek-OCR and DeepSeek-OCR-2 presets differ only in the checkpoint).

  • The prompt <|grounding|>Convert the document to markdown. as a text part after the image (the card's raw <image>\n<|grounding|>... prompt becomes image + text; the chat template inserts the image token).
  • No resolution mode is passed (no mm_processor_kwargs), so vLLM's default applies: Gundam (base 1024, tiles of 640, crop mode, up to 6 crops), the mode the card recommends for documents.

  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 8192 (the native context), --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt.
  • The completion is stored verbatim, grounding markup included; linecaster.engines.chat.deepseek_ocr.strip_grounding removes it for whoever wants the text alone. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice.

items.title: falcon-ocr
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

Falcon-OCR's whole-page product: the vendor's pipeline service (layout detection, one request per crop with a category prompt, the vendor's Markdown assembly) in the vendor's image, one page per request to POST /falconocr/parse. The engine (falcon.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: VendorServer starts the image's own single-GPU entrypoint (/app/entrypoint_single.sh: vLLM with the model on port 8000, the pipeline on 5002, both on GPU 0 of the container) and waits until both answer /health. The image's entrypoint binds both to every address of the container. The weights are the image's own (/models/Falcon-OCR, the model pin's files); the image digest fixes what runs.
  • The request: the page as RGB, scaled down (LANCZOS) so its longest side is at most 2,048 px, JPEG quality 95, as a data URI (linecaster's choice of payload), with skip_layout false (the vendor's full-page path; the direct VLM path is off-label).
  • Kept verbatim: markdown_result (the raw output, the text) and the layout regions (json_result, the extension field falcon__regions_json). The service reports no finish reason, so no loop can be counted; its output tokens are the step's completion_tokens. The Markdown can contain leaked >>UNUSED_N<< vocabulary tokens; removing them is left to whoever reads the output.
  • The image has Python 3.10 and no uv: on HF Jobs the pipeline cannot run inside it as it is (not tried).

Apache-2.0. Not run on HF Jobs.

items.title: indra-ocr
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

Indra OCR as its package runs it: indra-ocr (1.1.2) on the CPU, in the pipeline's process, each page through the package's own image path (Converter.convert(path), the call the indra-ocr command makes), so decoding to grayscale, orientation, deskew, detection, recognition, layout and reading order are the package's. The engine is indra.recognition.v1 (package linecaster-indra).

  • Settings: indra_ocr.load()'s defaults, written out: mode auto (an image is OCR'd), furniture false (page headers and footers dropped from the Markdown), math false, dpi 200 (PDFs only), one ONNX Runtime thread per task (the package's own workers are single-threaded, one per core: run as many tasks as cores).
  • The models: the pin of datalab-to/indra-ocr at the tag v1.1.0, the model set indra-ocr 1.1.2 is built against (indra_ocr/models.py: HF_REVISION), every pinned file checked.
  • The page goes to the package as its file's bytes, as the reader brought them (the engine's image_input is bytes), as the indra-ocr command reads a file; the package decodes it in grayscale with OpenCV. The pipeline script resolves OpenCV 4.11 (surya-ocr's pin, in the same environment).
  • Kept verbatim: the package's Markdown (the raw output, the text), with its layout blocks, rotation and skew (the extension fields indra__blocks, indra__rotation, indra__skew). A page the package reports as failed is the page's error; an empty Markdown (a blank leaf) is a transcription without text.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page).

items.title: kraken-ppocrv6-medium
items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

kraken's PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer through kraken's own code (RecognitionTaskModel), on every line of the page in the line step's order; the squiddle combination's recognizer.

  • batch_size 8. kraken pads a batch to its widest line, so the batch size can move numerics; one page per request, batching only within the page.
  • precision auto: bf16-mixed on CUDA (the model was trained in bf16-mixed), 32-true on the CPU. Needs the kraken fork with the inference autocast fix (storytracer/kraken 3d235ee8); on upstream kraken 7.1 the setting is inert. T4-class GPUs have no bf16 tensor cores: use 16-mixed or 32-true there (a new preset).
  • text_direction horizontal-lr; right-to-left material wants horizontal-rl.

items.title: lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

LightOnOCR-3-0.8B in its plain mode on whole pages (the model card's transcription call; LightOn's CLI calls it --mode plain): the page as Markdown, furniture unlabelled in the text. linecaster's default for LightOnOCR-3 is grounding mode (lightonocr-3-0.8b); this preset was lightonocr-3-0.8b until linecaster 0.10.4. The two plain presets differ only in the checkpoint.

  • The page image only, no text part (grounding is lightonocr-3-0.8b).
  • RGB, thumbnail((2048, 2048)), PNG: the card's target longest dimension. thumbnail only downscales, so a smaller page is sent as it is (unlike LightOnOCR-2's forced 1540 px).
  • Sampling from the card: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 4096; thinking off per request and server-side (--default-chat-template-kwargs).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 18000 (LightOn's README for the 0.8B, and the reference script uv-scripts/ocr lighton-ocr3-saturate.py at e2b0aa5; a 2048-px page is at most 4096 image tokens), one image and no video per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching; no --trust-remote-code.
  • Repair passes on demand (settings.repair.max_tokens: [8192, 12288], twice and three times the first 4096): a page whose completion stopped at max_tokens is sent again at 8192 tokens, and, if that stops at its cap too, at 12,288; never more (three passes at most). Temperature 0.1 (settings.repair.temperature, the reference script's); the same image, prompt and top_p. The page keeps the first completion that finished (stop), otherwise its first one. The second repair is linecaster's addition to the reference script's one; CHANGELOG.md names the evidence. --set recognition.repair_max_tokens=0 turns the passes off.
  • linecaster's vLLM, 0.30.0 or later: LightOn's repository says 0.27.1 makes these models loop.
  • The completion is stored verbatim; --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice. Experimental.

Editions: 1 served with --max-model-len 16384 (linecaster's choice then); 2 serves with LightOn's 18000, so that a repair pass has room, and states the repair settings (off); 3 turns the repair passes on at 8192 and 12,288 tokens.

items.title: lightonocr-3-0.8b
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

LightOnOCR-3-0.8B in its grounding mode on whole pages, following the model card's "Prompt Modes": every block of the page comes back with a label and a box, so page furniture (running heads, page numbers) is labelled instead of written into the text. linecaster's default for LightOnOCR-3 (this preset was lightonocr-3-0.8b-grounding until linecaster 0.10.4). Otherwise identical to the plain mode, lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain (revision, image size, sampling, repair, serve flags).

  • The page image, then the text part grounding (the card's vLLM call); the image as for transcription: RGB, thumbnail((2048, 2048)), PNG.
  • Sampling from the card's grounding call: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 4096 (the card's, although grounding writes about 25 % more tokens than transcription; a different cap waits for a measurement).
  • The completion: a placeholder ![label](x1,y1,x2,y2) before each block, its box in 0-1000 page coordinates, then its content (Markdown; tables HTML). linecaster makes one region per block (adapter lighton-ocr-3-grounding, linecaster.engines.chat.lighton_grounding), the boxes scaled to the page image read, in the order emitted: each block's content role: header, footer and page_number are header, footer and page_number (a page number's Docling label is page_header in the top 15 % of the page and page_footer below, as PP-DocLayout's page numbers); aside_text is marginalia (body text under the default policy); title is heading at the level of its #. The model's label stays the region's label.
  • The full text (verbatim_txt) keeps the furniture; the body texts (readable_txt, readable_md) leave it out.
  • What the model writes about a figure (image, header_image, footer_image: a description; chart: data read off it) is no printed text: kept as the region's description, in no text of the page.
  • The raw completion is stored verbatim (the transcription's raw output). Experimental.

Editions: 1 is the first.

items.title: minicpm-ocr-1.0
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 as a region reader, run the way OpenBMB's SDK (minicpm-ocr 1.0.1) runs it: the SDK finds PP-DocLayoutV3 regions, crops each one from the full-resolution page and sends the crop with the prompt for its region type. Here the layout comes from linecaster's layout step and RegionRecognizer sends the crops.

  • Prompt and token cap per region type from the SDK's DEFAULT_PROMPT_MAP["element_prompts"], looked up by the layout model's own label (PP-DocLayoutV3's class name, the SDK's vocabulary): Text Recognition: for text-like regions, Table Recognition: (8192 tokens), Formula Recognition: for display formulas, Chart to Table:, Seal Recognition:; unknown types get the SDK default (Text Recognition:, 8192). Caps are clamped to max-model-len - 512 as the SDK does (no effect at 40960).
  • Request: the crop, then the prompt; mm_processor_kwargs {"downsample_mode": "4x", "max_slice_nums": 9}; thinking off; temperature 0.01, top_p 0.001, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.0, no_repeat_ngram_size 100; PNG.
  • Every region is read but the image types (image, header_image, footer_image); charts and seals are read (the SDK's chart and seal recognition are on).
  • Crop: from the full-resolution page (no page scaling, no padding), the box truncated to whole pixels as PaddleX's CropByBoxes does, pixels outside the region's polygon white.
  • Serve flags from OpenBMB's SDK tutorial, served as minicpm-ocr; DSpark speculative decoding with the matching draft model (minicpm-ocr-1.0-dspark, 15 speculative tokens; --no-speculative in the recipe turns it off).
  • vLLM 0.33.0, not linecaster's 0.30.0, which has no --trust-request-mm-kwargs (2026-11-16, the top-15 run on an A40); 0.33.0 is the first release after the nightly the preset was validated on, 5d35ce3 (0.32.1rc1.dev602+g5d35ce393, with transformers at OpenBMB's pin, in the image cr.hf.co/davanstrien/minicpm-ocr:1.0-vllm-5d35ce3), which is not on PyPI. ninja must be on PATH or the engine fails at startup.
  • linecaster.engines.chat.minicpm_ocr.assemble_markdown assembles the page with the SDK's own code (extra linecaster[minicpm-ocr]), keeping footnote and aside_text.

Not reproduced: the SDK's PaddleX box filtering (filter_overlap_boxes) and its merging of aligned text blocks into one composite crop (merge_blocks); linecaster's layout step runs PP-DocLayoutV3's ONNX export with its own containment suppression. Experimental.

items.title: nemotron-3.5-parse
items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

Nemotron 3.5 Parse as its model card serves it (docs/serving.md, "Generation contract" and the H100 vllm serve block).

  • The control-token prompt </s><s><predict_bbox><predict_classes><output_markdown><predict_text_in_pic> as a text part FIRST, then the page image (the vendor client).
  • RGB at the original size, PNG (the server-side processor fits it to 2048 x 1664; a client-side resize would resample twice).
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, max_tokens 8744, skip_special_tokens false (the reply's coordinate and class tokens are kept).
  • Serve flags, the card's H100 block: --max-model-len 16384 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend uni --max-num-seqs 192 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, no prefix caching, one image per prompt, --attention-config '{"flash_attn_version": 3}'. FlashAttention 3 is a Hopper kernel: an Ada or Ampere GPU (L4, A10G) cannot run these flags as they are.
  • The architecture (RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM) is not in vLLM 0.26.0's registry. NVIDIA serves it through a vLLM general plugin (nemotron-parse 3.5.0.post7) shipped in the model repo; the adapter's serve_setup installs it into the vLLM image's own Python before vllm serve (the package source and NVIDIA's inference constraints from the model repo at the pinned revision, the lock's own nemotron-parse line dropped; the install fails if vLLM moved off 0.26.0). The plugin's one-token MTP speculative decoding stays on, as the card serves it. The image is vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0 by its amd64 digest.
  • The completion (coordinate tokens, <class_*> tokens and Markdown text) is stored verbatim; linecaster.engines.chat.nemotron_parse35.to_markdown renders it as the vendor's render_markdown from the model repo does.

items.title: oxr-1.0
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

OXR-1.0's whole-page product: the vendor's all-in-one service (D-FINE layout, the OXR VLM per region and its reading order, the vendor's oxr API assembling the page), one page per request to POST /v1/parse/sync. The engine (oxr.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: an image built unmodified from the vendor's docker/Dockerfile.allinone at github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR@c1a1dcb3 (on the vendor's pinned vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1; the vendor's plugin and entrypoint require vLLM 0.25.1 and Transformers 5.13.1), by digest. VendorServer downloads the model pin to /models/oxr-model (every pinned file checked, rather than mounting the weights) and starts the image's entrypoint, which serves vLLM on 8080 and the layout model on 8081 (loopback) and the API on 8000 (OXR_API_HOST 127.0.0.1); the API answers /docs once both model services are ready.
  • The request: the page as RGB, lossless PNG at its own size, as the multipart file, with api_key and one output_formats field each for markdown and json (httpx's encoding of a list). No feature_config or element_formats: the vendor's defaults (page headers and footers dropped, the overlap clean-up full_overlap_dedupe off).
  • Kept verbatim: the API's Markdown (the raw output, the text), its blocks (JSON) and warnings (the extension fields oxr__blocks_json, oxr__warnings). An answer with a non-zero code is the page's error. The service reports no finish reason or token counts (its per-region cap is 8,192 tokens in the vendor's configuration). The Markdown links the figure crops as images; removing the links is left to whoever reads the output.

License: the OXR License (Apache-2.0 with additional terms; see the model's page). Not run on HF Jobs.

items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

Qwen3.5-9B as a page reader, built from the model card and the checkpoint's config: greedy decoding with the card's penalties.

items.title: surya-ocr-2.5
items.text:
Preset · recognition · experimental

Surya OCR 2.5 as its package runs it: the surya-ocr package (0.23.0, the release that shipped with the checkpoint) and its full-page path, the call its surya_ocr command makes (RecognitionPredictor(manager)([page], full_page=True)), with the package's parser, blank-region filter and block-mode fallback. The engine (surya.recognition.v1, package linecaster-surya) reimplements none of it.

  • The server: the package would start vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1 with docker run. VendorServer starts linecaster's vLLM (validated on 0.25.1) on the pinned checkpoint instead (fetched, every pinned file checked, and served under the package's model name datalab-to/surya-ocr-2.5), with the flags the package's launcher passes for VLLM_GPU_TYPE=a100-80 (an A100 80 GB): --max-num-seqs 104 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, the package's dtype, model length, memory share, prefix caching and image limits; no MTP flag (the checkpoint has no MTP head). The engine attaches through SURYA_INFERENCE_URL, the package's own attach path. The image is the package's pin, by digest.
  • Every package setting is its default: full-page mode, 12,288 full-page tokens, guided layout JSON, SURYA_FULLPAGE_REGEN off (Datalab's own benchmark harness turns it on; the preset keeps the shipped default). The page goes in as an RGB image at its own size; the package scales it to fit 3072 x 2048 px.
  • The package and vLLM need separate environments (surya-ocr pins OpenCV 4.11, vLLM needs 4.13 or later): vLLM is the image's, surya-ocr the pipeline script's. surya-ocr declares pillow<11; the pipeline script overrides it with linecaster's Pillow pin (12.3.0).
  • Kept verbatim: the page's blocks as JSON (the raw output the lines were read from: label, raw label, reading order, HTML, skipped, error, confidence, box), and the full-page completion before the package parsed it (a second raw output, not kept). Rendering them to Markdown (with chandra's HTML converter, page headers and footers kept) is left to whoever reads the output. finish_reason is length when the page keeps a capped block's partial HTML; a failed block request is the page's error.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page). Not run on HF Jobs.

items.title: unlimited-ocr-2
items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

Unlimited-OCR-2 on Baidu's patched SGLang, following the model card. No vLLM support exists for it.

  • Server: SGLang in the image's own Python (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-cu130), with Baidu's wheel (sglang-0.5.20.dev10+g8d62f5fb9c, read from the model repo at the pinned revision) installed --no-deps and fastokens==0.3.2 first; served as Unlimited-OCR-2; the card's launch environment and flags, plus --enable-metrics (saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges). SGLANG_UOCR_EANABLE_DOC_LIMIT is upstream's spelling. serve.version is the wheel's version, which is the SGLang that runs.
  • No --revision: with it, Baidu's SGLang skips its tokenizer fix-up and fastokens refuses the tokenizer at boot, so the server loads the default branch. The default branch has moved on from the pinned commit (README and a newer wheel only), so the serve block checks that every file on the default branch other than README, .gitattributes, wheel/ and the paper PDF equals the pinned revision's (git blob ids).
  • The image, then <PAGE><image>Multi page parsing. (card-verbatim, the same prompt for one page as for many); full resolution, the same passthrough rule as v1.
  • max_tokens 8000, temperature 0.0, skip_special_tokens false, images_config {"crop_mode": true} (gundam, the card's single-page default), and the card's no-repeat n-gram guard as an SGLang custom logit processor (DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor, by its dill pickle reference) with its parameters.
  • The completion (<BLOCK>type[x1, y1, x2, y2]<FORK>text blocks) is stored verbatim and read into the transcription by linecaster's HTML importer (linecaster.engines.chat.unlimited_ocr.read_blocks): the running head and foot, page numbers and footnotes by their labels, titles as headings, the text literally. A response without content is an error.
  • The card's flags are for an 80 GB A800 (--mem-fraction-static 0.7, CUDA graphs up to 16384 prefill tokens); they also run on a 96 GB card.
uv run launch.py unlimited-ocr-2 IMAGES OUT
Step recognition (reads pages) Engine chat.v1 Model Unlimited-OCR 2 Revision 9cf077c4b206e0e2a31879df937b0b0bcba3661c License MIT Server sglang 0.5.20.dev10+g8d62f5fb9c Image lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-cu130 Produces text

items.title: unlimited-ocr
items.text:
Preset · recognition · core

Unlimited-OCR on vLLM, following the model card and the uv-scripts recipe unlimited-ocr-vllm.py.

  • The image, then the text part document parsing. (the card's <image>document parsing. minus the image token: over /chat/completions the image is its own content part).
  • Full resolution, no resize (the gundam crop grid is chosen from the input pixels): RGB PNG/JPEG bytes as they are, anything else RGB PNG.
  • Temperature 0.0, max_tokens 8192, skip_special_tokens false (the grounding tags must survive), and the card's no-repeat n-gram guard per request (vllm_xargs, the single-image setting) with its logits processor registered at boot, last on the command line (the flag takes a list).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 32768 --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt. linecaster's vLLM (validated on 0.26.0): the card's dedicated vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr image is obsolete, the architecture is registered.
  • The completion (grounded output, <|det|>type [bbox]<|/det|> headers) is stored verbatim. A response without content is an error, not an empty page.
