items.title: slanet-plus
items.text:
Preset · tables · core

PaddleX's table_recognition_v2 pipeline on every table region, fed with the page's own lines and their recognized text instead of its own OCR (use_ocr_model=False with an external OCR result); the cells come back with our text in PaddleX's HTML. The squiddle combination's table step.

  • SLANet_plus end to end for both table classes (e2e: structure and cell boxes from SLANet_plus's own prediction, the RT-DETR cell detectors unused), linecaster's choice where PP-StructureV3 uses SLANeXt_wired with a cell detector for what the classifier calls wired.
  • crop_pad 8: the table region's crop is grown by 8 px on every side (linecaster's choice).
  • The pipeline's other models are its submodels, by PaddleX name: the wired/wireless classifier (PP-LCNet_x1_0_table_cls, which picks the branch) and the two cell detectors (loaded by the pipeline, unused with e2e), each a pin of its model entry, so their files are part of the edition's hash.

Edition 2 (2026-11-03): the same models at the same revisions, moved from the option submodel_revisions (edition 1) to submodels, so their file hashes count too. Edition 1 was dropped from the lock when the catalogs were merged into one (2026-11-04), before any run recorded it. - Unruled rows come back as one cell per column with every PaddleX table model.

items.title: geometry-tags
items.text:
Preset · tagging · experimental

The property schemes geometry decides, by rules on the page's lines and regions: rotated and tiny on lines, multi_column on text regions, each with its evidence in the annotator's raw output. Nothing is recorded where the geometry does not decide; a model tagger (tagging.chat.v1) can ask about the rest.

  • max_tilt 5: the rotated vocabulary's "tilted by about 5 degrees or more". A line's tilt is its baseline's, else its polygon's when that is at least three times longer than high (elongation 3: a single glyph's box says no angle); a vertical writing direction recorded for the line is rotated too. A line with only a box is not decided, and neither is a half turn: an upside-down page has level baselines.
  • tiny 0.6: a line lower than 0.6 times the median height of the page's body text lines (body_roles: paragraphs and list items) is tiny. The vocabulary's fine print is about 6 pt, and body type is set at 10 to 12 pt, so 6 pt is 0.5 to 0.6 of it; a running header or a footnote at 8 to 9 pt, which the definition excludes, is 0.7 to 0.8. Line heights follow type sizes, since a line's box spans its ascenders and descenders. With fewer than five body lines (min_body_lines) the page has no measure of its body text, and nothing is decided.
  • multi_column: a text region is in columns when another text region sits beside it, their extents across the lines overlapping by a quarter of the shorter (min_overlap 0.25) and along the lines by at most a tenth of the narrower (max_overlap 0.1); it is not when it spans at least 80 % of the page's text width (full_width 0.8) with nothing beside it. A narrow region alone is left undecided: it may end a column whose neighbor ended higher.

The thresholds follow the vocabularies' definitions; none is yet measured against reviewed tags.

Step tagging (reads pages) Engine tagging.geometry.v1 Produces tags

items.title: squiddle
items.text:
Recipe · pipeline transcribe_modular.v1 · core

OCR for historical print from small models. PP-DocLayoutV3 finds the regions and their reading order, PP-OCRv6 medium detection finds the lines on the whole page, kraken's PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer reads them (batch 8, bf16 on CUDA), SLANet_plus rebuilds tables and PP-FormulaNet_plus-L reads formulas as LaTeX; rule-based steps make the typography, recompose the text into paragraphs (ratios, unicode-paragraphs) and compose the page document (linked-document). The item texts (--item-texts) are two: the item as read (literal:txt) and a normalized one (latin-historic+unicode-marks+flow:md: the historic letter forms modernized, the division marks no source marks resolved by squiddleocr's rule with the item's words as its lexicon, the rows flowed into paragraphs).

  • The recomposition changes paragraphs, not lines: a comparison of the lines is the same with or without it.
  • The normalized text is the recipe's opinion: unicode-marks joins most words divided at a line end rightly, but also many compounds divided at their own hyphen (on Wikisource's page-break words: 94.5 % of 345 compounds without a lexicon). Name the texts with --text for others; the literal text is always the transcription as read.
  • Edition 2 composes the page document with linecaster's own document (linked-document) instead of Docling's: the HTML, Markdown, text and JSON files differ, the transcriptions do not.
  • A downstream project that runs this recipe with other models runs a variation, not the recipe.
uv run launch.py squiddle IMAGES OUT

Its script, recipes/squiddle.py, is its environment: the engine packages its presets need. It runs without a checkout too:

uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py IMAGES OUT
Slot Preset layout pp-doclayoutv3 lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium tables slanet-plus formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l hierarchy ratios paragraphs unicode-paragraphs document linked-document Option Value text ['literal:txt', 'latin-historic+unicode-marks+flow:md']

items.title: alnum-nonmark
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

Letters and digits (alnum@1 before 0.10): a combining mark separates its word, a long s or a ligature does not match its plain letters.

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 nfc Unicode's canonical composition (NFC): the same characters, composed where Unicode composes them. 2 casefold Unicode case folding (ß as ss, final sigma as sigma). 3 letters-digits Only letters and digits (Unicode categories L, N) and U+FFFD; every run of anything else one space: a decomposed accent separates its word. 4 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: alnum
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

Letters, marks and digits of any script: formulas as the characters they print, markup removed, compatibility forms folded, case folded, everything else a word boundary.

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 latex-text Each LaTeX formula ($…$, $$…$$, (…), […]) as the characters it prints, its delimiters and TeX's whitespace gone: a formula compares equal to the same text typed (\frac{1}{2} and ½, \alpha and α, x^{2} and x², once compatibility forms are folded). For comparison: the structure is lost. 2 markup Markup removed, each match as a space: special tokens, box arrays, HTML tags of a fixed list, Markdown headings, bullets and rules, LaTeX macros, and the marks of emphasis, tables and formulas. 3 nfkc Unicode's compatibility composition (NFKC): ligatures split, the long s as s, superscripts and full-width forms as their plain characters. 4 invisible Invisible format characters removed: soft hyphen, zero-width space, non-joiner and joiner, word joiner, byte order mark. 5 casefold Unicode case folding (ß as ss, final sigma as sigma). 6 nfkc Unicode's compatibility composition (NFKC): ligatures split, the long s as s, superscripts and full-width forms as their plain characters. 7 letters-marks-digits Only letters, combining marks and digits of any script (Unicode categories L, M, N) and U+FFFD (an illegible character); every run of anything else one space. 8 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: ascii-alnum
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

ASCII letters and digits only, lowercased, HTML tags removed: what is not ASCII separates words.

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 html-tags Every HTML tag (anything between < and >) removed, as a space. 2 lowercase Lowercase (Python's str.lower). 3 ascii-letters-digits Only the ASCII letters a-z and digits and U+FFFD; every run of anything else one space: an accented letter separates its word. 4 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: diplomatic
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

Every character as written (NFC), whitespace runs as one space: case, punctuation, the long s, ligatures and diacritics count.

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 nfc Unicode's canonical composition (NFC): the same characters, composed where Unicode composes them. 2 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: latin-historic
items.text:
Strategy · for output

Historic Latin print in today's letters: the long s, the ligatures, the r rotunda and German print's superscript e folded; æ, œ, ø, å, ß and every other character as they are; spelling never modernized.

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 nfc Unicode's canonical composition (NFC): the same characters, composed where Unicode composes them. 2 superscript-e A combining superscript e (U+0364) over a, o, u (A, O, U) as ä, ö, ü (Ä, Ö, Ü): German print's umlaut; over any other letter it stays. 3 long-s The long s (ſ) as s. 4 ligatures The typographic ligatures ﬀ ﬁ ﬂ ﬃ ﬄ ﬅ ﬆ as their letters. 5 r-rotunda The r rotunda (ꝛ, Ꝛ) as r, R. 6 nfc Unicode's canonical composition (NFC): the same characters, composed where Unicode composes them.

items.title: reading
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

What a reader reads: formulas as the characters they print, markup removed, compatibility forms (ligatures, the long s), invisible characters, quotes and dashes folded, case folded. A hyphen at a line's end stays (no dehyphenation: reading@1 joined it).

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 latex-text Each LaTeX formula ($…$, $$…$$, (…), […]) as the characters it prints, its delimiters and TeX's whitespace gone: a formula compares equal to the same text typed (\frac{1}{2} and ½, \alpha and α, x^{2} and x², once compatibility forms are folded). For comparison: the structure is lost. 2 markup Markup removed, each match as a space: special tokens, box arrays, HTML tags of a fixed list, Markdown headings, bullets and rules, LaTeX macros, and the marks of emphasis, tables and formulas. 3 nfkc Unicode's compatibility composition (NFKC): ligatures split, the long s as s, superscripts and full-width forms as their plain characters. 4 invisible Invisible format characters removed: soft hyphen, zero-width space, non-joiner and joiner, word joiner, byte order mark. 5 quotes Single quotes, apostrophes, the backtick and the acute accent as ', curly double quotes as ". 6 dashes The dashes U+2010 to U+2015 (hyphen, non-breaking hyphen, figure dash, en dash, em dash, horizontal bar) as the hyphen-minus. 7 casefold Unicode case folding (ß as ss, final sigma as sigma). 8 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: typographic
items.text:
Strategy · for comparison

What a reader reads, with international typography folded (Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold, Apache-2.0, as catalog normalizations): reading's normalizations, and superscript digits after a digit set apart before nfkc; checkboxes as ☒ ☐, footnote markers [1] [^1] as their label, bullet glyphs and leaders as spaces after markup is removed; quote, prime, dash, space, arrow and CJK punctuation forms as ASCII or their plain form after nfkc; case folded and whitespace collapsed last. A hyphen at a line's end stays (no dehyphenation: line-end-hyphens opts in by name), as do language-specific letters (romanian-comma-below).

items.title: Normalizations
items.text: Normalization What it does 1 latex-text Each LaTeX formula ($…$, $$…$$, (…), […]) as the characters it prints, its delimiters and TeX's whitespace gone: a formula compares equal to the same text typed (\frac{1}{2} and ½, \alpha and α, x^{2} and x², once compatibility forms are folded). For comparison: the structure is lost. 2 superscript-digits Superscript digits (⁰ to ⁹) right after a digit set apart by a space, for comparison: 1,240¹ as "1,240 ¹", so that a footnote marker never joins the number it follows once nfkc folds it (1,240 1, not 1,2401), as a set apart by markup reads. Superscripts after anything else (m², x³) stay. Runs before nfkc. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 3 markup Markup removed, each match as a space: special tokens, box arrays, HTML tags of a fixed list, Markdown headings, bullets and rules, LaTeX macros, and the marks of emphasis, tables and formulas. 4 nfkc Unicode's compatibility composition (NFKC): ligatures split, the long s as s, superscripts and full-width forms as their plain characters. 5 invisible Invisible format characters removed: soft hyphen, zero-width space, non-joiner and joiner, word joiner, byte order mark. 6 checkboxes Checkboxes as two glyphs, for comparison: a checked box (☑ ☒ ■ ▣ ✓ ✔ ✗ ✘, and [x], [X], [✓], [✗], [checked] in any case) as ☒; an unchecked one (☐ □ ◻ ◼ ❏ ▢ ⬜, and [ ], [], [unchecked] in any case) as ☐. Every such glyph is read as a box wherever it stands (■ too, which some texts use as a bullet); other brackets stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 7 footnote-markers Footnote markers in brackets as their label after a space, for comparison: [1] (one to three digits) and the Markdown footnote [^1] or [^a] (one to three letters or digits) as " 1", " a", so that "12.3%[1]" does not read as "12.3%1" and a marker written as a reference matches one written as text. Spaces inside the brackets are allowed; other brackets ([12a], [1, 2], [1234]) and a marker without brackets stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 8 bullets A bullet glyph (• ‣ ◦ ▪ ▶ ∙ ●) starting a line, after any indentation and before whitespace or the line's end, as a space, for comparison: a list item compares equal with or without its bullet. The same glyphs elsewhere in a line stay, as do Markdown's - * + (markup's) and ■ (a checked box: checkboxes). Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 9 leaders Leaders and blanks as a space, for comparison: a run of three or more dots, ellipses or middle dots (. … ·), of dashes (- and U+2010 to U+2015, the minus sign), of underscores, of = or of asterisks (* ∗), optionally spaced (. . .), as one space, so that a table of contents' dot leaders or a form's blank compare equal however long they are. Dots and dashes form one mixed run; a dash before a digit after a space is a sign, not a leader (....... -4.8% keeps its -4.8%). Three dots are a leader too (an ellipsis compares as a space). Runs of fewer than three and single characters stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 10 quotes Single quotes, apostrophes, the backtick and the acute accent as ', curly double quotes as ". 11 dashes The dashes U+2010 to U+2015 (hyphen, non-breaking hyphen, figure dash, en dash, em dash, horizontal bar) as the hyphen-minus. 12 typography Typographic forms beyond quotes and dashes unified, for comparison: double primes (″ ‴ ‶ ‷ ⁗, and two to four primes ′′ as NFKC writes ″) and TeX's quotes (‘‘ ’’ '') as "; the low and reversed quotes „ ‟ and the guillemets « » as "; the low, reversed and single angle quotes ‚ ‛ ‹ ›, the prime and reversed prime ′ ‵, the saltillo ꞌ Ꞌ and the IPA stress mark ˈ as '; the minus sign U+2212, the two- and three-em dashes and the small and full-width hyphen-minus and em dash as -; the fraction slash ⁄ as / (½ after NFKC reads 1/2); the ellipsis … as ...; the no-break, en to hair, narrow, medium mathematical and ideographic spaces as a space; the asterisk operator ∗ as *; a middle dot (· ∙) between two digits as a decimal point; ≦ as ≤, ♢ as ◊; each family of arrows (double, white, heavy, long, harpoons) as its plain arrow → ← ↑ ↓. Whatquotesanddashes` fold (curly quotes, U+2010 to U+2015) is theirs, so a strategy names them too; a middle dot elsewhere, letters, digits and case stay. Runs after nfkc in a lane (it folds what NFKC leaves, ⁄ and ′′) and works without it. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0). 13 cjk-punctuation CJK and full-width punctuation as ASCII, for comparison: the ideographic full stop 。 and the full-width full stop ． as ., the ideographic comma 、 and the full-width comma ， as ,, the full-width : ; ! ? ( ) % = # $ & * + - / < > @ \ ^ _ ` | ~ [ ] { } and their half-width forms (｡ ､ ｢ ｣) as their ASCII characters; the corner brackets 「」『』, the double prime quotation marks 〝〞〟 and the double angle brackets 《》 as ", the single angle brackets 〈〉 as ' (as typography folds « » and ‹ ›); the lenticular and tortoise shell brackets 【】〔〕〖〗〘〙〚〛 as [ ]; the wave dash 〜 as ~. A table, so it works without nfkc (which folds the full-width forms but not 。、「」 or the brackets). Full-width letters and digits (nfkc's), the middle dots ・ ･ and the iteration and prolonged sound marks stay. Adopted from Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold (omni_parse_bench.normalize, Apache-2.0), extended to the brackets and quotation marks. 14 casefold Unicode case folding (ß as ss, final sigma as sigma). 15 whitespace Every run of whitespace one space, the text trimmed.

items.title: degraded
items.text:
Vocabulary · property scheme, yes or no · classifies lines, regions, pages

Whether the content is harder to read in the image than in a clean scan, because of the image's condition.

items.title: yes (answer degraded)
items.text:
The content is harder to read in the image than in a clean scan, because of the image's condition. Judge the image's condition, not the writing; handwriting that is also blurred, faded or noisy counts.

Counts:

  • blur
  • fading
  • noise or speckle
  • stains
  • bleed-through from the other side of the leaf
  • heavy compression artifacts
  • very low resolution
  • a photocopy of a photocopy

Does not count:

  • small print alone (the property tiny)
  • neat handwriting in a clean image
  • a clean scan on a colored or yellowed background

items.title: no (answer not_degraded)
items.text: The content is as easy to read in the image as in a clean scan.

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • Omni Parse Bench: the definition of its degraded tag (vocab.TAG_DEFINITIONS), adapted

items.title: form
items.text:
Vocabulary · property scheme, yes or no · classifies lines, regions

Whether the content is a field to fill in or a box to tick, or belongs to one.

items.title: yes (answer form_field)
items.text:
The content is a field to fill in or a box to tick, or belongs to one, its label, its filled value, the box, or the blank line. A label names what goes into one particular blank, box or checkbox next to it.

Counts:

  • such fields wherever they are, including a checklist in a manual or a survey printed in a report

Does not count:

  • instructions that tell how to fill the form in rather than naming a field
  • a title heading a section of the form
  • cells of a printed report's table

items.title: no (answer not_form_field)
items.text: The content is no field to fill in and belongs to none.

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • Omni Parse Bench: the definition of its form tag (vocab.TAG_DEFINITIONS), adapted

items.title: multi_column
items.text:
Vocabulary · property scheme, yes or no · classifies regions

Whether the content sits inside one column of a page laid out in two or more columns side by side.

items.title: yes (answer in_columns)
items.text:
The content sits inside one column of a page laid out in two or more columns side by side, a paragraph, heading, list, table or figure that fits within one column.

Counts:

  • either column of a two-column article
  • a sidebar beside the body text
  • either page of a scan or photograph that shows two facing pages

Does not count:

  • content that runs across the full width, such as a title, or a table or figure spanning all columns
  • the columns of a table on a page that is not laid out in columns

items.title: no (answer not_in_columns)
items.text: The content runs across the page's full text width, or the page is not laid out in columns.

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • Omni Parse Bench: the definition of its multi_column tag (vocab.TAG_DEFINITIONS), adapted

items.title: production
items.text:
Vocabulary · closed scheme · classifies words, lines, regions, pages

How the content was put on the page.

items.title: printed
items.text:
Made by a printing process, from type, plates or a printer.

Counts:

  • letterpress, lithography, offset, gravure
  • a laser or ink-jet print of a typeset page
  • a printed facsimile of a typeset page

Does not count:

  • text typed on a typewriter (typewritten)
  • a hand stamp (stamped)
  • a page rendered from a digital file and never printed (born_digital)

items.title: typewritten
items.text:
Typed on a typewriter, letter by letter.

Counts:

  • a typescript, its carbon copy
  • a duplicated typescript, such as a mimeograph or stencil copy

Does not count:

  • a computer's print in a typewriter-like font (printed)

items.title: handwritten
items.text:
Written by hand, with a pen, pencil, brush or stylus.

Counts:

  • a manuscript, a letter, a diary
  • handwritten values in a form, notes in a margin, a signature
  • the handwriting a photograph or facsimile of a manuscript shows

Does not count:

  • a typeface that imitates handwriting (printed)
  • a printed facsimile of a signature that is clearly typeset (printed)

items.title: stamped
items.text:
Applied with a hand stamp, a seal or a die.

Counts:

  • an ink stamp of a date, an owner or a library
  • an embossed or blind-stamped mark

Does not count:

  • a printed seal or ornament (printed)

items.title: born_digital
items.text:
Never physical, rendered from a digital document rather than scanned or photographed.

Counts:

  • a page image rendered from a digital PDF
  • a screenshot

Does not count:

  • a scan of a page printed by a computer (printed)

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • PAGE-XML: the production attribute of a text region (printed, typewritten, handwritten)

items.title: role
items.text:
Vocabulary · closed scheme · classifies lines, regions

What a zone or range is, its content role, whatever layer a rendering puts it in.

items.title: paragraph
items.text:
Running text of the page's content, read as part of its main text.

Counts:

  • a paragraph of prose
  • a stanza or a block of verse
  • a block quotation
  • the text of a letter, a dialogue or a speech

Does not count:

  • a heading or a title (heading, title)
  • an item of a list (list_item)
  • a note keyed to a mark (footnote, endnote)
  • text in the margin beside the main text (marginalia)
  • text set apart in a sidebar or box (floating)

items.title: heading
items.text:
A heading that names a section of the content that follows it, set on its own line or lines.

Counts:

  • a chapter, section or subsection heading
  • a numbered heading, such as "3.2 Methods"
  • a heading inside an article, a letter or a list of entries

Does not count:

  • the title of the document, an article or a chapter as a whole (title)
  • a table's column or row headings (table)
  • bold or spaced words that begin a paragraph (paragraph)
  • a running title in the top margin (header)

items.title: title
items.text:
The title of a whole document, article, chapter or story, set as its main heading.

Counts:

  • a book's title on its title page
  • an article's title on its first page
  • a newspaper article's headline
  • a chapter's title where it opens the chapter

Does not count:

  • a heading of a section within the work (heading)
  • the work's title repeated as a running title in the margin (header)
  • the name of a periodical in its masthead's running line (header)

items.title: caption
items.text:
Text that names or describes a table, figure, picture, chart or map, set next to it.

Counts:

  • a figure's or table's caption, such as "Table 2. ..." or "Fig. 3 ..."
  • the legend under a photograph or a plate

Does not count:

  • notes under a table, keyed to marks in it (footnote)
  • text drawn inside the figure (part of the picture, chart or map)
  • a line naming the photographer or rights holder (credit)

items.title: list_item
items.text:
One entry of a list, with its bullet, number or letter where the zone holds it.

Counts:

  • an entry of a bulleted, numbered or lettered list
  • a step of a numbered procedure
  • an entry of a glossary or a list of names

Does not count:

  • an entry of a reference list or bibliography (reference)
  • an entry of a table of contents or an index (toc_entry)
  • a numbered heading (heading)
  • a row of a table (table)
  • a paragraph that merely begins with a number (paragraph)

items.title: list_label
items.text:
The bullet, number or letter of a list item, set apart from the item's text in a zone of its own.

Counts:

  • a numeral or bullet a layout gives its own zone, left of the item's text

Does not count:

  • a label inside the zone of the item's text (list_item)

items.title: toc_entry
items.text:
An entry of a table of contents or an index, naming a part of the work or a term, usually with where it is found.

Counts:

  • a line of a table of contents with its page number
  • an entry of an index with its page references
  • an entry of a list of figures or tables

Does not count:

  • an entry of a reference list (reference)
  • a heading of the table of contents itself, such as "Contents" (heading)

items.title: footnote
items.text:
A note keyed to a mark in the text, set at the foot of the page or under the table it belongs to.

Counts:

  • a footnote with its mark
  • a note under a table keyed to a mark in it, such as "a P < 0.05"
  • a source line under a table

Does not count:

  • the part of a footnote carried over from an earlier page or column (footnote_continued)
  • a note gathered at the end of a chapter or book (endnote)
  • a running footer (footer)
  • a note in the margin (marginalia)

items.title: footnote_continued
items.text:
The rest of a footnote begun on an earlier page or column, continued here without its mark.

Counts:

  • footnote text at the foot of a page that starts without a mark and finishes a note from before

Does not count:

  • a footnote that begins here with its mark (footnote)

items.title: endnote
items.text:
A note keyed to a mark in the text, gathered with the others at the end of a chapter, article or book.

Counts:

  • an entry of a "Notes" section at the end of a chapter or book

Does not count:

  • a note at the foot of the page it belongs to (footnote)
  • an entry of a reference list (reference)

items.title: marginalia
items.text:
A note in the margin beside the main text, printed or written there.

Counts:

  • a printed side note or shoulder note
  • a gloss beside the text
  • a reader's handwritten note in the margin

Does not count:

  • a running header or footer (header, footer)
  • a page number (page_number)
  • a column of the main text (paragraph)

items.title: drop_capital
items.text:
An enlarged first letter of a paragraph or chapter, set into or beside several of its lines.

Counts:

  • a large initial that sinks into the first lines of the text
  • a decorated or historiated initial that begins the text

Does not count:

  • a capital letter in the size of the text (part of its line)
  • a large first word or line set on one line (part of the paragraph or title)

items.title: credit
items.text:
A line that names who made or owns a piece of the content.

Counts:

  • a photograph's or illustration's credit, such as "Photo: ..."
  • an article's byline
  • a copyright or rights holder's line under a picture

Does not count:

  • a caption that describes the picture (caption)
  • a copyright line of the publication in the bottom margin (footer)

items.title: floating
items.text:
Text set apart from the main flow of the page and placed where the layout had room for it.

Counts:

  • a sidebar or a boxed text
  • a pull quote
  • a short notice inserted between articles

Does not count:

  • a column of the main text (paragraph)
  • a note in the margin (marginalia)
  • an advertisement (advert)

items.title: reference
items.text:
An entry of a reference list or bibliography, describing one work cited.

Counts:

  • an entry of a "References" or "Bibliography" section
  • a numbered entry of a list of works cited

Does not count:

  • a footnote or endnote that cites a work (footnote, endnote)
  • a citation within the text (part of its paragraph)

items.title: code
items.text:
Source code, a command, a configuration or other text set as code, usually in a monospaced font or a code block.

Counts:

  • a program listing
  • a command line with its output
  • a configuration file's text

Does not count:

  • a name of a variable or a file in ordinary prose that is not set as code (part of its paragraph)
  • text that is typewritten (its production, not its role)

items.title: table
items.text:
A table, a grid of cells in which a heading is shared by several cells, so that a cell is read by the column heading above it, the row label beside it, or both.

Counts:

  • a table with its header cells, body cells, row labels and section rows
  • a grid with no printed headings whose rows repeat the same columns, such as a price list or a data sheet

Does not count:

  • a form whose fields each have their own label (form)
  • pairs of labels and values side by side (key_value)
  • the table's caption or its notes (caption, footnote)
  • two columns of prose (paragraph)
  • a table of contents (toc_entry)

items.title: formula
items.text:
Mathematical notation set apart from the text, as a display.

Counts:

  • a displayed equation, with its number
  • a system or derivation of equations set on several lines

Does not count:

  • a formula within a line of text (part of its paragraph)
  • chemical notation (chemistry)

items.title: chemistry
items.text:
Chemical notation set apart from the text.

Counts:

  • a structural formula
  • a reaction scheme or a chemical equation set as a display

Does not count:

  • a chemical formula written in a line of text, such as H2O (part of its paragraph)
  • mathematical notation (formula)

items.title: music
items.text:
Musical notation.

Counts:

  • staves with notes
  • tablature or another notation of music, with the words set under it

Does not count:

  • the words of a song set as text without notation (paragraph)

items.title: picture
items.text:
An image on the page, drawn, printed or photographed, that is none of a chart, a map or an advertisement.

Counts:

  • a photograph, an engraving, a drawing, an illustration
  • an ornament, a vignette, a printer's device, a logo
  • a seal, a stamp or a signature taken as an image
  • a diagram drawn as a picture

Does not count:

  • a chart or plot of data (chart)
  • a map or plan (map)
  • an advertisement (advert)
  • a line or rule between parts of the page (separator)

items.title: chart
items.text:
A chart or graph that shows data.

Counts:

  • a bar, line or pie chart
  • a scatter plot, a histogram

Does not count:

  • a table of the same data (table)
  • a drawing or diagram that shows no data (picture)
  • a map (map)

items.title: map
items.text:
A map or plan of a place, showing its area, routes or features.

Counts:

  • a map of a country, a town or the sea
  • a plan of a site, a building or a battle

Does not count:

  • a chart of data (chart)
  • a picture of a landscape (picture)

items.title: advert
items.text:
An advertisement, a notice set apart as one unit that promotes a product, a service, an event or a person.

Counts:

  • a display advertisement in a newspaper or magazine
  • a classified advertisement
  • a publisher's list of its other books at the end of a volume

Does not count:

  • an article about a product (paragraph, title)

items.title: form
items.text:
A form, or a part of one, with fields to fill in or boxes to tick.

Counts:

  • a field's label with its blank, line, box or filled value
  • checkboxes with their labels
  • a questionnaire printed in a report

Does not count:

  • instructions on how to fill the form in (paragraph)
  • pairs of labels and values set side by side with no field to fill in (key_value)
  • a table read by its column headings (table)

items.title: key_value
items.text:
Pairs of a label and its value set side by side, each label naming the value beside it.

Counts:

  • the lines of a data sheet, a receipt or a catalog record, such as "Date: 12 May"

Does not count:

  • a form's fields to fill in (form)
  • a table whose cells are read by shared headings (table)

items.title: header
items.text:
A running header, text in the top margin that belongs to the publication rather than to the page's content.

Counts:

  • a running title, the work's or chapter's name in the top margin
  • a journal's name, an author's name or a date line in the top margin

Does not count:

  • the page number (page_number)
  • the article's own title on its first page (title)
  • a heading of the page's content (heading)

items.title: footer
items.text:
A running footer, text in the bottom margin that belongs to the publication rather than to the page's content.

Counts:

  • a journal's citation line or a copyright line in the bottom margin
  • a running title set at the foot of the page

Does not count:

  • the page number (page_number)
  • a footnote (footnote)
  • a catchword or a signature mark (catch_word, signature_mark)
  • a table's last row near the bottom of the page (table)

items.title: page_number
items.text:
The number of the page, printed or written on it.

Counts:

  • a page number in the top or bottom margin
  • a folio number written in the corner of a leaf

Does not count:

  • a number in the text or a table
  • a page number given in a table of contents or an index (toc_entry)

items.title: catch_word
items.text:
The first word or syllable of the next page, printed at the foot of this one below its last line.

Counts:

  • a catchword in the bottom right corner of a page of an early printed book

Does not count:

  • the last word of the page's text (part of its line)
  • a signature mark (signature_mark)

items.title: signature_mark
items.text:
A printer's mark at the foot of a page that numbers the sheets for folding and binding.

Counts:

  • a letter, a number or a symbol with a number, such as A2, B, 3*, at the foot of a page

Does not count:

  • a page number (page_number)
  • a catchword (catch_word)

items.title: separator
items.text:
A line or rule that separates parts of the page and carries no text.

Counts:

  • a rule between columns or articles
  • a border or a frame around a part of the page

Does not count:

  • an ornament or a vignette (picture)
  • a dotted leader in a table of contents (part of its entry)

items.title: noise
items.text:
Marks in the image that are not content of the page.

Counts:

  • specks, stains or dirt
  • a punch hole, a tear, the edge of the scanner, a finger
  • a color chart or ruler photographed with the page
  • bleed-through of the other side of the leaf

Does not count:

  • a stamp, a seal or a signature (picture)
  • a reader's handwritten note (marginalia)

items.title: other
items.text:
Content that none of the other roles describes.

Counts:

  • content the annotator could not place in any other role

Does not count:

  • content that one of the other roles describes

items.title: Mappings
items.text: Role PAGE-XML Region label Default layer paragraph paragraph text body heading heading section_header body title heading title body caption caption caption body list_item paragraph list_item body list_label list-label list_item body toc_entry TOC-entry document_index body footnote footnote footnote body footnote_continued footnote-continued footnote body endnote endnote footnote body marginalia marginalia text body drop_capital drop-capital text body credit credit text body floating floating text body reference paragraph reference body code other code body table TableRegion table body formula MathsRegion formula body chemistry ChemRegion formula body music MusicRegion picture body picture ImageRegion picture body chart ChartRegion chart body map MapRegion picture body advert AdvertRegion picture body form other form body key_value other key_value_region body header header page_header furniture footer footer page_footer furniture page_number page-number page_header furniture catch_word catch-word page_footer furniture signature_mark signature-mark page_footer furniture separator SeparatorRegion picture none noise NoiseRegion picture none other other text body

items.title: Provenance
items.text:
• PAGE-XML: the region types and text region types, which the roles follow where PAGE has a name
  • SegmOnto: the zone types of its controlled vocabulary for the layout of historical documents
  • Omni Parse Bench: the definitions of its content tags (heading, caption, footnote, list, code, header and footer, table, form)

items.title: rotated
items.text:
Vocabulary · property scheme, yes or no · classifies lines, regions, pages

Whether the content's text is turned or tilted enough that a reader notices, as seen in the image.

items.title: yes (answer rotated)
items.text:
The content's text is turned or tilted enough that a reader notices, as seen in the image, by about 90 or 180 degrees, set vertically, or tilted by about 5 degrees or more.

Counts:

  • a page turned on its side or upside down
  • vertical text
  • a table set sideways
  • a page photographed at a clear slant

Does not count:

  • a slight tilt under about 5 degrees, as a scanner leaves it
  • italic text

items.title: no (answer not_rotated)
items.text: The content's text runs level, or tilted by less than about 5 degrees.

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • Omni Parse Bench: the definition of its rotated tag (vocab.TAG_DEFINITIONS), adapted

items.title: status
items.text:
Vocabulary · closed scheme · classifies spans, words, lines, regions

Whether something on the page or in its source counts as the page's text, and why not.

items.title: illegible
items.text:
Text that is there but cannot be read, its characters too damaged, faded or obscured to make out.

Counts:

  • a ground truth's span marked unclear, scored as one U+FFFD per character
  • a word worn away on the page whose length can still be seen

Does not count:

  • text the source leaves out entirely (gap)
  • text that is legible but hard to read in this image (the property degraded)

items.title: gap
items.text:
Text the source leaves out where the page has some; nothing is transcribed, and an empty span marks the place.

Counts:

  • an editor's omission, such as TEI's gap
  • a passage a ground truth did not transcribe, marked where it stands

Does not count:

  • text that is transcribed but cannot be read (illegible)
  • content the source keeps but leaves out of the text (suppressed, removed)

items.title: suppressed
items.text:
Content on the page that the source records but itself keeps out of the page's text; it stays in the record and is rendered nowhere.

Counts:

  • a ground truth's zone it marks as not part of the transcription it counts, such as a library's label or shelf mark in the image

Does not count:

  • content a step or an importer takes out (removed)
  • a second copy of a zone (duplicate)

items.title: duplicate
items.text:
A second copy of content another zone already holds, kept out of the text.

Counts:

  • a line detected twice, which the line assignment leaves out of the reading order

Does not count:

  • the same words printed twice on the page, such as a running title (each is the page's own text)

items.title: removed
items.text:
Content a step or an importer took out of the page's text; it stays in the record, with its reason where an importer kept it, and is rendered nowhere.

Counts:

  • a page number typography removes as uncertain
  • text of a source's markup an importer keeps as a region with a reason (hidden, generated, editorial, ...)

Does not count:

  • content the source itself keeps out (suppressed)
  • a second copy of a zone (duplicate)

items.title: Reasons
items.text: Why something present in a source is no text of the page (a classification's reason).

items.title: hidden
items.text:
A reader does not see it, and it takes no space on the page.

Counts:

  • markup a source's style hides, such as an element with display none

items.title: invisible
items.text:
A reader does not see it, but it takes its space; a space or line break stays where it was.

Counts:

  • text a source's style makes transparent or white on white

items.title: generated
items.text:
The source's software or markup draws it; the page does not print it.

Counts:

  • a number a wiki's template generates, a link icon, an automatic heading number the page lacks

items.title: editorial
items.text:
The source's editors wrote it; the page does not print it.

Counts:

  • an editor's note, a header the edition adds, a correction note

Does not count:

  • an editor's correction of the page's own text (an edit, corrected)

items.title: error
items.text:
A message of the source's software, not content.

Counts:

  • a template's or module's error message in the rendered markup

items.title: metadata
items.text:
Markup that is not content of the page.

Counts:

  • style sheets, scripts, metadata elements

items.title: apparatus
items.text:
The source's notation for something the page prints differently.

Counts:

  • a source's footnote mark where the page prints another mark or none

items.title: elsewhere
items.text:
Printed text that belongs to another page or another place.

Counts:

  • a source's text of the next page's first line, carried over to this page's record

items.title: layout
items.text:
Markup that only arranges the page and holds no text.

Counts:

  • an empty table row, a spacer

items.title: tiny
items.text:
Vocabulary · property scheme, yes or no · classifies lines, regions

Whether the content is printed noticeably smaller than the page's ordinary body text.

items.title: yes (answer tiny)
items.text:
The content is printed small, noticeably smaller than the page's ordinary body text, as fine print is, about 6 pt or less on a printed page.

Counts:

  • footnotes and legal fine print set small
  • dense small type in tables or forms
  • small labels on drawings

Does not count:

  • text set a little smaller than the body text, such as a running header
  • ordinary body text in a low-resolution image
  • text that only looks small because the whole page is photographed from far away or, for a large sheet, shrunk to fit the image

items.title: no (answer not_tiny)
items.text: The content is about the size of the page's body text, or larger, or only a little smaller.

items.title: Provenance
items.text: • Omni Parse Bench: the definition of its tiny tag (vocab.TAG_DEFINITIONS), adapted

items.title: Components
items.text: Every public component, by family: one page each with its contract, backends, options, behavior and where it comes in a pipeline. Terms are the glossary's; contracts and the builder are in pipelines.

items.title: Readers
items.text:
linecaster.components.readers

Component What it does ImageFolderReader Reads one page per image file of a folder or bucket. ImageParquetReader Reads one page per row of Parquet files with an image column. ManifestReader Reads one page per image of each item's manifest: IIIF Presentation 2 or 3, or METS with MODS (also inside an OAI-PMH response). PageRecordReader Reads the page records an earlier run wrote (JSON Lines or Parquet), so a pipeline can add one more part. PdfReader Reads one item per PDF file, one page per PDF page in order, each rendered to a lossless WebP image. ResourceReader Fetches the remote files of items as they are served, one document per resource, one item per task.

items.title: Images
items.text:
linecaster.components.images

Component What it does ImageConverter Converts each page's delivered image with an image engine and writes it, decoding and encoding as many pages at once as keeps the machine busy without overloading it. ImageFetcher Loads each page's image again from its address, for the components that need pixels.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
linecaster.components.layout

Component What it does LayoutDetector Detects the layout regions of every page, with their labels and reading order, by a layout engine.

items.title: Lines
items.text:
linecaster.components.lines

Component What it does LineAssigner Assigns the lines detected on the whole page to the layout regions and orders them row by row. LineDetector Detects the text lines of every page, with their geometry, by a line detection engine.

items.title: Recognition
items.text:
linecaster.components.recognition

Component What it does LineRecognizer Recognizes the text of every line by a line recognition engine. PageRecognizer Recognizes every page with a chat VLM or a page engine, whose output becomes the page's transcription. RegionRecognizer Recognizes each layout region of every page with a chat VLM, one request per region crop.

items.title: Tables
items.text:
linecaster.components.tables

Component What it does TableRecognizer Recognizes the structure of every table region by a table engine.

items.title: Formulas
items.text:
linecaster.components.formulas

Component What it does FormulaRecognizer Recognizes every formula region as LaTeX by a formula engine.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text:
linecaster.components.hierarchy

Component What it does HierarchyDetector Determines the typographic hierarchy of every page by a typography engine.

items.title: Paragraphs
items.text:
linecaster.components.paragraphs

Component What it does ParagraphBuilder Recomposes the running text of a page or an item into paragraphs by a recomposition engine.

items.title: Document
items.text:
linecaster.components.document

Component What it does DocumentComposer Composes the document (linecaster.document) of a page or an item by a composition engine.

items.title: Items
items.text:
linecaster.components.items

Component What it does ItemAssembler Binds each item's page records, in order, into one item record. ItemSplitter Splits each item record into its page records again, in the item's order, with what the item-level components added.

items.title: Importers
items.text:
linecaster.components.importers

Component What it does TranscriptionImporter Reads each page's source document into a named transcription, by an importer.

items.title: Tagging
items.text:
linecaster.components.tagging

Component What it does Tagger Classifies the zones of every page in property schemes (rotated, tiny, multi_column, degraded, form, ...) by a tagging engine, in the pipeline's process.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
linecaster.components.validation

Component What it does PageValidator Marks the page records that do not validate against Page or lack a required part with an error each. RecipeStamper Stamps the recipe a run follows on every step of every transcription, of a page or of each page of an item record.

items.title: Servers
items.text:
linecaster.components.servers

Component What it does EngineServer Starts linecaster serve inside the task for its served model components, through saturate's Engine. VLMServer Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine. VendorServer Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through.

items.title: Scoring
items.text:
linecaster.components.scoring

Component What it does PageScorer Scores each page of the stream against its ground truth, by a benchmark.

items.title: Writers
items.text:
linecaster.components.writers

Component What it does ImageFilesWriter Writes each page's image bytes as they came, one file per page. ItemDocumentWriter Writes the document of each item record by transcription strategies, one file per item and text. ItemTextWriter Writes the texts of each item record as JSON Lines, a row per item and text. PageFileWriter Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, JSON and more. PageJsonlWriter Writes the page records as JSON Lines, one file per task, or into item shards for a later stage. PageParquetWriter Writes the page records as Parquet, one file per task. RejectWriter Writes every page that carries errors to the task's rejects file and passes every page on. ResourceFilesWriter Writes each resource's bytes as they came, one file per resource. ResourceRecordWriter Writes each resource's record (doc.metadata["resource"], with its errors) as a JSON line, to <output_folder>/<rank>.jsonl.gz: one file per task, a failed resource included (error, errors). ScoreWriter Writes each page's score records and summary (doc.metadata["score"]) and passes the page on.

items.title: Composites
items.text:
linecaster.components.composites

Component What it does ModularTranscriber Reads a page's lines the modular way: layout, lines on the whole page, line assignment, line recognition.

items.title: Base classes
items.text:
linecaster.core: what the components above are built on; no pages of their own.

Class What it is for Composite Groups components under one name with an outward contract of its own. Contracted Gives a component the default contract(), read from its class attributes. ModelComponent Runs one model step's engine on every page, through its backend, and adds its part to the transcription. PageComponent Processes a stream of pages, one datatrove document per page, as the base of the page components. RuleComponent Runs a rule-based step's built-in engine on every page, in the pipeline's process, as the base of the rule components.

items.title: ModularTranscriber
items.text:
Component · composites · linecaster.components.composites

Reads a page's lines the modular way: layout, lines on the whole page, line assignment, line recognition.

Unit page Kind composite Reads image Adds ocr_new:line_confidences, ocr_new:line_regions, ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:reading_order, ocr_new:regions, ocr_new:text, ocr_new:word_confidences, ocr_new:words Replaces - Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader Comes before LineAssigner, LineRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, HierarchyDetector, ParagraphBuilder, DocumentComposer, Tagger, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source modular_transcriber.py

The contract is that of ModularTranscriber(lines='pp-ocrv6-medium-det', recognition='kraken-ppocrv6-medium', layout='pp-doclayoutv3'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description lines required a LineDetector, its backend, or a lines preset's ref. recognition required a LineRecognizer, its backend, or a recognition preset's ref. layout required a LayoutDetector, its backend, or a layout preset's ref; "single-region" reads the page as one region. formulas_separately bool False formula regions take no lines, for a formula step after it. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription every step works on (components given as components keep their own). name str 'modular transcriber' the composite's name in the graph and the plan. direction str | None None the writing direction the line assigner orders rows in (horizontal-rl: right to left; vertical-rl, vertical-lr: columns); None: each region's recorded direction, else horizontal-lr (LineAssigner).

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Expands into a LayoutDetector, a LineDetector, a LineAssigner and a LineRecognizer, each model step with its own engine and backend, in the transcription transcription. Outward contract: reads the page image; adds regions, reading order, lines, their assignment to regions and the recognizer's parts (text, words, confidences: its preset's).

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ModularTranscriber"]
    r0["image"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:line_confidences"]
    B --> a1["ocr_new:line_regions"]
    B --> a2["ocr_new:lines"]
    B --> a3["ocr_new:reading_order"]
    B --> a4["ocr_new:regions"]
    B --> a5["ocr_new:text"]
    B --> a6["ocr_new:word_confidences"]
    B --> a7["ocr_new:words"]

items.title: Example
items.text: ModularTranscriber("pp-ocrv6-medium-det", "kraken-ppocrv6-medium", layout="pp-doclayoutv3")

items.title: DocumentComposer
items.text:
Component · document · linecaster.components.document

Composes the document (linecaster.document) of a page or an item by a composition engine.

Unit page Kind transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:document Replaces - Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Step document Presets linked-document Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before ItemDocumentWriter, ItemTextWriter Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source document_builder.py

The contract is that of DocumentComposer(preset='linked-document'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description preset required the composition engine: a preset (e.g. linked-document) or an InProcess engine spec. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription to compose. unit str 'page' page (a document per page) or item (a document per item record, after a ItemAssembler). options dict[str, Any] | None None engine options over the preset's, e.g. {"sections": True}; None: the preset's. policy str 'page-layers' the rendering policy (a catalog policy entry) that puts each region into its layer.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
Text regions are composed from their paragraphs when a ParagraphBuilder made them, else from their lines as laid out (a diplomatic document). Reads regions and lines (and the paragraphs when there are); adds document; stat documents (pages) or items. Composition is a rendering: the transcriptions are left as they are (no annotator is added), and the document travels with the page or item record only, it is not stored.

unit="page": one document per page, named after the page id, in doc.metadata["document"] (as a dict), and the transcription composed in doc.metadata["document_transcription"], for the page writers (a writer without them renders the document itself). unit="item": one document per item record (linecaster.core.item), page n its n-th page, paragraphs continued across pages (an item-level ParagraphBuilder before it): doc.metadata["document"] and ["item_id"], doc.text its plain text (with furniture), as ItemDocumentWriter writes them.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["DocumentComposer"]
    r0["ocr_new:lines"] --> B
    r1["ocr_new:regions"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:document"]

items.title: Example
items.text:
DocumentComposer("linked-document")
DocumentComposer("linked-document", unit="item")

items.title: FormulaRecognizer
items.text:
Component · formulas · linecaster.components.formulas

Recognizes every formula region as LaTeX by a formula engine.

Unit page Kind model Reads image, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:formulas, ocr_new:latex Replaces - Backends in-process (InProcess), served (Served), a preset ref (id) builds one Step formulas Presets pp-formulanet-l, pp-formulanet-plus-l Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader, LayoutDetector, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source formula_recognizer.py

The contract is that of FormulaRecognizer(backend='pp-formulanet-plus-l'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description backend InProcess | Served | str required where the engine runs: InProcess, Served, or a catalog preset's ref (id or id) for its engine in the pipeline's process; a preset of another step is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription the step reads and adds to. params dict | None None keyword arguments for every call of the engine (in-process) or sent with every request (served); None: none. primary str | None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. name str | None None the component's name in stats and logs; None: "<step> (<backend>)".

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Reads the page image and the transcription's regions; adds formulas (a Formula annotation of each formula region, or what its preset produces: latex). A page without a formula region gets no image: the engine has nothing to read. A LineAssigner (or ModularTranscriber) with formulas_separately leaves formula regions without lines for it.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["FormulaRecognizer"]
    r0["image"] --> B
    r1["ocr_new:regions"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:formulas"]
    B --> a1["ocr_new:latex"]

items.title: Example
items.text: FormulaRecognizer("pp-formulanet-plus-l")

items.title: HierarchyDetector
items.text:
Component · hierarchy · linecaster.components.hierarchy

Determines the typographic hierarchy of every page by a typography engine.

Unit page Kind transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:hierarchy Replaces ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Step hierarchy Presets ratios Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source hierarchy_detector.py

The contract is that of HierarchyDetector(preset='ratios'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description preset required the engine: a catalog preset of the component's step (its id) or an engine spec, InProcess("module:Class", **options); a preset of another step, an engine of another step or options its engine does not have are refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription it works on. options dict[str, Any] | None None engine options over the preset's (recorded as the backend's overrides); None: the preset's as they are.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Heading levels from type size, headline splits, drop capitals, uncertain page numbers removed (see linecaster.text.hierarchy), each an annotation by the engine's annotator: roles and heading levels, a headline region with its lines linked to it, a drop capital joined to its line, status removed, a new reading order. Reads regions and lines; adds hierarchy; replaces regions and lines (what they are and how they are read). Stats: leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped. Its constructor is RuleComponent's (preset, transcription, options).

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["HierarchyDetector"]
    r0["ocr_new:lines"] --> B
    r1["ocr_new:regions"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:hierarchy"]
    B -. replaces .-> x0["ocr_new:lines"]
    B -. replaces .-> x1["ocr_new:regions"]

items.title: Example
items.text: HierarchyDetector("ratios")

items.title: ImageConverter
items.text:
Component · images · linecaster.components.images

Converts each page's delivered image with an image engine and writes it, decoding and encoding as many pages at once as keeps the machine busy without overloading it.

Unit page Kind transform Reads metadata Adds - Replaces metadata Removes image Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Step image Presets jp2-lossless, jpeg-q90, png, webp-lossy-q80, working-image Comes after any reader Comes before - Used in convert.v1 Source image_converter.py

The contract is that of ImageConverter(output_folder='out/images', preset='working-image'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the images go to. preset required the image preset (id, e.g. working-image) or an engine spec (InProcess("module:Class", **options)). keep_bytes bool False the converted image replaces doc.media, so later components need not read it again (it then also replaces image); without it the page leaves with no image bytes. options dict | None None engine options over the preset's (recorded as the backend's overrides). skip_existing bool True a page whose file exists is not converted again (a run that resumes). window int | None None pages in flight per stage, fixed; None: adapted (initial_window to max_window). initial_window int 8 the compute windows' start (the fetching and writing windows start at four times it). max_window int | None None the windows' upper bound (None: twice the CPUs, at least 4; the CPUs a Ray task reserved, else the machine's divided among the worker processes an executor runs at once): decoding and encoding. max_io_window int 256 the fetching and writing windows' upper bound: they wait on storage and the network, so they may be far wider than the CPUs.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
The preset says what: working-image (engine image.webp-lossless.v1) the working image, 8-bit sRGB lossless WebP at full resolution; an image.convert.v1 preset JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP (linecaster.images.transcode: decoded on a GPU where the machine has one and it supports the format, encoded there for JPEG and JPEG 2000, else with Pillow; each image records its decoder and encoder). The image is written to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.<ext> (_/<page_id>.<ext> for a page without item) under a temporary name (.part), renamed when complete; with skip_existing a page whose file is there already is not converted again (stat existing): its record names the file, its size read from the header. page.image becomes the converted image's PageImage (size, hashes, decoder; the encoder, the original and the step under extra): it reads and replaces metadata, and with keep_bytes replaces image; without it, it removes image. A page without an image address, over the size limit (check_size) or that cannot be read or converted keeps its image and carries the reason as an error (field image), so later model components pass it by and the RejectWriter writes it; the run goes on.

Pages go through four stages in threads (STAGES), each with a window of its own that saturate's controller (Auto) adapts: fetching (the resume check and reading the delivered file), decoding (a GPU batches the decodes that arrive together), encoding, and writing. So downloads run ahead of the decoders and uploads behind the encoders, each as wide as its own latency needs, as saturate's read-ahead does for requests. A window grows while its stage's throughput (kilobytes moved by fetching and writing, kilopixels by decoding and encoding) still rises and shrinks when the machine's memory or this process's open files run short (Pressure, saturate's kv gauge); window fixes them all instead. Into a Hugging Face bucket the files written at about the same time go up together (HfApi.batch_bucket_files), since the Hub takes only a few single uploads a second. Decoding and encoding are bounded by the CPUs (max_window), fetching and writing, which wait on storage and the network, by max_io_window. A page keeps its place in one stage until it has one in the next, so each window also bounds what waits behind it (decoded pixels among them). With an engine that does both steps in one call (image.webp-lossless.v1) the decoding stage converts and the encoding stage passes the result on. Each worker process uses one GPU (its worker index, round robin), so a machine's GPUs take one worker each. Pages leave the component in the order they came in. A worker's next task starts with the windows its last one reached.

    B -. removes .-> d0["image"]

items.text:
Component · items · linecaster.components.items

Binds each item's page records, in order, into one item record.

Unit page → item Kind binder Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source item_assembler.py

items.text: Option Type Default Description count_key str 'item_page_count' the page metadata key that holds the item's page count; a page without it waits for the end of the input.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
The item record is one datatrove document (doc.id the item id, doc.metadata["item"], linecaster.core.item) holding its pages in order (Page.sequence, then page id); a page without an item is an item of its own. The item-unit components after it (ParagraphBuilder and DocumentComposer with unit="item") and the item writers read it; the ItemSplitter turns it back into pages. It changes the stream's unit from pages to items and touches no part: the item record holds its pages as they came, every transcription with every part (the builder's checks carry them past the binder), but not the page images' bytes.

A task must see whole items: linecaster's run layout buckets page records by item (one item in one file), and the pages of an item must arrive in one task (with several tasks the builder cuts the pipeline here: the page records in item shards, then a stage over whole shards). An item is emitted once all its pages have arrived (when its pages' metadata give the count) or when the input ends (stat incomplete_items: items the input ended in before their count).

items.title: LineAssigner
items.text:
Component · lines · linecaster.components.lines

Assigns the lines detected on the whole page to the layout regions and orders them row by row.

Unit page Kind transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:line_regions Replaces ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:reading_order, ocr_new:regions Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in - Source line_assigner.py

The comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription whose lines and regions it works on. skip_labels frozenset({'chart', 'picture'}) region labels (region labels) that take no lines (default pictures and charts). formulas_separately bool True formula regions take no lines either and the lines inside them are removed, for a formula step that reads them as LaTeX; False: formula regions get lines like text regions. direction str | None None the writing direction rows and orphan regions are ordered in (horizontal-rl: right to left; vertical-rl, vertical-lr: columns); None: each region's recorded direction, the page's for the orphans, else horizontal-lr.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
Each line without a region goes to the region it overlaps most (a line that has one keeps it); lines outside every region (a page number the layout model missed, marginalia) become their own text regions (orphan_<n>, raw label orphan), one per visual row, slotted into the reading order; a line that lies mostly inside another is classified status duplicate, and a line inside a region that takes none status removed. Afterwards the list order of lines is the order a recognizer follows (regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region), and a new reading order ranks regions by reading order, then rows. Everything it adds is by its annotator, Annotator(kind="rule", step="assignment", name="line assigner") with its settings, seconds and datetime; line ids stay.

Reads lines and regions; adds line_regions; replaces regions (the orphan regions), reading_order and lines (their order). Stats: lines_in_skipped_regions, orphan_rows (the rows that became regions), lines.

items.text:
Component · paragraphs · linecaster.components.paragraphs

Recomposes the running text of a page or an item into paragraphs by a recomposition engine.

Unit page Kind transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:paragraphs Replaces ocr_new:paragraphs Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Step paragraphs Presets unicode-paragraphs Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source paragraph_builder.py

items.text: Option Type Default Description preset required the recomposition engine: a preset (e.g. unicode-paragraphs) or an InProcess engine spec. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription to recompose. unit str 'page' page (a stream of pages) or item (a stream of item records, after a ItemAssembler). options dict[str, Any] | None None engine options over the preset's; None: the preset's.

items.text:
The rows of each text region become paragraphs (ranges by the call's annotator), each with its decisions and its continuation links; a later recomposition makes them anew (its paragraphs are the page's from then on, the earlier ones stay in the record). Reads regions and lines; adds paragraphs and declares them replaced (an item-level recomposition after a page-level one). Stats: paragraphs, continuations, marks_removed, marks_kept (and items).

unit="page": each page by itself (a paragraph continues into the next text region of the page). unit="item": the pages of an item record together, in order (linecaster.core.item): the lexicon grows page by page, and a paragraph open at the foot of a page continues on the next one.

items.text:
Component · readers · linecaster.components.readers

Reads one page per image file of a folder or bucket.

Unit page Kind reader Reads - Adds image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, TranscriptionImporter, ImageFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in - Source images.py

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the images are read from. paths_file DataFileLike | None None a file listing the images to read, one path per line relative to data_folder; default: every file matching glob_pattern. glob_pattern str '**/*.{webp,jpg,jpeg,png,tif,tiff,jp2}' the image files to read; {a,b} alternatives are expanded. Default: WebP, JPEG, PNG, TIFF and JPEG 2000 files at any depth. recursive bool True datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. limit int -1 datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. skip int 0 datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. item_from_parent bool False the parent folder's name is each page's item_id; excludes item_id. item_id str | None None every page belongs to this one item; excludes item_from_parent. Default: pages without item. sequence bool False sets Page.sequence to the file's 1-based position among its item's files in sorted order; needs glob_pattern (every file of an item), not paths_file. file_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. default_metadata dict | None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. max_pages int | None None only the first max_pages files (sorted, or as paths_file lists them), for the whole run, divided over the tasks as all of them would be; default: every file. sample None only the pages of this linecaster.data.sample.SampleRule, chosen from the files' item and page ids ((item_id or "", page_id)) before any is read; the sample's files, in the listing's order, are divided over the tasks in turn, the same whatever the task count (the first file of an id that is listed twice). Excludes max_pages. Default: every file. read_images bool True read each file (image: its bytes, the page image's size and format from its header); without it each page carries only its image's address (metadata: page.image.uri, the format from the extension), for a component that reads the files itself, many at once (ImageConverter).

items.title: Behavior
items.text: The image files under data_folder matching glob_pattern, or the files listed in paths_file (one per line, relative to data_folder), are distributed over tasks in turn ([rank::world_size], as DataFolder.get_shard). Each page adds image (the file's bytes) and metadata (the page record: page_id is the file name without extension, the image's URI). limit and skip count pages per task, as in datatrove. An item's pages can land in different tasks: item-level steps run in a later stage over item shards (linecaster.components.writers.shards). No matching file fails the task with a PipelineConfigError.

items.title: ImageParquetReader
items.text:
Component · readers · linecaster.components.readers

Reads one page per row of Parquet files with an image column.

Unit page Kind reader Reads - Adds image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, TranscriptionImporter, ImageFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in - Source images.py

The contract is that of ImageParquetReader(data_folder='pages/'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the Parquet files. paths_file DataFileLike | None None datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. glob_pattern str | None '**/*.parquet' datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. recursive bool True datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. batch_size int 64 the rows read at once from a file. id_key str 'id' the column with the page id. A table without it names its pages <item>_<0001> from item_key and sequence_key, which it then needs. image_key str 'image' the column with the image; None: the table has none (pages without image, as a source's documents may be). item_key str | None None the column with the page's item_id; default: pages without item. sequence_key str | None None the column with the page's position in its item (Page.sequence). image_folder DataFolderLike | None None the folder relative image paths are read from; default data_folder. read_metadata bool False the other columns go into the page's metadata; without it only the named columns are read. file_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. default_metadata dict | None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False read the files of a task's shard in random order. http dict | None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields (rate limits, retries) for http(s):// image paths. Their images are requested ahead of the page being given on, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), and pages go on as their images arrive: a slow request (one being retried) delays only its own page. Rows read without a request (bytes, files) keep their order. max_pages int | None None only the first max_pages rows of the input, for the whole run: the tables are read as if they ended there, divided over the tasks (and auto_tasks counted) the same way; default: every row. task_per_item bool False the tasks divide the items (the item_key values, needs it; an item's rows need not be together), not the rows, and auto_tasks is one task per item: each item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item (pipelines/harvest.py). Default: rows in equal shards. reuse_folder DataFolderLike | None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.components.readers.existing: one listing per item), so a resumed harvest does not fetch it again; its record is complete and says image.extra["reused"]. A copy that cannot be read is fetched from the source. An item's listing that takes over LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) or fails is a warning and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and its pages are fetched again. Default: none. http_policy str | None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings for every host of the image URLs under http's, a host's own over both. sample None only the pages of this linecaster.data.sample.SampleRule, chosen from the id columns alone (id_key, or item_key and sequence_key; item_key) before any image is read; the sample's rows, in the tables' order, are divided over the tasks in equal shards (with task_per_item by item), and auto_tasks counts them. A row's image is read with the other sample rows of its row group. The first row of an id that is listed twice. Excludes max_pages. Default: every row. reuse_index str | None None the index of earlier harvests' page images (pipelines/harvest.py --reuse-from: OUT/logs/reuse-from.parquet, linecaster.components.readers.earlier): a page whose source URL an earlier harvest fetched is read from its copy there (checked by sha256) after this run's own copy (reuse_folder) and before a fetch, and written into this run's folder; its record says image.extra["reused_from"] and ["reused_from_uri"]. read_images bool True read each row's image (its bytes, size and format); without it a page names its image (a path column's value) and is read without it, as importing a source's documents needs.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
The rows of all files, in order, are divided over the tasks in equal shards, read by row group (linecaster.components.readers.tables), so any table works with any number of tasks; an item's pages can land in two tasks where a shard ends. auto_tasks is the task count for shards of about PAGES_PER_TASK pages, which linecaster.execution.run uses for a pipeline without engines. Each row adds image and metadata (the page record). The image column holds the image as Hugging Face's Image feature stores it ({"bytes", "path"}: the bytes when present, else the path), as plain bytes, or as a path: absolute (any fsspec URI or an http(s):// URL) or relative to image_folder. A row with neither bytes nor a path fails the task (a PageError: the table is wrong).

An image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after its retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) makes a page without image whose doc.metadata["errors"] says why (field image, raw_value the image's URI), so the task goes on: later model components pass the page by, ImageFilesWriter writes no file for it, and the page records and rejects keep it. More such pages than max_page_errors (a share of the task's pages, judged from page 100 on, ErrorBudget) fail the task, so a server that is down does not mark every page failed.

items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ImageParquetReader"]
    r0["page stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["image"]
    B --> a1["metadata"]
