items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike '.' the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the manifests or item tables, and the base of relative links; default the current folder. paths_file DataFileLike | None None datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. glob_pattern str | None None the entries to read; default **/*.{json,xml} (manifests), **/*.parquet with manifest_key. recursive bool True datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. manifest_key str | None None the column of an item table that holds each item's manifest link; default: the entries are manifests. item_key str | None None the column of an item table that holds each item's id; needs manifest_key. Default: the id from the manifest entry. read_metadata bool True an item table's other columns go into the metadata of each of the item's pages. manifest_format str | None None iiif or mets forces the format; default: told apart by content. item_id_pattern str | None None a regular expression whose first group, found in the manifest entry, is the item id (instead of the last path segment); an entry it does not match is a PipelineConfigError. existing_ocr bool False also fetch each page's own OCR file (transcription_file). manifest_folder DataFolderLike | None None where every manifest read is saved as fetched, <item_id>.json / .xml; default: not saved. http dict | None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields and HTTPFetcher settings over linecaster.net.http.HTTP_DEFAULTS (rate_limits of this task, timeout, proxy, iiif_format, iiif_quality, mets_image_groups, ...). file_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. default_metadata dict | None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. task_per_item bool False auto_tasks gives one task per item (pipelines/harvest.py); default about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task. reuse_folder DataFolderLike | None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.components.readers.existing); the manifest is still read. An item's listing that takes over LISTING_TIMEOUT (60 s) or fails is a warning and a stat (reuse_listing_timeouts, reuse_listing_errors), and its pages are fetched again. Not with existing_ocr (its OCR files would need fetching anyway). http_policy str | None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings per host, with http between its root and its hosts, for every request (manifests, images, OCR files). sample None only the pages of this linecaster.data.sample.SampleRule. The items are ranked from the entries' item ids before anything is fetched; a page's id (<item_id>_<sequence:04d>) needs its manifest, so computing the sample reads the manifests of the items in rank order, only as far as the rule reaches (every one with per_item alone), and an item whose manifest cannot be read stops it (the sample would depend on the failure). With manifest_folder each manifest it read is saved there with an index (SAMPLE_INDEX), and the tasks, and a later launch computing the sample again, read those copies instead of fetching them again. The sample's items are divided over the tasks as the entries would be (an item whole in its task); only their sample pages' images are requested. A IIIF Collection entry is a PipelineConfigError (list its manifests). Default: every page. reuse_index str | None None the index of earlier harvests' page images (pipelines/harvest.py --reuse-from: OUT/logs/reuse-from.parquet, linecaster.components.readers.earlier): a page whose source URL an earlier harvest fetched is read from its copy there (checked by sha256) after this run's own copy (reuse_folder) and before a fetch (looked up per item), and written into this run's folder; its record says image.extra["reused_from"] and ["reused_from_uri"]. Not with existing_ocr either.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
Entries:

  • without manifest_key: manifests: the files under data_folder matching glob_pattern, or the lines of paths_file (a manifest URL, or a path relative to data_folder), distributed over tasks in turn ([rank::world_size]) the way datatrove distributes files;
  • with manifest_key: Parquet item tables (the files matching glob_pattern, or a paths_file listing them), one item per row: its manifest link in manifest_key (a URL, an absolute fsspec path, or a path relative to data_folder), its id in item_key (optional), and, with read_metadata, every other column in the metadata of each of its pages. The rows of all tables, not the files, are divided over the tasks in equal shards (linecaster.components.readers.tables), so one table works with any number of tasks.

auto_tasks is the task count for about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task, or one item per task with task_per_item (pipelines/harvest.py), which linecaster.execution.run uses for a pipeline without engines.

A manifest is one entry, so an item's pages stay in one task (whole_items). An entry that is a IIIF Collection stands for its manifests, each an item named by its own link (a table's item_key does not apply to them); a collection listed in it, or a paged one, raises NotImplementedError (one level).

Each page adds image and metadata; with existing_ocr also transcription_file. Pages: item_id from item_key, else from the manifest entry (manifest_item_id: the last path segment that is not a generic manifest name); sequence the page's 1-based position among the manifest's pages with an image; page_id <item_id>_<sequence:04d>; image.uri the URL the image came from. metadata["manifest"] keeps the format, the manifest's URL, id, label, rights, required statement, identifiers and descriptive metadata, the page's own id and label, and the image request. Images are requested at full size (IIIF through the image service, iiif_format/iiif_quality in http; METS from the first image file group in mets_image_groups), with the fallback URL on 404.

With existing_ocr, a page's own OCR (ALTO or hOCR the manifest links: METS FULLTEXT, IIIF seeAlso / rendering) is fetched too, as a second media of the document (type document, metadata["format"] alto or hocr): a TranscriptionImporter after the reader reads it into the transcription ocr_original (the builder puts one there when the pipeline has none), and ImageFilesWriter(ocr_folder=...) writes the bytes.

A manifest that cannot be read or parsed, an image or OCR file that fails after its retries, or a response that is not an image is logged and counted (manifests_failed, pages_failed, pages_not_images, ocr_failed), and the task goes on.

Pages are requested ahead, across manifests, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one HTTPFetcher.shared per process and host's settings (linecaster.net.policy.Fetchers: http, and with http_policy the policy's for each URL's host, for the manifests, the images and the OCR files alike), so the rate limits hold across the tasks a worker runs one after the other; they go on as their images arrive, so a slow request delays only its own page (an item's pages can leave out of order; sequence keeps their place).

    B --> a1["metadata"]

items.title: PageRecordReader
items.text:
Component · readers · linecaster.components.readers

Reads the page records an earlier run wrote (JSON Lines or Parquet), so a pipeline can add one more part.

Unit page Kind reader Reads - Adds *, image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, TranscriptionImporter, ImageFilesWriter, ResourceRecordWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in bind.v1 Source records.py

The contract is that of PageRecordReader(data_folder='out/pages'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the page records. glob_pattern str '**/*.jsonl*' the record files to read; default JSON Lines (**/*.jsonl*), **/*.parquet for Parquet. fetch_images bool True read each page's image again (the part image); without it the pages carry no image. uri_map dict[str, str] | None None image URI prefixes rewritten before reading (e.g. a Hub path to a local copy of the same files). item_shards bool False the records are item shards (<shard>/<rank>...), each read whole by one task. http dict | None None linecaster.net.http.HTTPConfig fields for http(s):// image URIs. provides None the parts the records carry ("ocr_new:lines", "ocr_original:*", or Parts), for the builder's checks; default: anything (*; reads after this reader are not checked). The builder sets it when it starts a stage from the page records of an earlier one. http_policy str | None None an HTTP policy file (linecaster.net.policy): settings per host for those URIs, with http between its root and its hosts. sample None only the pages of this linecaster.data.sample.SampleRule, chosen from the records' ids (page.item_id or "", id), read from every record file before any image is fetched; each task reads its files as without it (only those holding sample pages) and passes on their sample pages alone (the first record of an id that is listed twice). Default: every record.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
Each pipeline of a workflow reads the previous one's pages/ folder (linecaster's page writers) and adds its part. The records bring metadata and, with fetch_images, image: page records never carry the image bytes, so they are read again from page.image.uri through datatrove DataFolders (http(s):// through linecaster.net.http); a URI with a fragment names a part of its file (file.pdf#page=<n>: that page rendered, file.parquet#<page_id>: that row's image, linecaster.components.readers.fragments), and one that cannot be resolved is the page's error (field image, stat image_errors), never the whole file. A page's errors come back as doc.metadata["errors"], so later model components pass it by.

Rows of an earlier format are read as today's (upgrade, by the row's schema): rows without schema name linecaster's transcription ocr (read as ocr_new), linecaster.page/1 rows a transcription's steps model (read as steps), linecaster.page/2 rows in the annotation model (linecaster.data.upgrade.upgrade); a folder .../pages that holds no records but has a sibling rows (the folder's earlier name) is read from there.

Files are distributed over tasks in turn; with more tasks than files, each file is shared by the tasks it falls to, each keeping every k-th of its records (k such tasks), so every task has work and every record is read by one task (a page scorer over a run written by fewer tasks). With item_shards the page records were written into item shards (PageJsonlWriter(item_shards=N)): the shard folders are distributed instead, each read whole, so a task sees every page of its items (whole_items). No shard folder is a PipelineConfigError.

items.title: PageRecognizer
items.text:
Component · recognition · linecaster.components.recognition

Recognizes every page with a chat VLM or a page engine, whose output becomes the page's transcription.

Unit page Kind model Reads image Adds ocr_new:markdown, ocr_new:text Replaces - Backends chat (Chat), in-process (InProcess), served (Served), a preset ref (id) builds one Step recognition Presets chandra-ocr-2, deepseek-ocr, deepseek-ocr-2, dots-mocr, dots-ocr, glm-ocr, lightonocr-2-1b, lightonocr-3-0.8b, lightonocr-3-0.8b-plain, lightonocr-3-4b, lightonocr-3-4b-plain, nemotron-3.5-parse, olmocr-2-7b-1025-fp8, ovisocr2, ovisocr3, paddleocr-vl-1.6, qianfan-ocr, qwen3.5-9b, smoldocling-256m-preview, unlimited-ocr, unlimited-ocr-2 Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader Comes before PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_page.v1, transcribe_vlm.v1 Source page_recognizer.py

The contract is that of PageRecognizer(backend='lightonocr-2-1b'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat | InProcess | Served | str required a Chat backend, an InProcess or Served backend of a page engine, or a preset's ref: a chat preset's (or a model's Hugging Face id: its page preset) for Chat on the task's VLMServer, a page engine's for its engine in the pipeline's process; a preset of another unit or any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription the completion becomes. primary str | None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build requests ahead of admission (decode, resize and PNG-encode the image; Pillow releases the GIL). name str | None None the component's name in stats and logs; None: "page (<model>, served <endpoint>)". repair_only bool False send only the repair pass, for the pages of earlier page records that need it (a Chat backend with repair_max_tokens set; PipelineConfigError otherwise).

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
On the Chat backend (served only) a stream transform: one request per page, built by the preset's adapter from the page image, the completion parsed into a new transcription (ChatAdapter.parse: its annotator, the completion verbatim as its raw output, and what was parsed from it) that replaces transcription. The completion's finish_reason and token counts go to its raw output and the annotator's measurements, and a completion cut off at max_tokens is counted (stat finish_length).

The repair passes (the chat option repair_max_tokens: a cap, or a list of rising caps, one per pass; linecaster.engines.chat.ChatAdapter): a page whose completion stopped at max_tokens waits in the component while its repair request goes into the same window at once (the same request body, so the same image and prompt and top_p, with max_tokens raised and the repair temperature); the other pages stream on. A repair that stops at its cap too is sent again with the next cap, until one finishes or the caps run out. Each repair's max_tokens is its cap, at most the served context minus the page's prompt tokens (the context from the server's /models max_model_len, else the preset's --max-model-len); where that is not above the cap before it, no more repairs are sent (none at all: stat repair_skipped). The page keeps the first completion that finished ("stop"), its first one otherwise: every request is one of the transcription's raw outputs (the completion verbatim, finish reason, tokens, pass 1, 2, ... and in settings the max_tokens as sent, temperature, top_p and preset), kept on the one the transcription's annotations were parsed from. The annotator's measurements sum the tokens of every request and list them per request (pass_prompt_tokens, pass_completion_tokens), its finish_reason is the kept one's; its settings add repair. Pages that stopped otherwise are recorded as without repairs (one raw output, no settings). A repair request that fails ends the repairs, and the page keeps what the passes before it give (stat repair_errors), not an error of the page. A page record is written only after its repairs, so an interrupted task sends every request again. Stats: finish_length (first requests), repair_sent (repair requests), repair_stop, repair_length (their finish reasons), repair_kept (pages that keep a repair), repair_skipped, repair_errors.

With repair_only it reads page records written earlier (PageRecordReader) and sends only the repair requests, by the same rules and recorded the same way: for the pages whose transcription's first completion stopped at max_tokens and has no repair yet (one raw output of the chat annotator, as linecaster writes a page without the repair pass or without room for it). Every other page passes through unchanged, without a request (stat repair_not_needed). The first request's prompt tokens and sampling come from the record. Where a repair is kept, the transcription is its parse, with the record's annotators (the chat annotator's place taken by the repair's) and every raw output; where none is, the record's transcription stays, with the repairs' raw outputs added.

On the InProcess or Served backend it runs a page engine (an engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: a vendor package, or a client of a vendor's service) as every model component runs its engine: the engine gets the page image and returns the page's transcription. Either way it reads the page image and adds text and what the preset produces (lines, markdown, html, ...); the Annotator records the preset and its hash. A failed request or call is the page's error.

    B["PageRecognizer"]
    r0["image"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:markdown"]
    B --> a1["ocr_new:text"]

items.title: Example
items.text:
from linecaster.backends import Chat

PageRecognizer("lightonocr-2-1b")
PageRecognizer(Chat("lightonocr-2-1b", "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", max_window=48, initial_window=8))
PageRecognizer(Chat("lightonocr-3-0.8b", overrides={"repair_max_tokens": [8192, 12288]}))   # repair passes
PageRecognizer("indra-ocr")             # a page engine, in the pipeline's process

items.title: RegionRecognizer
items.text:
Component · recognition · linecaster.components.recognition

Recognizes each layout region of every page with a chat VLM, one request per region crop.

Unit page Kind model Reads image, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:html, ocr_new:latex, ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Replaces ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Backends chat (Chat), a preset ref (id) builds one Step recognition Presets lightonocr-2-1b-regions, minicpm-ocr-1.0 Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader, LayoutDetector, ModularTranscriber Comes before LineAssigner, LineRecognizer, HierarchyDetector, ParagraphBuilder, DocumentComposer, Tagger, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source page_recognizer.py

The contract is that of RegionRecognizer(backend='minicpm-ocr-1.0'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat | str required a Chat backend, or a chat preset's ref (a model's Hugging Face id picks its region preset) for one on the task's VLMServer; any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription it reads the regions of and adds the lines to. labels frozenset({'caption', 'code', 'footnote', 'list_item', 'page_footer', 'page_header', 'reference', 'section_header', 'table', 'text', 'title'}) the regions' region labels it reads (Transcription.label; default: text-like regions and tables, no pictures or formulas). pad int | None None pixels around each region's box at the page scale; None: the adapter's region_pad, else 8. primary str | None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build the requests (crops, PNG encoding) ahead of admission.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: The same saturate machinery as PageRecognizer, results collected per page; any layout step can come before it. Reads the page image and regions; adds lines, text and what the preset produces, and replaces lines and text (the transcription's earlier lines, with their text, are replaced). Crops are cut at the scale the model expects for a whole page (the adapter's page_longest: the page is scaled so its longest side has that length, and the region is cut from it, pad px around the region's box at that scale), so a small region is not blown up; the adapter decides which regions it reads. Every read region gets one line: the region's box and polygon, the completion as its reading (verbatim; the completion, its finish_reason and tokens are a raw output of the step, which the line and its reading name), in reading order; the transcription's earlier lines are replaced. The step's Annotator records the preset, the settings with pad, page_scale and labels, and the token counts, regions and failed. A page whose regions all failed is the page's error, and so is a page without image bytes (stat errors); a page without readable regions passes through unchanged (stat pages_without_regions).

items.title: PageScorer
items.text:
Component · scoring · linecaster.components.scoring

Scores each page of the stream against its ground truth, by a benchmark.

items.text:
Component · servers · linecaster.components.servers

Starts linecaster serve inside the task for its served model components, through saturate's Engine.

Unit any Kind server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in - Source serve.py

The contract is that of EngineServer(models=[]); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description models list[dict] required the models to host, one dict each: {"name", "preset"} (a catalog preset, optional "overrides" over its options) or {"name", "spec", "kwargs"} (an engine class module:Class). A served model component asks for its model by name. port int 8100 the port the server listens on (loopback). python str | None None the Python that runs linecaster serve -m linecaster.cli; default this interpreter. Ignored with script. boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the server may take until every model is loaded. max_queue int 16 requests a model accepts before answering 429. script str | None None a pipeline script whose serve command starts the server in the script's own environment (uv run --script <script> serve); default: python.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: The server starts in warm_up() and is ready when every model is loaded; it stops when the task's pages are through. Its environment carries what the observers ask for (the task's trace file). A server that does not start fails the task (ServerError). Its kind is server and its unit any: it touches no part. It goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written.

items.title: VLMServer
items.text:
Component · servers · linecaster.components.servers

Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine.

Unit any Kind server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source serve.py

The contract is that of VLMServer(spec='lightonocr-2-1b'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description spec required the chat preset's adapter (linecaster.engines.chat.chat_model) or the preset's ref (id). port int 8000 the port the server listens on; Chat without an endpoint asks on 8000. host str '127.0.0.1' the address the server binds to; default loopback only. gpu_memory_utilization float | None None the share of GPU memory the server may take (for SGLang --mem-fraction-static); default the preset's flags alone. The deployment's choice. extra_args list[str] | None None more server flags, after the preset's. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on PATH, e.g. from the job image or a uv run --with vllm==... environment). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the server may take to answer. outside_venv bool False start the server without this interpreter's virtual environment (VIRTUAL_ENV unset, its bin taken off PATH), for a job image whose own Python has the server while the pipeline runs in a uv environment on top (HF Jobs); the server's helpers (ninja, python) then come from the image. python str 'python3' the Python that has SGLang (default python3, looked up on the server's PATH, then in the usual image locations). server_env str 'path' where the server comes from: "path" (the command on PATH, or the image's Python, as above), "uv" (its release, spec.server_version, with the preset's server_packages, in an environment uv builds once per machine: linecaster.components.servers.provision; the server then runs outside this interpreter's environment, its environment's bin first on PATH), or "auto": the one on PATH when it is the preset's release (an image at linecaster's vLLM pin), else uv's.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
The command comes from the chat preset's serve block (server, flags, environment, packages), whose server picks it:

  • "vllm": vllm serve <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT <spec.vllm_args(...)> (behind bash -c when the preset has a setup script);
  • "sglang": PYTHON -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT --enable-metrics <spec.sglang_args(...)> (metrics on: saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges).

The server starts in warm_up() and is ready when it answers a trial chat request (saturate's alive-only gate); it stops when the task's pages are through. Before it starts, the preset's server_packages are installed into the server's Python (uv pip install --python <that Python> ...), and for a preset with revision_flag: false (the server cannot be given --revision and loads the default branch) the component refuses to start unless the default branch's files equal the pinned revision's (check_default_branch); the preset's server_env goes into the server's environment. With OTLP configured, vLLM traces too (tracing_args). On a machine without a CUDA toolkit (no nvcc on the server's PATH, neither CUDA_HOME nor CUDA_PATH set) vLLM starts with VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 (flashinfer_env), unless that variable is set already: FlashInfer's sampler compiles its kernels at first use and fails without nvcc. A server that does not start fails the task (ServerError).

The server listens on port (8000 for Chat by default), so two runs on one machine collide unless each gets its own port and its own GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES): a second vLLM on a GPU that one already uses does not get its memory share, and a second server on the same port does not start.

Its kind is server and its unit any: it touches no part. Like EngineServer, it goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["VLMServer"]
    r0["any stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["any stream"]

items.title: VendorServer
items.text:
Component · servers · linecaster.components.servers

Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through.

Unit any Kind server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_page.v1 Source service.py

The contract is that of VendorServer(preset='falcon-ocr'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description preset str required the page preset whose serve block names the service (id); a chat preset (VLMServer starts its server), or a preset without such a component, is refused (PipelineConfigError). port int 8000 the port vLLM listens on (server: vllm); a vendor's entrypoint uses the image's own ports. host str '127.0.0.1' the address vLLM binds to; default loopback only. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on the service's PATH: the job image's). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the service may take until it is ready. server_env str 'path' for server: vllm, where vLLM comes from: "path" (vllm above) or "uv" (the preset's vLLM release, linecaster's VLLM_VERSION unless it names another, in an environment uv builds once per machine: linecaster.components.servers.provision), its bin first on the service's PATH, or "auto": the vllm on PATH when it is that release, else uv's.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
The preset's serve block says what runs:

  • server: vllm (an engine package that attaches to vLLM, e.g. surya-ocr): the model pin is fetched (every pinned file checked) and served from that folder, vllm serve <folder> --host HOST --port PORT <flags> --served-model-name <the model's Hugging Face id>, ready once /health and /v1/models answer 200;
  • server: vendor (a vendor's page pipeline in its own image, e.g. Falcon-OCR, OXR): with weights_dir the model pin is downloaded there first (every pinned file checked); then command, the image's entrypoint, starts the service, ready once every health URL has answered 200, in order.

The service runs in its own process group with the preset's env, without the pipeline's environment (PIPELINE_ENV, and this interpreter's bin off PATH), so the image's own Pythons and servers run as the image has them. A service that exits or is not ready within boot_timeout fails the task (ServerError). Its kind is server and its unit any: it touches no part. It goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the ports the image sets (one service per machine).

items.text:

    B["VendorServer"]
    r0["any stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["any stream"]

items.title: Tagger
items.text:
Component · tagging · linecaster.components.tagging

Classifies the zones of every page in property schemes (rotated, tiny, multi_column, degraded, form, ...) by a tagging engine, in the pipeline's process.

Unit page Kind transform Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:tags Replaces - Step tagging Presets geometry-tags Comes after LayoutDetector, LineDetector, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in - Source tagger.py

The contract is that of Tagger(preset='geometry-tags'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description preset required the tagger: a catalog preset of the tagging step (geometry-tags) or an engine spec, InProcess("module:Class", **options) (the model tagger, whose panel a run names); a preset of another step, an engine of another step or options its engine does not have are refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription it classifies. options dict[str, Any] | None None engine options over the preset's (recorded as the backend's overrides); None: the preset's as they are.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Each decision is a classification of the narrowest target (a line, a region, the page) by the engine's annotator, with its evidence: the geometry tagger's measurements, or every panel member's answer, as raw outputs; where the evidence does not decide, nothing is recorded. The page image is decoded for an engine that reads it (the model tagger, which shows the members the page and the target). Reads regions and lines (the model tagger: the page image and its targets); adds tags. Stats: tagged and undecided (classifications recorded and targets left undecided, over all schemes). The engine gets the page's id (page), which review items name.

    r1["ocr_new:regions"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:tags"]

Tagger("geometry-tags")
Tagger(InProcess("linecaster.engines:ChatTaggingEngine", schemes=["degraded"], panel=[...]))

items.title: ImageFilesWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes each page's image bytes as they came, one file per page.

Unit page Kind writer Reads image Adds - Replaces metadata Comes after ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PageRecordReader, PdfReader Comes before - Used in harvest.v1 Source images.py

The contract is that of ImageFilesWriter(output_folder='out/images'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the images go to. ocr_folder DataFolderLike | None None where a library's own OCR that came with the page (a document media, as ManifestReader's existing_ocr adds it) is written the same way, <ocr_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.xml (ALTO) or .html (hOCR), when the page has its ocr_original transcription; that transcription's source then names the copy (source.ocr__file, an extension field; source.uri stays where it came from). Default: not written.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Files go to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.<ext> (any fsspec folder; <page_id>.<ext> for pages without an item), the extension from the image's format. It reads image and replaces metadata: the page's image.uri then names the written file and image.extra["source_uri"] where it came from, so page records written after this component point at the copy (PageRecordReader fetches it from there), and ImageFolderReader(output_folder, item_from_parent=True) reads the folder as it is. Pages pass through; a page that carries errors and no image (e.g. its download failed) passes through unchanged, with no file written; a page read from the file an earlier launch wrote (image.extra["reused"], a reader's reuse_folder) gets its record as written, the file left as it is. A local file appears only once it is whole (written as <name>.part, then renamed), so a reader never takes a half-written file for a done page.

items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ImageFilesWriter"]
    r0["image"] --> B
    B --> a0["page stream"]
    B -. replaces .-> x0["metadata"]

items.text: It reads the item's document (an item-level DocumentComposer's, doc.metadata["document"]: the literal document), writes it by each text's strategy (linecaster.document.strategy) in the text's format (linecaster.document.export) to <strategy>/<item id><suffix>.<ext>; an item record without a document is counted (no_document). Item records pass through.

Writes the texts of each item record as JSON Lines, a row per item and text.

Unit item Kind writer Reads document Adds - Replaces - Comes after DocumentComposer Comes before - Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source items.py

items.text: Each text (<strategy>:<format>) is the item's document (an item-level DocumentComposer's) written by the strategy in the format (item_texts); a row holds id (the item), text and item_id, strategy, strategy_sha256, normalizations, format, page_ids, pages (count) and token_count with a token_counter, in <strategy>.<format>/<rank>.jsonl.gz. A stream entry that is no item record, or one without a document, is counted (no_item, no_document). Item records pass through.

items.title: PageFileWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, JSON and more.

Unit page Kind writer Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Adds - Replaces - Comes after LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source files.py

The contract is that of PageFileWriter(output_folder='out/files'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the files go to. formats tuple[str, ...] ('hocr', 'alto', 'page', 'txt') the formats to write, keys of PAGE_FILE_EXTENSIONS; an unknown one is a PipelineConfigError. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription written. suffix str '' added to each file's stem, before the extension (".paddle": <page_id>.paddle.md). furniture bool False keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html. bucket_by_item bool True one folder per item; False writes <page_id><suffix>.<ext> flat, in one folder. Pages without item_id are always written flat. detail str 'word' word (lines and words) or line (text per line) for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE. dividers bool False put --- between layout regions in md. text_fallback bool True a page without a document (lines only) still gets md and txt from Transcription.text; False writes them only from a document (the component then reads document). skip_failed bool False write no files for a page that carries errors (doc.metadata["errors"]); the default writes them as for any page. policy str 'page-layers' the rendering policy (a catalog policy) of every file it writes: the layers of a rendered document, the regions left out of the page files. strategy str 'literal' the transcription strategy md, txt, html and json are written by: literal (the default), a catalog strategy, or normalizations joined by +.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
Files go to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id><suffix>.<ext> (any fsspec folder: local, s3://, hf://buckets/...). It reads the parts its formats are written from (FORMAT_PARTS: lines for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, text for md and txt, document for HTML and JSON, image for plots) and adds nothing; pages pass through, so writers can be chained. A page without the transcription is counted (no_transcription) and passed on; with skip_failed, so is a page an earlier component failed on (skipped_failed): its files would hold what the components before the failure made of it, while the RejectWriter lists it and the page records keep it with its errors.

  • hocr, alto, page: linecaster's serializers (to_hocr/to_alto/to_page) at the page image's size; detail="line" leaves the words out (text per line);
  • md, txt, html, json: the document's serializations (linecaster.document.export), written by the transcription strategy (literal by default: as read; linecaster.document.strategy): the document a DocumentComposer composed for the page (doc.metadata["document"]), else the transcription rendered with the default options (linecaster.document.build_document) when it has regions or paragraphs; for a page of lines only, md and txt fall back to its literal text (linecaster.text.page.page_text: lines in reading order, tables as Markdown/HTML, the regions the policy puts nowhere left out; counted as <format>_from_page_text; only a strategy of character rules applies to it, others write none) and the others are skipped (counted as no_document);
  • transcription: the Transcription itself as JSON;
  • plot: a JPEG of the page image with the regions and lines drawn in (linecaster.images.plots).

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["PageFileWriter"]
    r0["ocr_new:lines"] --> B
    r1["ocr_new:text"] --> B
    B --> a0["page stream"]

items.title: RejectWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes every page that carries errors to the task's rejects file and passes every page on.

Unit any Kind writer Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in - Source rejects.py

The contract is that of RejectWriter(output_folder='out/rejects'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the rejects go to. prefix str '' put before each file name, so two writers that share a folder stay apart.

items.title: Behavior
items.text: The file is <output_folder>/<prefix><rank:05d>.jsonl, opened on the first reject (a task without rejects leaves no file), one line per error of doc.metadata["errors"]: key (the page id), field (else the step or component that failed), error, raw_value, and the entry's other keys (component, step, preset, type). The page records keep the failed pages with their errors. The builder puts one before the first writer of a pipeline with a run folder (<run_folder>/rejects) when it has none.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["RejectWriter"]
    r0["any stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["any stream"]

items.title: ResourceFilesWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes each resource's bytes as they came, one file per resource.

Unit item Kind writer Reads - Adds - Replaces metadata Comes after - Comes before - Used in harvest.v1 Source resources.py

The contract is that of ResourceFilesWriter(output_folder='out'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the copies go to (the run folder).

items.title: Behavior
items.text: Files go to <output_folder>/<kind>/<item>/<name>.<ext> (any fsspec folder), appearing only once whole (a local file as <name>.part, then renamed); a resource read back from its copy in this folder (reused) is not written again, one read from an earlier harvest's folder (reused_from) is, so the folder holds every file. The record's uri then names the copy, its source_uri where it came from. A resource that failed (no bytes) passes through without a file.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ResourceFilesWriter"]
    r0["item stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["item stream"]
    B -. replaces .-> x0["metadata"]

items.title: ResourceRecordWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes each resource's record (doc.metadata["resource"], with its errors) as a JSON line, to <output_folder>/<rank>.jsonl.gz: one file per task, a failed resource included (error, errors).

Unit item Kind writer Reads metadata Adds - Replaces - Comes after any reader Comes before - Used in harvest.v1 Source resources.py

The contract is that of ResourceRecordWriter(output_folder='out/resources'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the records (OUT/resources).

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ResourceRecordWriter"]
    r0["metadata"] --> B
    B --> a0["item stream"]

items.title: ScoreWriter
items.text:
Component · writers · linecaster.components.writers

Writes each page's score records and summary (doc.metadata["score"]) and passes the page on.

Unit page Kind writer Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in score.v1 Source scores.py

The contract is that of ScoreWriter(output_folder='out/scores'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every component's contract.

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the scores folder (local path or fsspec URI): records/ and pages/ in it.

items.title: Contract
items.text:
flowchart LR
    B["ScoreWriter"]
    r0["page stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["page stream"]

items.title: The parts
items.text: Part What it is ground truth transcriptions made or checked by people, as page records benchmark a definition of how to score against one ground truth: which pages, which lanes, which metrics score record one page's counts for one lane evidence record the result of scoring one run, with everything needed to compare it with another

items.title: How scoring works
items.text:
flowchart LR
    G[ground truth files] -->|importer| GR[page records]
    I[page images] -->|pipeline| RR[page records]
    GR --> S[score]
    RR --> S
    B[benchmark] --> S
    S --> E[evidence record]
  1. An importer reads the ground truth (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, TEI, HTML, plain text) into page records.
  2. A pipeline transcribes the same pages.
  3. Both sides are rendered the same way and normalized by the same lane.
  4. The scorer counts character and word errors for the page, and for each region, table and formula on its own.

Rates are computed from counts, so results can be added up across pages without bias.

items.title: What linecaster does not hold
items.text: Linecaster ships the scorer and the formats. Ground truths, benchmarks and results are data: they live in the repository of the evaluation that made them, not in linecaster.

items.title: Reference
items.text: Evaluation defines the lanes, the metrics and the record formats.

items.title: The three parts
items.text:
Part What it is Example model weights from upstream, pinned to a revision and checked by hash kraken-ppocrv6-medium engine code that loads a model and processes one unit per call kraken.recognition.v1 preset a named configuration: an engine, its options and a model kraken-ppocrv6-medium

You only ever pick a preset. The preset says which engine runs and which model it loads, so a run names exactly what it ran.

An engine works on one unit: a line, a region or a whole page. A line recognizer reads lines; a vision-language model reads pages.

items.title: The catalog
items.text:
The catalog is the list of everything you can pick. It ships with linecaster as YAML files:

  • models and presets,
  • recipes,
  • normalizations and strategies (see text and normalization),
  • rendering policies, conventions and vocabularies.

List the presets with linecaster presets. The catalog pages describe each entry.

items.title: Engine packages
items.text: Engines for kraken, PaddleX, Tesseract and others are separate packages (linecaster-kraken, ...), because their dependencies conflict with each other. The core has no torch and no model runtime. A pipeline script installs exactly the packages its presets need.

items.title: Recipes
items.text: A recipe is a tested combination: one preset for each slot of a pipeline template, plus options such as the texts to write. uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/ runs the recipe squiddle.

items.title: Nothing changes unseen
items.text: Each catalog entry has a hash of everything that affects its output. The file catalog.index lists the hashes, so a change of behavior shows up in review. A run record names every entry the run used, with its hash and the linecaster version. Together they reproduce the run.

items.title: Reference
items.text: The catalog reference describes the file formats and the commands.

items.title: Overview
items.text: Linecaster turns page images into text. This page explains its few main ideas and how they fit together. Each idea has a page of its own, and the glossary lists every term.

items.title: A pipeline of components
items.text:
A pipeline is an ordered list of components. Pages go through it one after another, and each component reads a page and adds something to it.

flowchart LR
    R[reader] --> L[layout] --> D[lines] --> T[recognition] --> H[hierarchy] --> P[paragraphs] --> C[document] --> W[writers]

This is the modular pipeline: a layout model finds the regions of a page, a line detector finds the lines, and a line recognizer reads each line. Rule-based components then find the headings, join the lines into paragraphs and build a document. A second kind of pipeline is shorter: a vision-language model reads the whole page in one go.

flowchart LR
    R[reader] --> V[recognition by a VLM] --> W[writers]

Each box is a step: one kind of work. What does the work at a step is your choice.

Read more: components and pipelines.

items.title: Models, engines and presets
items.text:
Three things work together at a step:

  • A model is a file of weights from upstream, pinned to an exact revision.
  • An engine is the code that loads a model and runs it. Rule-based engines need no model.
  • A preset is a named configuration of one engine with one model. A preset is what you pick: --recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium.

A recipe is a tested combination of presets, one for each step. All of these are listed in the catalog.

Read more: models, engines and presets.

items.title: The page record
items.text:
A pipeline's result is one page record per page. It holds everything every component said about the page: the regions, the lines, the text of each line, the tables, and who said it. Nothing in it is overwritten.

The text in the record is exactly what the model read. Changes such as joining hyphenated words are made only when you ask for a text to be written, by a strategy you name.

Read more: page records and text and normalization.

items.title: Running anywhere
items.text: Linecaster builds on datatrove, which runs a pipeline on a laptop, on a Ray cluster or on Hugging Face Jobs. The pipeline stays the same; only the command line changes. A run can be interrupted and resumed, and a page that fails is set aside with the reason.

items.title: Ground truth and scoring
items.text:
Linecaster also reads ground truth (transcriptions made by people) in many formats into the same page records, and scores a run against it.

Read more: evaluation.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:
• Run a recipe: your first transcription.
  • Run a vision-language model.
  • Score a run against ground truth.

items.title: Items and pages
items.text: An item is an ordered set of pages: a book, a newspaper issue, a PDF, a folder of images. A page is one page of an item, with its image.

items.title: What a page record holds
items.text:
A page record is the page as it goes through a pipeline and as it is stored. Each component adds to it:

flowchart TD
    P[page record] --> I[image reference]
    P --> T[transcriptions]
    T --> N["ocr_new: linecaster's own"]
    T --> O["ocr_original: delivered with the page"]
    T --> G["ground_truth: made by people"]
    N --> A[annotations: regions, lines, readings, tables, ...]
    N --> W[annotators: who added them]

A transcription is everything one source said about the page. A page can have several, side by side.

Each thing a source said is an annotation: a region, a line, the reading of a line, a table. An annotation names its annotator: the engine, the preset and the linecaster version that made it. Annotations are added, never changed.

items.title: Why it is built this way
items.text:
• You can always see who said what. If two engines disagree, both statements are in the record.
  • Nothing is lost. The raw answer of a model is kept next to what was parsed from it.
  • One format serves everything: OCR output, a library's delivered OCR and ground truth all use it, so they can be compared.

items.title: Where records are stored
items.text: A run writes its page records to OUT/pages/, as JSON Lines or Parquet. Other pipelines read them from there with --pages OUT/pages.

items.title: Renderings
items.text: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, Markdown, HTML and plain text are written from a page record when you ask for them (--files DIR --formats md,alto). They are renderings: outputs, never the stored truth.

items.title: Reference
items.text: The data model lists every field. Serialization describes each output format.

items.title: Components
items.text:
A component does one thing to a page: it finds the lines, reads them, or writes a file. Technically it is a datatrove PipelineStep. Components are named after what they do.

Step Components What they add reading input ImageFolderReader, ImageParquetReader, ManifestReader, PdfReader, PageRecordReader the page and its image layout LayoutDetector regions and their reading order lines LineDetector, LineAssigner lines, and which region each belongs to recognition LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer the text tables, formulas TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer table cells, LaTeX hierarchy HierarchyDetector heading levels paragraphs ParagraphBuilder paragraphs document DocumentComposer the document writing output PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter, PageFileWriter, ItemTextWriter, ... files

The components reference has a page for each.

items.title: Contracts
items.text:
Every component declares a contract: which parts of the page record it reads and which it adds. A LineRecognizer reads the image and the lines, and adds the text.

Before a run starts, linecaster checks the contracts of the whole pipeline. If a component reads something that no earlier component adds, the run does not start and the message says what is missing.

items.title: Writing a pipeline
items.text:
A Pipeline is a list of components:

from linecaster import Pipeline
from linecaster.components.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.components.lines import LineAssigner, LineDetector
from linecaster.components.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.components.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.components.writers import PageJsonlWriter

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3"),
    LineDetector("pp-ocrv6-medium-det"),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer("kraken-ppocrv6-medium"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
])
pipeline.check()        # the contracts, before anything runs
pipeline.run("out")     # on this machine

A model component takes a preset by its id. check() returns a plan of stages, and each stage is a list that any datatrove executor runs: pipeline.run() uses the local one. pipeline.to_dict() gives the pipeline as plain data, and Pipeline.from_dict() builds it again.

items.title: Pipeline templates and scripts
items.text:
Most people do not write the list themselves. A pipeline template builds a common kind of pipeline from command-line options, and a pipeline script in pipelines/ runs one template in its own environment:

Script Builds transcribe_modular.py layout, lines, a line recognizer, then hierarchy, paragraphs and the document transcribe_vlm.py a vision-language model per page, or per layout region transcribe_page.py a page engine per page harvest.py downloads page images from manifests bind.py item texts and item documents from page records convert.py converts page images import_transcriptions.py reads transcriptions in any format into page records score.py scores a run against a ground truth

A template has a slot for each step, and you fill a slot with a preset: --layout pp-doclayoutv3. No slot has a default. A recipe fills all slots at once.

items.title: Where a model runs
items.text:
A model component runs its engine in one of three places, its backend:

  • in the pipeline's own process,
  • behind linecaster serve, a server that hosts engines,
  • behind an OpenAI-compatible server such as vLLM, for vision-language models.

The result is the same in all three: a request carries one page, and a page's result depends only on that page.

items.title: Reference
items.text: Pipelines has the details: contracts, checks, failures, the run record, samples.

items.title: The text as read
items.text:
A page record stores each line's text exactly as the model or the source gave it. Linecaster does not even apply Unicode normalization to it. This stored text is the reading.

The reason is trust. A rule that looks safe can be wrong often. A rule that joins words divided at a line end, for example, also joins compounds that have a hyphen of their own. A silent change of this kind is an error that nobody sees.

items.title: Changes are named
items.text:
Every change of a text has a name and is a catalog entry, a normalization:

Normalization What it does nfc Unicode NFC long-s writes the long s (ſ) as s ligatures writes ligatures as their letters flow joins the lines of a paragraph into running text unicode-marks removes a hyphen where a word was divided at a line end

items.title: Strategies
items.text:
A strategy is an ordered list of normalizations. You name one when a text is written:

--text literal:txt                    # the text as read
--text latin-historic+flow:md         # a catalog strategy, then flow, as Markdown

literal is the strategy that changes nothing. There is no default strategy that changes text: if you name none, you get the text as read.

items.title: Scoring uses the same idea
items.text: When a run is compared with ground truth, both sides go through the same strategy first, called a lane. The lane diplomatic compares the texts almost as they are; reading ignores differences a reader would not notice.

items.title: Reference
items.text: The catalog reference lists the normalizations and strategies.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: What linecaster is made of and how a run fits together. Terms are the glossary's; contracts, the builder, failures and the run record are in pipelines, models, presets, recipes and engines in the catalog, the page record in the data model.

items.title: What linecaster is
items.text: An open, modular text-recognition suite for print and handwriting (OCR and HTR, old and new documents). It combines layout, line, text, table and formula recognizers with rule-based steps (typography, recomposition, composition) into reproducible datatrove pipelines that turn page images into text: the text as read, texts written by the transcription strategies a run names (normalized, flowed, dehyphenated only where a strategy says so), ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR on request. It also reads ground truth in any format into the same data model, writes it as page records and scores runs against it. It is a generalist tool: built on protocols (HTTP, S3/fsspec, OAI-PMH, IIIF), formats (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, HTML, Parquet, JSON Lines) and standards (METS/MODS, Unicode, CSS selectors, JSONPath), its code depends on no collection, site, institution or project; what a public source's markup means is declarative data in its catalog (conventions). Everything that produces text from images, and that reads, prepares and scores ground truth, lives here; evaluations and project pipelines (downstream projects) are built on top of it.

items.title: Packages
items.text:
Package Holds linecaster.data the data model: Item, Page, PageImage, annotation sets (AnnotationSet, Transcription) with their annotators (Annotator), raw outputs (RawOutput) and annotations, Text, rendering policies (RenderingPolicy), the measurements vocabulary linecaster.formats ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR out and in; HTML in (HtmlConverter, by HTML's semantics and a source's conventions); plain text in; DoclingDocuments in (the docling extra); the IIIF annotation page linecaster.document a page's or an item's document (Document, its blocks and their origins), built from transcriptions (DocumentBuilder) and written as HTML, Markdown, text and JSON linecaster.conventions conventions: their format (linecaster.conventions), layering, decisions, matchers (CSS selectors, JSONPath, regular expressions), coverage, and anchors into a source text by alignment linecaster.normalization the normalizations' rules on characters, LaTeX as text linecaster.text pure functions on text and on transcriptions: the rules of the hierarchy and paragraphs steps (hierarchy, paragraphs), scripts and writing directions, offsets through a change of text, a page's literal text linecaster.images the working image, plots linecaster.engines the engine API (linecaster.engines.api) and the built-in engines: the rule-based steps (hierarchy, paragraphs, document, image), the importers, the taggers and the single-region layout linecaster.core what every component builds on: Component, PageComponent, ModelComponent, RuleComponent, contracts, composites linecaster.components the components, one package per step or kind (components) linecaster.backends InProcess, Served, Chat linecaster.engines.chat one adapter per VLM family, ADAPTERS linecaster.evaluation the scorer: lanes, metrics, elements, benchmarks, evidence records, ground-truth tools linecaster.serving linecaster serve linecaster.net http(s) fetching (linecaster.net.http), the HTTP policy, the proxy pools (http) linecaster.net.broker the broker: leases, marks and worker slots in a shared folder; linecaster broker linecaster.pipeline Pipeline: a list of components checked, run and recorded as one linecaster.execution the builder, the pipelines' command line (options, wiring, allocation, run), executors, the run record, Jobs helpers, logs linecaster.templates the pipeline templates, one per pipeline script (pipelines) linecaster.catalog the catalog: its entries (normalizations and strategies among them), their schemas, the index, fetching pins linecaster.schemas every format by its schema id, and the JSON Schemas written from them linecaster.secrets EnvVar: a credential named by its environment variable linecaster.tracing tracing (OpenTelemetry) and linecaster traces linecaster.docs linecaster docs: the generated pages of the components and the catalog linecaster.testing test helpers: sample pages, fake engines (fake.<step>.v1, the page engine fake.recognition.page.v1), a fake chat server, a fake HTTP service, the conformance checks check_engine and check_component, the pytest markers

The packages are layers, and a module imports at its top only from its own layer or below (tests/test_import_rule.py):

errors, secrets ← data ← text, normalization, conventions, images ← formats ← document ← engines ← catalog ← evaluation ← net, backends ← core ← tracing ← components ← serving ← execution, pipeline ← templates ← schemas, docs, testing, cli

An import inside a function may reach up: the builder puts writers into a pipeline, and the catalog asks which engines are installed.

linecaster.data, formats, document, conventions, normalization, text, images, engines and evaluation load neither datatrove nor saturate, nor linecaster's components or runtime (tests/test_import_rule.py), so downstream projects can use the data model and the formats without the pipeline machinery. datatrove and saturate are required dependencies, datatrove with its io and s3 extras (s3:// paths work everywhere), and so is httpx (http(s):// through linecaster.net); engines, Ray and PDFium are not (engine packages and extras).

items.title: Components and backends
items.text:
A component is a datatrove PipelineStep with a contract; a pipeline is a list of components run by a datatrove executor. Each step or kind of component has a subpackage of linecaster.components (components has a page per component).

Model components (ModelComponent: LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer) each have a backend:

  • InProcess("pkg:Class", **kwargs) (or a preset ref) loads the engine in the worker, in warm_up() before the first page; a loaded engine is never pickled. In-process is always available and is the parity reference.
  • Served(endpoint, model=name) and Chat(preset, endpoint) (a VLM) stream pages through saturate (AdaptiveClient and through()): a window of pages in flight, adapted to the server's queue gauges and 429s; results passed on as they finish; secrets as EnvVar. The streaming exists once, in ModelComponent.

A page that failed a step carries doc.metadata["errors"], passes later model steps at once and goes to rejects/; more failures than the error budget fail the task (pipelines). Library code raises linecaster.errors, never SystemExit.

Rule components (RuleComponent: HierarchyDetector, ParagraphBuilder, DocumentComposer; and ImageConverter) run a built-in engine of a rule-based step in the pipeline's process, picked by a preset.

items.title: One page per request
items.text: A request carries one page; engines batch only within a page (kraken batches a page's lines). A page's result depends only on the page, never on what else is in flight, so runs are deterministic whatever the executor, the number of tasks or the backend.

items.title: Servers
items.text:
• linecaster serve hosts engines: stateless (no state between requests), one worker per model (several replicas per model were measured at +7–10 % and removed; NOTES.md), each with a bounded queue (--max-queue; a full queue answers 429 with Retry-After). Routes: POST /v1/linecaster/{step} (the image and the transcription so far in, the transcription with its part and the call's annotator added out; both linecaster.page/6 annotation sets), GET /v1/models, /health (status and protocol, the transcription format: linecaster.page/6) and vLLM-shaped /metrics (the gauges saturate reads). A Served client asks a server that already answers for its protocol when it warms up and refuses one that names another format or none (ServerError): both sides run the same linecaster version. Built-in engines are not served: they run in the pipeline's process.
  • VLMs run behind OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, SGLang, hosted endpoints): PageRecognizer and RegionRecognizer on the Chat backend, on /v1/chat/completions, served only. PageRecognizer also runs a page engine (an engine whose unit is the page) on the InProcess or Served backend: a vendor's package in the worker (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). A VLM is a catalog preset (engine chat.v1; its data: revision, prompt, sampling, serve block) plus an adapter in linecaster.engines.chat.ADAPTERS (its code: the request, the parsing; chat_model(<preset>)).
  • Servers inside a task (one GPU per HF Job): the server components EngineServer (linecaster serve) and VLMServer (vLLM or SGLang) start the server through saturate's Engine and go last in the pipeline, after the writer: datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. Each task starts its own servers. EngineServer(script=...) starts a pipeline script's serve with uv run --script. VendorServer starts the service a page preset's serve block names: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint (fetched and checked) for an engine package that attaches to vLLM, or a vendor image's entrypoint (with the weights downloaded to the folder it reads first), ready once its health URLs answer; it runs without the pipeline's environment, in the image's own. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the image's fixed ports: one service per machine.

items.title: Engines
items.text: An engine is a class with a versioned id (catalog). Engine packages live in engines/<engine>/, each its own package: linecaster-kraken, linecaster-paddlex, linecaster-tesseract, the page engines' linecaster-indra, linecaster-surya and linecaster-services (the clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's services), and the importer linecaster-mediawiki (MediaWiki wikitext through wikitextprocessor). An engine class (<Provider><Step>Engine) has engine_id (the entry point's name in linecaster.engines), step, capabilities (unit, produces), an Options model (its keyword arguments; a preset's weights besides), load() and __call__(image, transcription, **params) -> Transcription (the page image as an RGB array, or the image file's bytes for an engine whose image_input is "bytes", and the transcription so far, returned with its part added); an importer (step import) is called with a source document (SourceFile) and returns a new transcription. Engines with weights load exactly the pin (weights, linecaster.catalog.fetch). PaddleX's models load from the pinned snapshot (create_predictor(model_dir=...)); small-models-for-glam/kraken-blla-base (the BLLA base model of September 2026) is pinned in linecaster_kraken.models, and no engine uses it. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in linecaster's catalog. They import from linecaster only linecaster.data and the engine API (linecaster.engines.api: the Engine protocol, Capabilities, the weight helpers, and for importers Importer, conventions, HtmlConverter, SourceMap), have versions of their own with a range of linecaster releases, and their tests in engines/<engine>/tests/ (catalog).

items.title: Tests
items.text:
uv run pytest runs the core's tests, one after the other; uv run pytest -n auto (pytest-xdist, in the dev group) runs them on every core. Tests marked gpu or network (linecaster.testing.markers: gpu, network, slow; --strict-markers) skip where the device or the network is missing. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml, CPU only, no secrets, uv's cache kept between runs) runs uv sync --locked --all-extras (the extras' readers are tested and documented too), uv run pytest -n auto -m "not gpu and not network", linecaster catalog verify, linecaster docs and the site's strict build (the generated pages are not in git, so CI writes them and a broken reference in them fails the build). The docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) writes them too and publishes the site, built by Zensical, with mike (Zensical's fork) on the gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves (https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/): a release tag v<major>.<minor>.<patch> as version <major>.<minor>, with latest (the site's default) moved to it; nothing else is published. The engines' environments are too large for it (torch): their tests (engines/<engine>/tests/) and the PEP 723 test scripts (tests/test_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_line_recognizers.py) run locally. Every built-in engine and every public component passes the conformance checks of linecaster.testing (check_engine: the engine protocol; check_component: the contract against what the component does to sample pages, to_dict(), pickling, warm_up(), failed pages).

An engine package's tests run in an environment that has the engine: uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests. tests/test_engines_catalog.py holds kraken, PaddleX and Tesseract for the catalog's line-recognizer presets.

items.title: Recipe scripts
items.text:
A catalog recipe is YAML (src/linecaster/catalog/data/recipes/<id>.yaml: its presets and options; its hash in the index). Its environment and entry point is a uv script of its own, recipes/<id>.py: a PEP 723 block with linecaster[ray] and exactly the engine packages its presets need (recipe → presets → engines → packages: linecaster.catalog.code.recipe_packages), its lock, and a body that only calls linecaster.execution.run.recipe(__file__, "<id>"), which runs the recipe through its pipeline template with --recipe set. The pipeline scripts depend on no model choice (pipelines/transcribe_modular.py has PaddleX and Tesseract); the recipes bring theirs (recipes/squiddle.py: kraken and PaddleX).

The recipe scripts take linecaster and its engine packages from the main branch on GitHub, so a script runs from its URL with no checkout (uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py IMAGES OUT, hf jobs uv run <URL> ...) as well as from one (uv run recipes/squiddle.py, uv run launch.py squiddle). A run from the URL resolves the header afresh, and its run record names the script recipes/<id>.py (uv runs a temporary copy); a run from a checkout uses the script's lock, whose linecaster commit moves when it is relocked. Their HF Jobs need no --commit: jobs.dependencies installs linecaster from main with the lock's versions as constraints. With --endpoint the served engines need not be installed in the client's environment. To preview the site from a checkout: uv run linecaster docs, then uv run --group docs zensical serve.

items.title: Pipeline scripts
items.text:
There are no environment folders: a pipeline is a self-contained uv script in pipelines/ (a PEP 723 block, a <script>.py.lock next to it, uv run <script>) that runs one pipeline template with slots, one script per template, never one per machine. The template is library code, linecaster.templates.<name> (its options, engines, components, pipeline id and slots), so a downstream project's script can run it in its own environment with its own defaults (pipelines):

Script Pipeline id Does harvest.py harvest.v1 downloads page images (and a library's OCR, manifests) once into item folders, plus page records transcribe_modular.py transcribe_modular.v1 lines and a recognizer, optionally layout, tables, formulas, then post-processing; every step a preset the user picks; PaddleX and Tesseract, no kraken transcribe_vlm.py transcribe_vlm.v1 a VLM per page or per layout region transcribe_page.py transcribe_page.v1 a page engine per page, with the service its preset names bind.py bind.v1 item texts and item documents from page records convert.py convert.v1 page images converted to JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP by an image preset, on NVIDIA GPUs where the machine has them import_transcriptions.py import_transcriptions.v1 transcriptions in any format read into page records by an importer, a ground truth by default score.py score.v1 page records scored against a ground truth under a benchmark

linecaster.execution.run.main gives every pipeline the same command line: --on local|ray|hf-jobs, --backend in-process|served, --endpoint (a running server), serve (linecaster serve with the script's models), ray (Ray's CLI from the script's environment). Slots have no default presets: every slot is picked, or a recipe fills them (--recipe); launch.py runs a recipe or a page preset by name (catalog). Each script's page in the catalog's docs lists its slots and options.

Script environments: the repository is not a uv workspace (engine pins conflict). A script lists what it needs itself: linecaster with the extra every pipeline uses (ray for --on ray and ray start) and its engine packages (convert.py and the transcription scripts also nvimgcodec: NVIDIA's GPU codecs, used where the machine has a GPU); s3:// paths need no extra (the core installs datatrove's s3 extra, s3fs). A source is declared by the package that needs it, and uv lock applies the sources of path and git dependencies too: the kraken fork by linecaster-kraken, and stubs/opencv-contrib-python (the headless build of the version PaddleX pins; one cv2) by linecaster-paddlex. tests/test_scripts.py checks sources, locks and wheels for both machines (uv's required-environments does not work in scripts).

torch is never a dependency of the core. Only linecaster-kraken pins it (torch==2.14.0: kraken's upper bound is <=2.14, and the PyPI 2.14 wheels are the CUDA 13 build on Linux, aarch64 and x86_64), and only environments with linecaster-kraken are bound by that pin; the others take what their own dependencies allow. Each lock's torch is fixed in tests/test_scripts.py (TORCH), so it changes only on purpose:

Environment torch Why tests/test_engines_catalog.py 2.14.0 linecaster-kraken's pin pipelines/transcribe_page.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py 2.14.0 surya-ocr's (>=2.7,<3), not pinned: the version it was locked at tools/cuda_probe.py 2.14.0 its own pin: it probes the CUDA build of linecaster-kraken's torch on a Jobs host pipelines/transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, harvest.py, bind.py, convert.py, launch.py, tests/test_line_recognizers.py, linecaster's own (uv.lock) none no engine there needs it

items.title: Executors and Jobs
items.text:
--on Executor local datatrove's LocalPipelineExecutor ray RayGPUExecutor for stages with servers and single-stage pipelines with engines (each task holds one GPU; without --tasks, 4 tasks per GPU of the cluster, and one per GPU where each task starts a VLM's server, which takes minutes), RayExecutor (datatrove's RayPipelineExecutor) otherwise, on CPUs (an item stage, a harvest; extra [ray]); both stop the run at an error that is not the pages', fail a launch that left tasks unfinished, and check first that a live node can run a task hf-jobs JobsExecutor: datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor with JSON-lines logs; GPUJobsExecutor for multi-GPU flavors

datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor is experimental and dill-pickles the pipeline, so the launching machine and the Jobs run the same Python minor version (3.12). uv run outside a project drops [tool.uv.sources]: linecaster.execution.jobs.dependencies(commit, script) spells out a pipeline's dependencies and sources as URLs, the installed packages' own sources from the script's lock (the commit must be pushed), and pins every other package at the lock's version; each Job runs a uv script that carries the pins and the script's overrides, which uv run --with would ignore (pipelines).

Workers that share something beyond their tasks (a proxy list, whose proxies each worker may use only while no other does) agree through the broker, a folder any executor's workers can reach, on any storage datatrove supports: leases say who holds what, marks what is unavailable until when, and a worker is a slot of its machine that outlives the processes (on Ray every task is one) that take it over.

items.title: The run layout
items.text:
One job is one pipeline for one batch on one executor; resume is datatrove's, per task, so tasks stay small. A pipeline reads the previous folder and writes complete page records with one more part filled in:

Folder Holds originals/ the delivered images and files; never modified OUT/pages/ page records (PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter), bucketed by item id: a whole item in one file, so no joins OUT/rejects/ every page that carries errors (RejectWriter, put before the first writer by the builder): key, field, error, raw value OUT/logs/ datatrove's completion markers, logs and stats; OUT/logs/broker/, the broker by default OUT/traces/ the traces (tracing) OUT/run.yaml the run record (pipelines) OUT/sample.parquet the sample a run read, one row per page in sample order (pipelines) OUT/manifests/ the manifests a sample read (with sample.jsonl), or a harvest saved

PageRecordReader reads page records of linecaster's writers, fetching images again by URI (uri_map for local copies). Checks like PageValidator record on the page why it failed.

Readers follow datatrove's conventions (BaseDiskReader: data_folder, paths_file, glob_pattern, limit/skip per task; files distributed over tasks in turn, Parquet tables by rows in equal shards, linecaster.components.readers.tables, so a table needs no splitting): ImageFolderReader (image files), ImageParquetReader (an image column: bytes, an HF image struct or a path), ManifestReader (IIIF or METS, parsed by linecaster.formats.manifests, its files fetched through linecaster.net.http; a manifest, or a row of a Parquet item table, is an entry, so an item stays in one task; a IIIF Collection entry is its manifests, one level; existing_ocr fetches a library's OCR as a document media, which a TranscriptionConverter reads as ocr_original, the builder adding one when missing), PdfReader (PDF files as items, pages rendered with pypdfium2, extra [pypdfium2]) and PageRecordReader. Readers that fetch over http(s) request ahead in a window that grows while no request waits for the rate limits (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one fetcher per process and configuration, so the limits hold across a worker's tasks; ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader suggest a task count from their input (auto_tasks), which a pipeline without engines runs with (pipelines).

The workflow is harvest → transcribe → bind: pipelines/harvest.py downloads images (and OCR, manifests) once into item folders plus page records, the transcribe pipelines read those with --pages, pipelines/bind.py makes item texts and documents. An item's pages can land in different tasks; item-level steps are a second stage over item shards (--item-shards N writes OUT/pages/<shard>/<rank>, pipelines/bind.py reads whole shards), as datatrove's own multi-stage pipelines read per-bucket folders (pipelines).

items.title: Broker
items.text:
The broker is a shared folder through which workers across tasks, runs and machines agree on who uses which shared resource and what is unavailable until when.
