An item is what the input names: it gives the item's id (item_id) and its pages' order (sequence). linecaster assumes nothing about what an item is or how its pages came about: a scanned book, an issue, a PDF, a folder of images. page_id is <item_id>_<sequence:04d> unless the source has stable page ids of its own; a page id never contains #.

Page field Holds page_id, item_id, sequence the page's ids and its place in the item image its PageImage transcriptions name → Transcription: ocr_new (linecaster's), ocr_original (the library's own), ground_truth, <source> annotations name → AnnotationSet: sets without text (a layout of its own, an evaluation's markings) metadata the source's page metadata, namespaced keys (<ns>__<field>) measurements the page's time in the runs that worked on it: seconds, datetime (below)

PageImage is unchanged from linecaster.page/2: uri, format, width, height, sha256 (of the stored bytes), pixels_sha256 (of the decoded pixels), source_width, source_height and scale (for a derivative of a master), decoder, extra.

items.title: A page in a pipeline
items.text:
A page is one datatrove Document: id is the page id, text the primary transcription's text (Transcription.text, under the default policy), media[0] the image bytes, metadata["page"] the page record.

A page's time in the run is on its record, Page.measurements: seconds, the wall time from when the reader handed the page over to when it reached the first block that writes pages, binds or serves (the blocks' times between, waiting in served windows and queues included), and datetime, when the reader handed it over (ISO 8601, UTC). linecaster.core.observers.PageTiming sets them on every page stage that writes pages; a record read from an earlier run adds the new run's time to the one it carries and keeps the first datetime. Each annotator's own time is in its measurements.

items.title: Annotation sets
items.text:
An annotation set (AnnotationSet) is everything one source said about one page: the annotators that worked on it, their raw outputs, and their annotations. A transcription (Transcription, a subclass) is an annotation set that also holds text: readings, tables, formulas, paragraphs, edits. A page has any number of each, by name.

Field Holds In source where the set comes from (Source, below) both annotators who worked on it, in the order they ran (Annotator) both outputs their raw outputs, one per request (RawOutput) both regions Regions: the layout's zones both ranges Ranges, DocumentRanges and Paragraphs: the logical units, their pieces on this page both classifications Classifications: role, production, the annotator's own label, heading level, language, status, ... both descriptions Descriptions: what an annotator wrote about a zone that is not on the page both links Links: cross-references (caption of, note of) both orders ReadingOrders: one per annotator that ordered the page both lines Lines: the line zones, each with its Reading Transcription tables Tables: a region's table structure Transcription formulas Formulas: a region's formula Transcription edits Edits: the source's corrected, expanded, regularized or joined forms of a reading, a word, a cell or a span Transcription

Derived, not stored: text (the set rendered under a policy), confidence (reading confidences weighted by length), objects (regions in the shape of a Hugging Face objects column).

One of each per target and set: a line has at most one reading, a region at most one table and one formula in a set. A second recognizer of the same lines writes a transcription of its own; a second classifier of the same scheme adds a classification next to the first, and the policy's precedence says whose counts.

items.title: Source
items.text: Field Holds kind produced (made by linecaster's annotators), converted (read from a delivered file), ground_truth (a reference transcription, made or checked by people) format for converted sets and ground truth: alto, page, hocr, docling, text, markdown, or an evaluation's own name uri, sha256 the delivered file and its hash dataset, record for ground truth and converted sets from a dataset: repo@revision, and the row or file the set was read from revision the revision of the source text that the zones' anchors refer to (a wiki page's revision id, a commit) image_sha256, image_width, image_height the image the set's coordinates refer to scale the factors ([sx, sy]) a set was scaled by onto this image (AnnotationSet.scaled) normalized for a ground truth: the normalizations its transcription already embodies (catalog ids, from its conventions' transcription: long-s where it writes ſ as s); scoring warns where a lane does not apply one

items.title: Annotators and raw output
items.text:
An annotator (Annotator) is one thing that worked on a set: a model step, a rule-based step, a delivered file, or people. Annotations name it by its index in annotators.

Field Holds kind model, rule, file, human step the catalog step: layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, hierarchy, paragraphs, assignment, ordering, import, ...; for a file or people: transcription name the model (kraken-ppocrv6-medium); for a rule, what ran (unicodedata, the engine's id); for people, the group (proofreaders) engine, revision the engine's code id, the model's revision preset, preset_sha256, recipe, recipe_sha256 the preset and recipe it ran as, and their hashes conventions, conventions_sha256 an importer's: the conventions it applied, resolved (the chain, mediawiki>enwikisource), and the hash of what their rules do linecaster the linecaster that added the annotator (producer(): version and commit) backend in-process, or served with the server's address run the run that produced the annotator's work (its run id, RunRecord.run_id); None for files and people settings what decided the output besides the preset: the engine's options, a VLM's prompt and sampling; for people, their review: review (transcribed, proofread, validated, or the source's own word) measurements numbers of this page, in the measurements vocabulary (below)

A raw output (RawOutput) is one request's answer, verbatim:

Field Holds annotator its annotator content the completion as the model wrote it, or an engine's native result (JSON) format text, json, or the engine's own name pass_ which pass of the page it is (1, 2 after a repair pass); stored as pass kept whether the annotations were parsed from it (a repair pass keeps one) settings what this request was sent with when it differs from the annotator's: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, preset image_size the size of the image sent, when it is not the page image's finish_reason, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens as the server reported them error the request's error, when it failed

Engines that answer in-process with Python objects (a detector's boxes) store no raw output: their annotations are the output, and their raw form is not kept beyond them.

items.title: Measurements
items.text:
linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS is the vocabulary of Annotator.measurements and Page.measurements, key → meaning; linecaster code writes no other key. Values vary from run to run.

Key Meaning seconds wall time of the step on the page (the engine's call, in-process or in the server); on the page record, the page's time in the run datetime when the step started on the page, ISO 8601 in UTC; on the page record, when its reader handed it over device the device the step ran on request_seconds a served step: from its request being built to its (last) answer queue_seconds, decode_seconds a step served by linecaster serve: the wait in the server's queue, the decoding of the page image decoder what decoded the page image the step read (linecaster.images.pixels) prompt_tokens, completion_tokens a VLM's tokens, summed over the page's requests (each request's are on its raw output) finish_reason the kept request's: stop, length, repetition, content_filter, tool_calls, function_call, abort (FINISH_REASONS), or None regions, failed regions sent to a VLM one by one, and those whose request failed tables, formulas table regions given a structure, formula regions read changed strings a normalization changed body_size, leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped typography: the body type size in pixels, headings given a level, section headers classified as text, headlines split off, drop capitals joined, page numbers classified removed paragraphs, continuations, marks_removed, marks_kept recomposition: paragraphs made, continued, division marks removed, hyphens kept

items.title: Annotations
items.text:
Every annotation has an annotator and may name the raw output it was parsed from, what it was derived from, and a confidence:

Annotation field Holds annotator the index of its annotator in the set output the index of the raw output it was parsed from, if any derived_from references to what it was made from (PROV's wasDerivedFrom): a paragraph's lines, an edit's source, a classification's evidence confidence the annotator's confidence, 0 to 1, if it gave one <ns>__<field> extension fields, namespaced: an adapter's or a step's own (lighton__continuation, typography__reason), never shared vocabulary Class Motivation Target Is Region segmenting the page a zone found by a layout step Line segmenting the page a zone found by a line step Reading transcribing its line a line's text, with words and glyphs Table transcribing a region a region's table structure Formula transcribing a region a region's formula, as LaTeX Classification classifying a zone, a range, a reading span, the page one value of one scheme Description describing a zone text about the zone that is not on the page Edit editing a reading, a word, a cell, a paragraph, a span another form of the target's text Link linking two references a cross-reference ReadingOrder ordering the page an order of the page's regions and lines Range, DocumentRange, Paragraph structuring zones, spans, ranges a logical unit: its piece on this page

The motivation is the class's, not a stored field. IIIF exports transcribing as supplementing (IIIF's word for a transcription), the others as W3C Web Annotation motivations (classifying, describing, editing, linking) or linecaster's own (segmenting, ordering, structuring).

items.title: Zones
items.text:
A zone (Zone) is a place on the page image an annotator found; Region and Line are zones. Geometry without an annotator of its own (a word, a glyph, a cell) is a shape (Shape).

Field Holds In box [x, y, width, height] in pixels of the page image, or None (no geometry: a text-only answer, a ground truth without boxes) Shape polygon [[x, y], ...] as the annotator gave it, or None Shape id unique within the page and set (r3, l17); never contains #, / or [ Zone parent the zone it lies in (a running head's title and page number inside the running head) Zone anchor where its text comes from in the source text it was read from: {start, end}, characters of the source at Source.revision; set by importers, None for zones found on the image Zone label the annotator's own label (PP-DocLayout's aside_text, LightOn's page_number), verbatim Region region the region the line belongs to: set once, by the step that assigned it Line baseline [[x, y], ...] Line reading the line's Reading, None until a recognizer ran Line

Lines are found across the whole page and assigned to regions later; zones are therefore flat lists with stable ids, and a line names its region, set once by the step that assigned it. A later step that moves a line into another region (typography splitting a headline off) adds a part_of link; the line's region is the latest part_of target, else Line.region (Transcription.region_of). A line's confidence is its detection score; its reading's is the recognizer's.

items.title: Readings, words and glyphs
items.text:
A reading (Reading) is what a recognizer read on one line: text (exactly as the engine produced it, "" for a line read as empty), alternatives, words, formatting, and its own annotator, raw output and confidence. A Word (Shape) has text, confidence, hyphen (it ends in a division mark), alternatives, formatting and glyphs, and an id only where its source gave one other than <line>_w<n>; a Glyph (Shape) text and confidence. Engines with character positions keep them as glyphs.

Formatting says how characters are set: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, script (baseline, sub, super); on a word, it covers the word; on a reading, each Formatting has a charspan ([start, end] in the reading's text).

items.title: Tables and formulas
items.text:
A Table transcribes a region (target), stored lean: num_rows, num_cols, cells, and html when the model wrote the table as HTML. A Cell (Shape) has start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col (offsets, end exclusive), text, column_header, row_header, row_section. Spans and the grid are not stored (they follow from the offsets). A chart's data, when a model gives it, is a Table too, on the chart's region.

A Formula transcribes a region as latex; source is the LaTeX as the source wrote it, where the reading's differs (a wiki's formula as its software normalizes it).

items.title: Classifications
items.text:
A Classification gives one target one value in one scheme. Several annotators may classify the same target in the same scheme (the layout model and the typography rules); none overwrites another.

Scheme Values Typical annotator role what the content is (content roles) layout, typography, a grounding VLM, a ground truth production how it was made: printed, typewritten, handwritten, stamped, born_digital layout, a ground truth heading_level 1, 2, ... (1 the highest below the title) typography language a BCP 47 tag (well-formed), on the page (""), a zone, a word or a span recognition, a ground truth, an importer script an ISO 15924 code (Latn, Arab, Jpan), on the page, a zone, a word or a span a ground truth, an importer direction the writing direction: horizontal-lr, horizontal-rl (right to left), vertical-rl (columns, right to left: Chinese, Japanese, Korean set vertically), vertical-lr (columns, left to right: Mongolian) a ground truth, an importer, a layout step status illegible, gap (text left out), suppressed, duplicate, removed; a status may say why (reason, below) a ground truth, typography, an importer picture_class what a picture shows (photograph, map, stamp, signature, music, ...) a picture classifier code_language the programming language of a code region a VLM degraded a property, yes or no: the content is harder to read than in a clean scan, because of the image's condition a model tagger tiny a property, yes or no: the content is printed noticeably smaller than the page's body text the geometry tagger, a model tagger rotated a property, yes or no: the content's text is turned or tilted by about 5 degrees or more the geometry tagger, a model tagger multi_column a property, yes or no: the content sits inside one column of a page laid out in columns the geometry tagger, a model tagger form a property, yes or no: the content is a field to fill in or a box to tick, or belongs to one a model tagger

The annotator's own label is the region's label, not a classification; the mapping from it to a role is catalog data per engine (each engine's label map), applied by the annotator that made the region.

Vocabularies. What each value of a closed scheme means is its vocabulary, a catalog entry (vocabularies/<scheme>.yaml, catalog): every value with its definition, what counts and what does not. The vocabularies of role, status (with the reasons), production and the property schemes list exactly the data model's values (ROLES, STATUSES, REASONS, yes and no), which linecaster catalog verify checks. The definitions are the one text the docs, the taggers and the people who review their answers share: a model tagger's questions are generated from them.

Property schemes (linecaster.data.PROPERTIES: degraded, tiny, rotated, multi_column, form) say what content is like, as yes or no (Transcription.classify refuses another value); a vocabulary's answers name the two answers a model is asked for after the property (degraded, not_degraded). They are a tagger's, an engine of the tagging step (linecaster.engines.tagging), on the narrowest target the property is true of (a line, a region, the page), each with its evidence: the geometry tagger's measurements, or a panel of models' answers, as the annotator's raw outputs, which the classification names (output). Where the evidence does not decide, nothing is recorded: a property is never guessed into a record, and None (no classification) is not no.

Writing systems. language, script and direction are checked where they are made (linecaster.data.writing: a well-formed BCP 47 tag, a four-letter ISO 15924 code, one of the four directions) and read through what encloses a target: Transcription.language(target), .script(target) and .direction(target) take the value recorded on a span or word, else on its line, else on the line's region and the regions it lies in, else on the page (""); None where nothing records one. A value is never guessed into a record: a source or a step records it, and linecaster.text.scripts infers a text's script (dominant_script, with ISO 15924's Jpan and Kore for the combinations) or direction (first_strong_direction, the Unicode bidirectional algorithm's paragraph level) where a caller asks. What orders zones follows the direction (linecaster.data.geometry.frames: XY-cut, XY-Cut++, the line assigner's rows, unordered regions slotted in, the recomposition's margins, drop capitals): boxes are seen in the direction's frame, mirrored for horizontal-rl and turned for the vertical directions, so that right-to-left text reads from the right and vertical text by columns, from the right for vertical-rl and from the left for vertical-lr. The direction is a block's or engine's option where it has one, else the one recorded for the region or page; without either, horizontal-lr.

A status classification's reason says why something present in a source is no text of the page (linecaster.data.REASONS): hidden (not seen and taking no space), invisible (not seen but taking its space), generated (the source's software or markup draws it), editorial (the source's editors wrote it), error (a message of the source's software), metadata (markup that is no content), apparatus (the source's notation for something the page prints differently), elsewhere (printed text that belongs to another page or place), layout (markup that only arranges the page). An importer keeps such text, where its conventions say so, as a region with status removed and its reason, which no rendering takes.

items.title: Descriptions
items.text: A Description is text an annotator wrote about a zone that is not printed on the page (a VLM's description of a figure, chart data it read off, an editor's note): target, kind (description, data, note), text, format (text, markdown, html).

items.title: Edits
items.text:
An Edit is another form of a target's text; the target's own text stays. target (a reading, a word, a cell, a paragraph, a span of one), kind, text:

kind Is corrected an editor's correction of what is printed (a misprint); the reading keeps the printed form joined half of a word the source marks as divided across lines or pages (Wikisource's {{hws}}/{{hwe}}, ALTO's SUBS_CONTENT): the edit's target is the half's span, its text the whole word expanded, regularized abbreviations expanded, spelling regularized, as the source states them

Every edit is the source's: linecaster's steps write none (since linecaster.page/5; the nfc and normalized edits of page/4 are dropped when a record is read). A document carries them as spans of its literal text, and a strategy applies them when it names them: editors-corrections, editors-expansions, editors-regularizations, divided-words (the halves paired in reading order and written whole where the second stands).

items.title: Links
items.text: A Link is a cross-reference: kind, source, target. Kinds: caption_of, note_of (a footnote and its mark, source the note, target the mark's span), continues (source continues target: a paragraph or footnote from an earlier column or page), runs_into (source runs on into target), refers_to, part_of (a line in another region than the one it was assigned to; a drop capital's region, part of the line it begins: a document writes its letter at that line's start).

items.title: Reading orders
items.text:
A ReadingOrder orders the page: regions (region ids in reading order), lines (line ids in reading order) and rows (parallel to lines: each line's visual row within its region). An order of regions alone leaves lines empty. A layout model that learned an order, the line assigner, typography, XY-Cut++ and a ground truth each add their own; the latest counts unless the policy's precedence says otherwise.

Processing order is separate: the list order of lines (regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region), in which a recognizer processes and batches lines.

items.title: Ranges
items.text:
A range (Range) is a logical unit of content: a document, a chapter, a section, an article, a list, a paragraph. A page stores only the piece of a range that lies on it, under the range's id; pieces with the same id on other pages of the item are the same range, and the item record joins them in page order. Paragraphs are the exception: their ids are page-local, and a paragraph continued in the next column or on the next page is two paragraphs joined by links (runs_into, continues).

Field Holds id unique within the item (paragraphs: within the page, <region id>_p<n>); never contains #, / or [ kind chapter, section, list, ordered_list, inline, picture_area, form_area, key_value_area, comment_section, sheet, slide, document, article, work, paragraph, poem, stanza parent the range it is part of parts the zones, spans and ranges of this piece, in order title the range's title, if known

A document range (DocumentRange, kind document) is a document within or across items: an item holds one document unless ranges say otherwise. A paragraph (Paragraph, kind paragraph) is the bottom range of running text: structure only, no text of its own (since linecaster.page/5): rows (ParagraphRow: lines, the ids of every line on the visual row, empty ones too) and decisions (Decision: kind, reason, row; the vocabulary DECISIONS). Its text is its lines' readings, row by row; a strategy writes it (flow joins the rows).

Decision kind Reasons paragraph_break indent, gap, short_row continuation division_mark, end_margin

items.title: References
items.text:
A reference (Ref) names something in the same set:

Form Names <id> a zone or a range piece on this page <line>/<n>, <line>/<n>/<m> word n of the line's reading, glyph m of that word <region>/r<row>c<col> the cell of the region's table that starts at that row and column <ref>[<start>:<end>] characters start to end (end exclusive) of the text the reference names "" the page <page_id>#<ref> something on another page of the item

items.title: Content roles
items.text:
The role scheme's vocabulary, the content roles, is PAGE-XML's region types, with names of linecaster's own where PAGE has no word. Each role has a region label, the coarser word layout models and page files use (a layout preset maps its model's labels onto them), and a default layer:

Role PAGE-XML Region label Default layer paragraph paragraph text body heading heading section_header body title (heading) title body caption caption caption body list_item (paragraph) list_item body list_label list-label list_item body toc_entry TOC-entry document_index body footnote footnote footnote body footnote_continued footnote-continued footnote body endnote endnote footnote body marginalia marginalia text body drop_capital drop-capital text body credit credit text body floating floating text body reference (paragraph) reference body code (other) code body table TableRegion table body formula MathsRegion formula body chemistry ChemRegion formula body music MusicRegion picture body picture ImageRegion, GraphicRegion, LineDrawingRegion picture body chart ChartRegion chart body map MapRegion picture body advert AdvertRegion picture body form (other) form body key_value (other) key_value_region body header header page_header furniture footer footer page_footer furniture page_number page-number page_header, page_footer furniture catch_word catch-word page_footer furniture signature_mark signature-mark page_footer furniture separator SeparatorRegion picture none noise NoiseRegion picture none other other text body

Each role's definition, what counts as it and what does not, is in the role vocabulary. A content role says what the content is, not where it is rendered: the layers in the last column are the default policy's. A page number's region label depends on where it is: page_header when its centre lies in the top 15 % of the page (or without a box), else page_footer. A label that is neither a role nor a region label (a model's own) is kept as its own role and written as it is.

items.title: Rendering
items.text:
A rendering policy (RenderingPolicy, a catalog entry policy) decides which annotations go into which layer of a rendering: body, furniture (running heads and feet, page numbers), background, invisible, notes, plus metadata (kept out of the text, written to the rendering's metadata) and none.

RenderingPolicy field Holds id as a preset's rules RenderingRules, the first that matches wins: role, production, status, motivation (each None: any) → to (a layer, metadata or none) precedence whose annotations count where several annotators gave one of a kind: an ordered list of steps or annotator names, per scheme (role: [typography, layout]), for reading orders (order: [layout, ordering]) and ranges tables, markdown what counts as a table when written out (TableRules); the Markdown a rendering writes (MarkdownRules)

The default policy, page-layers, gives every role its default layer, status suppressed, duplicate and removed → none, descriptions → metadata; without precedence the latest annotator's classifications count (typography's over the layout's). page-layers-described puts descriptions (motivation describing) in the body instead: the texts, the elements and the document then have each one after its region (a picture without lines in its place in the reading order; the page's last), a document as a paragraph block with the role description (RenderingPolicy.described). A policy decides layers, never text. A run names its policy (--policy); without one it uses the default, and the run record says which.

Renderings are made from a set under a policy and are not stored: the document (below), ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, the IIIF annotation page, and the texts.

items.title: The document (linecaster.document)
items.text:
A page's or an item's document (Document, linecaster.document/2) is what a reader reads, in reading order: its pages and its blocks. A block (Block) is one unit of the rendering, of a kind made from its region's content role: title, heading (with its level), paragraph, list_item, caption, footnote, toc_entry, reference, code, page_header, page_footer, formula (its LaTeX the text), table (its grid: size and cells) or picture (its file and the text read inside it). Each block has its content role, the layer the policy put it in, its text (literal: the readings as read, rows separated by \n; wraps: the positions of the \n that are breaks of the layout, which flow joins) with formatting, languages, inline formulas and the source's edits over spans of it (an edit span: edit, edit_text; a span's language and direction where they are not its block's), its language and direction where they are not the document's, the section it is in (the heading block that opens it, with sections), and an Origin per piece: the page, the region and lines it comes from, its box on the page image (clamped to the page; none without geometry) and the characters of the block's text it gives. The document's language and direction are its pages' where every page records the same one; like a block's, they are only what the transcriptions record (Transcription.language, .direction), never inferred, and absent from the JSON where nothing records one.

DocumentBuilder makes it (composition), literal (strategy: literal): one block per region as laid out (one row per visual row: lines share a row when the order says so and their boxes overlap), or per paragraph of a recomposition (every break between its rows a wrap); a paragraph or region that continues another (its continues link, on the same or an earlier page of the item) is one block with it, on a new row (a wrap, unless a part has several rows and the first does not end in a division mark: verse). A drop capital (part_of its line) is written at its line's start. linecaster.document.strategy.apply(document, strategy) writes a strategy's document from it (strategy names it); linecaster.document writes either as HTML (HTML5 with DPUB-ARIA roles for notes and page furniture), Markdown (by the policy's Markdown rules: a wrap a plain newline, another row break a hard break, a row that would start a Markdown block escaped), text and JSON; the JSON is the complete document and reads back (from_json; a document/1 file is read as it is, its strategy not stated).

items.title: Texts and transcription strategies
items.text: A text is a document written by a transcription strategy in a format: <strategy>:<format> (literal:txt, latin-historic+unicode-marks+flow:md). literal changes nothing; a strategy of the catalog (linecaster.catalog: normalizations and strategies) applies its normalizations in order: rules on characters (linecaster.normalization.rules: nfc, long-s, ligatures, r-rotunda, superscript-e, ...) to every block's text and cell, and rules on the document: the source's edits, divided-words, unicode-marks (division marks resolved by squiddleocr's rule, the document's words as the lexicon), flow (the wraps joined: by a space, or none where Unicode's line breaking joins the words; a row that still ends in a division mark joined without a space, the mark kept). Spans, wraps and origins move with the text they cover. Nothing is written unless a run names it: by default the document as JSON, literal. The scope (full page or body only) is the layer choice when it is written (furniture).

items.title: Steps and what they add
items.text:
Step Adds layout regions, role and production classifications (by the engine's label map), a reading order if the model learned one lines lines (geometry only) assignment each line's region recognition readings (words, glyphs, formatting), raw outputs; language, script classifications tables, formulas tables, formulas typography role and heading_level classifications (a demoted heading is classified paragraph again, by typography), status removed for what it drops, a part_of link from a drop capital's region to the line it begins, a split-off headline as a region with parent and part_of links, a new reading order ordering a reading order (XY-cut, XY-Cut++) tagging classifications in property schemes (and other closed schemes), each naming the raw output that holds its evidence: the geometry tagger's measurements, or every panel member's answer recomposition paragraphs (rows and decisions, no text) and their runs_into and continues links a VLM page step regions, lines with readings, tables, formulas, descriptions, classifications, raw outputs a ground-truth import everything its source has, source.kind ground_truth, an annotator of kind human or file

Composition (the DocumentComposer) adds nothing: it renders the set as a document (linecaster.document), which travels with the datatrove document (doc.metadata["document"]) to the writers and is not stored in the page record.

Nothing is overwritten: an engine call appends one annotator and adds annotations; it changes none that was there (setting a line's region or reading from None aside). The conformance checks (linecaster.testing.check_engine, check_component) check it.

items.title: Geometry
items.text: Every box is [x, y, width, height] in pixels of the page image; polygons and baselines are lists of [x, y] points exactly as the annotator gave them. Algorithms derive boxes from the polygon (geometry.bbox_of). AnnotationSet.scaled(sx, sy) moves every coordinate to another image size and records the factors in source.scale.

items.title: Item records (linecaster.core.item)
items.text: An item travels as one datatrove Document: id is the item id, metadata["item"] the item record, {"item_id": ..., "pages": [...]}, its page records (as JSON-compatible dicts) in order (sequence, then page id), without the image bytes. The ItemAssembler makes it from a page stream; the item-unit blocks add to the page records inside it (ParagraphBuilder(unit="item"): paragraphs whose pieces span pages), and DocumentComposer(unit="item") adds the item's document next to it; the renderers join a range's pieces across pages; the ItemSplitter passes the pages on again, each with what the item-level blocks added.

items.title: Mappings
items.text:
linecaster IIIF Presentation 3 / W3C Web Annotation PAGE-XML PROV Item Manifest (a METS file group) Entity Page Canvas Page Entity AnnotationSet, Transcription AnnotationPage PcGts Collection Annotator creator / generator (Software, Person) Metadata/MetadataItem Agent, Activity RawOutput (none; a linecaster extension) (none) Entity, wasGeneratedBy Annotation Annotation (an element) Entity derived_from (extension) (none) wasDerivedFrom Zone.box, polygon FragmentSelector xywh=, SvgSelector Coords Region + role Annotation, motivation classifying TextRegion@type, other regions Line, Reading Annotation, motivation supplementing, textGranularity line TextLine, TextEquiv Word, Glyph textGranularity word, glyph Word, Glyph Edit motivation editing TextEquiv@index wasRevisionOf Classification motivation classifying @type, @production, TextStyle Description motivation describing (none) Link motivation linking Relations ReadingOrder Range of canvases' annotations ReadingOrder Range, DocumentRange Range (none) Paragraph Annotation, textGranularity paragraph (TextRegion of type paragraph) Table, Cell (body as HTML) TableRegion, TableCell

The IIIF export (linecaster.formats.iiif.to_annotation_page) writes one AnnotationPage per set and page: regions (classifying, the content role as the body), readings and words (supplementing, IIIF's motivation for a transcription, with the text granularity extension's textGranularity), edits (editing) and descriptions (describing), each targeting the canvas with a media fragment (#xywh=), with its annotator as generator (creator for people). It is validated against the IIIF Presentation 3 JSON Schema in the tests.

items.title: From linecaster.page/2
items.text:
PageRecordReader upgrades a page/2 record when it reads one (linecaster.data.upgrade.page_2_to_3). What page/2 had already lost cannot come back: text before the unicode step, labels before typography, regions typography dropped beyond extra["retyper_dropped"]. Every field:

page/2 page/3 Page.page_id, item_id, sequence, image, metadata, measurements the same Page.transcriptions the same, each upgraded PageImage.uri, format, width, height, sha256, pixels_sha256, source_width, source_height, scale, decoder, extra the same Transcription.regions regions Region.id Region.id Region.label a role classification (region label → role), by the layout annotator; by typography where its step changed it Region.raw_label Region.label Region.polygon Region.polygon Region.bbox Region.box Region.score Region.confidence Region.reading_order the layout annotator's ReadingOrder Region.heading_level a heading_level classification Region.extra["table"] a Table Region.extra["formula"] a Formula Region.extra["generated"] a Description Region.extra (other keys) extension fields page2__<key> Transcription.lines lines Line.id Line.id Line.region_id Line.region Line.reading_order, Line.row the ReadingOrder's lines and rows Line.bbox, polygon, baseline Line.box, polygon, baseline Line.score Line.confidence Line.text, confidence, alternatives, words Line.reading: text, confidence, alternatives, words Line.normalized dropped (page/5 stores no derived text) Line.extra extension fields page2__<key> Word.id None where it was <line>_w<n> (its index in the reading); kept otherwise Word.text, confidence, hyphen, alternatives the same Word.bbox Word.box Word.extra extension fields page2__<key> Transcription.paragraphs Paragraph ranges Paragraph.id, region_id Paragraph.id, parts Paragraph.rows rows ParagraphRow.lines the same ParagraphRow.start, end dropped (page/5) Paragraph.text, decisions decisions (page/5: no text, no mark decisions) Paragraph.normalized dropped (page/5) Paragraph.continues, continues_from runs_into and continues links ParagraphRef.id, page_id the links' target: <id> or <page_id>#<id> Decision.kind, reason, row, separator kind, reason, row (page/5) Paragraph.extra extension fields page2__<key> Transcription.docling not stored: rendered on demand Transcription.language a language classification on the page Transcription.steps annotators StepInfo.step, name, engine, revision, preset, preset_sha256, recipe, recipe_sha256, backend, settings, measurements the same Annotator fields; kind from the step Transcription.source source Source.kind, format, uri, image_sha256, image_width, image_height the same Source.extra["scale"] Source.scale Source.extra (other keys) extension fields page2__<key> Transcription.extra["raw"], ["passes"], ["kept"], ["finish_reason"] outputs Transcription.extra["retyper_dropped"] the regions again, with one line holding their text, classified status removed by typography Transcription.extra (other keys) extension fields page2__<key>

items.title: From linecaster.page/4
items.text: A page/4 record is upgraded when it is read (linecaster.data.upgrade.page_4_to_5), and so is every older one, through page/4: the derived text goes, the source's stays. Dropped: the nfc and normalized edits, Paragraph.text, ParagraphRow.charspan, the decisions on division marks (mark_removed, hyphen_kept) and Decision.separator. A drop capital's whole-line joined edit (typography's) becomes a part_of link from its region to the line, and the removed status typography gave the region goes. The source's edits (corrected, expanded, regularized, a divided word's halves) stay as they were.

items.title: Evaluation
items.text:
linecaster scores transcriptions against ground truths and writes the result as evidence. It ships the scorer, the lanes (comparison strategies of the catalog), the score pipeline and the formats (linecaster.benchmark/2, linecaster.score/1, linecaster.evidence/3); it ships no benchmark and no evidence: those live with the evaluation that made them (catalog). Any two evidence records with the same benchmark, policy, output strategy, lanes (by hash), unit, word and element metrics are comparable, whatever model, pipeline or machine produced the runs they measure.

ground truth ──import──► transcription (source.kind ground_truth) ─┐
                                                                   ├─ render (one policy, one output strategy) ─ elements ─ lanes ─ count ─► score records ─ aggregate ─► evidence
run's page records ─────► transcription (ocr_new) ─────────────────┘
                                                                   └─ export ─► an external benchmark's files ─► its own evaluation

items.title: Ground truth, benchmarks and evaluations
items.text:
What Is Where it lives a source transcriptions made or checked by people, in their own format (PAGE-XML, TEI, wikitext, a benchmark's JSON) the source conventions what a public source's markup means, declaratively (linecaster.conventions) linecaster's catalog page records the neutral exchange format: a ground truth imported into linecaster's data model, or a run's output the dataset (linecaster ground-truth publish), the run rendering policy, output strategy, lanes how both sides are rendered, written and compared linecaster's catalog the scorer page and element metrics, strata, aggregation linecaster (linecaster.evaluation) a benchmark a definition: a ground truth, its page set, the policy, lanes, metrics (linecaster.benchmark/2; linecaster benchmark init) the evaluation an evaluation the runs scored under a benchmark, their score records and evidence the evaluation's own repository an external benchmark another project's ground-truth format, scorer and dataset (OmniDocBench) that project; linecaster imports its ground truth and exports to it

linecaster holds the tools and the formats; ground truths, benchmarks and evidence are data and live elsewhere. An external benchmark's code never runs inside linecaster: its ground truth is read by an importer, so linecaster's scorer can score models on its pages, and a ground truth and a run are written as its files by an exporter, so its own evaluation scores them unchanged (export).

Scoring is linecaster.evaluation (import-light, like linecaster.data); its alignment needs the extra linecaster[rapidfuzz].

items.title: Ground truth
items.text:
A ground truth is a transcription like any other, stored in the page record under its name (ground_truth, or the dataset's), with source.kind = "ground_truth", source.dataset (repo@revision), source.record (the row or file it came from) and source.sha256. Its annotator is of kind human (people transcribed or checked it; their review in settings.review: transcribed, proofread, validated, or the source's own word) or file (a delivered file whose making is unknown). It holds what its source has and no more: roles, boxes, reading order, notes, continuations, corrections, illegible spans, each as the data model defines them, and, in source.normalized, the normalizations its transcription already embodies (from its conventions' transcription: a source that writes ſ as s embodies long-s).

Ground truth is read by importers, the engines of the import step, which TranscriptionImporter runs and pipelines/import_transcriptions.py runs over a source's documents into page records: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, plain text, HTML and DoclingDocuments (the docling extra) in linecaster (import.*.v1, presets alto-import, ...), and formats that need more in engine packages (MediaWiki wikitext: linecaster-mediawiki). A source with conventions of its own (a wiki's templates and classes, a project's markup) is read with its conventions, a catalog entry its importer applies: each rule a match in the format's standard and a decision in the data model's vocabulary (what is text, what is a role, a note, an edit, what is removed and why). The importer records the conventions' chain and hash, the coverage (what no rule handled) and, for a source text, where every line comes from (Zone.anchor). No source needs code of an evaluation's own any more.

What a ground truth supports is recorded in its benchmark (below): which roles it marks, whether it has boxes, a reading order of components, notes, continuations across pages. A metric that needs what it lacks is not computed.

items.title: Rendering both sides
items.text:
Ground truth and output are rendered under the same rendering policy, named in the benchmark. Two texts per page are scored:

Text Layers Is full body, furniture everything printed on the page, in reading order body body the page without its furniture (running heads, page numbers, catchwords, signature marks)

Each is the page's literal text as laid out (its lines' readings in reading order, tables as Markdown or HTML, a formula region as $LaTeX$ in place of its lines, as a ground truth writes a formula), then the benchmark's output strategy's rules on characters (output, default literal: nothing changed): what a model writes about a figure (descriptions) is in neither, unless the policy puts it in the body (page-layers-described: after its region, one per line). A ground truth's corrected edits are not applied: the output is compared with what is printed. Its illegible spans become U+FFFD, one per character.

items.title: Lanes
items.text:
A lane is a comparison strategy (a catalog strategy with use: comparison, catalog): normalizations both sides go through before they are counted, named by id and recorded with its hash. A benchmark that names no lanes is scored in diplomatic (DEFAULT_LANE): the comparison with the fewest assumptions, NFC and whitespace only (so that two encodings of the same text, and a text written in printed lines against one written in paragraphs, are equal), case, punctuation, ſ, ligatures, diacritics and markup kept; every other lane adds decisions.

Lane Normalizations diplomatic (default) NFC; whitespace runs to one space, trimmed. Case, punctuation, ſ, ligatures and diacritics kept reading formulas as the characters they print (latex-text: $\frac{1}{2}$ as 1⁄2, which NFKC makes of ½ too; $\alpha$ as α; sub- and superscripts as their characters); markup removed (special tokens, box arrays, HTML tags of a fixed list, Markdown headings, bullets and rules, LaTeX macros, and the characters ` * \| ~ { } $ \); NFKC; invisible format characters removed; quotes and dashes unified; casefolded; whitespace collapsed. No hyphen at a line end is joined: that is a strategy's choice, never a lane's typographic reading, with international typography folded as Omni Parse Bench's comparison fold does: superscript digits after a digit set apart before NFKC (1,240¹ as 1,240 1); after markup is removed, checkboxes as ☒ and ☐ ([x], ✔, [ ], □), footnote markers [1] and [^a] as their label after a space, a bullet glyph starting a line and leaders (runs of three or more dots, dashes, underscores, = or *) as a space; after quotes and dashes, hierarchy (low quotes, guillemets, primes, the minus sign, special spaces, arrows, the fraction slash, …, a middle dot between digits as .) and cjk-punctuation (。、「」【】（）… as ASCII); casefolded; whitespace collapsed. No hyphen at a line end is joined (line-end-hyphens is opt-in by name, typographic+line-end-hyphens), and language-specific letters stay (typographic+romanian-comma-below) alnum formulas as the characters they print (latex-text); markup removed; NFKC (ſ to s, ligatures split, superscript digits to digits); invisible format characters removed; casefolded and NFKC again; only letters, combining marks and digits of any script kept, each run of anything else one space alnum-nonmark NFC; casefolded; only letters and digits kept (0.9's alnum@1) ascii-alnum HTML tags removed; lowercased; only the ASCII letters and digits kept (accented letters, ſ and ligatures separate words)

A lane from before 0.10 (alnum@2, diplomatic@1, ...) is read as today's (alnum, alnum-nonmark for alnum@1; reading@1 without its hyphen join) with a warning. NFKC appears only in a lane, never in an output text: a lane makes two texts comparable, it is not a reading text.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
A ground truth that declares the normalizations its transcription embodies (source.normalized) is checked against each lane: a declared normalization that neither the lane nor the output strategy's rules on characters apply, themselves or through one that subsumes it (nfkc subsumes nfc, long-s, ligatures), is a difference the comparison counts that is the ground truth's convention, not the output's error. Each score record names those (conventions), and the run warns once per lane (ConventionsWarning, and on the console of linecaster score). English Wikisource scored in alnum, for example: r-rotunda and divided-words (Wikisource rejoins words divided at a line end; the output as read does not).

U+FFFD in the ground truth marks one illegible character: it matches any one character of the output and is excluded from both the errors and the reference length.

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
Per page, per text (full, body) and per lane:

Metric Is s, d, i, h substitutions, deletions, insertions and hits of the alignment of output against ground truth (Levenshtein, U+FFFD as above), in the benchmark's unit: grapheme clusters (the default: a base letter with its combining marks is one character) or codepoints; n = s + d + h cer (s + d + i) / n token_recall the share of the ground truth's words (the benchmark's tokenizer on the lane's text, below) the output has, as multisets over_extraction the share of the output's words the ground truth does not have

Per page and role, where the ground truth marks the role (no boxes needed):

Metric Is role_words_true, role_words_output, role_words_both the words (as for token_recall) the ground truth puts in the role, those the output puts there, and their multiset intersection; precision and recall per role follow

Words. The word metrics cut the lane's text into words by the benchmark's tokenizer (words, linecaster.evaluation.tokens); a word with an illegible character is left out:

Tokenizer Words whitespace runs between whitespace, everything but letters, combining marks, format characters, digits and the underscore a boundary: a word keeps its combining marks (Devanagari vowel signs, Arabic vowel marks, Hebrew points, Thai vowels) and its joiners (the zero-width non-joiner and joiner, the Mongolian vowel separator), while the zero width space separates words; a text without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) is one word per run uax29 (default) Unicode's word boundaries (UAX #29): Chinese ideographs, Hiragana and Thai one word per character (Unicode leaves those scripts to a dictionary), Katakana runs whole, the other scripts by their own boundaries characters grapheme clusters with a letter, mark or digit

Role words are each line's words written as the scored texts are: its illegible spans as U+FFFD, then the output strategy, then the first lane and the tokenizer.

Per page, where both sides have boxes: regions matched one to one by IoU (greedy, highest first, IoU ≥ 0.5), and a confusion table of their roles (role_true, role_output, count), with the unmatched on either side as none.

Per page, always: whether the output is missing, its error and the finish_reason of its last annotator that recorded one, so that missing, failed and truncated pages are read next to the scores.

items.title: Elements
items.text:
The page metrics compare one string per page, so an output that reads every paragraph right but puts them in another order, or cuts a paragraph in two, is charged as if it misread. The element metrics compare content where it is, as OmniDocBench does: each side is cut into elements, the ground truth's elements are matched to the output's, and each match is compared on its own; the reading order is scored apart (metrics: [elements, tables, formulas, reading_order], the default with the page metrics).

Elements (linecaster.evaluation.elements), in each side's reading order: a region's run of lines (its text, as the texts render it: illegible spans as U+FFFD), a table (by table_kind: data tables are tables, the rest text, unless the benchmark's elements.tables is all), a formula (a formula region, or a line that is a display formula), a description where the policy scores it (page-layers-described). An output without regions (a model's Markdown) is cut into its lines, with the components that span lines recognized: an HTML table, a pipe table, a $$…$$ or \[…\] formula, a # heading. Each element records its role, kind, layer, and the writing system and classifications that hold for it.

Matching (linecaster.evaluation.matching): both sides' contents written by the output strategy and the matching lane (elements.lane, default alnum: letters, marks and digits of any script, so markup, punctuation and formula notation do not keep a match apart), as units (grapheme clusters by default), so it works the same in every script. An element's candidates are the elements of the other side sharing the most n-grams of units; its home is the candidate it lies in or holds the most (containment: one minus the edit distance of the shorter aligned against the best stretch of the longer, over its length; at least elements.containment, default 0.5), ties broken by similarity, then by position. Short elements (elements.short, default 4 units) need that similarity instead. The homes' connected components are the match groups: one, split (one ground-truth element, several output elements), merge, many, missed (no partner), extra; past elements.max_cells aligned units a page is one group (page). The matching is deterministic.

Counts. A group's sides are compared as wholes, each joined with spaces in its order, and the edits are attributed to the ground-truth elements they fall in (edit_counts_by, summing to the group's counts): the element score forgives the order between groups. It is no bound on the page score: a wrong match costs, and tables are compared by their cells' text where the page texts write them as HTML or Markdown. A missed element counts all deletions; an extra element all insertions; extra text is never free.

Metric Is element_cer Σ(s + d + i) / Σn over the elements element_ned Σ(s + d + i) / Σm, m = max(n, h + s + i): normalized edit distance, at most 1 teds, teds_s per ground-truth table, the tree-edit-distance similarity (Zhong et al., 2020) to the output table of its group, of content and structure or structure alone (linecaster.evaluation.teds, from the tables' cells; 0 without one) table_recall the share of ground-truth tables the output gives as tables table_precision the share of the output's tables that are in a group with a ground-truth table formula_cer, formula_ned per ground-truth formula, the edit distance of the cleaned LaTeX (linecaster.normalization.formulas.clean, without spaces) to the output's in its group order_kendall of the pairs of matched ground-truth elements (those of regions the ground truth's order ranks, where it has one: furniture it leaves unordered is not ordered), the share the output puts the other way round (linecaster.evaluation.order) order_edit the edit distance between the ground truth's order of its matched elements and the output's, over their number: OmniDocBench's reading-order measure

The element rates are per text and lane (element_cer_full_diplomatic); the formula and order rates are for the first text and lane. Element rows (elements.parquet, beside the score records) hold one row per element, text and lane: level (element), side (truth or output), element, index, kind, role, layer, group, match, the counts, teds, teds_s, table_kind, as_table, latex_* and attributes.

items.title: Strata
items.text:
Rates by strata are a run's rates on part of what was compared (linecaster.evaluation.strata). The element rates are always given by role and kind; a benchmark's strata adds dimensions:

  • of an element: role, kind, layer, match (its group's kind), table_kind, and any scheme it records: language, script, direction (the writing system that holds for it), its region's classifications (a tag such as degraded);
  • of a page (pages:<dimension> in the result): slice and any scheme the page records, for the page rates.

Only recorded values count: what records none is in the stratum unrecorded, never given an inferred value.

items.title: Score records (linecaster.score/1)
items.text: One row per page, text and lane, in OUT/scores/*.parquet: page_id, item_id, text, lane, unit, words (the tokenizer), s, d, i, h, n, the word counts words_true, words_output, words_both, the page's flags (missing, error, finish_reason), and the ids that tie the row to its sources: run_id, benchmark, benchmark_sha256, policy, output, scorer, and conventions (the conventions check). Rates are not stored: they are derived from the counts, so corpus rates are exact. Element rows are in OUT/scores/elements.parquet (elements).

items.title: Aggregation
items.text:
• Corpus rates pool the counts over the pages and divide once (micro average): cer = Σ(s + d + i) / Σn.
  • Intervals: a percentile bootstrap over items (pages of one item are drawn together), with the seed, the number of resamples and the level the benchmark gives; the evidence names all three.
  • Strata: rates by role and kind of element, and by the dimensions the benchmark names (strata).
  • Eligibility: a run is scored only on exactly the benchmark's page set; a page the run failed counts as an empty output, and the evidence says how many there were. A run that lacks pages of the set is not eligible.

items.title: Scoring many pages (pipelines/score.py)
items.text:
linecaster score scores a run in one process. pipelines/score.py (the pipeline score.v1) scores the same way over many tasks, here (--workers) or on a Ray cluster (--on ray), like every other pipeline:

uv run pipelines/score.py RUN/scores --pages RUN/pages --ground-truth TRUTH --benchmark benchmark.yaml --tasks 32

Each task scores a share of the run's page records (PageScorer: its pages' ground truth read in one pass, only their lines decoded) and writes their score records and page summaries (ScoreWriter: OUT/records, OUT/pages). When every task is done, the driver puts them together (linecaster.evaluation.run.aggregate): the pages the run lacks are scored as empty outputs, then the rates, intervals and conventions check as above, into OUT/scores.parquet and OUT/evidence.yaml. The score records are the ones linecaster score writes, page for page. With more tasks than page-record files, the tasks share each file (every k-th record each), so any number of tasks has work.

items.title: Benchmarks (linecaster.benchmark/2)
items.text:
A benchmark definition is a YAML file in the evaluation's repository:

Field Holds schema linecaster.benchmark/2 (/1 is read, upgraded: its lanes by today's names, unit: codepoint) id, edition its name and edition (the evaluation's own versioning); its hash covers its functional content dataset the ground truth: repo@revision, the transcription's name, the importer pages the page set: a list of page ids, or a sample rule (linecaster.data.sample: seed, items, pages per item, pages, and stratify, per_stratum, splits, split) applied to the ground truth when no ids are listed, and its sha256 (of the sorted page ids, one per line) supports what the ground truth has: roles (a list), boxes, reading_order, notes, continuations policy the rendering policy both sides are rendered with texts, lanes which texts and lanes are scored output the output strategy both texts are written with (literal by default) unit grapheme (default) or codepoint: what a character error counts; part of the hash words the word metrics' tokenizer: uax29 (default), whitespace or characters; part of the hash where it is not the default (so benchmarks that name none keep theirs) metrics which metrics, of those the ground truth supports; default the element metrics (elements, tables, formulas, and reading_order where the ground truth supports it) and the page metrics cer, token_recall, over_extraction elements how elements are cut and matched: lane, tables (data or all), containment, short, ngram, candidates, stop, max_cells (elements); part of the hash when element metrics are named bootstrap seed, resamples, level strata dimensions to report rates by (strata)

items.title: Evidence (linecaster.evidence/3)
items.text:
One measurement per file, kept by the evaluation:

Field Holds schema linecaster.evidence/3 preset or recipe what was measured, by id (the run record has its hash) source own-run, card-claim, vendor-benchmark run uri (the run folder), run_id, pipeline_sha256, record_sha256 (of run.yaml) benchmark id@edition and its sha256 scoring policy, output and each of lanes by id and sha256, unit, words (the tokenizer and the version of the word metrics' rules: 1 dropped combining marks and format characters, 2 keeps them; absent: whitespace, 1), elements (with element metrics: the version of the element scorer's rules, linecaster.evaluation.ELEMENTS_VERSION, and the matching lane by id and sha256), scorer (the linecaster that scored, version and commit) metrics name → {value, lo, hi, n}: cer_full_diplomatic, cer_body_alnum, role_recall_header, ... (<metric>_<text>_<lane>, role_precision_<role>, role_recall_<role>) slices slice → {definition, pages, metrics}: CER and word recall on the pages whose ground truth has data tables (tables, linecaster.evaluation.tables), formulas (formulas), or neither (plain); linecaster.evaluation.slices strata dimension → value → {pages, elements, metrics} (strata) hardware gpu (model and count), driver, cuda, cpu, from the run record software the server's version (vLLM, ...), the engine packages' versions date, notes

linecaster.evidence/1 and /2 records stay readable, upgraded when read (their lanes by today's names, unit: codepoint, marked not comparable with evidence/3 where a hash is missing); linecaster evidence check validates a file of any version, and linecaster evidence compare puts evidence records side by side, only those scored the same way (benchmark, policy, output strategy, lanes by hash, unit, word metrics, element metrics).

items.title: Export to OmniDocBench (linecaster export omnidocbench)
items.text:
linecaster runs no external benchmark's code: it writes a ground truth and a run in the benchmark's formats, and the benchmark's own evaluation scores them, where and how its owners run it. For OmniDocBench (opendatalab/OmniDocBench, its end-to-end evaluation):

linecaster export omnidocbench OUT --ground-truth TRUTH/pages --pages RUN/pages [--ids IDS] [--tables data] [--strategy nfc]

OUT holds truth.json (OmniDocBench's ground-truth JSON), predictions/<page id>.md (a page the run lacks or failed on: an empty prediction), export.yaml (what was exported and with what) and a README.md naming OmniDocBench's own command; OmniDocBench runs in an environment of its own (Python before 3.12).

The formats (linecaster.evaluation.omnidocbench): the ground truth's regions in reading order become its elements, their roles its categories (paragraphs text_component, headings title, running heads and feet header and footer, page numbers page_number, footnotes page_footnote, captions figure_caption, tables table with their HTML, formula regions equation_isolated); a line a formula fills (an equation number may follow) is its own equation_isolated, an inline formula stays in its text as $…$. No boxes are written: OmniDocBench scores by text and order. A run's page is Markdown: components in reading order, a heading # at its level, tables as HTML, formula regions $$…$$; a transcription without regions (a VLM's completion) as the model wrote it. Pages carry the attributes tables (data tables) and formulas (yes/no, the slices), by which OmniDocBench groups its page results.

Which tables are tables (--tables, default data; linecaster.evaluation.tables), on both sides alike: a table is data (printed as a table: at least two rows and two columns of filled cells, text or numbers alike), contents (a table of contents or an index laid out as a table: entries with page, chapter or section references, the references rising or the entries in alphabetical order) or layout (one row, one column or one cell, one column in practice, a brace grouping lines). Only data tables are written as tables; the others are their text. --tables all writes every table as a table. --strategy applies an output strategy to every text of both sides (nfc puts both in one form).

What OmniDocBench measures (at 7ddb8df): its text score keeps only letters, digits and CJK ideographs (\w), so combining marks (Devanagari vowel signs, Arabic vowel marks, Hebrew points, Thai vowels), punctuation and spaces are not compared, and nothing is put in NFC; predicted text that matches no ground-truth element and predicted tables that match no ground-truth table are not counted; captions and footnotes are matched but not scored; its "overall" needs its formula metric CDM (TeX Live) and pages with tables and formulas. Its reading-order distance is not 0 for a page against itself where its matching splits or merges components. Its results are another view than linecaster's own scoring, not one of its lanes; for scripts with combining marks linecaster's scoring is the measure.

items.title: Checking a ground truth (linecaster ground-truth check)
items.text:
linecaster ground-truth check TRUTH [--transcription ground_truth] [--ids FILE] [--json OUT]

reads a ground truth's page records (a folder, local or fsspec; JSON Lines, gzipped or not, or Parquet) and reports, per page and in total (linecaster.evaluation.truth: check_page, check, render):

Reported Is lines, lines_with_text, empty_lines the lines, those whose reading has text, those without (no reading, or an empty one) regions, regions_with_box, boxes_outside the regions, those with a box, and the zones whose box lies outside the image (by more than half a pixel; the source's image size, else the page image's; none without a size) reading_order, unranked_regions, unranked_lines none, partial or complete: every region and line ranked (by an order of regions, a region's lines with it; by an order of lines, each line) conventions, unmapped the conventions its importer applied, with their hash, and what no rule of them handled (the importer's unmapped measurement) characters, illegible_characters the readings' characters (code points) and those with status illegible (a span, a word or a line); in total their share language, script, direction; languages, scripts, directions the value recorded on the page (Transcription.language(""), ...), and every value recorded anywhere on it; in total the pages without one roles, statuses the regions' content roles and the statuses, with counts tables, table_kinds, formulas tables with cells by kind (linecaster.evaluation.tables: data, contents, layout); formulas of regions and inline (of a span) notes, continuations note regions (footnotes, endnotes) and note_of links; continues links normalized the normalizations the source declares it embodies

In total also the pages whose texts are the same (whitespace aside: duplicates) and what the ground truth supports (below). The text report names at most ten pages of each problem; --json writes everything (linecaster.truth-check/1). A check changes nothing: what it finds is fixed in the source or its import.

items.title: Benchmark definitions from the data (linecaster benchmark init)
items.text:
linecaster benchmark init TRUTH OUT.yaml [--id ID] [--transcription ground_truth] [--dataset REPO@REVISION]
    [--importer IMPORTER] [--sample N] [--sample-items M] [--sample-per-item K] [--seed S]
    [--stratify SCHEME] [--per-stratum K] [--split NAME:FRACTION ...] [--in-split NAME]

writes a linecaster.benchmark/2 definition, validated, of the ground truth's pages (linecaster.evaluation.truth.benchmark):

  • pages: the page ids, sorted, with their sha256; every page, or the sample's (a sample rule, below), and then the rule too (pages.rule);
  • supports from the data, as truth check finds it: roles every content role a region has, boxes where every region has a box, reading_order where every page is ordered (partly or completely), notes where a note region or link is, continuations where a continues link is;
  • dataset: --dataset, else the one the sources name (all pages one); importer: --importer, else the import annotator's preset or engine, else the source's format;
  • lanes: diplomatic and reading; with --stratify, its scheme as the benchmark's strata; the other fields their defaults.

Comment lines above it say where it was made from, the metrics the data supports besides the defaults (role_words with roles, confusion with boxes) and, for each script recorded (a script, else the script subtag of a language: zh-Hans), what the lanes and the tokenizer do with it: a script written without spaces is cut into words by uax29, the default; a script whose letters take combining marks is counted by grapheme cluster, the default; a right-to-left script is compared in the order stored. The definition is the evaluation's to edit and keep.

items.title: Samples: strata and splits (linecaster.data.sample)
items.text:
The sample rule (linecaster.sample/1) takes two optional parts; a rule without them selects, and is written and hashed, as before:

  • splits: named fractions of the items (--split test:0.2 --split train:0.8, SampleRule(splits=..., split=...)). An item is in the split where H(f"split\t{seed}\t{item_id}") / 2**64 falls among the fractions' running sums, in their order: every page of an item in one split, the same split whatever else is listed, another split for another seed (split_of). A sample takes one split (split; --in-split, else the first named) and the rule's limits within it.
  • strata: a page value (stratify) the caller supplies per page (select(..., strata=...): a mapping of page ids or a function of the item and page id; linecaster.evaluation.truth.page_values: a scheme recorded on the page, metadata.<key>, source.<field>), each value's pages a stratum sampled apart by the rule: per_stratum pages of each, or pages shared in proportion to the strata's pages (largest remainders, ties by the value), or the rule's items and per_item in each. The strata's pages together come in the order of the rule's hashes; a page without a value is in the stratum "". A stratified sample reads the whole listing.

Both are recorded in the rule (stratify, per_stratum, splits, split), and a sample's record (Sample.record()) names the split hash (split_hash) where splits were used.

items.title: Publishing a ground truth (linecaster ground-truth publish)
items.text:
linecaster ground-truth publish TRUTH OUT [--transcription ground_truth] [--images FOLDER | --no-images]
    [--split NAME:FRACTION ...] [--seed S] [--license LICENSE] [--name NAME] [--shard-pages 1000]

writes a ground truth's page records as a dataset the Hugging Face Hub reads (linecaster.evaluation.publish): OUT/data/<split>-<n>-of-<m>.parquet, one row per page, and a dataset card, OUT/README.md.

Column Holds id, item_id the page's ids image the page image (the Hub's Image feature: bytes, path): from --images (the file of the image's name, else of the page id), else read from the record's image.uri; none where it is not found text the transcription's literal text, as laid out (Transcription.text) language, script the values recorded on the page page the page record as JSON (linecaster.page/N)

The card's front matter has the license the records record (an extension field or metadata key <ns>__license; several: other), else --license, else other; the languages recorded (their primary subtags); the task category image-to-text; the size category; and the splits as data files (by item, as above; default every page in train). Its body lists the sources (source.dataset with page counts), the conventions with their hashes, the languages, scripts and directions recorded with page counts, what the ground truth supports, the normalizations it embodies (source.normalized), the counts, the splits, the columns, and the linecaster that wrote it.

items.title: Run records
items.text: A run record (OUT/run.yaml) carries what evidence names: run_id (stamped on every annotator the run adds), pipeline_sha256, the recipe and every catalog entry the run used with its settings and hash (catalog: presets, policy, conventions, the strategies its texts were written by), hardware (GPU model and count, driver, CUDA, CPU) and the software versions.

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
The words linecaster uses. Each word has one meaning. A word that needs a second meaning gets a qualifier ("content role", "datatrove Document") and is never used bare for it. Code, docs and commit messages use these terms; a new term is added here before it is used.

The first four sections are the core: what you need to read any other page. The sections after them belong to one subject each and link to the page that explains it.

items.title: Pipelines
items.text: Term Meaning component One processing unit of a pipeline. Technically a datatrove PipelineStep with a contract. Components are named after what they do: LineRecognizer, ParagraphBuilder, PageJsonlWriter. step One kind of work in a pipeline: layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, image, hierarchy, paragraphs, document, import, tagging. An engine does the work of one step and a preset belongs to one step, so the presets of a step are interchangeable. datatrove's class is always written PipelineStep. contract What a component reads, adds, replaces and removes in the page record, with its unit and its kind (reader, writer, model, transform, server). Contracts are checked before a run starts. part One named piece of a page record that a contract refers to: image, lines, text, paragraphs. The parts table lists them. unit What one call of a component or an engine processes: a line, a region, a page or an item. condition A test on the page record. A component with a condition (when=) processes only the pages that pass; the others go through unchanged. composite A named group of components that is used like one component, with one contract (ModularTranscriber). pipeline An ordered list of components that a stream of pages passes through. A datatrove executor runs it. pipeline template The code that builds one kind of pipeline from options (linecaster.templates.transcribe_modular), with an id (transcribe_modular.v1). slot A place in a pipeline template that a preset fills. It is named after its step, and so is its flag (--layout, --recognition). No slot has a default preset. pipeline script A self-contained uv script in pipelines/ that gives one pipeline template its environment and its command line. recipe A tested way to fill a pipeline template, as a catalog entry: a preset for each slot and the options. stage One datatrove pipeline run as part of a longer computation. Stages run one after another and hand over through files. A pipeline is cut into stages where the unit changes from page to item. executor, job, task, worker, shard datatrove's terms. The executor runs a pipeline as tasks. A job is one launch (one HF Job, one Slurm job). A task is one unit of work. Workers are tasks running at the same time. A shard is the part of the input one task reads. backend Where a component's engine runs: in the pipeline's process (InProcess), behind linecaster serve (Served), or behind an OpenAI-compatible server (Chat). server A process that hosts models: linecaster serve, vLLM or SGLang, or a vendor's own image. The server components EngineServer, VLMServer and VendorServer start one inside a task; they go last in a pipeline. run One execution of a pipeline over one input, into one run folder. run folder The output folder of a run: pages/ (the page records), rejects/, logs/, traces/ and run.yaml. run record run.yaml in the run folder: the pipeline as it ran, with every component's parameters, the recipe, the command line and the software versions. sample The pages a run reads when it is given a sample rule (--sample N). The same input and rule always give the same pages. reject A page that failed a check or a component. It is written to rejects/ with the reason and stays in the page records with its errors. error budget The share of a task's pages that may fail in a component before the task fails. warm-up What a component loads before its first unit: an engine, a client. functional parameter, operational parameter A functional parameter can change what a run writes. An operational parameter only says where things are or how the work runs (folders, ports, worker counts). The run record's hash covers the functional ones. downstream project A project built on linecaster, with its own pipelines, components or engines. Project-specific code lives there, never in linecaster.

items.title: Parts
items.text: Part Meaning image The page image's bytes, as the reader brought them. metadata The page record's own fields: ids, sequence, the image's record, the metadata. transcription_file A transcription delivered with the page as a file (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text). The TranscriptionConverter reads it into a transcription. regions, reading_order, lines, baselines, text, words, ... What presets produce (PRODUCES in the catalog's schema). line_regions Lines assigned to the layout regions and ordered within them (LineAssigner). hierarchy Heading levels, headline splits and drop capitals (HierarchyDetector). paragraphs The paragraphs of the rows, with the decisions that made them (ParagraphBuilder). Structure only, no text. tags Tags with their basis (Tagger). document The document of a page or an item (DocumentBuilder). It travels with the page through the pipeline and is not stored in the page record.

items.title: Models and the catalog
items.text: Term Meaning model Weights from upstream (or learned data such as hyphenation patterns), pinned to a revision. engine Code that does the work of one step: it loads a model and processes one unit per call. Engines have a versioned id (kraken.recognition.v1). Rule-based engines need no model. Built-in engines are in the core; engine packages (linecaster-kraken, ...) add more. preset A named configuration of one engine: its options and the model it loads. A preset is what you pick for a step (--recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium). catalog linecaster's register of models, presets, recipes, normalizations, strategies, rendering policies, conventions and vocabularies. It holds no measurements. catalog entry One thing in the catalog: a YAML file, with an optional Markdown file for prose. revision The exact upstream commit a model is pinned to. code id The versioned id of an engine or a pipeline template: <name>.v<n>. index catalog.index: the hash of every catalog entry. A change in it is a change of behavior.

items.title: Pages, items and text
items.text: Term Meaning item A named, ordered container of pages: a book, an issue, a PDF, a folder of images. linecaster assumes nothing more about it. page One page of an item, with its image and its annotation sets. page record A page as stored and as passed through a pipeline (Page): the image reference, the annotation sets and the metadata. Components read it and add to it. item record An item with its pages in order, as the ItemAssembler passes it on. page image The image a page's coordinates refer to (PageImage). annotation One thing an annotator said about a page: a zone, a reading, a table, a formula, a classification, an edit, a link, a reading order. Never changed after it is added. annotation set Everything one source said about one page (AnnotationSet). transcription An annotation set that also holds text (Transcription). A page has named transcriptions: ocr_new (linecaster's), ocr_original (delivered with the page), ground_truth. annotator Who or what added annotations (Annotator): a model, a rule-based engine, a delivered file, or people. It records the engine, the preset, the recipe and the linecaster version. raw output What one request returned, verbatim (RawOutput): a model's completion or an engine's native result. zone A place on the page image (Zone): a region or a line, with a box and a polygon. region A zone found by layout analysis. line One printed or written line (Line): a zone and, once recognized, its reading. reading The text a recognizer read on one line (Reading), with its words and alternatives. Stored exactly as given. reading order The order in which a page's regions and lines are read. row The lines of one region that sit side by side at the same height.
