A downstream project's pipeline runs on Jobs from its own script (its sources pinned to a linecaster tag), read as it is on disk.

uv run --with (datatrove's way of installing a Job's dependencies) ignores constraints and overrides, whether given as UV_CONSTRAINT, UV_OVERRIDE or a uv.toml; only a script's own [tool.uv] brings them to uv run. So JobsExecutor given Dependencies uploads, in place of datatrove's launch_pickled_pipeline.py, a uv script of the same name whose inline metadata holds the requirements, constraint-dependencies and override-dependencies (Dependencies.script) and which then runs datatrove's launcher. Constraints only bound what the requirements bring: a package the lock holds for another platform is not installed. --dry-run prints the three lists; the run record keeps them (dependencies, constraints, overrides).

items.title: Serialization and working images
items.text:
linecaster.formats.{alto,pagexml,hocr} write and read the three XML formats on lxml, linecaster.formats.iiif writes an annotation set as an IIIF annotation page and reads one, linecaster.document writes a page's or an item's document as HTML, Markdown, text and JSON, linecaster.formats.docling reads a DoclingDocument (the docling extra), linecaster.formats.tei a page of a TEI P5 document and linecaster.formats.text plain text (a line per line, or the text of a line image); linecaster.images.convert turns any page image into the working image. None of them imports datatrove, saturate or an engine. Each writer renders an annotation set under a rendering policy; what it writes is a rendering, not stored in the page record.

The importers (linecaster.engines.importers, step import) read these formats into transcriptions. A source document's context may state the page's writing system, as a line-level dataset's columns do (language, a BCP 47 tag; script, an ISO 15924 code; direction): each becomes the page's classification by the importer where the file records none of its own. text-import with the option line_image reads the text of an image of one line: the page is that line, its box the whole image (import_transcriptions --read-images gives the importer the image's size).

items.title: Common rules for ALTO, PAGE and hOCR
items.text:
1. Native first, extension for the rest. Every value goes into the format's own vocabulary where it has a place. What it cannot hold, or what a reader would infer differently, goes into a small JSON extension on the element: ALTO OtherTag[@TYPE="linecaster"]/@DESCRIPTION referenced by TAGREFS; PAGE UserDefined/UserAttribute[@name="linecaster"]/@value; hOCR @data-linecaster. Writers compute what their own reader would infer and only write the extension when it differs, so ordinary pages carry few (ALTO: line confidences and scores; PAGE: usually only {"polygon": null} for box-only lines). extensions=False writes pure files; they then round-trip only what the format holds natively. Foreign files have no extensions and readers fall back to the inferred values.
  2. What is written (linecaster.formats._xml.file_layout): of the transcription t, under the policy policy (to_alto, to_page, to_hocr; default page-layers, linecaster.data.DEFAULT_POLICY):
  3. regions: id, polygon and box, detection confidence (the region's score), the annotator's own label (Region.label, the raw label) and the region's region label, from its content role (t.label; handwritten_text for running text classified as handwritten), and its heading level (its heading_level classification, unless a later annotator classified its role anew);
  4. lines: id, region (t.region_of: the latest part_of link, else Line.region), box, polygon, baseline, detection confidence (the line's score) and its reading: the literal text (t.text_of: the reading's text, exactly as read), confidence, alternatives, and the words with their ids, text, box, confidence, alternatives and hyphen flag, and a word the source marks as half of a divided word (a joined edit covering exactly the line's last or first word) as ALTO's SUBS_TYPE (HypPart1, HypPart2) and SUBS_CONTENT (the whole word), which the ALTO reader reads back as those edits; a line not read has no reading;
  5. the reading order that counts (t.order): each region's rank in it, each line's rank on the page and row in its region;
  6. languages, scripts and directions as recorded (t.language, t.script, t.direction: a target's own classification, else its line's, its region's or the page's; never an inferred one): the page's, and a region's, line's or word's where it differs from the level that encloses it in the file (a word's line, a line's region, else the page), so a value the page records is written once.

Regions the policy puts in layer none (a status of removed, suppressed or duplicate under page-layers; the roles separator and noise) are left out with their lines, and so are lines whose own status the policy puts there (a line assignment's duplicates); ranks are counted among what is written. Not serialized: the other classifications (production apart from handwritten running text, status, picture class, code language; spans' languages and directions), edits (corrected, expanded, regularized; ALTO's divided words apart), descriptions, links, ranges and paragraphs, tables and formulas, raw outputs, glyphs and formatting, annotations' annotator, output, derived_from and extension fields, annotators of kind file and human, annotators' measurements other than datetime, and the source. 3. Reading (linecaster.formats._xml.transcription): a reader makes one transcription of the file: its regions (the raw label as Region.label, a role classification of the region label they read as, linecaster.data.policy.classify_label, and a heading_level one), its lines with their readings, and one reading order (the regions with a rank, the lines by rank, with their rows). A language, script or direction the file states becomes a classification (by the annotator that made the readings) of the narrowest target it holds for, the page, a region, a line or a word (<line>/<n>), where it differs from the enclosing level's: a value an element inherits from one the reader does not keep (hOCR's ocr_par, a nested PAGE region, a synthetic block) is recorded on what lies in it. A language as BCP 47 with the ISO 639-1 code for a three-letter one (eng, deu and ger read as en, de; linecaster.formats._languages.canonical); a value that is no language, script or direction is not recorded. A content role comes back as the role of its region label: roles that share one (marginalia, credit, floating and drop capitals read as paragraphs; endnotes and continued footnotes as footnotes; a page number as a header or footer) come back as that label's role. The annotators are the steps the file names (provenance, below); without any, the file is the one annotator (kind file, step transcription, named after its format). What each annotator made: regions by the latest layout step (else recognition, else lines), roles and heading levels by the latest typography step (else layout, else recognition), lines by the line step (else recognition, else layout), readings by recognition (else lines), the reading order by the latest of typography, assignment, ordering, lines, layout and recognition, and by the first annotator where none of these ran. The source is kind="converted", format, uri and the image size, with ALTO's scale factors (scale) and the extension fields alto__namespace (the file's namespace), alto__measurement_unit (when not pixel), alto__other_languages (OTHERLANGS), page__namespace, and PAGE's page-level extension fields (below). ground_truth=True (every reader) makes the source a ground truth (kind="ground_truth") and the file's own annotator people (kind human); steps the file names stay what they are. Readers return regions and lines in document order, which may differ from the original list order; tests compare by id.

Provenance round-trips: every annotator of kind model or rule, as a step record (step, name, engine, revision, preset, preset hash, recipe, recipe hash, backend, settings; datetime as ALTO processingDateTime and PAGE MetadataItem/@date), is written as ALTO Processing, PAGE MetadataItem type="processingStep" with Labels, and hOCR linecaster-step-<n> metas next to ocr-system and ocr-capabilities (computed from what the file contains); readers turn each back into an annotator, of kind rule for the rule-based steps (RULE_STEPS), else model. Annotators of kind file and human are the set's source, not steps, and are not written. Other tools' provenance is read too (ALTO Processing and OCRProcessing: the description as the step, the software's name and version as model and revision, other settings as raw; OCR-D PAGE steps: name as the step, value as the model, their parameters as settings; hOCR ocr-system: one recognition step). METS agents per step: linecaster.execution.provenance.mets_agents. 4. Writing order. Regions are written by their rank in the reading order (regions it leaves out after the others, in list order), each region's lines by rank. A line without a region goes before the first region whose first line comes after it; consecutive ones share one block. Readers rank the lines by their position in document order and give each the row of its position in its block, and rank the regions by the format's reading order; the writers record the original rank or row in the extension whenever that differs (gaps, a running head read last, a region outside the order), so irregular orders survive too. 5. Lines without a region. ALTO and PAGE need a block around every line: they get a synthetic TextBlock/TextRegion (id lc_block_<n>, extension {"synthetic": true}) that the reader drops again (with extensions=False it comes back as a text region). In hOCR such lines sit directly in the ocr_page. The synthetic blocks are part of the format's reading order, so consumers that follow it do not lose those lines. 6. Rounding. ALTO coordinates are floats in the schema: to_alto writes them exactly (shortest repr) by default, precision=0 writes integers. PAGE and hOCR hold integers only: points are rounded half up (floor(v + 0.5), deterministic); boxes are rounded by their corners (x0 = r(x), x1 = r(x + w), w = x1 - x0) so edges agree with the rounded polygons; PAGE clamps negative values at 0 (its schema forbids them). Rounding happens once: a second round trip is the identity (tested). 7. Confidences. ALTO WC and PAGE TextEquiv/@conf / Coords/@conf are floats in 0..1 and written exactly. hOCR x_wconf is an integer percentage: confidences come back to 0.01. ALTO has no line confidence: a reader derives it as the length-weighted mean of the words' WC (as for foreign files); the writer stores the real line confidence in the extension when it differs from that mean. 8. Line text vs. words. Words are joined with one space; when a line's literal text is not that join (double spaces, None with words), the text goes into the extension. A line without words is written as a single ALTO String carrying the line text and confidence (extension {"wordless": true}), as a PAGE TextLine with only a line TextEquiv, as an hOCR line with the text directly in the span. text=None (not recognized) and text="" (recognized as empty) stay distinct in all three. 9. Output is deterministic: same input, same bytes (PAGE Created/LastChange default to 1970-01-01T00:00:00; pass created= for a real timestamp). 10. Ids are written as they are. Schema-valid output needs ids that are XML NCNames (letters, digits, _ - ., not starting with a digit); the producers' ids (text_2, orphan_0, ...) are. Ids the writers make up themselves (synthetic blocks, tags, the page) avoid every existing id. 11. Known limits. Characters XML cannot carry (C0 controls other than tab/newline) make the writers raise lxml's ValueError; text is not silently altered. 12. Tests cover the fixture in tests/conftest.py (polygon regions, baselines, box-only lines, empty and unrecognized lines, a region-less line, hyphenation, alternatives), irregular orders, 300 seeded random transcriptions per format (every tenth also validated against the XSD), and foreign files (ALTO v2 mm10, v3 without namespace, eScriptorium v4; PAGE 2010 and Transkribus 2013; Tesseract hOCR and tag-soup HTML); languages, scripts and directions (tests/formats/test_writing_systems.py) in round trips and foreign files of each format.

items.title: ALTO (writes 4.4, reads v1 to v4)
items.text:
What is written ALTO region TextBlock (Illustration TYPE=<label> for picture/chart regions without lines); Shape/Polygon only when the polygon is not the box region label LayoutTag TYPE="label" LABEL=<region label>, one per distinct label, in TAGREFS raw label (Region.label, when set) LayoutTag TYPE="raw_label" LABEL=<raw> region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/ElementRef (regions with a rank + synthetic blocks); without ReadingOrder readers use document order (ALTO's implicit order) line TextLine with BASELINE="x,y x,y ..." (4.2+ points syntax), Shape/Polygon word String (WC, ALTERNATIVE), SP between words; a hyphen word that ends in - ¬ ⸗ ‐ soft hyphen = is split into String + HYP (reader re-joins: word text and line text unchanged) region and line score (detection confidence), heading level, line confidence extension language (BCP 47) LANG on Page, TextBlock, TextLine, String; an Illustration's in the extension direction BASEDIRECTION on TextBlock and TextLine: horizontal-lr ltr, horizontal-rl rtl, vertical-rl and vertical-lr ttb. Page has none: every block carries the page's direction (or its own); a vertical block's direction, a word's and an Illustration's also in the extension script extension (ALTO has none); the page's on every block model and rule annotators Description/Processing (category, date when recorded, the step as processingStepDescription, the step record as JSON in processingStepSettings, linecaster as softwareCreator with the model and its revision), all referenced from Page/@PROCESSINGREFS

Reading foreign ALTO: namespaces v1–v4 or none; blocks anywhere under Page (margins, PrintSpace, nested ComposedBlocks, which are transparent); raw label = the LABEL of the first referenced tag (Transkribus StructureTag, eScriptorium OtherTag), the region label (and so the role) mapped from it; BASELINE as a single number (ALTO < 4.2) becomes a horizontal line across the line box; SUBS_TYPE/SUBS_CONTENT are ignored (the word keeps its CONTENT); missing ids are generated (line_<rank>, <line>_w<k>, block_<n>); GraphicalElements are not read. Units: pixel is read as is; with image_width/image_height and Page/@WIDTH/@HEIGHT every coordinate is scaled to the image (also corrects pixel ALTO made on a master of another size); mm10 and inch1200 without the image size need dpi= (px = v * dpi / 254 resp. / 1200); otherwise from_alto raises ValueError rather than guessing. Languages and directions: LANG of the Page is the page's language, of a TextBlock (or its deprecated language), TextLine or String the region's, line's or word's; OTHERLANGS is kept as the source's alto__other_languages. BASEDIRECTION ltr reads as horizontal-lr, rtl as horizontal-rl; ttb says the lines are vertical but not in which order the columns run, so on a line it reads as its block's vertical direction and is otherwise not recorded: the value is kept as the region's or line's extension field alto__base_direction, as is btt.

items.title: PAGE (writes 2019-07-15, reads 2009–2019)
items.text:
What is written PAGE region TextRegion with @type from the region label (below); ImageRegion, ChartRegion, TableRegion, MathsRegion for picture, chart, table, formula regions without lines (PAGE does not allow lines in them) raw label (Region.label, when set) @custom="structure {type:<raw>;}" (Transkribus convention; ; { } \ escaped as \uXXXX) region and line score (detection confidence) Coords/@conf region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/RegionRefIndexed (nested groups read recursively, index sorted) line TextLine: Coords = polygon (the box when there is none, extension {"polygon": null}), Baseline, TextEquiv/@conf; alternatives as TextEquiv/@index 2.. (primary 1) word Word: Coords = box, TextEquiv box not in PAGE: readers take the bounds of Coords; the writer stores the box when it differs heading level extension language primaryLanguage of Page, TextRegion and TextLine, language of Word: PAGE's English name of the tag's language (German for de and de-1901; linecaster.formats._languages); a tag PAGE names otherwise (de-1901) or not at all (grc) in the extension (not written without it) script primaryScript of Page, TextRegion, TextLine and Word (Latn - Latin); a code PAGE's list lacks in the extension direction Page and TextRegion: readingDirection and textLineOrder, horizontal-lr left-to-right and top-to-bottom, horizontal-rl right-to-left and top-to-bottom, vertical-rl top-to-bottom and right-to-left, vertical-lr top-to-bottom and left-to-right; TextLine and Word: readingDirection (left-to-right, right-to-left, top-to-bottom for both vertical ones; within a level that is not vertical, a vertical one also in the extension); another region's (ImageRegion, ...) language, script and direction in the extension model and rule annotators Metadata/MetadataItem type="processingStep" (as OCR-D records its processors): name the step, value the preset or the model, date when recorded, Labels externalModel="linecaster" with externalId="model" (name, engine, revision, preset, preset hash, recipe, recipe hash, backend, software) and externalId="settings" (one label per setting); a summary in Comments

Label mapping, region label → TextRegion/@type: text, paragraph, list_item, handwritten_text, reference → paragraph; title, section_header → heading; page_header → header; page_footer → footer; caption → caption; footnote → footnote; document_index → TOC-entry; others → other (or paragraph). Reading: structure {type:...} wins when it is a known name, then @type: paragraph → text, heading → section_header, header → page_header, footer, page-number, signature-mark, catch-word → page_footer, footnote(-continued)/endnote → footnote, TOC-entry → document_index, list-label → list_item, everything else → text; the raw label is the structure type, else @type, else the element name (TableRegion). The writer adds the region label to the extension when the reverse mapping would not return it (e.g. title → heading → section_header). The same name table (_xml.RAW_TO_LABEL) also maps eScriptorium/SegmOnto zones and PP-DocLayout names. Old PAGE Coords/Point children are read; text on glyphs only is joined into the word.

Languages, scripts and directions are read from the same attributes. A language name maps to its tag by linecaster.formats._languages (generated from the 2019 schema's names and the ISO 639-3 code table: the ISO 639-1 code where there is one, else the ISO 639-3 code; Cambodian and Khmer both read as km, Panjabi and Punjabi as pa), a script value to its four-letter code. A nested TextRegion takes what it does not say from the region it lies in; a region's readingDirection or textLineOrder alone is completed by the page's, and a horizontal readingDirection without any line order reads with lines top to bottom. A line's or word's top-to-bottom reads as the enclosing vertical direction. What has no value of linecaster's is kept as an extension field of the page (the source), region, line or word: page__language (other, a name the table lacks), page__script, page__secondary_language and page__secondary_script (PAGE's secondary values, read only), and page__reading_direction with page__text_line_order for a combination that is no direction (top-to-bottom lines stacked top-to-bottom).

items.title: hOCR 1.2
items.text:
What is written hOCR region div of class ocr_carea (page_header → ocr_header, page_footer → ocr_footer, picture/chart → ocr_photo, table → ocr_table, formula → ocr_math) with one p.ocr_par; bbox, poly when not the box line span.ocr_line: bbox, baseline slope offset (hOCR's straight line from the box's bottom-left), poly, x_wconf baseline that baseline cannot express (polyline, vertical) also x_bline x1 y1 x2 y2 ... (custom property) word span.ocrx_word: bbox, x_wconf raw label, region and line score, heading level, hyphen, alternatives extension model and rule annotators meta name="linecaster-step-<n>", the step record as JSON; ocr-system is linecaster with its release, ocr-capabilities what the file contains the page's language html/@lang and xml:lang; ocr-langs for an ISO 639-1 code a region's, line's or word's language lang and xml:lang of its ocr_carea (or its class's div), ocr_line or ocrx_word direction on the ocr_page and a region's, line's or word's element: dir="ltr" (horizontal-lr), dir="rtl" (horizontal-rl), style="writing-mode: vertical-rl" (or vertical-lr); a horizontal one within a vertical level also writing-mode: horizontal-tb script extension (hOCR has none), the page's on the ocr_page

Reading foreign hOCR: XHTML or tag-soup HTML (lxml.html fallback); regions are the top-level float/area classes, lines are ocr_line, ocr_textfloat, ocr_caption and ocr_header/ ocr_footer spans inside a region (Tesseract's line classes); word text includes nested <strong>/<em>; image "..." may contain ;. A language, script and direction hold as in HTML, from the element or the nearest element it lies in that states one (hocr.writing_at): lang (xml:lang), dir (ltr, rtl; auto states none) and CSS's writing-mode in style (vertical-rl, vertical-lr; horizontal-tb without a dir reads as horizontal-lr). The page's are those of its ocr_page; a paragraph's (Tesseract writes lang on ocr_par) count for its lines.

items.title: IIIF annotation page (linecaster.formats.iiif)
items.text:
to_annotation_page(t, canvas, id, policy=DEFAULT_POLICY) writes an annotation set as one IIIF Presentation 3 AnnotationPage (W3C Web Annotations on the page's canvas canvas), its annotations numbered <id>/<n>, with the IIIF Presentation and text granularity contexts:

Annotation set Annotation region, in reading order motivation classifying, the content role as a TextualBody (purpose classifying) line with a reading, in reading order supplementing (IIIF's motivation for a transcription), textGranularity line, the text as written, the line's language as the body's language word supplementing, textGranularity word, the word's language as the body's language edit of a line's reading (or of a word or span of it) editing, the edited text with its kind as the purpose and its target's language as its language, targeting the line's annotation (a word's: the word's annotation; a span's: those characters of the line's or word's text, a SpecificResource with a TextPositionSelector; a glyph's edit is left out) description of a region describing, its text with its kind as the purpose

Targets are the canvas with a media fragment (#xywh=, rounded) where the annotation has a box (a line without one: its region's), the canvas itself where it has none. Each annotation names its annotator as generator (Software), or as creator (Person) for people, with the annotator's name. Regions the policy puts in layer none are left out with their lines and descriptions, and so are lines whose own status puts them nowhere. The output is validated against the IIIF Presentation 3 JSON Schema in the tests.

A body's language is the one its target records (data model: Transcription.language, its own language classification, else its line's, its region's or the page's), never an inferred one; a body without one has no language, and a region's body never has one.

from_annotation_page(data, uri=None, ground_truth=False, image_width=None, image_height=None) reads an annotation page back (import.iiif.v1, preset iiif-import; auto-import tells a JSON annotation page apart): linecaster's own and other software's that follow the same conventions.

Annotation Transcription classifying with a box a region, the body's value its role supplementing (also transcribing, commenting and painting with textGranularity line), line or no granularity a line, the body's value its text textGranularity word a word of the line whose box holds most of it (none: the word is left out) editing whose body's purpose is an edit kind (corrected, expanded, regularized, joined), targeting a line's annotation, characters of it (TextPositionSelector) or a word's annotation an edit of that line, span or word describing with a region's box a description of that region, the purpose its kind

A target is a media fragment (#xywh=, in pixels, or percent: of the canvas's size where image_width and image_height give it), a SpecificResource with a FragmentSelector or an SvgSelector with a polygon, or the canvas itself (a line without a box). A line belongs to the region whose box holds more than half of its own. The bodies' languages are recorded on the page where every line states the same one, else on each line, and on a word that states another. Annotators are the annotations' creator (people, kind human) and generator (software, kind model; with ground_truth, people too); without either, the file. A comment without a granularity is no line, and an annotation of another motivation is left out.

items.title: HTML import (linecaster.formats.html)
items.text:
HtmlConverter reads an HTML tree into a transcription by HTML's own semantics (blocks, headings, lists, tables, pictures, MathML formulas, DPUB-ARIA furniture and notes, the CSS that decides what is printed) and, where a run names them, a source's conventions. What the page says of its writing is recorded as language and direction classifications, each on the narrowest thing it differs on, by whoever the text is by:

HTML Recorded as lang (xml:lang before it) of the root (html, its body) the page's ("") language dir and CSS writing-mode of the root the page's direction: rtl horizontal-rl, ltr horizontal-lr, vertical-rl and vertical-lr as they are lang, dir, writing-mode of a block (a paragraph, heading, list item, page header or footer, note, table) that differ from the page's its region's lang, dir of inline elements (span, bdo, bdi, ...) that differ from their line's a span of the line (<line>[a:e]), consecutive runs of one value one span, without its spaces at either end

A value is inherited as in HTML: a note or a table cell has the language of the element it stands in. dir="auto", and a bdi without dir, leave the direction to the text: nothing is recorded. A writing-mode on an inline element does not apply. A lang that is no well-formed BCP 47 tag is skipped and counted (HtmlReading.ill_formed_languages).

items.title: TEI import (linecaster.formats.tei)
items.text:
from_tei(data, page=1, uri=None, ground_truth=False) reads one page of a TEI P5 document (namespace http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0, or none; of a teiCorpus, its first TEI) into a transcription; the importer import.tei.v1 (preset tei-import) runs it, and import.auto.v1 picks it for a file whose root is TEI or teiCorpus in TEI's namespace. The document's first form decides how it is read:

Form Pages Regions Lines diplomatic: sourceDoc its surfaces (also in surfaceGrp) each zone with lines or text of its own (a zone of zones alone is none), its geometry @points, else @ulx @uly @lrx @lry line and zone[@type='line'], with their geometry and a path as the baseline; a zone without lines: its text broken at lb, without geometry; a line on the surface: a line without a region, or a region of its own where all its text is one fw, note or head facsimile and text: facsimile with text as in a text; pb[@facs] names the page's surface as in a text, with the geometry of the zone a block's @facs points to (else the bounds of its lines) as in a text, with the geometry of the zone an lb or l points to text: text (front, body, back) pb begins one; text before the first pb is a page of its own p, ab, lg, byline, dateline, signed, trailer, ... paragraphs; head a heading (its level the number of div around it); titlePart the title; item a list item; fw, note, figure (its head and p captions linked to it, its figDesc its description), table (a line per row) lb and l begin one; cb ends a block; no geometry

page is the page's number (1-based) or the xml:id of its surface or pb; a page the document does not have is a ValueError. The page's surface gives the image size (its graphic's @width and @height in pixels, else its own extent) and the source's uri (the graphic's @url, unless uri is given); coordinates are converted from the surface's grid (its origin @ulx @uly, scaled to the graphic's size) to pixels of that image.

Roles: a zone's @subtype, else its @type (paragraph, column, head, running-title, header, footer, pageNum, catch, sig, marginalia, note, figure, table, caption, ...; other names as PAGE-XML's and SegmOnto's region names read), else the element that holds all its text, else a paragraph. fw is the page's furniture by its @type: header (and running-title) a header, pageNum a page number, catch a catchword, sig a signature mark, footer a footer; another type a header above the page's first text and a footer below it. note is a footnote, a marginal note (@place margin, left, right, ...) marginalia, @place="end" an endnote. In a text, a note inside a block is a region after it, linked to it (note_of), and furniture comes first or last by where it stands, as in the HTML import.

Inline markup Recorded as choice: sic/corr, abbr/expan, orig/reg the source's reading (sic, abbr, orig) in the line's text, the other as a corrected, expanded or regularized edit of its span; another choice its first child, app its lem (else its first rdg) unclear its text, its span with status illegible (U+FFFD where it is scored) gap no text; status gap on the empty span where it stands (<line>[a:a]) @rend (on hi and any element): italic, bold, underline, strikethrough, sup, sub and their usual spellings the reading's formatting lb[@break='no'] the last word of one line and the first of the next, each with a joined edit holding the whole word (the first half without its division mark) xml:lang a language classification (language_tag; an ill-formed value skipped) where it differs from what encloses it: the page (TEI, text and body, or TEI, sourceDoc and the surface), a region, a line (line, l), else the span of a line it covers space a space

Anything else keeps its text and is otherwise ignored (teiHeader, figDesc, desc and the like hold no text of the page); an unknown element never fails the import. One annotator made all of it: people (kind human) with ground_truth, which also makes the source a ground truth, else the file (kind file), named tei, step transcription. The source has format tei and, for a namespaced file, tei__namespace.

items.title: The document (linecaster.document)
items.text:
A page's or an item's document is a rendering (data model): build_document(t, ..., policy) makes one page's, DocumentBuilder an item's, and export writes it. The DocumentComposer puts it into doc.metadata["document"] for the writers; it is not stored. Each serialization writes the body, the furniture (page headers and footers) only with furniture:

Format Writes HTML (to_html) an HTML5 document: a title h1, a heading of level n h(n+1) (at most h6), a paragraph p, list items li in a ul, a note aside role="doc-footnote", a caption p class="caption", code pre, a page header and footer header role="doc-pageheader" / footer role="doc-pagefooter", a formula block its LaTeX between \[ and \], a table with its cells' spans and header cells (table_html), a picture a figure with its image and the text read inside it; formatting as i, b, u, s, sup, sub, languages as lang, line breaks as br; the document's language as <html lang>, its direction as <html dir="rtl"> or a writing-mode style; a block's language and direction where they are not the document's as its element's lang, dir="rtl" (dir="ltr" in a right-to-left document) and style="writing-mode: vertical-rl" (or vertical-lr) Markdown (to_markdown) by the policy's Markdown rules (MarkdownRules): headings #, list items -, formula blocks $$…$$, tables as HTML or as pipe tables (HTML where a cell spans), a picture the rules' placeholder, italic *, bold **, strikethrough ~~, scripts and underline as HTML with html_scripts, characters Markdown would read escaped with escape; dividers puts --- between the blocks of one layout region and the next; no language or direction (Markdown has none, and neither has text) text (to_text) each block's text, blocks separated by a blank line; a table one row per line, cells separated by tabs JSON (to_json) the complete document, every layer and origin (linecaster.document/2), a language or direction only where one is recorded; from_json reads it back

items.title: Docling (linecaster.formats.docling, the docling extra)
items.text:
from_docling(source, page_no=None, ground_truth=False, name="docling", dataset=None, record=None) reads a DoclingDocument (a document, its dict or its JSON) into a transcription:

  • one region per item of the body, furniture and notes layers (on page page_no, or on every page), in the document's order, which is also the transcription's one reading order: id <label>_<k>, the Docling label as the region's label and, read as a content role, its role classification; the box of the item's first provenance entry (in top-left coordinates; None without one); a section header's level as a heading_level classification;
  • a text item's text as one line per text line (<region>_l<j>, without geometry), each read with its text;
  • a table as a Table of its region, with one line holding its cells' text, so it renders; a picture as a region without lines.

One annotator made all of it: people (kind human) with ground_truth, which also makes the source a ground truth, else the file (kind file), named name, step transcription. The source has format docling, dataset and record as given, and the image size of the page.

items.title: OmniDocBench import (linecaster.evaluation.omnidocbench)
items.text:
from_omnidocbench(entry, ground_truth=True, uri=None) reads one page of OmniDocBench's ground truth (an entry of its JSON list: layout_dets, page_info, extra; or the entry's JSON) into a transcription; the importer import.omnidocbench.v1 (preset omnidocbench-import) runs it on a source document whose data is one entry's JSON. entries(path) yields (page id, entry) for each entry of the JSON (the page id: image_path's file name without its extension), the rows of a table pipelines/import_transcriptions.py reads:

rows = [{"id": pid, "entry": json.dumps(e, ensure_ascii=False)} for pid, e in entries("OmniDocBench.json")]
pyarrow.parquet.write_table(pyarrow.Table.from_pylist(rows), "omnidocbench.parquet")
uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py OUT --parquet omnidocbench.parquet --id-key id --data-key entry \
    --importer omnidocbench-import
OmniDocBench Read as an element of layout_dets a region r<anno_id>: poly its polygon and box, category_type its label, verbatim, and its role: title heading, text_block paragraph, figure picture, figure_caption, table_caption, code_txt_caption caption, figure_footnote, table_footnote, page_footnote footnote, table, equation_isolated formula, header, footer, page_number, code_txt code, reference; equation_caption, abandon and any other other; its attribute and other keys as extension fields (omnidocbench__attribute, omnidocbench__anno_id, a table's omnidocbench__latex) ignore, the category abandon status suppressed: in no text text the region's lines: each row of its spans (line_with_spans, else its merge_list's) a line, cut from the text where the row's first span begins, with the row's box; a division mark a span prints and the text dropped (evap- of evaporator) kept, and both halves a joined edit with the whole word; where a span is not found in the text, in order, or without spans, a line per line of the text, without boxes a span in LaTeX ($…$: equation_inline, footnote_mark) an inline formula, a Formula of its span of the line; without spans, $…$ in the text a table's html a Table of the region (linecaster.formats.html_table), the HTML kept; no lines a display formula's latex (equation_isolated) a Formula of the region, without $$; no lines order the reading order of the regions that have one, and of their lines; furniture and discarded elements, which OmniDocBench leaves unordered, come last in the entry's order extra.relation parent_son to a caption a caption_of link, to a footnote a note_of link; truncated a continues link from the later part; others kept as the transcription's omnidocbench__relation a block's text_language, a table's language a language classification of the region where it is not the page's page_info image_path the source's record, width and height its image size, page_no and every page_attribute extension fields of the source (omnidocbench__data_source, omnidocbench__layout, omnidocbench__special_issue, omnidocbench__language, ...); the language also the page's classification: en/english en, simplified_chinese zh-Hans, en_ch_mixed mul (BCP 47's multiple languages)

One annotator made all of it: people (kind human) with ground_truth, else the file (kind file), named omnidocbench, step transcription; the source has format omnidocbench. The importer fits the transcription to the page image like every importer, except where the size the entry states is the image's transposed (width for height): its coordinates are then the image's, and the stated size is kept (omnidocbench__stated_size). truth_page writes a ground truth as such an entry (evaluation), and from_omnidocbench reads it back with its texts, roles (as far as its categories tell them apart), order, tables and formulas.

items.title: Working images (linecaster.images.convert)
items.text:
The working format for converted images is lossless WebP at full resolution (the block ImageConverter, preset working-image): what the models read is never lossy. Delivered images used as they are (an access derivative) stay as delivered. Pages larger than the size limit go to rejects/. Other formats for other uses are the next section's.

  • Size limit (check_size): width ≤ 16,383 and height ≤ 16,383 (WebP) and width × height ≤ 2 × PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, read at call time, never changed. 2× is exactly where Pillow's Image.open raises DecompressionBombError; that error is turned into ImageTooLarge with the same kind of reason. Checked from the header (Image.open without load), so oversized pages are never decoded; between 1× and 2× Pillow's warning is silenced and the page converted.
  • Color: embedded ICC → sRGB (LittleCMS, perceptual); a profile that cannot be applied is reported (icc_error) and the plain conversion used. 16-bit grayscale → 8 bit as round(v·255/65535); Pillow reads 16-bit RGB as 8-bit itself. Grayscale/bilevel/palette → RGB. Alpha is composited onto white (alpha_flattened); fully opaque alpha is just dropped. CMYK without a profile: Pillow's conversion. EXIF orientation is not applied (coordinates refer to the stored pixels) but reported as exif_orientation.
  • Encoding: always lossless WebP (VP8L), full resolution, method=0, exact=True; effort (Pillow's quality for lossless) defaults to Pillow's 80.
  • info: format, width, height, source_format, source_mode, pixels_sha256 (sha256 of the decoded 8-bit RGB bytes, row-major, what the WebP decodes to), sha256 (of the WebP), decoder (Pillow x / <source library> y / libwebp z), webp_settings, icc_applied, alpha_flattened, and warnings when the image has image warnings (glossary); the keys match PageImage where they overlap.
  • Image warnings: a fault the image is read around is reported, not fatal: a PNG's optional chunk with a wrong checksum is left out when read (as libpng does; Pillow alone refuses the file), and what Pillow warns about while reading, EXIF that cannot be read and an ICC profile that cannot be applied are listed in warnings (also in the page image's extra, and logged). A fault that keeps the pixels from being read rejects the page.

items.title: Image conversion (linecaster.images.transcode, linecaster.images.accel)
items.text:
Page images for other uses (publishing, downloads) are converted by the same block with an image.convert.v1 preset (webp-lossy-q80, jpeg-q90, jp2-lossless, png; pipelines/convert.py): JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB, with the working image's size limit, colour handling and image warnings.

  • Decoding: JPEG (nvJPEG), JPEG 2000 (nvJPEG2000) and TIFF (nvTIFF) in 8-bit gray or RGB on an NVIDIA GPU where the machine has one and nvImageCodec is installed (linecaster[nvimgcodec], CUDA 13 wheels for aarch64 and x86_64); every other image, and every image on a machine without them, with Pillow. Only nvImageCodec's GPU decoders are allowed, so an image it cannot do on the GPU is decoded by Pillow, never by another CPU library. A GPU decode hands the pixels on in the source's own mode with the ICC profile from the header, and the colour handling above runs after either decoder.
  • Encoding: JPEG (nvJPEG) and JPEG 2000 (nvJPEG2000) on the GPU where it can, else with Pillow (libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG); PNG and WebP always with Pillow (zlib, libwebp): no GPU library writes them (nvImageCodec only through its CPU OpenCV extension).
  • Fallback: whatever keeps the GPU from an image, the CPU does it: a file its decoder or encoder rejects (nvJPEG2000, for one, rejects code streams with the vertically causal context, code-block style 0x08), or a failing GPU (an error, too little memory). The image's record says so (gpu_fallback), the block counts it, and a failure of the GPU is logged as a WARNING; accel gpu makes either an error.
  • Choice: found out per machine, never configured (cuda_devices asks the CUDA driver; nvImageCodec is used when installed). accel auto takes the GPU where it can, cpu never, gpu is an error where it cannot. Each image records its decoder and encoder: a GPU and a CPU decoder can round lossy JPEG and JPEG 2000 differently, and a GPU and a CPU encoder write different bytes at the same quality. linecaster images compare FILES decodes images both ways and says how far the pixels differ.
  • Throughput: decoding and encoding are stages with windows of their own, adapted by saturate's controller to the pixels per second and cut when memory or open files run short; a GPU decodes what arrives together in one batch. One worker process per GPU (round robin by worker index); the windows' bound divides the CPUs among the workers.
  • Files: <output_folder>/<item>/<page>.<ext> under a temporary name (.part), renamed when complete; a file that is there already is not converted again (skip_existing).
  • record (page.image, its extra): format, width, height, sha256, pixels_sha256, decoder; encoder, bytes, icc_applied, alpha_flattened, and when present exif_orientation, icc_error, warnings; the delivered image under original, the step under step.

items.title: Tracing
items.text: Every run is traced with OpenTelemetry (linecaster.tracing): spans per task always, spans per page for a trace sample chosen by page id plus every page that failed. Traces go to the run folder and, when the standard OTEL_* variables say so, to an OTLP endpoint; nothing is sent anywhere else. Terms are the glossary's.

items.title: What is traced
items.text:
Task spans, for every task:

Span What it covers Attributes (besides linecaster.component) linecaster.task the task, from its first page to its end (failed: status error, linecaster.error.type) task, tasks, sample (the trace sample's share), stage, units.failed_exported linecaster.warm_up a component loading its engine or client (warm_up()), per component that loads something component.name, preset, engine, model, backend, server linecaster.server.start a server component's warm-up: starting linecaster serve or vLLM/SGLang until it answers server, model, preset, port linecaster.reader.file a file a reader is through: a Parquet file, a file of page records, a manifest (wall time, while its pages also passed the later components) file, pages, seconds.own (the time spent reading) linecaster.writer.flush a page record writer closing its files (a remote file is uploaded then) files

An image folder's file is one page: its reading is the page's, not a task span.

Unit traces, one per page (or item):

Span Parent What it covers linecaster.page (linecaster.item for items a binder makes) none: the trace's root from the reader (or the earliest fetch for it) to the end of the stage's last component linecaster.http.fetch the page each http(s) request a reader made for it: http.host, http.status, http.attempts, http.retries, http.wait_seconds (the rate limits' and the breaker's wait), http.pause_seconds (the time paused after a block such as a 429, or waiting for a usable proxy, when there was a pause), http.tries (each attempt: a status such as 200 or 429 for a response read whole, 200-cut for one the deadline per attempt cut, 200-html for an HTML page where another format was expected, no-response for a timeout or a connection or proxy error; http), http.what (image, ocr) linecaster.component the page one per component, from the boundary before it to the one after it: for a served component it includes the time the page waited in the window linecaster.request.prepare the served component's span building the request (image encoding), in saturate's prepare threads linecaster.request the served component's span from the built request to its result: the wait for a window slot, the HTTP call, retries; tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason linecaster.serving.decode, linecaster.serving.queue, linecaster.serving.model the request in linecaster serve: the image decoded and the transcription read, the wait for the model's worker, the model call (lines, regions, words of its result)

A page's spans are children of its context explicitly, never of "the current span": pages are interleaved in the stream. A page that leaves the stage's components through a binder ends its trace there; the items get their own. A page that never reaches the end of the stage (a component dropped it) is ended when the task ends (linecaster.unfinished).

A failed page (an entry added to doc.metadata["errors"] in this stage) has status error on its root and on the component's span, with linecaster.error.type.

Attributes are identifiers and numbers under linecaster.*, never text or images: component (class), component.name (datatrove name), component.family, unit, page.id, item.id, step, preset (traces from before 0.10 also edition), engine, model, backend (in-process, served), server (the endpoint), counts on a component's span as the page leaves it (lines, regions, words of the component's transcription), tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason, error.type, region (a region recognizer's request). The resource of every span: service.name (linecaster), service.version, host.name, linecaster.process (pipeline, serve), linecaster.run (the run folder's name, or LINECASTER_RUN), linecaster.task, linecaster.tasks, linecaster.stage, linecaster.gpu and linecaster.gpus (from the NVIDIA driver, when there is one); OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES adds to them.

Log records carry trace_id and span_id in extra (JSON lines on Jobs show them): the page a record names by page_id, else the span of the per-unit component running in the thread, else the task's span.

items.title: The trace sample
items.text:
--trace-share SHARE (build(..., trace_share=), default 0.01): a page is in the trace sample when a hash of its id (BLAKE2b, 64 bits) is below SHARE, so the same pages on every rerun and machine, and a larger trace sample contains a smaller one. It is not the sample a run reads (--sample, pipelines). 0 traces only failed pages and the task spans; 1 traces every page. A sampled page's record carries its trace id (page.metadata.trace_id), so the page records lead to the trace.

Every page gets a trace context (doc.metadata["trace"]["traceparent"], W3C, flags 01 for a sampled page, 00 otherwise). The spans of an unsampled page are recorded but not sampled and held per page in a span processor (linecaster.tracing.export.PageBuffer) until the page's root ends: if the page failed in the stage they are exported, otherwise dropped. The memory this takes is bounded by the pages in flight: about 3 KB per ended span, one per component and two per request (about 40 KB per page for the twelve components of the squiddle recipe). In-process a page or two are in flight; a served component holds at most its window and its result queue (max_window + 4 × max_window pages), so with the default window of 32 and five served components about 800 pages, some 30 MB. A page dropped by a component is held until the task ends. linecaster serve records nothing for an unsampled page: a failed unsampled page's trace has the pipeline's spans, not the server's.

items.title: Where traces go
items.text:
• The run folder, always: OUT/traces/<rank>.jsonl.gz per task (OUT/traces/<stage>/<rank>.jsonl.gz with several stages), any fsspec folder like the logs; linecaster serve started by a task (EngineServer) writes <rank>.serve.jsonl.gz next to it (the task gives it the file in LINECASTER_TRACES). The format is OpenTelemetry's file exporter format: one ExportTraceServiceRequest per line in the OTLP JSON encoding, gzipped. Spans are written in batches (every 2 s), each flushed to the file, which is closed (uploaded, for a remote folder) when the task ends, also when it fails; a process killed outright loses its last batch, and linecaster traces reads such a file as far as it goes. A rerun of a task replaces its file. linecaster serve closes its file when it is stopped (the first SIGTERM or SIGINT ends it gracefully; its handlers are set again after the engines load, since an engine's library may replace them).
  • An OTLP endpoint, when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT is set (and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER is not none): OTLP over HTTP (protobuf), configured by the standard variables (headers, timeouts). linecaster serve exports there too; VLMServer starts vLLM with --otlp-traces-endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf.

Without a run folder (run_pages, tests) and without OTLP nothing is traced.

The trace context and the servers. saturate sends the same headers with every request, so a served component puts the page's traceparent into the request body ("traceparent"), which linecaster serve reads (as it reads the header, if a client sends one). An OpenAI-compatible chat server reads it from the headers only: vLLM continues a traceparent header when started with --otlp-traces-endpoint, so with OTLP configured its spans reach the backend, but as traces of their own, not joined to the pages'.

items.title: The command
items.text:
linecaster traces OUT [--by component|preset|task] [--slowest N] [--json]

reads OUT/traces/**/*.jsonl.gz (a task still running: what its file has so far) and prints:

  • per component (or preset, or task) the duration of its linecaster.component spans over the traced pages (n, p50, p90, p99, errors); for served components the split: prepare, request (as the pipeline saw it), and the server's queue, decode and model;
  • the gaps: per component the time it had no page in it between its first page and its last (it waited for its input), when every page was traced (--trace-share 1);
  • the N slowest traced pages (default 10) with their id, seconds, lines, slowest component and trace id;
  • per task its duration, GPU and trace sample, the warm-up of each component and the server starts, the reader's files (pages, seconds reading) and the writers' flush.

--json gives the same as data.

items.title: Run a recipe
items.text: This tutorial transcribes a folder of page images with a recipe: a tested combination of models.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• Python 3.12 and uv 0.13.6 or newer
  • a folder of page images, here scans/

An NVIDIA GPU is recommended: the models run much faster on one.

items.title: 1. Get linecaster
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster

There is nothing to install: every pipeline is a uv script that brings its own environment on its first run.

items.title: 2. See what you can run
items.text:
uv run launch.py

This lists the recipes and the presets of the catalog.

items.title: 3. Run the recipe
items.text:
uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/

The first run installs the engines and downloads the models. squiddle is a modular recipe: a layout model, a line detector and a line recognizer, followed by rule-based steps that find headings and paragraphs.

items.title: 4. Look at the result
items.text:
In out/ What it is pages/ one page record per page: everything that was found, with who found it rejects/ pages that failed, each with the reason run.yaml the run record: what ran, with which presets and versions

To get files you can open, name the formats:

uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/ --files out/files --formats md,alto

items.title: 5. Change one step
items.text:
Options after the recipe's name replace single steps. This keeps the recipe but changes one option of its recognizer:

uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out2/ --set recognition.batch_size=4

The run record lists what you changed.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Run a vision-language model instead of the modular pipeline.
  • Read the overview to see how the parts fit together.

items.title: Score a run against ground truth
items.text: This tutorial measures how well a run read its pages. You need a run (see Run a recipe) and ground truth for the same pages: transcriptions made or checked by people.

items.title: 1. Import the ground truth
items.text:
Linecaster scores page records against page records, so the ground truth is imported first. Here the ground truth is a Parquet table with one row per page and the page's ALTO file in the column alto:

uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py truth/ --parquet ocr.parquet --data-key alto --importer alto-import

The page records are in truth/pages. Other importers read PAGE-XML, hOCR, TEI, HTML and plain text; linecaster presets --step import lists them.

items.title: 2. Check it
items.text:
linecaster ground-truth check truth/pages

This reports what the ground truth holds: how many pages, lines, tables and formulas, in which languages.

items.title: 3. Write a benchmark
items.text:
A benchmark says how to score: which pages, which comparison and which metrics. This writes one that fits the ground truth:

linecaster benchmark init truth/pages benchmark.yaml

Open benchmark.yaml and read it. It is short, and every choice in it is yours to change.

items.title: 4. Score the run
items.text:
linecaster score out/ truth/pages --benchmark benchmark.yaml

The results are in out/scores/:

File What it is scores.parquet the counts for every page evidence.yaml the summary: error rates with their confidence intervals, and exactly how they were measured

items.title: 5. Compare two runs
items.text: Score a second run with the same benchmark. Two evidence records with the same benchmark were measured the same way, so their numbers can be compared.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Evaluation explains the parts.
  • The evaluation reference defines every metric.

items.title: Run a vision-language model
items.text: A vision-language model (VLM) reads a whole page in one request and returns its text, often with layout and tables. This tutorial runs one on a folder of page images.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• everything from Run a recipe
  • an NVIDIA GPU
  • the vllm command on your PATH, or let linecaster build an environment for it with uv

items.title: 1. Pick a preset
items.text:
uv run launch.py

The list shows the VLM presets, for example lightonocr-2-1b.

items.title: 2. Run it
items.text:
uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/

Linecaster starts a vLLM server for the model, sends the pages to it and stops the server when the run ends. Starting the server takes a few minutes.

items.title: 3. Use a server that is already running
items.text:
If you already serve the model, name its address and no server is started:

uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --recognition lightonocr-2-1b \
  --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1

items.title: 4. Let a layout model find the regions first
items.text:
Some presets read one layout region at a time. Add a layout preset, and the model reads each region:

uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0

items.title: What is in the page record
items.text: The model's answer is kept verbatim as a raw output, next to the regions, lines and text that linecaster parsed from it. If a page looks wrong, the raw output shows what the model actually wrote.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Score a run against ground truth.
  • The catalog has a page for every preset, with the model's settings.
